quduri.b: If he guarantees to pay the amount of the buyer it is valid. If he guarantees to produce the items sold on behalf of the seller then it is not valid.

quduri.f: A man hires a mount to load goods. Another man guarantees himm transport of the load. Is the guarantee valid?
quduri.b: If he guarantees the specific mount, then it is not valid. If it is not specific then it is valid.

quduri.f: Must the Makful lahu accept the guarantee for it to be valid?
quduri.b: The guarantee is not valid unless the Makful lahu accepts it in the Majlis of the transaction. An exception is if a sick person instructs his heir to stand as his guarantee. In that case the guarantee is valid even though the creditor was not present.

quduri.f: Two men sought credit and stood guarantee for each other. They paid his debt. Can he seek imbursement from the second debtor?
quduri.b: No, unless he paid an amount above what he personally owed.

quduri.f: Two men stood guarantee for a third man having a debt of 1000. Both would also be guarantors for each other. One of them paid part of the amount or the entire amount. Can he ask for reimbursement from his partner?
quduri.b: Yes, he can ask for half the amount he paid, be it a little or much.

quduri.f: Can a guarantee be given for Kitabah [contract whereby a slave pays a specified amount for his freedom]?
quduri.b: No, neither a free man nor a slave may stand guarantee in this case because it is not a true debt.

quduri.f: A man dies without any assets and has unpaid debts. Can someone guarantee to the creditors for his debts?
quduri.b: Not according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى but the other two Imams permit it.

quduri.f: What is Hawalah?
quduri.b: It is the transfer of debt from one person's responsibility to another's responsibility. It is permissible with debts, not goods and rights.

quduri.f: Is the consent of both parties a condition? [i.e. for Hawalah]
quduri.b: The consent of the Muhil (who is the debtor); Muhtal (creditor); and Muhtal 'alayhi (the one who undertakes to pay the debt) are all required.

quduri.f: Can the creditor then claim from the original debtor? [i.e. after Hawalah]
quduri.b: Once the debt is transferred the debtor is absolved. The creditor may not claim from him unless his rights become Tawa.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Tawa? How does it arise?
quduri.b: Tawa is destruction. It arises according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى in one of two ways - if the Muhtal 'alayhi denies the transfer under oath and the creditor does not have proof; or if the Muhtal 'alayhi dies bankrupt. The other two Imams add a third form of Tawa which is if the court rulers that the Muhtal 'alayhi is bankrupt while still alive.

quduri.f: If the Muhtail 'alayhi demands from the Muhil an amount equal to the amount transferred and the Muhil says, "I do not owe you anything. I transferred a debt you owed me", will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: No, he will owe the amount equal to the debt.

quduri.f: If the debtor claims the transferred amount from the Muhtal, "I transferred to you an amount for you to take on my behalf." The Muhtal denies this, "You transferred a debt you owed me." How will a decision be made?
quduri.b: The Muhil's word will be accepted under oath.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of safatij (Bills of Exchange) according to Fuqaha?
quduri.b: Makruh.

quduri.f: What does the word and term mean? [i.e. safatij]
quduri.b:
It is the plural of Suftajah meaning a paper. It is a loan given so that the lender is safe in his travel.161 

161 E.g. a man gives a trader x amount of Dirham on condition that the trader's agent at another city will pay him that amount. If done without conditions then there is no harm. If safety of the road is stipulated thne it is Makruh because that is deriving benefit from a loan [al-Jawharah].

quduri.f: What is Sulh?
quduri.b: A dispute erupts between two parties concerning rights. They agree to accept part of what is disputed and renounce the remaining claim. This is called Sulh. "Sulh is best."

quduri.f: How many types of Sulh are there?
quduri.b:
There are three categories:
Sulh with confession.
Sulh with silence.
Sulh with denial.
All three are permissible in Shari'ah.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Sulh with confession?
quduri.b: The defendant confesses to a right against him. The plaintiff then compromises upon something.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Sulh with silence?
quduri.b: The defendant neither admits to nor denies the claim, but is pleased to compromise to free himself of the dispute.

quduri.f: What is Sulh with denial?
quduri.b: The defendant denies that there is a claim against him but is willing to compromise to end the dispute.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Sulh with confession?
quduri.b: If it is compromise of money on money then it is treated as a sale. If it is on a benefit it is treated as a hire.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Sulh with denial or silence?
quduri.b: These are implemented with oaths. With regards to the defendant it is deemed the termination of the dispute. With regards to the plaintiff it is deemed an exchange.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of pre-emption if they compromised with a house or about a house?
quduri.b: Pre-emption arises if they compromised with giving a house. It does not arise if they compromised about a disputed house.

quduri.f: If the compromise is with confession, can the defendant demand his share which he is entitled to under the compromise?
quduri.b: Yes, he can claim what was offered in exchange.

quduri.f: The defendant gave up in a compromise of silence or denial. It is discovered that a third party is entitled to the disputed item. What does the plaintiff do?
quduri.b: He will return what the defendant gave him and continue the case with the new claimant. If his claim is established in part of the disputed item, then he will have returned that proportion from whatever the defendant had given in exchange. He will continue the remainder of the dispute with the new claimaint.

quduri.f: A man claimed a right in a house but did not specify the right. The defendant gave him a substitute as a compromise on the claim. Someone then claims part of the house. Will the original plaintiff return what the defendant gave him?
quduri.b:
No, he need not return anything.162

162 Because it is possible that his claim is in the part of the house which the new claimaint does not dispute. The matter is different if he is entitled to the entire house. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: Can compromise be made on a claim to wealth, a benefit, deliberate violations, mistakes [jinayatul 'amad wal khata] and penal punishments?
quduri.b: It is allowed in all that except penal punishment.

quduri.f: A man claims that a woman is his wife. She denies it and pays him as a compromise to leave her. Is this valid?
quduri.b: The compromise is valid and is deemed a Khul' [payment from the woman for divorce].

quduri.f: A woman claims a man is her husband. He denies it and pays her as a compromise to leave him alone. Is this valid?
quduri.b: The compromise is not valid.

quduri.f: A man claims another as his slave. The defendant pays him as a compromise. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: It is permissible. It will be deemed from the claimaint's side as freeing a slave in exchange for money.

quduri.f: The man appointed an agent to compromise on his behalf. Is it the agent's duty to present the amount compromised on?
quduri.b: No, unless it was stipulated. The money is the liability of the principle.

quduri.f: If a man compromised on behalf of another without his authorisation, who is liable for payment?
quduri.b:
There are four scenarios:
He compromised with money and took liability for the money.
He said, "I compromise with you for 2000/this slave." In these two scenarios the compromise is concluded and the amount becomes obligatory upon him.
He says to him, "I have compromised with you upon 1000", and gives it to him. The compromise is complete in this case as well. If he paid to settle the claim against a third party he cannot claim the money back from the third party.
If he says to him, "I compromise with you upon 1000 without liability of it", and does not attribute it to himself, nor that the rendering will be done by him. This compromise is suspended until the defendant confirms it, in which case the 1000 becomes obligatory upon him. If he does not validate it, the compromise is void.

quduri.f: Two partners have a debt against someone. One of the partners compromises on his share with a cloth. What can the other partner do?
quduri.b: He can claim half the debt from the debtor; or he can take half the cloth and make his partner liable for a quarter of the debt. Similarly if one partner had received his half of the debt, then the other partner can share with him what he received, and both will claim the remainder from the debtor.

quduri.f: What if one of them bought something with what he received from the debt? [i.e. two partners have a debt against someone and one of the partners compromises on his share]
quduri.b: The other partner can make him liable for a quarter of the debt.

quduri.f: Two partners sold something on terms of Salam. The one compromises with the other on his share of the item by paying him from the money received. Is this allowed?
quduri.b: It is not allowed according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is allowed.

quduri.f: A man died leaving behind several heirs. The heirs made a settlement with one of them. They paid him and excluded him from the inheritance. Is this allowed?
quduri.b:
The question requires a detailed response:
If the inheritance is land or goods then the settlement is permissible, whether they gave him a lot or a little.
If the inheritance was silver and they gave him gold; or was gold and they gave him silver, then it is permissible as well.
If it is gold, silver and goods, then it is necessary that what they give him must be more than his share of that type of wealth, until his share matches it. The excess will be for his right to the remainder of the inheritance.
If the inheritance is debts against people and one of them paid him money so that he will give up his share of the debt will be amongst them, then the compromise is void.
If they however stipulated that they would absolve the debtors of their debts and would not claim the share of the compromiser, then it is permissible.

quduri.f: A man is owed 1000 immediately. He compromises on 1000 debt, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: This is permissible. It is as if he has delayed the right.

quduri.f: He is entired to 1000 Dirham immediately. The debtor offers to Dinars after a month instead.
quduri.b: This is not permissible. It is a form of Sarf (currency dealing) and delay is not allowed in it.

quduri.f: he is owed 1000 on credit. The debtor offers to compromise with 500 immediately. Is this allowed?
quduri.b:
It is not allowed.163 

163 Cash is better than credit. He is not entitled to the immediate payment. The compromise amount will be in exchange for time which is not permissible.

quduri.f: A man is owed 1000 black Dirham. Can he settle for 500 white Dirham?
quduri.b:
It is not permissible.164 

NOTE: A compromise on a debt owing will not be interpreted as an exchange [for what would be Riba]. It is interpreted as receiving part of a right and forgiving the rest. For example, he is entitled to 1000 genuine Dirham from a man, and settles for 500 alloyed Dirham. That will be as if he forgave part of his right.

164 Because he is not entitled to the white at the time of the contract which is better quality than the black. Thus the exchange of 1000 for 500 with an increase in quality is Riba. However, if he was owed 1000 white and accepted 500 back instead then it is permissible because it is a forfeiture of part of a right in quality and quantity. It is not allowed to compromise on the quantity in exchange for quality because that is an exchange of like for like. Here no regard is paid to the difference in quality other than it has to be taken possession of in the gathering. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: What is Hibah?
quduri.b: Assumption of ownership without compensation.

quduri.f: What are its preconditions? [i.e. of Hibah]
quduri.b: Offer and acceptance.

quduri.f: What else is required after offer and acceptance to complete the deal?
quduri.b: Taking possession is necessary. If the Mawhub lahu [recipient] takes it in the gathering of the offering, even without the explicit permission of the Wahib [presenter] it is valid. It is not valid if he took it after they separated unless the presenter gave the recipient permission.

quduri.f: What are the words the presenter should utter to enact the gift?
quduri.b:
I gift unto you/ I present you with/ I give you/ I am feeding you this food/ I have made his robe yours. "This is for you for the rest of your life"165 "I have made you the rider of this mount" if he intends thereby gifting it to him.

165 When the recipient dies the gift is returned to the presenter/his heirs.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of giving a section as a gift of something which can be physically divided?
quduri.b: It is not permissible unless the gifted part is separated.

quduri.f: Can a share in a jointly owned property be gifted?
quduri.b: It is permissible in things which cannot be divided e.g. a slave, bath, water-wheel etc.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he gifted a section of a jointly owned property which can be divided?
quduri.b: The gift is Fasid. If the goods are divided and a section is given to the recipient then it will be permissible.

quduri.f: A man gave the "flour" in the wheat as a gift; or "the oil in this sesame seeds is a gift to you." What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The gift is Fasid.

quduri.f: If he grinds the wheat and then gives it?
quduri.b: It is still not correct, unless he concludes a new agreement.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that taking possession is a condition of a valid gift. What happens if the intended recipient already has the gift with him?
quduri.b: His prior taking it will suffice and ownership passes with the act of gifting it. This includes a father gifting to his non-adult son. The son immediately becomes the owner because the father's having it in his possession is on behalf of the son.

quduri.f: A stranger gives a gift to a child. How will the deal be completed?
quduri.b: The father, or the guardian if the father died, will collect it.

quduri.f: The mother caring for an orphan collected the gift. Is this permissible?
quduri.b: Yes, even if the orphan was in the care of a stranger, the stranger may colllect it for him.

quduri.f: Is the deali valid if the child collects it [i.e. the gift] himself?
quduri.b: It is valid if the child has intelligence. Otherwise whoever is raising him must collect it as discussed above.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of one man gifting a house to two people; or two people gifting to one man?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى the first gift is valid and the second invalid. According to the other two Imams both are valid.

quduri.f: Is a gift valid if compensation is stipulated?
quduri.b: Yes. In that case taking possession on both sides are required. When both have done so then the deal is correct. However, it will be regarded as a sale. Hence it may be returned due to defect or right of sight and the right of pre-emption will be enacted where applicable.

quduri.f: A man was given a slave-girl except for her foetus. What is the status of this exception?
quduri.b: The gift is valid and the exception is void.

quduri.f: What is the ruling on taking a gift back?
quduri.b: If someone gave a stranger a gift, he may claim it back, unless he gave something in exchange; or the recipient increased in the gift an increase which is joined; or one of the two parties died; or the recipient no longer owns the gift. Although taking a gift back is allowed under these conditions it is Makruh Tahrimi to the worst degree. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The one who takes a gift back is like a dog who laps its own vomit. We have no worse comparison." [al-Bukhari]

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated a stranger? [i.e. when taking back a gift] Can a gift not be taken from a relative?
quduri.b: A gift given to a blood relative who cannot be married or to a spouse cannot be claimed back.

quduri.f: You mentioned that if the recipient gave something in exchange the gift cannot be taken back. Explain this exchange.
quduri.b:
It will be in the case therecipient says, "Take this in exchange for your gift/as a substitute/in place of." Once the presenter takes the recipient
s gift he can no longer reclaim his gift. The same applies if a third party offers him a gift because of the gift he gave and he accepts, he may then no longer reclaim his gift.

quduri.f: The recipient [i.e. of the gift] gave something in exchange. It transpires that a third party is entitled to half the original gift. What can he claim?
quduri.b: The claimant can claim half the item given in exchange.

quduri.f: If the claimant is entitled to half the item given in exchange. Can the presenter reclaim his gift?
quduri.b: No, unless he first returns the item he received and then he can claim the entire gift back.

quduri.f: What are the conditions to validly take a gift back?
quduri.b:
When reclaiming a gift is permissible, then it must be through mutual consent or a court ruling.166

166 Because the recipient's ownership has been established in the goods it cannot be removed except with consent or a court decision.

quduri.f: The gift perishes and a third party emerges as the legitimate owner and holds the recipient liable. Can the recipient claim against the presenter?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Must a poor man take physical possession of charity to establish his ownership?
quduri.b: Charity is the same like a gift. Ownership is not established until possession is taken. Charity of a jointly owned item which can be divided is not allowed.

quduri.f: Can a single item be given to two poor people in charity?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Can charity be reclaimed?
quduri.b: It cannot be taken back once possession has been taken.

quduri.f: Is 'Umra167 and Ruqba168 permissible according to our Three Imams?
quduri.b:
'Umra is permissible. It belongs to the recipient and to his heirs after him. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى Ruqba is invalid. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is valid.169

167 To give a house to someone for the duration of his life. The ownership is valid and the condition void. We have explained that Fasid conditions do not nullify gifts. [al-Hidayah]
168 My house is for you as Ruqba [awaiting death].
169 According to him, "For you," establishes ownership and "as Ruqba" is Fasid as in 'Umra. The proof of the other two is that Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted 'Umra and not Ruqba. They also say the Ruqba means, "If I die before you then the house is yours." These words indicate a condition of ownership based on danger which is void. The only form of validity is according to them is that of 'ariyah [use without ownership].

quduri.f: What is Ghasb?
quduri.b: It is the removal of the legimate hand through the establishment of a nullifying hand over respectable wealth with monetary value which can be transferred without the permission of the owner.

quduri.f: A man usurped something and claims that it has perished. What is the ruling against him?
quduri.b: In principle he is supposed to return the usurped item itself. If he claims that it is perished the judge will detail him until satisfied that if it still existed he would have revealed it. The judge will then rule that he should substitute it.

quduri.f: What will the substitute be? [i.e. when a man usurped something and it perished]
quduri.b: If he usurped that which has a replacement of the same kind e.g. wheat, and it perishes in his hands then he is liable to replace it with a like good. If it is something which does not have an exact substitute like counted goods which differ, then he should compensate with the price.

quduri.f: Does it make a difference if the item perished on its own and if the usurped destroyed it?
quduri.b: There is no difference. The usurper is liable if it perished in his hands, through his action or otherwise.

quduri.f: What is the effect of damage to the usurped goods?
quduri.b: The usurper is liable to pay for it.

quduri.f: A usurped item changed because of the usurper in a manner that it is no longer called the same item and its major benefits have been lost e.g. a man usurps a sheep, slaughtered it and roasts/cooks it; or wheat and he ground it; or iron and he made a sword out of it; or brass which he made into a vessel. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The victim is no longer the owner of the substance which the usurper now owns. The usurper may not use it until he substitutes it for the victim.

quduri.f: A man usurped a white cloth and dyed it red; or cereal which ie mixed with butter, what is the ruling?
quduri.b: The owner can give the cloth to the usurper and make him liable for the price of the white cloth/give him the cereal and demand that he substitute it; or he can take his goods back and owe him the price of the dying/butter.

quduri.f: If a man usurps land and builds on it?
quduri.b: The owner no longer has it and the usurper must pay him the price.

quduri.f: The usurped item disappeared and the owner claimed the price. The two parties differ in the evaluation. What will be paid?
quduri.b: The usurper's word will be taken under oath, unless the owner can produce evidence that it is more. Once the usurper undertakes liability of that price he becomes the owner.

quduri.f: The usurper became liable to pay for the missing usurped item whether through the word of the owner; the proof of the owner; the refusal of the usurper to take an oath; or the oath of the usurper. The item is then found and its price is more than the amount he took liability for. Has the owner any right over the difference?
quduri.b:
If the usurper took liability through his own word under oath then the owner can let go of further liability or he can take his item and return the compensation paid. 

If he took liability because of the word of the owner or the proof the owner presented, or his refusal to take an oath then the owner has no choice - the usurper owns it.

quduri.f: He usurped gold/silver and made it into Dirham/Dinar or vessels. Has the ownership been transferred?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى the owner retains ownership because the substance of the item remains from all aspects.170

170 According to the other two the usurper will owe the amount of gold/silver he usurped and will own the usurped item because he had added craftsmanship to it. If he however beat it into sheets then ownership has not been transferred accroding to all three Imams.

quduri.f: A man slaughtered a sheep without the owner's permission. What can the owner do?
quduri.b: He can give him the carcass and demand the price of the sheep; or he can claim the value of the damage.

quduri.f: A man burnt the cloth of someone else. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If the burn is slight, the burner will be liable for the damage. If the damage is substantial whereby the general benefit is lost, the owner may claim the price from him.

quduri.f: When you defined Ghasb you stipulated that it must be of "respectable wealth with monetary value which can be transferred..." What is the relevance of these conditions?
quduri.b:
The relevance can be seen from the following examples:
A Muslim destroyed wine/pigs belonging to another Muslim. He will bear no liability because these are not respectable items and have no monetary value by a Muslim. If however a Muslim destroys a Zimmi's wine/pig he is liable because they have monetary value to the Zimmis.
Usurpation is not found in land according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى because land cannot be transferred and move. Thus if the land is destroyed171 the usurper is not liable according to them, but is according to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى.
171 For example, a flood sweeps away the soil and trees.

quduri.f: Usurpation does not occur on land, but if someone took over land and whether by his actions or residence the land is damaged is he liable?
quduri.b: Yes, he is liable according to all three Imams.

quduri.f: A man usurped a land and built a building or planted trees. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The usurper must uproot the trees/demolish the builindg and return the empty land to the owner. If that will however damage the land, then the owner may pay him for the building/tree free of the earth and assume possession over them.

quduri.f: The usurped item increased in the hands of the usurper. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The increase such as a baby of a usurped female or the fruits of a garden is amanah [trust] in the hands of the usurper. If it perishes he is not liable unless he was neglectful or he refused to give it to the owner when he owner claimed it.

quduri.f: A man usurped a slave-girl. He or someone else had intercourse with her whilst she was in his hands. She gave birth as a result and her value dropped. Who is liable for the loss?
quduri.b: The usurper is liable. If the baby is worth the lost value then the baby is in settlement of the loss and the usurper has no further liability. If the baby's value does not fully compensate, its value will be deducted from the loss and the usurper will be liable for the remainder.

quduri.f: A man usurped a mount and rode it/ a house and inhabited it/ a slave and used his services. He did this for a month for example. Does he owe anything for the benefit he got?
quduri.b:
No, unless the usage caused damage.172

172 He is not liable in a court of law, but morally he is a sinner.

quduri.f: What is Wadi'ah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
quduri.b:
It is derived from Wad', meaning to leave behind. In Shari'ah it means to leave an item behind by a person who is capable of protecting goods, whilst the item remains under the ownership of the owner.173

173 The difference between Wadi'ah and Amanah is that the aim of Wadi'ah is protection of the item, whilst Amanah is something which has unintentionally fallen into someone's control, like if the wind blew a cloth into someone's lap. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Wadi'ah when in the possesion of the Muda' [one who is entrusted with the Wadi'ah]?
quduri.b: It is an Amanah [trust] in his hands. He is not liable if it perishes unless he was negligent.

quduri.f: Must the Muda' protect it himself? [when he is entrusted with Wadi'ah]
quduri.b:
He must protect it himself or with someone from his household. If he gives it to someone else to protect or places it as Wadi'ah by a third party then he is liable. Exceptions are if his house burnt and he gave it to his neighbour for safekeeping; or he was on a ship and feared that it would sink so he sent it to another ship. In these cases he is not liable because he acted in the interests of the Mudi' [owner of the Wadi'ah]174 

174 However he will not be believed in these cases unless he takes an oath [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: The owner instructed the Muda' not to give the Wadi'ah to his wife. He gave it to her. Or he instructed him, "Guard it in this room," he then guarded it in another room of the same house. The Wadi'ah perished. Is he liable?
quduri.b: Not in these cases. If however he left it at another house he is liable.

quduri.f: The owner comes to collect the Wadi'ah. For this purpose he hires someone to help him. Who pays this fee?
quduri.b: The owner.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of laibility if the Wadi'ah became mixed with the wealth of the Muda' or the Muda' mixed it himself?
quduri.b: If the Wadi'ah became mixed with his wealth without his action, then he becomes a partner with the owner. If he mixed it until it becomes indistinguishable from his wealth then he is liable for it.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of liability if the Muda' spent from the Wadi'ah?
quduri.b: If he spent it all, he is liable for the full amount. If he spent some of it and the rest perished, then he is only liable for the amount spent.

quduri.f: If he spent part of it [i.e. the Muda' spent from the Wadi'ah] and then repaid that amount so that it became mixed and undistinguishable, is he liable for the enitre or part amount?
quduri.b: He is liable for the entire amount.

quduri.f: The owner came to collect the Wadi'ah. The Muda' refused to give despite being able to. It then perishes in his hands without any negligence. Is he liable?
quduri.b: He is liable. His not being negligent will not be a deference as his refusal to surrender it when able to, is also transgression.

quduri.f: The Muda' transgressed with the Wadi'ah. He rode the animal/wore the clothing/used the slave/ or gave it to a third party as Wadi'ah. The transgression terminated and it returned to his hands. Is he liable?
quduri.b:
No, the liability then ends.175

175 Meaning that the liability for that transgression ends. If he transgresses again the liability is reimposed.

quduri.f: The owner comes to collect the Wadi'ah and the Muda' denies that he left a Wadi'ah by him. What is his liability?
quduri.b: He is permanently liable. Even if he later confesses to the Wadi'ah his liability does not terminate, even if it perishes without his doing. The denial is a transgression in itself.

quduri.f: Can the Muda' travel with the Wadi'ah?
quduri.b:
Yes, unless the owner had prohibited it, and as long as there is no fear about it when taking it out.176

176 These are the conditions of Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to the other two Imams he may not travel with it if it needs to be ported or otherwise incurs inconvenience.

quduri.f: If it needs to be transported and is inconvenient, can he still travel with it?
quduri.b: He may as per the conditions mentioned.

quduri.f: Two men leave a Wadi'ah by one man. One of them comes and asks for his share. Must the Muda' give it to him?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى he may not give him anything until the other man comes. According to the other two Imams he may give him his share.

quduri.f: If a man gives a Wadi'ah to two men, can one of them give the entire trust to the other?
quduri.b: If it is something which can be divided then it will not be allowed. It must be divided and each will look after a half. If it cannot be divided then one of them will look after the entire item with the permission of the other.

quduri.f: The Muda' returned the Wadi'ah to the owner's house, not to the owner personally. Is he liable if it perishes?
quduri.b:
Yes.177

177 Because the owner was not satisfied with anyone else protecting it. If he was he would not have left it as Wadi'ah by the Muda'.

quduri.f: Who bears the expenses of returning the Wadi'ah?
quduri.b: The one who made the Wadi'ah [e.g. the owner].

quduri.f: What is 'Ariyah?
quduri.b: Assumption of ownership of a benefit without compensation.

quduri.f: What is its status in Shari'ah? [i.e. of 'Ariyah]
quduri.b: It is permissible.

quduri.f: With what words is it enacted? [i.e. 'Ariyah]
quduri.b: When the Mu'ir [owner who allows the use of his property] says, "I have given you this as 'Ariyah/I give you this slave to use/my house is for you to reside/my house is for you to reside for the rest of your life." If he says, "i feed you from this earth/I favour you with this cloth/I let you ride on this animal," then it is a valid 'Ariyah unless he intended it as a gift.

quduri.f: What is the status of the 'Ariyah in the hands of the Musta'ir [borrower]?
quduri.b: It is a trust; if it perishes without transgression then he is not liable.

quduri.f: Can the borrower hire the 'Ariyah to a third party?
quduri.b: No, that is a transgression. If he does so and it perishes then he is liable.

quduri.f: Can the lender borrow the 'Ariyah to a third party?
quduri.b: Yes, as long as he does not give it to such a person through which the use will substantially change.

quduri.f: Can Dirhams, Dinars, weighed goods and measured goods be lent as 'Ariyah?
quduri.b: Yes, they are loans even if the parties call it 'Ariyah.

quduri.f: A man lent a horse and returned it to the master's stable. It then perished. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He is not liable because he handed it in a way people recognise. The same applies if he returned a borrowed slave to the master's house. Although he did not return him to the master personally he is not liable.

quduri.f: Who is liable for the expense of returning the 'Ariyah?
quduri.b: The borrower bears the expense just as a usurper is liable for the expense of returning the usurped goods. The cost of returning hired goods is upon the hirer.

quduri.f: Can the lender demand the 'Ariyah back?
quduri.b: Yes, he can demand it whenever he wishes.

quduri.f: If someone borrowed land to build thereon or plant a tree, he has done so when the owner demands it back; what happens to the tree/building?
quduri.b:
If the 'Ariyah was given for a specific time and the owner demands it bakc before the allotted time expires then the owner is liable to compensate the borrower for his losses in uprooting the tree/removing the building. If there was no specified time then he can force the borrower to remove the building/tree. In this case he has no liability.178 

178 That is according to al-Quduri. According to al-Hakim ash-Shahid the owner is liable to pay the borrower the cost of the tree/building and he will own it, unless the borrower wishes to remove them. He will not be liable for the price because it is his property. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: What is Muzara'ah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: It is zar' (sowing)) on the syntax scale of mufa'alah. In Shari'ah it is a deal between a landowner and a labourer whereby the labourer will farm the land and will be entitled to a stipulated share such as a third or a quarter.

quduri.f: What is the status of Muzara'ah according to our three Imams?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is void. According to the other two there are four types:
The land and seeds belong to one party and the labour to another.
The land belongs to one party and the labour, cattle and seeds belong to another.
The land, seeds and cattle belong to one party and the labour to another. These three types are permissible.
The land and cattle belong to one party and the seeds and labour belong to another. This type is not allowed.179
179 Because the cattle is being hired for part of the [non-existing] crops which is not permissible.

quduri.f: What conditions are required to valudate the Muzara'ah in the three permissible types?
quduri.b:
There are two conditions:
The time must be stipulated.
That the crops must be jointly owned between them.

quduri.f: Two parties entered into a Muzara'ah agreement. They stipulated a set amount of Qafiz of the crop for one of them. What is the status of this Muzara'ah?
quduri.b: It is void.

quduri.f: And if they stipulated that whatever grows by the banks of the rivulet or stream belongs to a specified one of them?
quduri.b: This is also void.

quduri.f: When the Muzara'ah is valid, how are the crops shared?
quduri.b: The crops will be divided according to the ratio they had stipulated. If the earth did not grow any crops then the labourer will not get anything.

quduri.f: The Muzara'ah was Fasid, but the crops grew and the labourer worked on them. How will the crops be shared?
quduri.b: There will be no sharing. Instead, the crops will belong to the owner of the seeds. If the seeds belonged to the landowner then the labourer will receive a market fee which will not exceed the amount they had agreed upon. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he will receive a market fee whatever amount it may reach. If the seeds were from the labourer then the landowner will receive a market fee instead.

quduri.f: The owner of the seeds refused his labourer after the agreement had been reached. Can he be forced upon it?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If the party which does not have the seeds refuses, what will be decided?
quduri.b: The judge will force him to fulfil his labour.

quduri.f: What will they do if the time period has expired but the crops are not yet ripe?
quduri.b: They will leave the crops until they ripen. The farmer [labourer] pays a market rent in proportion to his share of the produce of the earth until the crops are harvested. They will share the expenses of the farming in proportion to their rights.

quduri.f: Who bears the expenses of harvesting, transport, griding and sifting?
quduri.b: It will be shared amongst them according to their shares. If they stipulate it upon the worker the Muzara'ah is void.

quduri.f: If one of the parties dies does the contract remain?
quduri.b:
The contract is nullified.180

180 Al-Quduri has left it in those general terms. According to al-Jawharah that is if he dies before crops grow. If the landowner dies after the crops grow then the land will be left for the labourer to tend and upon harvest it will be divided as agreed. If it was the labourer who died his heirs will work on his behalf. The landowner may not prevent him as he will not be harmed, but if the crops are uprooted the heirs will suffer. They will not receive a fee for their work. If they want the crops uprooted they cannot be forced to work on the crops instead. The landowner will be told, "Uproot it and share it between you/ Give them the price of their share and the crops are all for you/ spend on their share and you can be reimbursed from their share."

quduri.f: What is Musaqah?
quduri.b: It is Saqy (irrigation) on the syntax scale of mufa'alah. In Shari'ah it is to hand fruit trees to the care of another party to care for them in exchange for an agreed share of the fruit such as a third or quarter.

quduri.f: What is the status of Musaqah?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is void. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is valid on condition that a time a stipulated and as well the each party's share of the jointly owned fruit.

quduri.f: In which trees can Musaqah be made?
quduri.b: It is valid in palms, vines and other trees and fruit bearing plants and in tubers like egg-plant.

quduri.f: Is there an additional condition?
quduri.b: If the tree is handed over Musaqah and the fruit increases through his labour then the Musaqah is valid. If his labour does not increase the fruit then it is not valid.

quduri.f: If the agreement is Fasid what does the labourer receive?
quduri.b: Market related wage.

quduri.f: Is the contract ever nullified?
quduri.b: Yes, through the death of either party, just as in Muzara'ah.

quduri.f: Is the contract cancelled in any circumstances?
quduri.b: Yes, just as valid reasons cancel contract of hire, they also cancel Musaqah.

quduri.f: What is Mawat [virgin land]? How is its Ihya [revival/cultivation] made?
quduri.b: Mawat is such land from which no benefit is derived, because the land no longer receives water; or it is submerged in water; or for any other similar reason which prevents cultivation. It is permissible to cultivate ancient land which has no master; or it had an owner during the Islaamic period but its specific owner cannot be identified. The land must be so far from the city that if one stood by the building right at the end of the city and shouted, one would not be heard in that land.

quduri.f: Is the permission of the Imam needed for that? [to cultivate land which has no master]
quduri.b: Yes, the permission of the ruler is needed. He who cultivates a land with the ruler's permission owns it. According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى if one cultivates it without permission then he does not own it. The other two Imams say that he will own it even if he cultivates it without permission.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a Zimmi cultivating the virgin land?
quduri.b: His cultivation is the same as a Muslim's and he owns it.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of cultivating the virgin land?
quduri.b: It entails tilling the land, irrigating it or digging canals to it and bring water to it, or to dig a well in it, or to build a dam to store the water, or to sow seeds in it, or t o plant in it or to build on it.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated the condition that the land be far from the city?
quduri.b: Because people might be in need of the land near the city. They gather their crops there and graze their herds there. Hence cultivation of such land is not allowed.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if someone digs a well it counts as reviving the land. If someone digs the land then what does he acquire from the land?
quduri.b:
He acquires a Harim around it which he will own.181

181 Having the rights and what is associated around it. It is called Harim because it is Haram to the non-owner. [Raddul Mukthar]

quduri.f: What is the extent of this Harim? [i.e. if someone digs a well on dead land]
quduri.b: If he uses the well to water his animals then it is 40 arms-spans in all directions. If he brings the animals to draw the water to water his crops then it is 60 arm-spans.

quduri.f: If the well has a flowing spring in it, what is the Harim? [i.e. when someone digs a well and revives the land]
quduri.b: 500 arm-spans.

quduri.f: What is the effect of granting a Harim to the one who dug a well?
quduri.b: No-one else may dig a well in that area.

quduri.f: If the Tigris or Eupharates [i.e. a river] changes course, can the revealed land be claimed for cultivation?
quduri.b: If it is possible that the river will return there, then the land may not be claimed. If it will not return then it may be claimed if not within the Harim of habitation. Whoever cultivates it under these conditions and with the permission of the ruler becomes the owner.

quduri.f: A man owns a canal which flows through the land of another man. Does he have Harim?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى he does not, unless he has proof of it. According to the other two Imams he can dam the canal and close it up with the earth.

quduri.f: A man has established a claim on virgin land but does not inhabit it, and leaves it like that. Can the judge rule against him?
quduri.b: He will be given respite of three years, after which the land will be confiscated and given to someone else.

quduri.f: What is a Mazun/Ma'dhun?
quduri.b: It is the opposite of Mahjur [incapitated person[. We explained in Katabul Hijr that there are three causes for incapacitation: childhood, slavery and insanity. We shall explain here some Masail which related to a slave whose owner has given him permission to buy and sell. At the end of the chapter we shall discuss Masail related to a child who has been given permission.

quduri.f: What is the status of the slave's transactions when the owner has given him permission?
quduri.b: If the owner has given general permission then the slave may engage in any trade. He may buy, sell, give collateral and take collateral. If he has been given permission for one kind of trade he may do all trades.

quduri.f: What is the ruling when the owner gives permission for a specifically defined transaction, e.g. to buy a robe for wearing/food for the family?
quduri.b: This is not permission to trade. He is limited to do what he has been ordered to. The laws of Mazun will not apply to him.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Mazun confesses to debts, usurpation and Wadi'ah?
quduri.b: His confession is valid.

quduri.f: If he [i.e. Mazun] has been given general permission can he marry?
quduri.b: He may neither marry himself, nor may he let a slave - male or female - he bought marry.

quduri.f: Can he [i.e. the Mazun] make a Mukatab contract with a slave he bought or free him for money?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Can he give gifts and charity?
quduri.b: He may not give gifts, with or without receiving compensation from the recipient. He may however give a little food or invite someone to join him in his food.

quduri.f: A Mazun trades and incurs debts. Who is liable for them?
quduri.b: The debts will be on his neck [slavery] and he will be sold for the creditors, unless the owner ransoms him. Once he is sold the creditors will share the price in proportion to their shares. If there remains an outstanding amount then it will be claimed from him when he is free.

quduri.f: A Mazun slave incurs debts covering the value of his possessions and himself. Does his owner still possess what he owns?
quduri.b: No he does not. Thus if the owner sets free a slave of that Mazun slave, the slave will not be freed. This is according to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to the other two Imams, the owner owns what is in the possession of the Mazun slave even if the debts encompass it.

quduri.f: What is the status of the owner setting his indebted Mazun slave free?
quduri.b: The slave is free and the owner is liable to pay the creditors the value of the slave. In shortfall in their claim must be paid by the ex-slave.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of the Mazun selling something to his owner?
quduri.b: The Mazun slave may sell to his owner at market rates or more; but not less, if the slave is indebted. If he is not, then the sale has no basis because the slave and his possessions belong to the owner in any case.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the owner sells something to his Mazun slave?
quduri.b:
It is permissible at market rates or less, not more. This condition is also only when the slave is indebted. If the owner hands the item over before payment, the price is void.182

182 Because if the item is handed over before taking the price then it becomes a debt against the slave, and debts to the owner are not established against a slave. Once the price is void it is as if the owner sold without a price. The sale is thus not valid. What is meant by the price being void is that the owner cannot demand it from the slave and will instead take the goods back from him. [Al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: If the owner retains the goods until the slave pays?
quduri.b: That is permissible.

quduri.f: Can the owner declare the slave to be incapacitated?
quduri.b:
Yes, the slave will become incapacitated, on condition that the owner announces his incapacitation in the market.183

183 Because they believed that they could transact with him. That belief will not be rectified without knowledge. It is a condition that most of the people of the market are informed. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: Is there another way the Mazun slave can be incapacitated?
quduri.b:
Yes, if the owner dies, becomes insane or enters the land of the Kuffar as an apostate then the slave becomes incapacitated.184 When a Mazun slave runs away he becomes incapacitated. When a Mazun slave-girl gives birth to her owner's child she becomes incapacitated.1

184 If the slave becomes completely insane he becomes incapacitated, as when he enters the land of the Kuffar as an apostate. According to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he becomes incapacitated as soon as he abandons Islam. According to the other two Imams when he enters the lands of the Kuffar.

quduri.f: What is the status of the confession of a Mazun slave to debts, usurpations and amanat when he has been incapacitated?
quduri.b: The confession is valid for whatever he holds according to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى. According to the other two Imams his confession is invalid.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a guardian giving a child permission to trade?
quduri.b: The permission is valid. Once he has been given permission then his buying and selling is the same as a Mazun slave's. His transactions will take effect if he understands buying and selling.

quduri.f: What is Waqf?
quduri.b:
Literally it means to keep back. In Shari'ah it is to keep an item in the status of ownership of the Waqif [one making the endownment] whilst giving the benefit in charity.185

185 Which is according to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to the other two Imams, it is keeping an item in the status of the ownership of Allah. "Ownership of the Waqif" according to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى means before a court decision, because after a judge rules then the ownership is removed from the Waqif according to him as well.

quduri.f: Why has Waqf been given recognition in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: In order that people in need186 may utilise its benefit whilst the substance remains intact. Also, so that the substance can remain as Sadaqah Jariyah [perpetual charity] for the Waqif. Rasulullah ﷺ said, "When a human dies his deeds end except for three - perpetual charity, or knowledge through which people benefit, or pious offspring who pray for him." [Muslim]

quduri.f: When is the ownership of the Waqif over the endowment terminated?
quduri.b:
According to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it does not terminate unless the judge rules thus; or he attaches it to his death and says, "When I die then I make my house Waqf for ..." According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it terminates with his mere utterance. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it does not terminate until he appoints a trustee for the Waqf and hands it over to him, because it is the right of Allah.187

187 According to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is not finalised until the judge rules that it moves out of his ownership by way of a bequest. According to the other two it is finalised without that. The general 'Ulama agree with that and that is correct. According to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is finalised by his mere utterance because it is the same as setting a slave free. The Fatwa is upon this. [Raddul Muhtar]

quduri.f: Does the Waqf become the property of the Mawquf 'alayhi [one for whom the endowment has been made] after it leaves the property of the Waqif?
quduri.b: Once the Waqf is validated as per the differences we have mentioned, it leaves the property of the Waqif but does not become part of the property of the Mawquf 'alayhi.

quduri.f: Is there any condition for the correctness of the Waqf according to our three Imams?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the Waqf is not complete until it is made for a party which does not ever end.188 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى if he mentioned a beneficiary which comes to an end then it is correct. It will then pass onto the poor even if he did not mention it.

188 Whereby he says, "I make this a charity Waqf forever for the sake of Allah for the descendants of so-and-so as long as the line continues. If the line ends, then it is for the poor," because there will always be poor.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of jointly owned Waqf?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is permissible. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is not permissible.189

189 This difference is on that which can be divided. As for that which cannot be divided then joint Waqf is allowed according to Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى as well. There is no joint Waqf in Masajid and graveyards according to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى as well.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Waqf of land?
quduri.b: It is permissible.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Waqf of items which can be moved and transported?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it is not permissible. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى if a land is given as Waqf with its cattle and labourers who are slaves, then it is permissible. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى transport and weapons can me made Waqf in the way of Allah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of selling, making an owner and dividing a Waqf?
quduri.b: It may not be sold or an owner made over it. Joint Waqf can be divided if the partner so requests. This is according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى who recognises joint Waqf.

quduri.f: When does the ownership of the Waqif terminate over the land if he built a Masjid on it?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it does not terminate until he detaches it from his property by way of the path and allows people to pray in it. Thus when even one person has prayed in it, his ownership is terminated. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it terminates with his saying, "I have made this a Masjid."

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a water-source [e.g. well], hostel for travellers, hospice or graveyard?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى these remain his property until the court rules otherwise. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى his ownership terminates when he says he made these Waqf. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى when he gives people water from his water-source; or when the people start living in the hostel and hospice; or they bury the dead in the graveyard; then his ownership is terminated.

quduri.f: What must the trustee do with the income of the Waqf?
quduri.b: It is Wajib for him to first spend in on the maintenance of the Waqf, whether the Waqif stipulated it or not.

quduri.f: If a man made a house Waqf for living, who will repair and maintain it?
quduri.b: Whoever lives there will repair and maintain it. If he refuses or is poor, then the judge will rent it out and use the rent to repair it. Once it is repaired he will return it to the one who has the right of living there.

quduri.f: If a Waqf house is destroyed can the rubble be shared amongst those entitled to the Waqf?
quduri.b: The judge will use the rubble to restore the Waqf if he needs it. If he does not, he will leave the rubble until it is needed. It is not permissible to share it amongst those entitled to the Waqf.

quduri.f: A man declared a Waqf but stipulated the benefits/the trusteeship for himself. What is the ruling?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is permissible. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is not.191

191 As for the first [keeping the benefits] as-Sadr ash-Shahid said that the Fatwa is on the view of Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى in order to encourage people to establish Waqf.

quduri.f: What should someone do who finds an abanonded boy or a girl?
quduri.b: He should take the child lest it perish and should protect it. It is called Laqit because it has been picked up.

quduri.f: When the one who has discovered the child picks it up, who should bear its expenses?
quduri.b: He will spend money from the Baytul Mal [public treasury] on it.

quduri.f: A man finds a child. Can another man take the child from him?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If someone claims that the child is his [i.e. the foundling], will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: Yes, his word will be accepted under oath.

quduri.f: What if two men both claim that the child is theirs?
quduri.b: If one of them can describe some feature on the child's body then it is his. If none can, then it is for both unless one of them claimed the child first, in which case he will get the child.

quduri.f: A child was found in a city or town of the Muslims. A Zimmi claims the child. Will the child's lineage be attributed to the Zimmi?
quduri.b: Yes, but the child will be classified as a Muslim because he was found in the realms of Islam.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the child was found in a town of Zimmis; or a place of worship of the Christians or Jews?
quduri.b: It is a Zimmi in this case.

quduri.f: A man claims that the child is his slave. Will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: No, the child will be free.

quduri.f: A slave claims that the child is his, will his word be accepted?
quduri.b: His word will be accepted but the child will be deemed free.

quduri.f: Money was found tied to the child. To whom will it belong?
quduri.b: It will belong to the child because it was in his hands. He is most entitled to own it.

quduri.f: A man found a child. He later wishes to get the child married or to transact in its wealth. May he do so?
quduri.b: He may neither get the child married nor may he transact with its wealth. He does however have trusteeship to spend from its wealth and buy necessities from it such as food and clothing.

quduri.f: If someone gives a gift to the child, who must take possession of it?
quduri.b: The one who found the child.

quduri.f: Can the one who found him send him to learn a craft or hire out his services?
quduri.b:
Yes.192

192 That is according to al-Quduri. Al-Jami'as-Saghir states that it is Makruh to hire out the child and that is more correct.

quduri.f: What is a Luqtah?
quduri.b: It is wealth flung in some place. It is called Luqtah [picked up] because one who sees it rushes to pick it up.

quduri.f: If someone sees it [i.e. wealth flung in some place] can he pick it up?
quduri.b: If he fears that it will be destroyed it is Wajib to pick up. If not, then it is not Wajib, but permissible. If he picks it up he should make someone witness that he has picked it up to safeguard it for its owner and will return it to him.

quduri.f: Once he picks it up [i.e. wealth flung in some place] what should he do?
quduri.b: If it is less than 10 Dirham then he should announce it for a few days. If it is at least 10 Dirham then he should announce it for a longer period up to a year. If the owner claims it, well and good, otherwise he should give it in charity.

quduri.f: What happens if the owner claims it after he gave it away?
quduri.b: The owner can validate the charity or he can make the donor liable.

quduri.f: Can a lost sheep, cow or camel be collected like this?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man picked up a lost animal. Who is liable for the expenses he incurred to maintain the animal?
quduri.b:
If he spends on it without the permission of the court, then he has given freely from his side. Nobody is indebted to him. If he did it with the court's permission then that is a debt against the owner.193

193 It is also said that he should announce until he is satisfied that the owner will not be claiming it. It is appropriate that he announce it at the place he found it and at the Jami' Masjid. If it is something one knows that the owner will not look for, such as date pits, one need not announce it and may use it. However, ownership remains with the owner.

quduri.f: If the finder spends so much on a found animal that his expenses equal the value of the animal, what should he do?
quduri.b: He should present his case before the judge. If the animal has some benefit the judge will hire it out and spend the rental on the animal's maintenace. If it has no benefit and fears that the maintenance costs will cover the value of the animal then he will sell it and safeguard the price. The better option is to order the maintenace of the animal and the costs will be a debt against the owner.

quduri.f: A man spent on the animal with the court's permission. The owner comes to claim it. Can the finder refuse to return the animal until the owner reimburses his costs?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man found a lost item. Someone comes and claims that he is the owner. Will he be given it based on his mere claim?
quduri.b: No, he must produce evidence.

quduri.f: The claimant cannot produce any evidence but gives a description of the item. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The finder is allowed to give it to him. However, the court cannot force him to do so.

quduri.f: The finder announced the found item for days/a year. He gave up on finding the owner and intended giving it away in charity. To whom can he give it?
quduri.b: He may give it to the poor, not the rich.

quduri.f: Can he not take it for himself? [i.e. the finder after announcing the found item for days/a year and after he gave up on finding the owner]
quduri.b: He cannot if he is rich. He may if he is poor.

quduri.f: The finder wished to give it to someone else because he was rich. He gave it to his father/mother/adult son/wife who were poor. Is that permissible?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Is there a difference with an item found in the Hill or the Haram?
quduri.b: No, the ruling is the same.

quduri.f: What is the legal status of a baby born with a penis and vagina i.e. a Khuntha [hermaphrodite]?
quduri.b: If it urinates from the penis, it is a boy. If it urinates from the vagina it is a girl.

quduri.f: And if it urinates from both organs?
quduri.b: It will be attributed to whichever organ it urinates from first. If the urine comes out of both at the same time then it will be attributed to whichever organ more frequent urine comes. This is according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى frequency of urine is not considered.

quduri.f: Are there other signs by which sex can be determined?
quduri.b: If the hermaphrodite attains pubert and grows a beard or is inclinded to women then it is a man. If it grew breasts like a woman/milk merged from its teats/it menstruated/it became pregnant/it allowed sexual penetration into its vagina, then it is a woman.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if none of these signs emerge? [i.e. growing beard, inclination to women, growing breasts, milk emerging from its teats, menstruation, pregnancy or sexual penetration into the vagina]
quduri.b: It will neither be classified as male or female but will be called Khuntha Mushkil [Undetermined Hermaphrodite].

quduri.f: In which row will the Khunta Muskhil stand for Salah?
quduri.b:
He will stand between the men and women, behind the children.194

194 Rulings regarding it will be according to caution. If he prays with the men then due to the possibility that it is a woman, the men on its right, left and behind should repeat their Salah. If it prays with the women then it should repeat its Salah because it might be a man. Hence it will stand between the men and women. It should cover whatever a woman must cover in Salah because of the possibility that it is a woman.
It will be Makruh for its entire life to wear jewellery or silk; to expose itself before men or women; to be alone with a non-Mahram of either sex. If it enters Ihram while not yet pubescent then according to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى, "I do not know about its attire, because if it is male then it is Makruh to wear stitched clothing. If it is female then it is Makruh to leave the stitched clothing." According to Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى, "it should wear the clothing of women, because if it is female and leaves the stitched clothing it is more shameful than if it s a male and it wears female clothing. There is no fine on it because it is not an adult."

quduri.f: What does the Khuntha Mushkil inherit from its father?
quduri.b:
According to Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى it inherits the share of a female. Thus if the deceased left behind a son and the Khunta Mushkil, the son will inherit two-thirds and the Khuntha Mushkil one-third, unless it is established otherwise.195 

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the Khuntha Mushkil will get half a male's share plus half a female's share. This is the view of ash-Sha'bi رحمه الله تعالى.

195 This is an indication that the Khunta Mushkil sometimes inherits as a male, e.g. a woman dies and leaves behind her parents, husband and Khunta Mushkil child. The estate is divided into 12 shares. The husband gets 3; the parents get 4; the Khunta Mushkil gets 5. Had it been a daughter she would have gotten 6 and the total shares reclassified as 13. Another scenario is that a woman dies and leaves behind her husband, a maternal-brother; and a Khunta Mushkil who is her full sibling. The estate will be divided into 6 shares. The husband gets 3 shares; the brother gets 1 share and the Khunta Mushkil gets the remainder of 2. Had the Khunta Muskil been a sister she would have gotten 3 shares.

quduri.f: Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى adopted the view of ash-Sha'bi [i.e. regarding the inheritance of the Khuntha Mushkil]. Is there a difference in the interpretation?
quduri.b: Yes, according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the money will be divided into 7 between a son and a Khunta Mushkil. The son gets 4 shares and the Khuntha Muskil 3. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the money will be divided into 12 shares between them. The son will get 7 and the Khunta Mushkil 5.

quduri.f: Who circumcises a Khunta Mushkil?
quduri.b: A slave-girl will be bought for him from his money; or if he does not have money the ruler will buy her from him from the public treasury. After she circumcises him, the ruler will sell her and return the price to the treasury.

quduri.f: What is Nikah in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: It is a contract deliberately aimed at owning the right to Mut'ah [enjoyment]. Ownership of Mut'ah refers to a man's right with a woman to sex, touching and kissing.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated "deliberately"? [i.e. "a contract deliberately aimed at owning the right to Mut'ah]
quduri.b: Because ownership of Mut'ah is sometimes attained automatically such as when buying or inheriting a slave-girl.

quduri.f: How is marriage contracted?
quduri.b: It is contracted by offer and acceptance, with words in the past tense; or at least one in the past tense and one in the future tense. An example of the first is where the guardian says, "Zawwajtuha Iyya - I have married her to you," and the groom replies, "Qabiltuha - I have accepted her." An example of the second is where the groom says, "Marry her to me," and the guardian says, "I have given her to you in marriage." Whilst the groom used the command tense it is interpreted as future tense here.

quduri.f: With which words is the marriage contracted?
quduri.b: With Nikah and Tazawwuj [to marry], also from the side of the guardian if he uses Inkah/Tazwij [grant in marriage]; Tamlik [grant ownership]; Hibah [gift]; and Sadaqah on condition that accepted is uttered thereafter.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the guardian says, "I have hired her to you/I have lent her to you/I have made her permissible to you"?
quduri.b: Thse words do not establish marriage.

quduri.f: Are there other conditions besides offer and acceptance?
quduri.b: Yes, it is a condition that there be two witnesses present. They must be free, sane, Muslim adults; or a man and two women with the same qualities mentioned. It is necessary that the witnesses hear the offer and acceptance. The marriage is not valid if the witnesses are deaf or sleeping. It is valid with blind witnesses who listened.

quduri.f: The offer was made with witnesses who are not adil [just]. Is the marriage valid?
quduri.b: Yes, it is not a condition for the validity of the marriage contract that the witnesses be adil.

quduri.f: Is the marriage contract valid if the witnesses are men who were punished with the Hudd for slander?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A Muslim married a lady-Zimmi. Two Zimmis were the witnesses. Is the marriage valid?
quduri.b: It is valid according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. The contract is not in effort according to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى who stipulates Muslim witnesses in this case.

quduri.f: Can a man or woman in Ihram marry?
quduri.b: They may marry but not engage in sex and its incitements.

quduri.f: Does the Shari'ah set a limit for the amount of wives one may marry?
quduri.b: Yes, a free man can have a maximum of four free or slave women as his wives at a given moment. If he divorces any and her 'iddah is complete or any die, then he may marry another. A slave however cannot have more than two wives at a time. A woman cannot marry a man besides the man in whose marriage she is, until he divorces her or dies and she completes her 'iddah. This is because it is Haram for a woman to be married to two men at the same time.

quduri.f: What is the status of a marriage if the man married two women in a single ceremony but one of them was not permissible for him to marry?
quduri.b: The marriage with the woman he was permitted to marry is valid and the other is void. The entire Mahr [dowry] will go to the one whose marriage is valid.

quduri.f: A man gives another his sister or daughter in marriage on condition that he in turn gives his sister or daughter in exchange. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both marriages are valid. The dowry of each will be Mahr Mithl [average dowry for that family, status etc]

quduri.f: A man got another man or woman married without permission. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The marriage is suspended until the person who had not been asked either validates ir or repudiates it. This is called Nikah al-Faduli in the terminology of the jurists.

quduri.f: What is the status of Muwqattat1 and Mut'ah2 marriages?
quduri.b:
Both are void.

1 Marriage with a time limit, e.g. the marriage was performed with witnesses and stipulated to last 10 days.
2 He says to a woman, "I shall enjoy you for such an amount of time for such amount of money."

quduri.f: How should a man who has several wives treat them?
quduri.b: He must treat them well. THis includes being just in his time amongst them.

quduri.f: What form does this justice take? [i.e. being just in his time amongst several wives]
quduri.b: He should share his nights with each. Thus if he spends one night for example with one, he must spend a night with the next one.

quduri.f: Is it Wajib upon him to have sex with his wife when he spends her turn with her?
quduri.b: The sharing is Wajib in as far as spending the night is concerned, not with regards to sex. Sex requires energy which might not be available every night.

quduri.f: Is there a difference in Qasm [i.e. sharing time between wives] between a virgin and a non-virgin; between and old and new wife?
quduri.b: No, he must be ewual whether any is a virgin, non-virgin, old wife or new.

quduri.f: How does he share if one wife is a free-woman and the other a slave?
quduri.b: He will spend two nights with the free wife for every one he spends with the slave.

quduri.f: What is the regulation of Qasm during a journey?
quduri.b: The wives do not have a right to Qasm when the husband is travelling. He may take whom he wishes with him. It would be best if he drew lots and took whomever's name emerged, so that their hearts will be pleased.

quduri.f: One wife was happy to give her Qasm to another wife. Is this allowed?
quduri.b: Yes, but she can claim her right back whenever she wishes.

quduri.f: Which women are Haram to marry?
quduri.b: There are several categories of Haram - women forbidden by lineage [nasabiyah]; women forbidden by Rada' [fosterage i.e. by the drinking of a particular woman's milk]; Musaharah [in-laws]; Jam' [uniting certain women together in one's marriage]; women upon whom there are rights of others; and women of Kufr and Shirk.

quduri.f: Explain the women forbidden by lineage.
quduri.b: They are mothers, daughters, sisters, sisters of one's father, sisters of one's mother, daughters of one's brother, daughters of one's sister - all these have been explicitly mentioned in the Quraan in Suratun Nisa. Mothers include a man's actual mother, as well as his grandmothers from both his father's and mother's side and thus going back and forbidding all female ancestors. Similarly daughters include a man's biological daughter, the daughters of his sons and daughter and thus all female descendants. Sisters include full sisters as well as half-sisters from either the mother's or father's side. In this way, daughter of a brother includes daughters of full-brothers, and daughters of half-brothers from either the mother's or father's side. Deduce the same for nieces from one's three kind of sisters. In the same way a paternal aunt is Haram whether she is one's father's full sister or half sister with a common father or half-sister with a common mother. Deduce the same for a maternal aunt in all three cases.

quduri.f: Which women are forbidden through Rada?
quduri.b: It is Haram for a man to marry his mother who suckled him; the foster-sister i.e. the girl who drank from that mother; and hence all those who are forbidden through lineage are forbidden through fosterage. There are exceptions which we shall explain in the chapter on Rada' Inshaallaah.

quduri.f: Which women are forbidden by Musaharah?
quduri.b: A man may not marry a woman his father had married, whether intercourse occurred or not. Similarly he may not marry the women of his grandfathers, whether paternal or maternal, or the wives of any ancestor further up. He may not marry his son's wife, his grandson's wife or the wife of any descendant further down- whether these said descendants had intercourse with these women or not. A man may not marry the mother of his wife, whether they had intercourse or not. He may not marry his wife's daughter, whether the daughter was in his care or not.

quduri.f: Which women cannot be married at the same time [Jam']?
quduri.b:
One may not join blood relatives in marriage at the same time. Thus one may not marry two sisters at the same time as explicitly stated in the Quraan.

Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade marrying a woman when married to her paternal aunt; a paternal aunt when married to her brother's daughter; a woman when married to her maternal aunt; a maternal aunt when married to her sister's daughter. Do not marry the small one when married to the big one. Do not marry the big one when married to the small one. [Abu Dawud and at-Tirmizi]

From this the jurists have derived a general rule. If either one of the two women has to be regarded as a man, and marriage between them would not be allowed (whether by lineage or fosterage) then marrying both at the same time is also forbidden.

quduri.f: Which women cannot be married because of Kufr and Shirk?
quduri.b:
If a man is outside the pale of Islaam then a Muslim lady may not marry him, whatever religion he may belong to. A Muslim man may not marry a polytheist, an idol-worshipper, a fire-worshipper or any other kind of Kafir3 unless she is a Christian or Jew.4 

3 A man may also not have sex with a polytheist or fire-worshipper slave. A Kafir is anyone who denies the necessary beliefs of Islam. This includes the Qadianis, the Batiniyah, the Shi'ah and the Ithna 'Ashariyah who claim the Quran is corrupted. SOme Muslims have been deceived by their claims of Islam and have married their daughters despite them being Kafirs.
4 Although marriage to a female Christian or Jew is permissible, 'Umar رضي الله عنه forbade it.

quduri.f: Can the prohibition through Musaharah arise through Zina as well?
quduri.b: Yes, thus if a man commits Zina with a woman or touches her with lust or she touches him with lust, then it is Haram for him to marry her mother or daughter.

quduri.f: Can a man marry at the same time a woman and her ex-husband's daughter from another woman?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man divorces a woman. Can he marry her sister?
quduri.b:
If he has divorced her Batt5 or Raj'i then he may not marry the sister until her 'iddah is complete.

5 Includes Mughallazh and Bain.

quduri.f: A man owns two slaves who are sisters. Can he have sex with them by right of ownership?
quduri.b: He may not have sex with both of them, but may choose whichever one of the two he wishes to enjoy. Once he has used the first, he may not have sex with the second until he prohibits the first unto himself.

quduri.f: How will he prohibit her unto himself? [i.e. a man used to have sex with a slave]
quduri.b: He will marry her to another man; or make her a Mukatab; or remove her from his possession by freeing her; or gifting her away; or selling her; or giving her as charity.

quduri.f: Who is the Wali [guardian]?
quduri.b:
Guardianship of marriage arises from four sources: Qarabah [relationship]; Wala [setting a slave free]; Imamah [government]; and Milk [ownership].

As from the aspect of relationship, paternal relatives ['asabat] are the guardians in the same order as in inheritance. The closes then the closest has preference. The closest guardian to a woman is her son; then her son's son and proceeding down. Then the father; then the father's father and proceeding up. Then a full brother; then a half-brother with a common father. Then a son of a full-brother; then a son of a half-brother with a common father. Then a son of a full-brother; then a son of a half-brother with a common father and then proceeding down. Then a paternal uncle who is a full brother of her father. Then a paternal uncle who is a half-brother sharing a father with her father. Then a son of a paternal uncle who is a full brother of her father. Then a son of a paternal uncle who is a half-brother sharing a father with her father. Then proceeding downwards. Then a paternal uncle of her father who is a full brother of her father's father. Then a paternal uncle of her father who is a half-brother sharing a father with her father's father. Then their descendants in this order.

Then from the aspect of Wala which refers to the rights the master retains when freeing a slave; if a woman does not have a guardian from paternal relatives then the owner who freed her from slavery is the guardian. He is counted as the last of paternal relatives. If there are no paternal relatives then her maternal relatives will be her guardians, whether she is a child or adult.

If there are no such relatives at all then the guardianship falls on the Imamah or government, referring to the ruler or judge.

Guardianship of Milk refers to the right of the slave's owner (whether the slave is male or female) to get them married, even if they are displeased. If the male or female slave marries without the owner's permission then the marriage is suspended pending the owner's ratifying it or rejecting it.

quduri.f: What is the status of a free adult woman's marriage if she willingly married without the guardian contracting it?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the marriage is valid as long as she is a sane adult. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the marriage is not validated without the guardian's permission.

quduri.f: Can a guardian force a sane, adult virgin to marry?
quduri.b: No. She has a greater right to herself whether she is a virgin or not.

quduri.f: We accept that she cannot be forced. [i.e. a sane adult virgin] However, women generally do not get married themselves, but their guardians get them married. Must the guardian ask her permission?
quduri.b: Since he cannot force her he has to ask her permission, "I wish to marry you to that person." If she agrees then the marriage will be valid or else if she refuses it is not.

quduri.f: A virgin is shy to respond verbally. How can she give her consent?
quduri.b: If the guardian asks her and she remains silent or laughs or cries without any sound then that counts as consent. If someone besides the guardian asks her or a guardian besides whom there is a more entitled guardian then her consent must be expressed verbally.

quduri.f: If she refuses, what can the guardian do? [i.e. the sane adult girl]
quduri.b: He cannot marry her when she refuses.

quduri.f: A woman married and became a widow. Must her guardian ask her permission if he wishes to get her married a second time?
quduri.b:
It is necessary for him to ask her and it is also necessary for her to give verbal consent. Her silence, laugh or cry will not suffice as consent.6
