quduri.b: It is allowed.

quduri.f: He bought his father or his son and intended thereby that they would be free and his Kaffarah paid. Does that suffice his Kaffarah? [i.e. for Zhihar]
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man and his partner own a slave. He frees his half as Kaffarah and accepts liability for the partner's half. The partner then sets his half free. Has the Kaffarah been fulfilled? [i.e. for Zhihar]
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is not fulfilled. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى if the one setting him free is well-off then it is fulfilled, if he is poor then it is not.

quduri.f: If a man sets half his slave free as Kaffarah of Zhihar and later sets the other half free, is the Kaffarah fulfilled?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is fulfilled on condition that he does not have sex with the wife against whom he pronounced the Zhihar in between the period of the two manumissions.43

43 Because he accepts partial manumission.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if the man cannot free a slave as Kaffarah of Zhihar he may fast two months consecutively. Is his Kaffarah valid if he fasts Sha'ban and Ramadan?
quduri.b: It is not valid. The fast of Ramadan is Fard upon him due to him being a Muslim, not because of the Zhihar. Thus the fast of Ramadan cannot be included in the Kaffarah.

quduri.f: If he fasts Shawwal and Zul Qa'dah, or Zul Qa'dah and Zul Hijjah, is his Kaffarah acceptable? [i.e. for Zhihar]
quduri.b: No, because fasting on the Day of Fitr and Nahr and the Days of Tashriq are forbidden. Fasting those days will not fulfil the Wajib requirement.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he has sex during the two months of Kaffarah with the wife upon whom he pronounced Zhihar?
quduri.b:
If he consciously has sex in the night or forgetfully in the day44 then he begins anew according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى he need not begin anew.

44 If he had sex deliberately in the day then it is unanimously agreed that he will begin anew.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he failed to fast a day during the two months, whether with or without an excuse? [i.e. as Kaffarah for his Zhihar]
quduri.b: He has to begin anew because he missed the condition of consecutiveness.

quduri.f: You mentioned that if he cannot fast two months consecutively then he must feed sixty poor. [i.e. as Kaffarah for his Zhihar] How is this feeding done?
quduri.b:
He must feed each poor person a half Sa' of wheat, or a Sa' of dates or barley or the price of these. If he feeds them lunch and supper until they are full,45  then it suffices for them whether they ate a little or a lot.

45 It is not valid if there is amongst them those who were full nbeofre the meal, or a small child not close to puberty.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he fed one poor person for sixty days? [i.e. as Kaffarah for his Zhihar]
quduri.b: It suffices as his Kaffarah.

quduri.f: He gave a single poor person 30 Sa' of wheat or 120 Sa' of barley in a single day. Is his Kaffarah fulfilled? `[i.e. his Kaffarah of Zhihar]
quduri.b: Only his first day's Kaffarah is fulfilled. He must feed another 59 poor people.

quduri.f: He was giving a poor man a half Sa' of wheat each day. He approached the wife upon whom he had pronounced the Zhihar before the completion of feeding 60 poor. Must he begin anew?
quduri.b:
No, the text of the Quraan does not stipulate such a condition in reference to the feeding.46

46 The ayah states, "...he who is not able should feed 60 poor", and does not add onto the condition of feeding by saying "...before they touch each other..." as in the cases of freeing a slave and fasting.

quduri.f: Sundry Masail [extra's]
quduri.b:
If a slave pronounces Zhihar on his wife, his only recourse to Kaffarah is fasting, because he does not own anything. Even if his owner frees a slave on his behalf, or feeds 60 poor on his behalf then it will not validate as his Kaffarah.
A man is liable for two Kaffarahs of Zhihar. He set two slaves free but did not make a specific intention which is for which. Both his Kaffarahs are fulfilled.
Similarly if he is liable for two Kaffarahs and he fasted 4 months or fed 120 poor, and did not specify, then both Kaffarahs are fulfilled..
If he only freed one slave for two Kaffarahs, or only fasted 2 months, he may apply that as Kaffarah for whichever one he wishes.

quduri.f: Whom is it Wajib to spend maintenance on?
quduri.b: It is Wajib to spend on one's wives, children, divorcee, parents and blood relatives.

quduri.f: Explain the Masail of maintenace of wives.
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
It is Wajib for a man to maintain his wife, be she Muslim, Christian or Jew; when she has surrendered herself in his home. He is also obligated to feed and clothe her. Both of their conditions are taken into account for this, whether the husband is rich or poor.
If she is disobedient and does not surrender herself to his home, then he is not obligated to maintain her until she returns home.
If she refuses to give herself over to him until he pays her Mahr, then she is still entitled to maintenace.
If the wife is so small that she cannot be sexually enjoyed, then she is not entitled to maintenace even if she hands herself to him.
If she is an adult and hands herself to him. But he is a minor, incapable of sex. She will receive maintenance from his wealth.
If a woman is detained because of debts or is forcibly kidnapped, then she is not entitled to maintenance.
If she journeys for Hajj with someone besides her husband then she is not entitled to maintenance.
If she is ill in the husband's home, then he must maintain her.
A man marries a slave-girl. Her owner lets her stay with him. He must maintain her.

A slave marries a freewoman with his owner's permission. Her maintenace will be a debt against which the slave can be sold; unless the owner pays from his wealth.

quduri.f: A woman had a servant in her father's house before marrying. Is it the duty of the husband to pay for a servant for her?
quduri.b: Yes, if he is rich. Also, he is not obligated to hire more than one servant.

quduri.f: A man is unable to pay for his wife's maintenance. Will they be separated?
quduri.b: No, she will take credit against him. When he can afford he must pay those debts.

quduri.f: The judge ruled that he must spend on her according to a poor man. He later becomes rich and she claims the maintenance of the rich. Must he fulfil the maintenace of the rich to her?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: For some time he does not spend on her. She then demands the amount she spent on herself. Must he pay it?
quduri.b: No, unless the judge had ruled an amount for her, or he cmpromises on an amount.

quduri.f: The court has ordered a maintenace amount for her. Months pass and he does not pay and he dies. What is the status of that outstanding amount?
quduri.b: The maintenance is forfeit.

quduri.f: He gave her enough to last her a year. One of them dies before the amount is finished. Will it be claimed from her?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى no. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى her past expenses will be calculated and the remainder is the husband's.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that the husband must pay for her residence. In what house will he keep her?
quduri.b: He must keep her in a separate chamber where none of his family stays, unless she chooses otherwise.

quduri.f: He provided her with accommodation. [i.e. his wife] Her parents, family and children from another husband come to visit. Can he stop them?
quduri.b: He can stop them from entering, but he may not stop them from looking at her and speaking to her at any time.

quduri.f: Who must maintain a woman during her 'Iddah
quduri.b:
If a man divorces his wife, whether revocable or irrevocable48, he is responsible for her maintenance and accomodation. As for a widow, there is no maintenance from the husband's estate. She may spend her share of the inheritance.

48 As well as Mughallazh divorce.

quduri.f: Does any circumstance arise whereby a divorcee's maintenance is cancelled?
quduri.b: If the separation is due to a sin from her side, such as abandoning Islaam or giving herself to her husband's son before the divorce, then she is not entitled to maintenance.

quduri.f: And if he she gave herself to her husband's son after divorce? [i.e. then what is the status of her maintenance?]
quduri.b: She is still entitled to maintenance.

quduri.f: If a couple has a child, whether boy or girl, whose duty is it to maintain the child?
quduri.b: The father is responsible for maintaining minor children. Nobody shares that responsibility, just as nobody shares the husband's reponsibility in maintaining his wife.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated "minor"? [i.e. the father is responsible for maintaining minor children]
quduri.b: The father is not responsible for maintaining adult male children because they are able to earn for themselves, unless the adult son is chronically adult, in which case the father is responsible for two-thirds of his maintenance and the mother is responsible for a third. The parents are also responsible for the unmarried daughter in the same proportion. They are only responsible for the adult chronically ill son and adult unmarried daughter if they are Muslims.

quduri.f: Is maintenance of minor children a duty in all circumstances?
quduri.b: The parents are responsible to spend on their maintenance if the children do not own their own wealth. If however, they do own wealth in their own right then they should spend on them from the children's wealth.

quduri.f: How can the minor have wealth when he cannot earn?
quduri.b: He can have wealth when someone gives him a gift; leaves him a beques after his death; or the child inherits wealth.

quduri.f: Whose duty is it to maintain the parents?
quduri.b: If someone owns wealth he will first spend on himself, whether he is young or old, man or woman. This rule is general and covers parents and others but not wives. The husband is responsible to maintain the wife even if she is rich. If one or both the parents are poor then the children are obligated to maintain them. Nobody shares the responsibility of the child to support his parents. Just as it is Wajib to maintain the parents, it is also Wajib to maintain grandfathers and grandmothers if they are poor.

quduri.f: The parents of an absent man, spend his wealth which they have in their possession, on themselves. Are they liable to repay it?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: An absent man had some goods or land which is parents sold to maintain themselves. Can they do that?
quduri.b: If they sold the goods because of a need to maintain themselves, then it is permissible according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. They cannot however sell the land.

quduri.f: A man is absent and his parents need him to spend on them. Can the judge rule that they will be spent upon from his wealth?
quduri.b: Yes, the judge will rule accordingly.

quduri.f: A stranger is holding the wealth of an absent son. The stranger spent on the son's parents from that wealth. Is he liable to compensate that amount?
quduri.b: If he spent with the court's permission then he is not liable. If he spent without permission then he is liable.

quduri.f: Is maintenance still a duty when the parties have different religions?
quduri.b: It will still be a duty to maintain one's wife, parents, grandfathers, grandmothers, children and grandchildren. Besides these, it is not a duty to spend on relatives of another religion, just as a poor man is not obligated to spend on them.

quduri.f: How can a minor child be of a different religion to his father's?
quduri.b:
For example, a Christian/Jew marries a woman of his religion. She bears his child and then embraces Islaam while he does not. The child will be a Muslim like its mother. The court will rule that the Kafir father must maintain his Muslim child.

NOTE: If a man admits that he is holding the wealth of an absent man and acknowledges that a certain woman is his wife, the judge will rule that he must spend from it on his wife, minor children and parents. The wife will stand as Kafil for the amount. The court will not rule for maintenance for any besides these people.

quduri.f: Is maintenance for relatives besides parents and children wajib?
quduri.b:
Maintenance is Wajib for blood relatives one cannot marry according to their inhertiance shares;50 when it is a poor minor, or poor adult female, or chronically ill male, or poor blind person.

NOTE: If the court rules that he must maintain children, parents and relatives and some time passes without him paying then the amount is forfeit unless the court permits them to incur debt against him.51

50 e.g. he has a grandfather and son of son. The grandfather is responsible for a sixth of his maintenance and the son's son for the rest; because if he dies then they inherit from him in that proportion.
51 i.e. the passage of time does not absolve him of liability of debts incurred with the court's permission.

quduri.f: Is a man obligated to pay for the maintenance of his slave or slave-girl?
quduri.b: He must spend on them. If he refuses they may acquire earnings and maintain themselves from it. If they cannot earn then the court will force him to sell them.

quduri.f: A baby of breastfeeding age has both parents. Whose duty is it to see the child's breastfeeding?
quduri.b: If the mother is willing to breastfeed him then that would be best for the baby. However, she is not obligated to do so. I she refuses then the father must hire someone to breastfeed him on behalf of the mother.

quduri.f: Can the mother not feed him [i.e. a baby of breastfeeding age] in exchange for payment, just as another woman would be hired to do it?
quduri.b: If the nurse is the baby's father's wife or divorcee in 'Iddah who is receiving maintenance then she may not take a fee for feeding her baby; because her maintenance is Wajib upon the father from another aspect. If the divorcee has completed her 'Iddah, she may take a fee for feeding him.

quduri.f: The father hires a nurse, and the mother whose 'Iddah is complete is willing to accept the same fee as the nurse. Who is more entitled to feed the baby?
quduri.b: The mother is more entitled to feed her baby.

quduri.f: If the mother demands a fee greather than that of the other nurse [i.e. with regards to breastfeeding her baby], can the father be forced to accede?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: The couple has separated. Who is more entitled to the children?
quduri.b: The mother is most entitled. If there is no mother, then the mother's mother is more entitled than the father's mother. If there is no maternal grandmother then the paternal grandmother is more entitled than the sisters. If there is no paternal grandmother then the sisters are more entitled than the paternal - and maternal aunts. The sister with both parents in common is most entitled, then a sister with only a mother in common, then a sister with only a father in common. Thereafter the maternal aunts are more entitled than the paternal aunts. Then come the paternal aunts. The maternal and paternal aunts are ranked the same way as sisters in the three relevant categories.

quduri.f: Is the right to custody ever lost?
quduri.b: Whoever of the above [i.e. the mother, then the mother's mother, then the paternal grandmother, then the sisters; specically the sister with both parents in common, then a sister with only a mother in common, then a sister with only a father in common, then the maternal aunts and then the paternal aunts] marries looses her right of custody; except for a grandmother whose husband is the grandfather. Similarly the mother's right is not lost when she marries a Mahram of the child e.g. the child's paternal uncle.

quduri.f: The mother does not want custody and there are no other women who can assume custody. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The mother will be forced to take the child.

quduri.f: If there are no women of the child's family to take custody of the child and the men fight over it, who will receive custody?
quduri.b:
The closest in terms of Asabiyah is most entitled.52

52 First will be the father, then the father's father and ascending thus. Then a full brother, then a brother with a common father. Then the son of the full brother. Then the son of the brother with a common father. And thus all their descendants. Then a full brother of the father. Then a brother of the father who has a father in common. Then cousins, first is the son of a full brother of the father; then the son of a brother of the father who has a father in common. The cousins will not get a girl's custody because they are not Mahram. Also she will not be given to an untrustworthy mother or sinful relatives; nor to the owner who set the slave free; in order to avoid trouble.

quduri.f: For how long are the women entitled to custody?
quduri.b: The mother and grandmother are entitled to a boy until he can do the following on his own: eat, drink, dress and Istinja. They are entitled to a girl until she menstruates. Women besides the mother and grandmother are entitled to the girl until she reaches an age when she is sexually desirable.

quduri.f: What are the custody rights of a Christian/Jewish woman who bore a child for her Muslim husband?
quduri.b: She is entitled to him as long as he does not yet understand the difference in religions and there is no fear yet of him being influenced by disbelief.

quduri.f: What are the custody rights of a slave-girl over her child?
quduri.b: A slave-girl and an Ummul Walad do not have custody rights before bein set free. Once free, they have the same rights as a freewoman.

quduri.f: A woman is divorced and being most entitled, gets custody over her child. She then intends taking the child away from the city where the child's father is. Can she do that?
quduri.b: She may not, unless she takes him to her homeland where his father married her.

quduri.f: A man has disappeared from his town and his location is not known; nor if he is living or dead. Who will guard his wealth and other issues?
quduri.b: The court will appoint someone to guard his wealth, fulfil his obligations and spend on his wife and minor children from his wealth.

quduri.f: Can the judge separate the missing man and his wife, and thereby permit her to remarry?
quduri.b:
He may not separate them until 120 years53 have passed since the day he was born. Upon completion of this period the judge will rule that he is legally dead and the wife will spend the 'Iddah of a widow. She may then remarry who she wishes.

53 This is according to Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and is the safest. However, the latter Hanafiyah observed the increased temptations and decrease in piety and patience of women, and hence ruled according to the Mazhab of al-Imam Malik رحمه الله تعالى. Accordingly the woman will present herself to the judge and provide Shar'i evidencethat her husband is missing. The judge will conduct further investigations. If nothing is learnt he will rule that the woman must wait a further 4 years. If in that period no further information is obtained and it is not known whether he is dead or alive then the court will declare him dead. She will spend the 'Iddah of a widow and may thereafter remarry.

quduri.f: How will the inheritance be divided if any of the missing man's heirs died beofre he was declared dead?
quduri.b: Only those heirs living at the time of the declaration will inherit.

quduri.f: Does the missing inherit from his relatives who die before he is declared dead?
quduri.b: He does not inherit from anyone who dies while he is missing.

quduri.f: How does a freeman/woman become a slave?
quduri.b: Jihad will continue until the Day of Resurrection. Thus when the Believers wage Jihad against the Kuffar and capture them, the Amirul Muminin may decide to enslave them. Once he decrees that, they are slaves and will be divided amongst those entitled to booty.

quduri.f: The enemies of Islaam object that enslavement is a violation of humanity.
quduri.b:
Their objections are mistaken and their words unsophisticated if Kuffar captives are returned to their lands they will be even harsher against Islaam and the Muslims. They will be even further from the guidance with which the Quraan was revealed. If the ruler should keep them imprisoned then their maintenance will be a urden upon the Public Treasury. That is an expense without any benefit. It is therefore appropriate that he divides them amongst the warriors to serve them. Each slave will earn for his master and eat from his home. The slave will thus not be a complete burden upon the master, but will be like a member of the household. In this way both the master and slave benefit in wordly terms. As far as Din is concerned, the slave will live in a Muslim home and observe their Salah, Fasting, Worship, Remembrance of Allaah and their good character. He will be affected by that and enter Allaah's Din. He will be saved from the punishment of Hell - what a great favour that is upon him. The pages of history are replete with slaves of either sex who embraced Islaam and acquired lofty stages in regards knowledge and pious deeds.

Enslavement is not necessary and the ruler has other options which will be described in Kitabus Siyar InshaAllaah. The Shari'ah greatly encourages manumission of slaves and commands that they be set free as Kaffarah. It also instituted the processed of declaring slaves Mudabbar and Mukatab as ways of freeing him.

quduri.f: How does a man free his slave?
quduri.b: If a sane adult says to his slave/slave-girl, "You are a free person/you are set free/you are freed/you are made free/I have freed you/you are manumitted", then the slave is free; whether the owner meant manumission or not, because these words are explicit manumission and do not depend on intention.

quduri.f: If the owner specifies the freedom to certain organs of the slave, is the slave free?
quduri.b:
If he says, "Your neck/face/head/body is free", then the slave is free. Similarly if he says to a slave-girl, "Your vagina is free."54

54 Because these words symbolise the entire body. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: What if he says, "I have no ownership over you?"
quduri.b: If he intended manumission then the slave is free, if not then the slave is not free. The same rule applies to any other non-explicit words of manumission, such as, "You have left my ownership/ I have no authority over you."

quduri.f: What if he says, "I have no Sultan [power] over you?"
quduri.b: The slave will not be freed even if the owner intended it as manumission.

quduri.f: If the owner says, "This is my son"55, and remains firm on his statement or says, "This is my freed-slave", or calls him, "O my freed-slave", is the slave free?
quduri.b: Yes, these expressions are treated as explicit declarations of freedom.

quduri.f: And if he says, "O my son/O my brother/You are like a freeman."
quduri.b: The slave is not freed.

quduri.f: If the owner says about a slave who cannot be his son, "This is my son", what is the ruling?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he is freed. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he is not freed.

quduri.f: If the owner says to his slave-girl, "You are divorced", and intends thereby freeing her, is she freed?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If he says to his slave, "You are nothing but free", what is the ruling?
quduri.b: The slave is free.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a man is forced to free his slave, or was drunk when he freed the slave?
quduri.b: The slave is free.

quduri.f: A man frees a pregnant slave-girl. What is the status of the foetus?
quduri.b: Mother and foetus are both free.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if only the foetus is freed?
quduri.b: The foetus and not the mother are free.

quduri.f: Can freedom be attached to possession or other conditions?
quduri.b: Yes, thus if he says to someone else's slave, "If I own you, you will be free", then the salve will be free if he comes to own him. If he says to his own slave, "If you enter the house you are free", and the slave enters the house then he is free.

quduri.f: Is there a way of manumission without the owner setting the slave free?
quduri.b: Yes, if someone acquires a Mahram blood relative, whether by purchase, inheritance or gift, then that relative is free even if the owner had no intention of manumission.

quduri.f: If the owner sets part of the slave free, is the part of the entire slave free?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the part only is free and the slave will work to earn his complete freedom. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammad رحمه الله تعالى he is entirely free and need to work to complete his freedom.56

56 The principle according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى is that the slave can be divided into parts whilst according to them (i.e. Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى) as well as Imaam ash-Shafi'i رحمه الله تعالى it cannot.

quduri.f: Two partners share a slave. One frees his slave. What is the status of the remaining share?
quduri.b: If the freedom-grantor is rich then the partner has a choice, he may either free his share as well, or hold the other liable, or he can demand that the slave earn and pay him for his share. If the freedom-grantor is poor, the partner has the same option except that he cannot hold his partner liable. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he can only hold the rich partner liable and if the partner is poor he must demand that the slave pay him.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if a blood-relative Mahram comes into possession he is automatically free. If two partners buy or inherit a slave who is the son of one of the partners, is the slave free? If so what is the other partner's right?
quduri.b: The father's share is freed and he is not liable for his partner's share. The partner can either free his share or make the slave work to compensate him.

quduri.f: Two partners own a slave and each claims that the other freed his share. Both deny that they set their share free. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The slave will be entirely free. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he will work to repay both partners, whether they are rich or poor. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he will only work and compensate a poor partner(s) and will not compensate a rich partner(s).

quduri.f: People free their slaves for Allaah's sake. If someone says, "I free you for Satan's sake/an idol's sake", is the slave free?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Sundry Masail
quduri.b:
If a slave belonging to a Kafir flees from the lands of the Kuffar to us [i.e. Muslim lands] then he is free.
If a slave-girl bears the child of her owner, then the offspring is free.
Her child from her slave husband belongs to her owner.
The offspring of a freewoman from a slave is free.

quduri.f: What is Tadbir?
quduri.b: It is when the owner says, "When I die then you are free/You are free after [dubur] me/You are a Mudabbar/I have made Tadbir of you."

quduri.f: What is the ruling when he says that? [i.e. when a slave owner says "When I die then you are free/You are free after [dubur] me/You are a Mudabbar/I have made Tadbir of you."]
quduri.b: The slave is classified as a Mudabbar i.e. he will be freed upon the owner's death. He may not be sold; nor gifted to anyone; nor hired out; nor given to serve anyone else.

quduri.f: If he [i.e. the slave owner] makes Tadbir of a slave-girl, can he still have sex with her? Can he marry her to another man?
quduri.b: Both acts are permissible.

quduri.f: The owner then marries her [i.e. a slave-girl who is Mudabbar] to another man who fathers her child. What is the child's status?
quduri.b: The child is a Mudabbar like its mother.

quduri.f: When the owner dies, is the Mudabbar free without any price or must he compensate the heirs?
quduri.b: If the third of the estate in which the deceased could make bequest covers the slave's value then he is free without further liability. If the entire estate consisted of nothing but the slave, then the slave must compensate them for two-thirds of his value. If debts consume the entire value of the estate, then the slave will compensate the creditors for his entire value.

quduri.f: Is the Tadbir valid if the owner attaches a specific description to his freedom, e.g. "If I die in this illness of mine/in this journey/of such-and-such a disease"?
quduri.b: The slave is not a Mudabbar and may be sold and gifted away. However, if the specified condition is found, he will be freed from the third of the estate.

quduri.f: What is Istilad?
quduri.b: When an owner impregnates his slave-girl and she gives birth to his child, then he has made Istilad with her. The slave-girl is called Ummul Walad [child's mother]. This is on condition that he acknowledges the child, in which case its lineage will be attributed to him.

quduri.f: What are the regulations concerning an Ummul Walad?
quduri.b: She may not be sold or otherwise transferred into another's possession. The owner may have sex with her, take service from her, hire her out, and get her married. When the owner dies she is freed from the entire estate [i.e. she is not limited to the third only] and is not obligated to compensate the heirs or the creditors. If he had gotten her married and she then bears another child, the child is in the same status as her i.e. it will be free when she gains her freedom.

quduri.f: You have stipulated that the owner must acknowledge the child for Istilad. What happens if he does not?
quduri.b: The lineage will not be attributed to him.

quduri.f: He [i.e. the slave owner] acknowledges a child and then she [i.e. the Ummul Walad] bears a second child. Is it necessary for him to acknowledge the second as well, or is the first acknowledgement sufficient?
quduri.b: The second child's lineage will be attributed to him with need for acknowledgement. If however he specifically denies the child, then the lineage will not be attributed to him.

quduri.f: A man marries a slave-girl. She bears his child and he then comes to own her. Does she become his Ummul Walad?
quduri.b: Yes, the laws of Ummul Walad apply to her.

quduri.f: A man owns a slave-girl. His father has intercourse with her and she bears his child. The father claims the child. Will the child's lineage be attributed to him?
quduri.b: It will be attributed to the father who claimed him and she will be his Ummul Walad.

quduri.f: When she becomes the Ummul Walad of the father [i.e. the father of the slave-owner] who made the claim [i.e. claimed the child she bore], does the father have to pay his son who owned her?
quduri.b: Yes, the father is liable to pay her price to him.

quduri.f: Does he owe anything else, such as 'Uqr57 or the price of the child? [i.e. when the father of the slave-owner has intercourse with his slave-girl and she bears his child, and he has to pay her price]
quduri.b:
No.

57 Dowry for having sex by mistake [al-Mughrib]

quduri.f: A man owns a slave-girl. His grandfather has intercourse with her and she bears his child. The grandfather claims the child. Will the child's lineage be attributed to him?
quduri.b: If the owner's father is dead the lineage will be attributed to the grandfather, but not if he is alive.

quduri.f: A slave-girl owned by two partners bears a child. One of the partners claims the child. Will its lineage be attributed to him?
quduri.b: Yes, and the slave becomes his Ummul Walad. He must pay his partner half her 'Uqr and half her price. He is not liable for the price of the child.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if both parties claim the child? [i.e. a slave-girl owned by two partners bears a child]
quduri.b: The child will be attributed to both and she will be the Ummul Walad of both. Each will pay half 'Uqr. They will mutually settle their accounts.

quduri.f: How will the inheritance be distributed if one of these partners or the child dies? [i.e. when a slave-girl is owned by two partners bears a child and both parties claim the child]
quduri.b: The child will inherit from both of them as a full child. Each of them will inherit from the child as one father.

quduri.f: A man made his slave Mukatab. The Mukatab bought a slave-girl and the Mukatab's owner cohabited with her. She then bore his child. What is the child's status? What does the owner owe the Mukatab?
quduri.b: If the Mukatab accepts his word then the lineage is attributed to the owner who is liable for her 'Uqr and child's price. She does not however become his Ummul Walad. If the Mukatab does not accept his word then the lineage is not established to him.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of the owner making a Mukatabah agreement with his slave?
quduri.b: It is when the owner says to his slave or slave-girl, "i impose upon you 1000 Dirham (for example) payable to me within a specified period beginning from this date to that date. If you do that then you are free. If you do not then you remain a slave." If the slave accepts that then he becomes a Mukatab. This transaction is called Mukatabah. The amount which the slave renders to the owner is called Badalul Kitabah [exchange for written agreement]. Allaah says, "Those who seek a Kitab agreement from amongst your slaves then agree to it if you see good in them." [an-Nur:33]

quduri.f: Can the money be demanded immediately or must it be after a period? [i.e. from the Mukatab]
quduri.b: It can be immediate, deferred or specified for a date.

quduri.f: Can the owner make Mukatabah with a minor slave?
quduri.b: Yes, if the minor understands buying and selling.

quduri.f: When the owner makes a Mukatabah what laws are applicable?
quduri.b:
If the agreement is valid, then the slave is free of the master's control but does not leave his ownership. The slave is free to buy, sell and travel.58

58 Thus certain jurists define Kitabah as freedom of control for the slave without freedom in wealth.

quduri.f: Can the Mukatab marry?
quduri.b: Only with his owner's permission.

quduri.f: The Mukatab earned money for the Mukatabah. Can he give a gift or charity from it?
quduri.b: He may only give a small amount.

quduri.f: A Mukatab bought a slave-girl and had sex with her. She had his child. What is the status of the child?
quduri.b: The child enters the Mukatabah and is the same ruling as his father. His earnings are his.

quduri.f: The owner got his slave married to his slave-girl. He then made a Mukatabah agreement with both of them. The slave-girl has his child. What is the child's status?
quduri.b: He is included in his mother's Kitabah and his earnings are his.

quduri.f: A man makes Mukatabah with his slave-girl and then has sex with her. Does he owe her anything?
quduri.b: Yes, 'Uqr.

quduri.f: The owner violates the Mukatab slave-girl or her child. What is the violation?
quduri.b: He will be held accountable just af if anyone else had committed the violation.

quduri.f: The owner destroyed the wealth of the Mukatab slave-girl. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He is liable for whatever he destroyed.

quduri.f: A Mukatab buys his father or son, will the father/son be automatically freed?
quduri.b: He will not be immediately freed. He will join him in the Mukatabah and will be free with the Mukatab.

quduri.f: The Mukatab bought the mother of his child [Ummul Walad] with his child. What is the child's satus?
quduri.b: The child enters into the Kitabah and he cannot sell the mother.

quduri.f: If he [i.e. a Mukatab] buys a Mahram blood relative other than his father or son, does that relative enter the Kitabah?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he does not enter the Kitabah unless he and the purchases have a relationship of birth.

quduri.f: The Mukatab pays his due on the set dates, and then a date arrives where he is unable to pay. Will the court declare him unable to pay?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى59 if the slave has debts which he must pay or wealth advanced to him then there should not be haste in declaring him unable to transact. He should be given two or three days' respite. If thereafter he cannot present any valid excuse the owner may demand that he be incapacitated and the Kitabah annulled by the court. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى he will not be incapacitated until he misses two dates.

59 And Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: When the Mukatab is again incapacitated does he become a normal slave again?
quduri.b: Yes, and whatever he earned belongs to the owner.

quduri.f: The Mukatab possesses the amount of the contract. Does his death annul the contract?
quduri.b: No, the amount of the Kitabah will be taken from his wealth and he will be deemed to have been free in the final part of his life.

quduri.f: After the court ruled that he was freed in the final part of his life and the amount of the Mukatabah taken from his wealth, some wealth was left. [i.e. the Mukatab possessed the amount of the contract but died]
quduri.b: His heirs will take it.

quduri.f: What is the status of his children? [i.e. of the Mukatab who possessed the amount of the contract but died]
quduri.b: They will also be deemed to have been freed.

quduri.f: The Mukatab did not leave enough to fulfil the contract and left behind a child born during the Kitabah period. What is the status of the child? Does it remain upon the Kitabah?
quduri.b:
The child will be a Mukatab and will pay according to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى according to the dates of his father. Once he fulfils the amount the father will be deemed to have been freed before his death and the child will be freed as well.

If the Mukatab bought a boy during the Kitabah, the boy will either have to pay up the amount immediately or revert to full slavery.

quduri.f: A Muslim man demanded pig or wine from his slave as Kitabah. What is the status of the agreement?
quduri.b: The Kitabah is fasid.

quduri.f: If the Mukatab then pays the pig or wine will he be deemed free? [i.e. a Muslim man demanded pig or wine from his slave as Kitabah]
quduri.b: Yes, but he will have to earn the price of it and pay an amount not less than the stated amount but it can increase.

quduri.f: The Kitabah was for the value of the Mukatab himself. What is the status of this agreement?
quduri.b:
It is Fasid because the price is unknown in terms of number, type and description. Nevertheless, if he does pay it he is freed.60

60 Because he is the substitute.

quduri.f: The owner agreed to a Kitabah for an unspecified animal or cloth of unspecified type. What is the status of the Kitabah?
quduri.b:
It is valid in the first case, not the second.61

61 Meaning that if he specified the species but not the quality; it will be interpreted as medium quality. The owner will be forced to accept the price. If he did not specify the specie, e.g. he only says "A beast", then it is not valid. There are many species thus the requirement is completely unknown. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: The owner makes a Kitabah with his two slaves for 1000 Dirham. Is this correct?
quduri.b: Yes, thus if they render the amount they will both be freed, if they are unable, both revert to normal slavery.

quduri.f: He made a Kitabah of two slaves whereby each is liable for the other. Is this valid?
quduri.b: Yes, whichever pays the entire amount frees both of them and will claim half the amount from the other.

quduri.f: He [i.e. the slave owner] made a Kitabah and then freed the Mukatab. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He is freed with the manumission and the amount of the Kitabah is forfeit.

quduri.f: The owner made a Kitabah agreement and then died. Is the agreement nullified?
quduri.b: No, the Mukatab will continue to pay the heirs upon the agreed dates.

quduri.f: If one of the heirs frees him, [i.e. the owner made a Kitabah agreement and then died] is his manumission valid?
quduri.b: If one frees him, he is not free. If they all free him then he will be free and the amount is forfeit.

quduri.f: Can the owner make Kitabah with his Ummul Walad?
quduri.b: Yes, but if he dies before the amount is paid she is still freed due to being his Ummul Walad.

quduri.f: He made Kitabah with his slave-girl and then impregnated her and she bore his child. What does she do?
quduri.b: She can either continue paying to free herself; or she can declare herself incapacitated and await his death for her freedom as her Ummul Walad.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he makes Kitabah with his Mudabbar?
quduri.b: The Kitabah is valid. If the owner dies and leaves no wealth besides the slave, then he can either compensate the estate two-thirds of his value or the full Kitabah amount.

quduri.f: A man made Kitabah with his slave-girl then Tadbir. What is her status?
quduri.b: The Tadbir is valid. She maychoose to fulfil the Kitabah or she may incapacitate herself in which case the laws of Tadbir will apply upon her.

quduri.f: If she chose the Kitabah [i.e. a man made Kitabah with his slave-girl then Tadbir] and the owner dies, will she be freed on the basis of Tadbir?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى if she chose the Kitabah and the owner dies and she is his only wealth, then she may either pay two-thirds of the Kitabah amount to the estate or two-thirds of her value.62

62 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى she will pay whichever is the lesser of the two.

quduri.f: A Mukatab bought a slave from the Kitabah money. He then frees the bought slave in exchange for money. Is that permissible?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If he [i.e. a Mukatab bought a slave from the Kitabah money] instead gives this bought slave as a gift in exchange for compensation?
quduri.b: The gift is not valid.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the Mukatab makes Kitabah with the bought slave? [i.e. a Mukatab bought a slave from the Kitabah money]
quduri.b: The Kitabah is valid. If the second one pays his amount before the first then he is free and his wala is owned by the original owner. If the pays after the first Mukatab then the first Mukatab has his Wala.

quduri.f: Can the Mukatab get a slave-girl he bought married?
quduri.b:
Yes he can.63

63 Because he wil acquire the Mahr, hence it is an earning.

quduri.f: What is Wala linguistically and in Shar'iah?
quduri.b: It is derived from Wali, meaning "near". In Shari'ah it is the right of the ex-owner arising from freeing his slave; or Muwalah agreement. Thus there are two kinds of Wala - Walaul 'Itaqah [manumission] & Walaul Mawalah [voluntary clientship].

quduri.f: Explain the laws related to Walaul 'Itaqah.
quduri.b: When a man frees his slave, male or female, then he holds Walaul 'Itaqah. This is whether he frees him in exchange for wealth or for free. If the Mukatab is freed after the death of the owner then the heirs hold the Walaul 'Itaqah.

quduri.f: A man made Tadbir with his male or female slave, or he made his slave-girl Ummul Walad. Who holds the Wala?
quduri.b: The Mawla [owner] holds the Wala because they were freed through him.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if one holds one's Mahram relative then the relative is freed. Does the owner then hold Wala?
quduri.b:
Yes, the owner holds Wala.64

64 An example is if one of two sisters buys their father and he then dies. The two sisters together inherit two-thirds as per the Quranic stipulation and the one who bought him gets another thirds as Wala holder. If there are no 'asabah relatives because Wala is further than 'asabah.

quduri.f: One man's slave married another's slave-girl. The slave-girl's owner then frees her after the slave husband had impregnated her? Who holds the child's Wala?
quduri.b:
The child is freed with its mother and its Wala is held by the one who freed the mother. It will not aver from him ever. The same applies if she gave birth to the child in less than six months.65

65 Because it is certain that she was pregnant with it at the time of manumission.

quduri.f: If she gave birth [i.e. one man's slave married another's slave girl, and the slave-girl's owner then frees her after the slave husband had impregnated her] after more than six months since manumission, who has the Wala of the child?
quduri.b: The mother's owner has the child's Wala as well, unless the child's father was also freed, in which case the Wala goes to the father's ex-owner.

quduri.f: A non-'Arab married a slave-girl whom an 'Arab had freed. She then has children. What is the status of the children in terms of Wala?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the mother's ex-owners hold the Wala. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the father holds the Wala because lineage is attributed to fathers.

quduri.f: A man frees his slave and stipulates that he does not hold his Wala, but the Muslims in general hold it. Is this valid?
quduri.b:
No, Wala is established to the one who freed the slave. His denial of it has no effect.66 

66 Because the stipulation contradicts the clear words of the Hadith, "Wala is for the one who frees." [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: What is the effect of this Wala? [i.e. a man frees his slave and stipulates that he does not hold his Walah, but the Muslims in general hold it]
quduri.b: It has the effect of including one amongst the 'Asabah, who are those who inherit after the Ashab al-Furud [those stipulated in the Quraan. If the freed slave has 'Asabah in terms of lineage then they are more entitled than the ex-owner. If he does not have such 'Asabah, then the ex-owner inherits. The ex-owner is less entitled than the 'Asabah of lineage and more entitled than Zawil Arham [relatives not 'Asabah].

quduri.f: The ex-owner dies then the freed slave dies. The ex-owner has children. Who inherits the slave's estate?
quduri.b:
The sons of the ex-owner inherit, not the daughters.67 

67 Because the Wala is based on 'Asabah, which does not include females.

quduri.f: Do women acquire Walaul 'Itaqah?
quduri.b:
Yes, if women free a slave, or the slave they freed frees a slave; or they make Kitabah or the slave they made Kitabah with made Kitabah; or they made Tadbir or the slave they made Tadbir with made Tadbir; or drawing Wala of those they freed68; or the freed one of one they freed.

68 The scenario if the drawing: A woman owns a slave. With her permission he marries a slave-girl who was freed. She then bears his child. The child's Wala is held by the ex-owners of the mother. If the woman then frees her slave, the child's Wala becomes drawn to himself. The ex-owner then draws that to herself.
The scenario of drawing the Wala of a freed slave's freed slave is that a woman freed a slave then that slave bought a slave. The second slave then married a freed slave-girl who then bore his child. The ex-owners of the mother hold the child's Wala. If the first slave frees the second slave, the second slave draws the child's Wala, then the first slave draws it to himself, then the woman's ex-owner draws it to herself.

quduri.f: The ex-owner dies. He leaves behind a son and sons of another son. The freed-slave then dies. Who takes the inheritance of the freed-slave?
quduri.b: The son inherits, not the grandsons. Wala goes to the most senior i.e. the closest, and the son is closer to the deceased than the grandsons.

quduri.f: Explain Walaul Mawalah and its regulations.
quduri.b: When a man embraces Islaam on the hands of another and establishes Wala with him whereby the second man will inherit from him and pay any blood money that may arise; or if he establishes the Wala with one besides the man on whose hands he had embraced Islaam then the Wala is valid and the Mawla is liable for the blood money. If the man dies without heirs the Mawla inherits from him. If there is an heir, the heir is more entitled than the Mawla.

quduri.f: Two men established Wala. Can one of them change Wala to another man?
quduri.b:
It is allowed as long as the Mawla did not yet pay any blood money on his behalf.

NOTE: The Mawla of Walaul 'Itaqah cannot make Walaul Mawalah.69

69 The two differ in three aspects: In Walaul Mawalah both inherit from each other if they both agree, unlike Walaul 'Itaqah. Secondly, Walaul Mawalah can be cancelled unlike Walaul 'Itaqah. Thirdly, Walaul Mawalah has less entitlement than Zawail Arham, Walaul 'Itaqah is the opposite. [al-Jawharah].

quduri.f: What is Ibaq?
quduri.b: It is the deliberate, disobedient running away of a slave from his owner. The runaway is called Abiq.

quduri.f: A man returns a runaway slave to his owner. Does the man deserve a reward?
quduri.b: Yes, if he returned him from a distance of three days' journey or more then the owner must give him 40 Dirham. If less than that, then in proportion.

quduri.f: And if the slave is worth less than 40 Dirham? [i.e. he ran away but someone brought him back]
quduri.b: He will be paid the slave's price, less 1 Dirham.

quduri.f: A man seizes a runaway slave to return him to his owner. The slave escapes from the man. What is the status of his reward?
quduri.b: He is not entitled to a reward just as he is not liable for the slave escaping from him. It is apporpriate for him to make witnesses that he is taking the runaway to his owner when he seizes him.

quduri.f: The runaway was Rahn. A man seized him and returned him. Is his reward due from the Rahim or Murtahin?
quduri.b: Murtahin.

quduri.f: What are the linguistic and Shar'i definitions of Jinayah?
quduri.b: Linguistically it is to commit an act which causes harm to someone. In the terminology of the Fuqaha it is the transgression of one party against another in his life or appendages. Transgression in life means murder, whether it is deliberate or accidental. Transgression against appendages means cutting a hand, leg, ear or putting out an eye etc.

quduri.f: Are there different kinds of Qatl [murder]?
quduri.b:
There are five kinds:
Amad [premeditated]
Shibhu 'Amad [resembling premeditated]
Khata [mistake]

That which is legally deemed a mistake.
al-Qatl bi sabab [killing via a means]

quduri.f: Explain the regulations of these five categories [i.e. of the different kinds of Qatl (murder)]:
quduri.b:
Premeditated murder is the deliberate striking with a weapon or what can be used as a weapon such as a sharp piece of wood or stone. It is a sin and causes the perpretrator to be disinherited. Qisas [retaliation] will be implemented unless the Awliya [family] forgives him. No Kaffarah is accepted.
Shibhu 'Amad is the deliberate striking with that which is neither a weapon nor is used as a weapon. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى if one strikes with a large rock or large wood then it is also regarded as 'Amad. They define Shibhu 'Amad as deliberately striking with that which generally does not kill. In either case, both parties agree that it is a sin and Kaffarah must be paid. There is no Qisas, but there is Diyah Mughallazhah upon the 'Aqilah. We shall explain the meanings of these terms later InshaAllaah.
Khata consists of two kinds: Mistake in intention, e.g. a man shot another, thinking him to be prey. Mistake in action, e.g. he aimed at  a target but it hit a man instead. In these cases he is not guilty of murder but must pay Kaffarah which is Diyah to the 'Aqilah.
That which is legally deemed a mistake, e.g. someone is sleeping and turns over onto another person, killing him. The ruling is the same as Khata.
al-Qatl bi sabab e.g. a man digs a well or places a rock in a property which is not his. Someone slips and dies. He must pay Kaffarah, and diyah to the 'Aqilah.70

70 But he is not disinherited.

quduri.f: What is Qisas?
quduri.b: It is the killing of the murderer in retaliation for the life of the victim. It is Wajib for the killing of every person whose blood is held permanently sacred when killing deliberately.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a freeman killing a freeman or a slave; or a slave killing a freeman or a slave?
quduri.b: In each case the murderer will be executed irrespective whether the murderer is slave/freeman or the viction is slave/freeman.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of retaliation for killing a Zimmi and Mustamin [foreign Kafir who obtained permission to enter tje lands of Islaam]?
quduri.b: A Muslim will be executed for killing a Zimmi. Neither a Muslim nor a Zimmi will be ececuted for killing the Mustamin.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a man killed a woman; or a woman killed a man; or an adult killed a minor; or a healthy person killed a blind/chronically ill/insane/one who lost limbs?
quduri.b: Retaliation will occur in all these cases. Allaah says, "We had decreed upon them that a life for a life and an eye for an eye and a nose for a nose and ear for ear and a tooth for a tooth and retaliation for wounds." [al-Maidah:45]

quduri.f: Is there retaliation if a man killed his son/slave/Mudabbar/Mukatab/son's slave?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man has the right to claim retaliation against his father. Will the father be executed?
quduri.b: No, the execution wil be lifted due to respect of the fatherhood.

quduri.f: A child or madman deliberately killed. Will they be executed?
quduri.b: Their premeditated murder is deemed Khata. The 'Aqilah will pay Diyah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the killer pays a compromise to the Awliya of the victim?
quduri.b: The execution is omitted and the money is Wajib, however little or much it may be.

quduri.f: If one of the partners foregoes the retaliation; or compromises on his share for a cosideration, what do the rest do?
quduri.b: Retaliation is foregone in both cases. The remaining parties are still entitled to their shares of the Diyah. The murderer should not give them difficulty but should pay them in a good way, just as the family of the victim should not harm him. Allaah says, "He who is pardoned for killing his brother then he must be pursued in a good manner and payment made with kindness." [al-Baqarah:178]

quduri.f: A man killed several people. The victims' demanded retaliation. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He will be executed as soon as retaliation is demanded for one of them. The claims of the rest are then forfeit.

quduri.f: A group of people killed one person. Will they be executed?
quduri.b: Yes, all will be executed.

quduri.f: A murderer died before he could be executed. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The retaliation is forfeit. Nothing can be claimed from his estate.

quduri.f: A slave confesses to premeditated murder. Will he be executed?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man shot another deliberately. The arrow continued and killed another. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He will be executed for the first murder and must pay Diyah to the 'Aqilah of the second victim.

quduri.f: A man made Kitabah with his slave. The Mukatab was then killed. Who is entitled to retaliation?
quduri.b: If the Mukatab has no other heir besides the owner, then the owner has right of retaliation if he did not leave enough to cover the Kitabah. If he did leave enough, and the heir is not the Mawla, then the Mawla does not have retaliation, even if the heirs are joined with the Mawla.

quduri.f: A man left his slave as colleteral. That slave was killed. Will the killer be executed?
quduri.b: Yes, retaliation is Wajib on condition that the Rahin and Murtahin both demand it.

quduri.f: A man wounded another. The victim remained wounded and bedridden until he died. Is there retaliation?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: How are executions performed?
quduri.b: Executions are only done by sword.

quduri.f: What are the laws of retaliation for body parts?
quduri.b:
If a man cuts the hand of another from the joint, the cutter's hand will be amputated. Similarly if he cuts a leg or soft part of the nose, those organs will be amputed from the cutter.
If a man strikes another on the eye and thereby puts it out then there is no retaliation. If the eye remains but is blinded, then there is retaliation. A mirror will be heated. Moist cotton will be placed on his eye. His other eye will face the mirror until it is blinded.71 
If a man extracts the tooth of another then there is retaliation. There is no retaliation in bones, other than teeth.
There is retaliation for fracturing a skull where fracturing can be mimicked.
There is no retaliation for cutting of the tongue or the penis, unless it is cut from the glans.72 
There is no retaliation between a man and a woman besides retaliation for a life; just as there is no retaliation between a freeman and a slave, and between two slaves for anything besides life.
There is retaliation for organs between a Muslim and a Zimmi.
A man cuts into half a man's arm and it heals. There is no retaliation.
If an internal wound is afflicted and it heals then there is no retaliation.
If a man with a cripple or defective hand cuts a non-defective hand then the victim has a choice - he can either have the perpetrator's defective hand cut with no further claim, or he can demand complete Arsh. (Diyaat - compensation)
A man fractures the skull of another, temple to temple. The victim has a choice. He can demand retaliation, beginning from whichever temple he wishes, or he can demand complete Arsh. (Diyaat - compensation)
If two men cut the hand of one man then there is no retaliation. Each of them must pay half the Diyah of a life.
A man cuts the right hands of two men. They both present their claims. They can cut off his hand and take half Diyah of life which will be shared in two halves amongst them. If one presents the case and has his hand cutoff, then the other can claim half Diyah.
Shibhu 'Amad is only found in life retaliation. Everything else is 'Amad or Khata.

71 This is according to the medical knowledge of the time. If modern medicinal methods are used, then there is no problem as long as the limits of retaliation have not been exceeded.

72 i.e. if the tongue is partially cut. If cut from the root, then there is retaliation according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. As for the penis, it erects and subsides, hence equality in retaliation is impossible. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى there is retaliation if cut from the root.

quduri.f: What is Diyah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: It is a root-word on the scale of 'idah whereby the Faul Kalimah has been dropped. The grammatical sequence is read, "wada yadi wadyan wa diayatan fahuwa wadin." In Shari'iah it is money which becomes Wajib upon the killer when he committed Khata, or Shibu 'Amad, or cut an organ. The compensation for cutting organs is also called Arsh.

quduri.f: Explain the rules and amount of Diyah.
quduri.b:
When a man kills another Shubhu 'Amad then the killer's 'Aqilah must pay Diyah Mughallazha and the killer must give Kaffarah. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى Diyah Mughallazhah is 100 camels as follows - 26 Bint Makhad [female in second year]; 25 Bint Labun [female in third year]; 25 Hiqqah [in fourth year]; and 25 Jaza'ah [in fifth year]. There is no Mughallazh in anything besides Shibhu 'Amad; and when Diyah is decided upon as anything besides camels then there is also no Mughallazh even in Shibhu 'Amad.
In Qatlul Khata, Diyah is Wajib upon the 'Aqilah and Kaffarah upon the killer. The Diyah here is in five groups - 20 Bint Makhad [female in second year]; 20 Ibn Makhad [male]; 20 Bint Labun [female in third year]; 20 Hiqqah [in fourth year]; and 20 Jaza'ah [in fifth year]. This Diyah is not Mughallazh.
Diyah in gold is 1000 Dinar and in silver is 10,000 Dirham.

According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى there is only these three kinds of Diyah. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى Diyah is of these three categories as well as cattle, goats and clothing. If the court rules according to cattle, it will be 200 head of cattle, if goats then 1000, if clothing then 200 sets - each set being two pieces of clothing.
A complete Diyah of a life is Wajib in Shibhu 'Amad and Khata and is Mughallazh in the first case.
A complete Diyah - 100 camels - is due for cutting of a nose, tongue or penis.
A complete Diyah is due if one struck a man on the head, making him lose his mind.
A complete Diyah is due if one plucked or shaved a man's beard and it did not regrow.
A complete Diyah is due if one plucked or shaved a man's head and the hair did not regrow.
A complete Diyah is due if one hit a man or otherwise did such an act which resulted in him losing his eyebrows or eyes.
A complete Diyah is due if one cut both hands/legs/ears.
A complete Diyah is due if a man's lips or two middle incisors were cut; or a woman's two nipples were cut.
If one of these things were cut then it is a half Diyah.
A complete Diyah is due if the eyelids were cut. If one eyelid was cut then a quarter Diyah.
Each finger or toe, irrespective which is a tenth of a Diyah.
For every joint of a finger or toe which has three joints the Diyah is a third of the Diyah of the digit. Similarly it is half for every digit which has two joints.
If all the fingers of a hand are cut, or the palm is cut with the fingers, then it is half Diyah in both cases.
If the arm is cut up to half the forearm, then for the fingers and arm there is half Diyah. Excess is judged by a just person.
For an extra finger will be the ruling of a just person.
If a toe is cut off and an adjacent toe becomes lame as a result, then there is Arsh for the two and not Diyah according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى.
For every tooth there are 5 camels. Molars and other teeth are treated equally.
If a tooth is taken out and another grows in its place then the Arsh is forfeit.
If an organ is struck and loses its use, then there is full Diyah just as if it was cut, e.g. if an arm becomes paralysed or an eye is blinded.
If it is undetermined whether an eye/tongue/penis ofa child does not function then the ruling of a just person is made.

quduri.f: Explain the kinds of skull wounds.
quduri.b:
There are ten kinds:
Hasirah [scratching the skin without bleeding]

Dami'ah [blood emerges but does not flow]

Damiyah [blood flows]

Badi'ah [the skin is cut]

Mutalahimah [the flesh is penetrated]

Simhaq [the periosteum or skin between the flesh and bone is penetrated]

Muwaddihah [the bone is exposed]

Hashimah [the bone is broken]

Munaqqilah [the bone moves after being broken]

Ammah [penetrates to the brain]

quduri.f: What are the rulings of these wounds? [i.e. skull wounds]
quduri.b:
Muwaddihah - if deliberate then there is Qisas.

There is no retaliation in other kinds of wounds.73
Anything less than Muwaddihah will be according to the judgement of a just person.

For Muwaddihah there will be a twentieth of Diyah if it was accidental.
For Hashimahi there will be a tenth of Diyah.
For Munaqqilah there will be a tenth of twentieth of Diyah.
For Ammah a third of Diyah.
For Jaifah74 there is a third of Diyah. If it penetrates both [hollows] then it is two Jaifah and for that there is two-thirds of Diyah.
73 Because exact equality cannot be assured.

74 Wound which penetrates to the hollow of the stomach or back.

quduri.f: A man wounded another Muwaddihah. As a result he lost his senses or hair. Does he pay two Diyah?
quduri.b:
No, the Arsh of Muwaddihah is included in the Diyah.75

75 Because the loss of senses is the loss of the benefit of all organs and the loss of hair is accounted in a Muwaddihah wound.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he lost his hearing or sight or both?
quduri.b:
The Arsh of Muwaddihah and the complete Diyah are both payable.76

76 According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى Arsh of Muwaddihah is included in Diyah of hearing and speech but not sight.

quduri.f: A man wounded another's skull Mutalahimah. No trace remained and the hair grew again. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the Arsh is forfeit. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى he is liable for the Arsh of the pain. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he is liable for the doctor's expenses.

quduri.f: A man wounds another whereby retaliation becomes Wajib. When will it be taken?
quduri.b: When the victim recovers, not before.

quduri.f: A man cut another's hand by accident. Then before he could recover he killed him by accident. Do two Diyah become Wajib?
quduri.b:
He is liable for a complete Diyah and the Arsh of the hand is forfeit. If he recovered before being killed then there is Diyah of the hand and another for the life.

NOTE: The Diyah of a Muslim and a Zimmi are equal. The DIyah of a woman is half that of a man.

quduri.f: A man dug a well in the pathway of the Muslims or placed a rock there. As a result a human got killed. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: His 'Aqilah is responsible for a complete Diyah. We had mentioned before that there is no Kaffarah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if an animal got killed? [i.e. a man dug a well in the pathway of the Muslims or placed a rock there.]
quduri.b: He is liable to pay for it.

quduri.f: A man constructs a skylight or gutter along the road. It falls and kills a man. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Complete Diyah is liable, the 'Aqilah is responsible for it.

quduri.f: A man dug a well in his own property. Someone died because of it. Is the digger liable?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A wall started leaning towards the road of the Muslims. The owner was requested to break and he did not. The wall then fell and killed someone or caused loss of wealth. Is the owner liable?
quduri.b: If witnesses were made to the request for demolishing the wall and he did not demolish it within a time that he could, then he is liable for whatever life or wealth is lost.

quduri.f: A Zimmi requested that he demolish it. [i.e. A wall started leaning toward the road of the Muslims. The owner was requested to break and he did not. The wall then fell and killed someone or causes loss of wealth] Is his rights the same as a Muslim's in this?
quduri.b: A Muslim and a Zimmi are the same in this.

quduri.f: A wall was leaning on a man's house. Someone besides the house's owner requested the wall to be demolished. The wall's owner did not, and it fell, destroying life or property. Is he liable?
quduri.b: The request is the exclusive prerogative of the house's owner. If there are other inhabitants then they may also request it.

quduri.f: If a mount knocks something, who is liable?
quduri.b: The rider is liable for what it tramples or destroys with its forelegs or bites. He is not liable for what is knocked by its hind legs or tail.

quduri.f: If the mount urinated or defecated in the road, by which a human got killed, is the rider liable?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: You only mentioned a rider. What about one who drags or pushes an animal? [i.e. if the animal knocks something]
quduri.b: The one who brings the animal up from its behind is responsible for the damage of its forelegs and hind legs. The one who brings the animal up from front is responsible ofr its forelegs, not hind legs.

quduri.f: A man leads a herd. One of the animals tramples a man or wealth. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He is liable. If he had someone bringing the animals from behind as well then both are liable.

quduri.f: Two horsemen collided and died. Who is liable?
quduri.b: The 'Aqilah of each will pay the Diyah of the other.

quduri.f: Who is liable for the accidental violation of the slave?
quduri.b: The owner can either hand the slave over to the victim or he can ransom the slave by paying the Arsh of the violation.

quduri.f: If he commits a crime a second time? [i.e. who is liable for the accidental violation of the slave]
quduri.b: The ruling of the second is the same as that of the first.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he commits two violations?
quduri.b: The owner may either hand him over to the two victims who will share him as per the value of their rights, or the owner may ransom him by paying the Arsh of both victims.

quduri.f: A slave committed a violation. His owner then set him free, knowing about the violation. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The ex-owner is liable to pay the Arsh.

quduri.f: Who is liable if a Mudabbar or Ummul Walad commits a crime?
quduri.b: The owner is liable. He will pay whatever is the lesser of the slave's price and the Arsh.

quduri.f: If the slave commits another crime, and the owner had already paid the slave's price to a victim, what must the owner do now?
quduri.b: If he made the first payment through a court order, then he does not pay anything. The second claimant will claim from the first and they will share in what the first claimant took. If it was without a court order, then the second claimant may either claim from the slave's owner or from the first claimant.

quduri.f: A man killed a slave by mistake. What is he liable for?
quduri.b: He will be liable for the price of the slave. If however the price is 10,000 Dirham or more, then he will pay 10,000 less 10.

quduri.f: A man killed a slave-girl by mistake. What is he liable for?
quduri.b:
He is liable for her price. If her price is more than Diyah, then he must pay 5,000 less 5.77

77 Al-Hidayah mentioned "less 10", which is the Zhahirur Riwayah. Al-Quduri mentions the narration of al-Hasan from Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: What is a man liable for if he cuts off the hand of a slave?
quduri.b: He is liable for the price of the slave to an amount not exceeding 5,000 less 5. Whatever is valued in terms of Diyah for a free victim, is valued according to the price of the slave in regards his organs.

quduri.f: A man struck a freewoman's belly. As a result she had a miscarriage. What is he liable for?
quduri.b:
He is liable for Ghurrah which is a twentieth of a Diyah.78 

78 i.e. a twentieth of the Diyah of a man (500 Dirham), whether the foetus is male or female. This is when at least part of the foetus's form has become apparent. According to us the 'Aqilah must pay it within a year. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: If the baby came out prematurely because of the strike, [i.e. a man hit the belly of a pregnant woman], but was alive and only died later, what is the penalty?
quduri.b:
Complete Diyah.79

79 Upon the 'Aqilah [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: What is the pentalty if she drops the dead foetus and then she herself died? [i.e. if someone hit a pregnant woman]
quduri.b: Complete Diyah for the mother and Ghurrah for the foetus.

quduri.f: And if she died and then the dead foetus emerged? [i.e. a man hit a pregnant woman]
quduri.b: Complete Diyah for the mother and nothing for the foetus.

quduri.f: If the mother died then the baby emerged alive and then died, what is the penalty? [i.e. if a man hit a pregnant woman]
quduri.b: Two Diyah.

quduri.f: What do you say if someone struck a slave-girl's stomach and she had a miscarriage?
quduri.b: If the dead foetus is male then the penalty is a twentieth of the boy's value had it lived; and if it is female then a tenth of the price.

quduri.f: Who is the recipient of the foetus' penalty? [i.e. if a man hit a pregnant woman]
quduri.b: If the mother was a freewoman then the penalty will be shared by the heirs of the foetus according to their inheritance shares. If the mother was a slave then her owner gets the penalty money.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that Kaffarah is due in the killing of Shibhu 'Amad and Khata. Explain whether this is Kaffarah.
quduri.b: Allaah has explained the Kaffarah of killing in SUratun Nisa, "... freeing a believing slave. He who does not find should fast two consecutive months as obtaining Allaah's forgiveness".

quduri.f: Is there Kaffarah for killing a slave, slave-girl or foetus?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Can one not feed the poor as in Kaffarah of Zhihar?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man was found murdered in a certain district. The murderer is not known. How will the murder be investigated?
quduri.b: Rasulullaah ﷺ has taught a way for it. It is to take an oath from 50 men of that district. This process is called Qasamah.

quduri.f: Who chooses these 50? [i.e. for Qasamah when there's been a murder] How are the paths taken?
quduri.b: The Wali of the victim will choose them. There may not be any children, madmen, women, slaves, Mudabbars or Mukatabs amongst them. They will swear, "By Allaah, we neither killed him, nor do we know who killed him."

quduri.f: Are they completely absolved once they have taken the oath? [i.e. after 50 men have been summoned for Qasamah after there's been a murder]
quduri.b: No, the people of that district must pay Diyah.

quduri.f: If the Wali himself is of that district [i.e. where there was a murder], will the oath be taken from him as well?
quduri.b: He will not be forced to take the oath. He will not contribute to the Diyah even if he takes the oath.

quduri.f: The Wali chose the 50 men. [i.e. for Qasamah after a murder] Some of them refused to take the oath. What will be done?
quduri.b: They will be detained until they take the oath.

quduri.f: The Wali chose less than 50 men. [i.e. for Qasamah after a murder] What will be done?
quduri.b: Those chosen will repeat their oaths until 50 oaths have been taken.

quduri.f: A corpse was found with no sign of murder. Will Qasamah occur and Diyah paid?
quduri.b: There is neither Qasamah nor Diyah in this case.

quduri.f: Is there Qasamah if a corpse was found with blood flowing from its nose, anus or mouth?
quduri.b: This will not be regarded as murder. There will be neither Qasamah nor Diyah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if blood is flowing from its eyes or ears? [i.e. when a corpse is found]
quduri.b: It will be deemed a murder and Qasamah will occur.

quduri.f: A man leads a beast on which a murdered corpse is found. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The Diyah is Wajib up the 'Aqilah of that man, not of the district.

quduri.f: A man was found murdered in someone's house. Who will take the oath?
quduri.b: Only the person of the house will take the oath. The Diyah is upon his 'Aqilah.

quduri.f: Some of the residents of houses of a district are owners and others are tenants. Will the oath be taken from all of them? [i.e. Qasamah for murder]
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the tenant will not take the oath with the original owners who according to him are those for whom the ruler had allocated the land, not those who bought property there, even if there is only one of the original owners left.80

80 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the buyers will also be included. [Sharhuzz Zayla'i]

quduri.f: Who will take the oath if a murder victim is found on a ship?
quduri.b: The passengers and sailors who are on the ship.

quduri.f: Who takes the oath if the corpse is found in the local Masjid?
quduri.b: Upon the people of the district.

quduri.f: If he is found [i.e. a corpse] in the Jam' Masjid or the Highway, from which district will the 50 men be chosen?
quduri.b: There is no Qasamah in these two scenarios. The Diyah will be paid from the Baytul Mal [Public Treasury]

quduri.f: If he is found between two towns [i.e. the corpse] upon who is the Qasamah?
quduri.b: Upon whichever town is closer.

quduri.f: If the corpse is found in the desert, who takes the oath?
quduri.b:
If there are no buildings nearby81 then no oath will be taken and there will be no consequence for his blood.

81 Nearby buildings are as defined previously as based upon if a shout can be heard.

quduri.f: If the corpse is found in a river, who will take the oath?
quduri.b: If the corpse was found in the middle of flowing water then there is no consequence to his blood. If it was found trapped on a bank, then the people of the nearest town will take the oath.

quduri.f: If the Wali makes an accusation against a specific person, does the Qasamah fall away from the rest?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he [i.e. the Wali] accuses a specific person who is not one of them? [i.e. the group of 50 people]
quduri.b: The Qasamah and Diyah fall away from them.

quduri.f: A man asked to take an oath testified to a specific person having committed the murder. Will his word be taken?
quduri.b: No, he will be made to swear, "By Allaah, I neither killed hi, nor do I know anybody to have killed him besides so-and-so."

quduri.f: Two men testified that a man outside the district had committed the murder. Will their Arsh be accepted?
quduri.b:
No.82

82 According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى, It will be accepted according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: You have often mentioned that the 'Aqilah pays the Diyah on behalf of the killer. What is the meaning of 'Aqilah?
quduri.b:
'Aql/Ma'qulah is the paying of Diyah on behalf of the killer. Those who do this are called the 'Aqilah. Every Diyah Wajib due to actual killing [i.e. excluding compromise payments] is Wajib upon the 'Aqilah. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى 'Aqilah is those on the Diwan83 if the killer is from amongst them. The Diyah will be taken from their stipends84 over a three year period. If the stipends are issued after longer than three years or less, the Diyah will still be taken from there. If the killer is not of the people of the Diwan then the 'Aqilah is his tribe. They will pay over three years. Each member will not pay more than 4 Dirham, 1 and third per year. If the tribe has many members then the individual contributions will be reduced. The killer will be included in their number and will pay the same as any other member.

83 The registered names of the army.
84 The annual or twice-a-year allotments made to the soldiers.

quduri.f: If the tribe is unable to pay, how will the Diyah be fulfilled?
quduri.b:
The closest tribe will be joined to them.85

85 In terms of lineage. First the closest then the next closest will be joined as per the 'Asabah sequence. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: Explain in detail what the 'Aqilah is liable for and what not.
quduri.b:
The 'Aqilah is responsible for the following:
Diyah of Shibhu 'Amad. We mentioned before that this Diyah is Mughallazah.

Diyah of Qatl al-Khata.

Diyah of Qatl bi Sabab.

Diyah if someone constricted a skylight or gutter along the public way and it fell and killed someone.

The deliberate murder by a child or madman is deemed Khata. The 'Aqilah must pay the Diyah.
When freman commits a violation by mistake on a slave then his 'Aqilah is responsible.
The 'Aqilah is not responsible for the following Diyah:
Every 'Amad in which retaliation is dropped due to doubt results in the Killer paying the Diyah, not the 'Aqilah.
If a father kills his son deliberately then the Diyah is from his wealth over three years, not the 'Aqilah.
The 'Aqilah does not pay for a slave's violation.
The 'Aqilah is not responsible if the perpretrator confessed to the violation. The Diyah is from his money. If they however proclaim his innocence then they must pay.
The 'Aqilah is not liable for amounts due to Sulh.

quduri.f: Sundry Masail
quduri.b:
The 'Aqilah of a freed slave is his Mawla's tribe.
The Mawla and his tribe are 'Aqilah for the one who entered into Mawalah with him.
