The 'Aqilah is not responsible for less than a twentieth of a Diyah. They bear from a twentieth and greater. Less than that is the responsibility of the perpretrator.

quduri.f: What is Hadd linguistically and in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: Linguistically it is "prevention". In Shari'ah it is every prescribed punishment inflicted as fulfilling Allaah's right.

quduri.f: For which sins is the Hadd prescribed?
quduri.b: The ruler will inflict the Hadd for Zina, drinking wine, slandering a chaste man or woman with Zina, and cutting the hand for stealing. We shall discuss the first three first.

quduri.f: Explain the Hadd of Zina.
quduri.b: There are two categories: 100 lashes for non-Muhsan, whether male or female; and Rajm or stoning for the Muhsan, male or female.

quduri.f: How do the courts establish Zina to have been committed?
quduri.b:
It is established through evidence or confession.

Evidence: Four witnesses testify that a man or a woman committed Zina. After they testify the court will question them, "What is Zina? How was it done? Where? When? With who?" Once they have clarified that and said, "We saw him penetrating her vagina just as an antimony-stick enters the antimony bottle", the judge will investigate the piety and justice of the witnesses. If they fulfil the requirements of justice in secret and open, he will rule according to their Arsh and inflict the Hadd. If their number falls below four or one of them is established as Fasiq [open sinner] then all the witnesses will be inflicted with the Hadd of slander.

Confession: A sane adult confesses four times to having committed Zina. The confessions will be four separate gatherings. Each time he confesses the judge will refuse him. It is recommended for the judge to refuse him in these words, "Perhaps you just touched or kissed her." When the person completes his confession as mentioned, the judge will ask him "What is Zina? How was it done? Where? With who?" Once he does that the Hadd becomes mandatory.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that a non-Muhsan is lashed 100 times. Describe this lashing.
quduri.b: His clothing will be removed except that which is needed to cover his private region. He will then be lashed with moderate force using a lash which does not have any fruits on it. The lashes must be spread over different body parts. The head, face, penis and vagina may not be lashed.

quduri.f: Is the ruling of a man and woman different? [i.e. regarding lashes as a non-Muhsan]
quduri.b: They are the same except that a woman's clothing will not be removed except for her furs and padding.

quduri.f: Should they stand or sit while being lashed? [i.e. the non-Muhsan]
quduri.b: The man will stand and the woman will sit.

quduri.f: What is Ihsan [state of being Muhsan]?
quduri.b:
Ihsan of stoning86 is for the perpretator to be a free, sane, adult Muslim who has had sex with his wife from a correct marriage.87 It is a condition that both husband and wife must be Muhsan.88 

86 As distinguished from Ihsan of slander which does not have the conditions of marriage and sex,
87 As distinguished from a Fasid marriage e.g. marriage without witnesses.
88 Each has to be Muhsan for the other to be Muhsan. Thus if a freewoman or a slave-girl marries a slave then there is no Ihsan unless he has sex with her after manumission. The Ihsan only counts thereafter. So if a Zimmi has adultery with a Muslimah then accepts Islam he will be lashed not stoned.

quduri.f: How is one who commits Zina after Ihsan stoned?
quduri.b: He will be flung with stones until he dies. The judge will take him out of the land here sentence will be executed. The witnesses must begin stoning, then the judge, then the people. If the witnesses refuse to begin, then the stoning falls away. If the perpretator had confessed, then the judge will begin, followed by the people. If a hole is dug to place the woman to be stoned it will be better.

quduri.f: Will the executed adulterer be given Ghusl and Salatul Janazah?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man has a slave or slave-girl who must be lashed for Zina. Will he do it himself?
quduri.b: He may not without court permission.

quduri.f: A man retracts his confession. Will the Hadd still be inflicted?
quduri.b: He will be released even if he recants before or during the stoning and his retraction will be accepted.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if a witness recants after the decision for stoning has been passed but before the implementation?
quduri.b: All the witnesses will be lashed for slander. The stoning falls away from the accussed. If one of the witnesses recants after the stoning, he alone will be lashed and will be liable for a quarter Diyah.

quduri.f: When will the Hadd be applied and when not
quduri.b:
If a man has non-vaginal sex with an unrelated woman he will receieve Ta'zir not Hadd.
He who has sex with the slave-girl of his son or his son's son will not receive the Hadd even if he says, "I knew that she is forbidden unto me."

A man had sex with the slave-girl of his father, or mother, or wife. If he says, "I thought she is permissible for me", he will not receive the Hadd. If he says, "I knew that she is forbidden unto me", he will receive the Hadd. Similarly if a slave has sex with his owner's slave-girl and he says, "I thought she is permissible for me", he will not receive the Hadd. If he says, "I knew that she is forbidden unto me", he will receive the Hadd.
The Hadd will be inflicted if one has sex with one's brother's slave-girl or paternal uncle's slave-girl, even if one says, "I thought that she is permissible for me."
There is no Hadd if the woman presents someone other than his bride on the wedding night and says that she is his wife. If he has sex with her he must pay Mahr.
The Hadd is applied if a man finds a woman on his bed and has sex with her.
There is no Hadd if a man marries a woman he is forbidden to and has sex with her.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى Ta'zir and not Hadd will be inflicted on one who has anal sex with a woman or commits the act of the people of Lut عليه السلام. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is the same as Zina and the Hadd will be applied.89 
There is no Hadd upon one who commits bestiality.
There is no Hadd upon one who committed Zina in the lands of the Kuffar or the rebels and then returned to the land of Islaam.
89 Ash-Shami mentions that the Hadd will not be applied for once-off sodomy but the ruler will execute the sodomite for repeat offences.

Ibnul Humam narrates that Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه consulted the Sahabah and they agreed with 'Ali رضي الله عنه that the homosexual should be burned.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رضي الله عنه there is no Hadd for sodomy not because it is lighter than Zina, but because of clear evidence. It is worse than Zina, because Zina is understandable intellectually and according to human nature, not so sodomy.

quduri.f: Sundry rulings
quduri.b:
If a male or female slave commits Zina he/she will be lashed 50 times because the Hadd of slaves is half that of free people. They are not stoned due to lack of Ihsan.
A Muhsan will not be lashed and stoned.
A non-Muhsan will not be lashed and exiled unless the ruler sees a benefit in it. In that case he will exile him for a period he deems appropriate.
If witnesses testified to a Hadd committed a while back and the distance from the court was not a factor in preventing them from testifying, then their Arsh will not be accepted, except for slander.
If a sick man commits Zina whereby the sentence is stoning, it will be implemented. If the sentence is lashing it will be postponed until he has recovered.
A pregnant woman will not be punished with the Hadd until she has given birth. If the punishment is lashing, she will only be lashed after her Nifas. If stoning, then she will be stoned during the Nifas.

quduri.f: What is Hadd of Shurb?
quduri.b:
It is the punishment for drinking wine. He who drinks wine and is seized and is still stinking of wine, or confesses and is still smelling of wine, will be inflected with the Hadd. If he confesses after the stench has departed then there is no Hadd.

There is no Hadd until he becomes sober.
The drinking is established through the Arsh of two witnesses or if he confesses once. The Arsh of women with men will not be accepted here.

quduri.f: Is the Hadd applied for drinking anything besides wine?
quduri.b:
Hadd will be applied if he becomes intoxicated90 with Nabiz [date infused water]. He will not be lashed until it is known that he became drunk with it and drank willingly.91

90 I.e. he will not be lashed if not intoxicated, as opposed to wine, the mere drinking of which is punishable. [al-Jawharah]
91 It is possible that he became intoxicated with another substance or was forced.

quduri.f: A man stinks of wine or vomits it. There are no witnesses to him drinking, nor does he confess. Will the Hadd be applied?
quduri.b:
No.92

92 Since he might have been forced, or had no water and had to drink the wine. The doubt lifts the punishment.

quduri.f: What is the punishment for a drinker of wine and a drunkard?
quduri.b: He will be lashed 80 times. The lashes will be spread over his body as we have mentioned in Hadd of Zina.

quduri.f: A man confessed to drinking wine or became drunk, he then retracted his confession. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The Hadd is lifted.

quduri.f: What is the punishment for a slave that drunk?
quduri.b: Half that of a freeman, i.e. 40 lashes.

quduri.f: What is Hadd of Qazf?
quduri.b: The punishment for one who explicitly93 slanders a male or female Muhsan [chaste] with Zina. It is estbalished by the Arsh of two men or the confession once of the slanderer. The Hadd becomes Wajib if the slandered party requests redress.

quduri.f: What is the punishment of the slanderer?
quduri.b: He will be lashed 80 times. The lashes will be spread over his body. His clothing will not be removed except for fur and padding. Allaah says, "Lash them 80 times and do not ever accept their Arsh."

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the slanderer is a slave?
quduri.b: The Hadd is halved. He will be lashed 40 times.

quduri.f: What are the requisites for Ihsan in this case? [i.e. with regards to Qafz/slander]
quduri.b: The slandered must be free, adult, sane, Muslim and chaste from Zina. He or she who fulfils these requirements is Muhsan and his or her slanderer will be lashed.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if someone confesses to slander and then recants?
quduri.b: The retraction will not be accepted. The slanderer will be lashed if the slandered so desires.

quduri.f: A man says to another, "You do not belong to your father". Is that slander?
quduri.b: Yes, he will be lashed.

quduri.f: A man says to another, "O son of adultery (i.e. bastard)". The second man's mother is deceased and she was Muhsan. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If the man demands it, the slanderer will be lashed. The Hadd may not be demanded in the case of a slandered dead person except by one whose lineage is defiled by the slander, i.e. the son and father.

quduri.f: A man slandered a Muhsan. Can the Muhsan's Kafir son or slave demand the Hadd?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A slave has a free mother. His owner slanders his mother. Can the slave demand the penalty of slander against his owner?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man says to an 'Arab, "O Nabatean!" or what the Nabateans call themself, "O son of Heavenly Water!  Will the Hadd be applied against him?
quduri.b: No, that is not considered slander.

quduri.f: A man attributes the lineage of a man to the man's paternal uncle, or maternal uncle, or mother's husband. Is that slander?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man committed forbidden sex and the other party is not his possession. Another man slanders him about it. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: There is no Hadd for this slander.

quduri.f: A man slanders his wife. They do Li'an at the court. The man then again slanders her. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If the Li'an was for the purpose of denying a child's lineage then the husband slanders her, there is no Hadd. If it was for the sole purpose of the husband having accused her of adultery without the involvement of any child, then he will be lashed if he slanders her after the Lian.

quduri.f: A man slanders a slave, slave-girl or Kafir. Is there Hadd?
quduri.b: There is Ta'zir, not Hadd.

quduri.f: If he says to a Muslim, "O Fasiq [open sinner]/Kafir/Khabith [spiritual filthy]", is there Hadd?
quduri.b: No, there is Ta'zir.

quduri.f: Is there Ta'zir or Hadd if he says, "O donkey/pig"?
quduri.b: Neither.

quduri.f: Is there Diyah if someone died while being Islaamically lashed for Hadd/Ta'zir?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Is there any additional punishment for the slanderer besides being lashed?
quduri.b: A Muslim who has been lashed for slander may never again testify even if he repents. Allaah says, "Lash them 80 times and do not ever accept their Arsh."

quduri.f: A Kafir slandered someone and received the Hadd. He thereafter embraced Islaam. Can he testify?
quduri.b:
Yes, his Arsh is accepted.

NOTE:
The maximum Ta'zir is 39 lashes and the minimum is 3. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رضي الله عنه the maximum is 75.
The judge may also detain him in addition to the lashes.
The hardest lashing is for Ta'zir, then Hadd of Zina, then Hadd of drinking, then Hadd of slander.

quduri.f: What is Sariqah linguistically and in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: Literally it is to take wealth secretly. In Shari'ah it is a Mukallaf [person obligated by Islaamic Law] taking something worth 10 Dirham or more which have been demarcated according to possession or otherwise protected.

quduri.f: What punishment does the Shari'ah stipulate for the thief?
quduri.b: When a sane adult, slave or free, male or female, steals at least 10 Dirham or its value, whether in the form of currency or not, from the Hirz (demarcated for possession) in which there is no doubt, then it is Wajib to cut the thief's hand. Allaah says, "The male and female thief - cut off their hands because of what they have earned as a punishment from Allaah." [al-Maidah:38]

quduri.f: From where is the thief's hand cut?
quduri.b: The right hand is cleanly cut off at the wrist.

quduri.f: And if he steals a second time? [i.e. after a thief's right hand is cut off after stealing]
quduri.b: The left foot is cut. If he steals a third time then he will be indefinitely imprisoned until he repents.

quduri.f: A man stole at least 10 Dirham from a demarcated area. His left hand is lame or amputated, or his left leg has been cut off from before. Will the judge rule that his hand still be cut?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: How is theft established?
quduri.b: Through his confession once or the Arsh of two witnesses.

quduri.f: Must the one who was robbed be present at the cutting? [i.e. cutting of hand/foot]
quduri.b: The thief's hand cannot be cut unless the victim is present. He will be summoned to establish the theft. Thus if he had gifted the item to the thief, or sold it, or it is worth less than the prescribed amount i.e. 10 Dirham, the thief's hand may not be cut.

quduri.f: Besides having his hand cut, is the thief liable for the stolen amount?
quduri.b: If the item remains intact in his possession then he is liable to return it. If it has been destroyed, then he is not liable.

quduri.f: A group committed the left. Will all their hands be cut?
quduri.b: If the value of the stolen goods divided amongst them is worth at least 10 Dirham their hands will be cut. If it is worth less, then none of their hands will be cut.

quduri.f: What is deemed Hirz in this law?
quduri.b: There are two categories: Place such as buildings, houses and shops and personal. Thus if the thief stole from a demarcated place or the goods were guarded by a person then the thief's hand will be cut.

quduri.f: A group entered a Hirz with the intention of stealing. Some of them were appointed to do the actual stealing whilst the rest did not. Will all of their hands be cut?
quduri.b: Each member of the group will have his hand cut if the loot is divded and equals at least 10 Dirham per head.

quduri.f: A thief enters his hand in the money-box or in someone's pocket. Will his hand be cut?
quduri.b: If the loot is worth at least 10 Dirham, yes.

quduri.f: A man broke the wall of a house. He stole goods and passed it onto his accomplice outside. Will their hands be cut?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If he threw the goods outside and then picked it up, will his hand be cut?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man broke the wall of a house. He loaded loot onto his donkey and led it out. Will his hand be cut?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: If he pierced the wall and entered his hand inside whilst remaining outside, and took something, will his hand be cut?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if someone stole something from the Masjid?
quduri.b: His hand will be cut if the owner of the goods was by the goods.

quduri.f: In which circumstances will a thief's hand not be cut?
quduri.b:
It will not be cut in these scenarios:
For items which is regarded as free and permissible for all in the lands of Islaam e.g. wood, grass and reeds and fish which is still in the water nad prey which is still in the wild.
Items which swiftly detoriate, e.g. fresh fruit, milk, meat, watermelon, fruits on the tree, unharvested crops.
Mutribah [ilicit party] drinks.

Tunbur [eastern mandolin]

Tabl, Daff [eastern drums] and flutes.

Mushaf of the Quraan, even if be jewelled.

Crucifix, even if it be of gold and silver.
Chess.
Backgammon.
Kidnapping a free child, even if he has jewels on him.
Abducting an adult slave. However, the hand is cut for stealing a minor slave.
Registers, except for accounting registers.
Dogs and cheetahs.
The one who cheats does not have his or her hand cut.
Grave robber.
A looter.
Embezzler.
One who steals from the public treasury or booty.
Wealth in which one has a share.
Stealing from a parent, child or blood related Mahram.
One spouse stealing from the other.
If a slave steals from his owner, or owner's spouse.
If the owner steals from his Mukatab.
Stealing from public baths or a building in which the public is allowed access.
A guest who steals from his host.
If the thief claims that the stolen item is his property, even if he does not produce evidence.

quduri.f: You mentioned that there is no cutting off hands for stealing wood. Which wood did you refer to?
quduri.b: Worthless wood which is not demarcated for ownership, If wood which has worth, which is sold and demarcated, is stolen then the thief's hand will be cut, if the value reaches 10 Dirham e.g. Indian oak, bamboo, ebony and sandalwood. Hands are also cut for stolen woodwork such as utensils and doors.

quduri.f: A man stole an item and his hand was cut for it. He returned the item to the owner and then stole it again. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If the item remains in its condition as when he returned it, his hand will not be cut. If the condition has changed then his hand will be cut, e.g. he stole thread and his hand was cut. He returned it and it was then embroided. He then came and stole it a second time. He will again be cut.

quduri.f: What is the punishment of highway robbers?
quduri.b:
Allaah has explained it thus, "Verily the punishment for those who wage war against Allaah and His Rasul and strive to spread corruption is to be killed or crucified or to have the hands and feet cut from opposite sides or to be exiled from the land. That is a humiliation for them in the world. In the Aakhirat (Hereafter) is a great punishment. Except those who repent before you gain control over them. Then know that Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful". [al-Maidah:33-34]

Thus if a gang or an individual capable of obstructing goes out with the aim of highway robbery, and they are apprehended before having stolen anything or killed anyone, the ruler will detain them until they repent. If they had stolen wealth of a Muslim or Zimmi, to the extent that if divided amongst them it would be worth at least 10 Dirham per head, then the ruler will cut their hands and feet from opposite sides.

If they killed anyone without taking any wealth, they will be killed as per the Hadd. If the victim's family wish to pardon them, their pardon will not be considered. If they both killed and plundered, then the ruler may either kill them or crucify them.94

94 Whether with cutting their hands and feet first, or just killing/crucifying them. [al-'Inayah]

quduri.f: What is the method of cruficixion?
quduri.b: He will be crucified whilst living. His belly will be pierced with a spear until he dies. He will not be crucified for more than three days.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if amongst the gang was a child, madman, or blood relative of the victim?
quduri.b: The Hadd is lifted from the rest as well. The issue of the murder is taken to the victims' Awliya who may have them killed or pardoned.

quduri.f: One of the Highway Robbers murdered. Will the responsibility be applied to the entire gang?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Which drinks are forbidden to consume?
quduri.b:
There are four forbidden drinks:
Khamr [wine]: It is grape juice when it ferments and becomes intoxicating and emits foam.

'Asir [juice]95 when it is boiled unless less than two-thirds evaporates.

Naqi96 of dates when it ferments and intoxicates.

Naqi' of raising when it ferments and intoxicates.

95 i.e. a grape juice.

96 When dates/raisins is soaked in water in order to absorb its sweetness, the resultant water is called Naqi'

quduri.f: What do you say about boiled Nabiz of dates or raisins?
quduri.b: It reamins Halal if slightly boiled even if intoxication sets in it, when drunk and one's overwhelming thought is that it will not intoxicate, when drunk nor merely for entertainment or frivolity.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Khalitan?98
quduri.b:
Halal.

98 Mixing the date and raisin water and boiling it slightly and leaving it until it becomes fermented and potentially intoxicating.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Nabiz of honey, figs, wheat, barley and sorghum?
quduri.b:
They are Halal whether boiled or not99 when drunk without frivolity and entertainment.

99 According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they are Haram in large or small quantities because according to him that which intoxicates in large quantities in Haram in small quantities and is Najas also. The Fatwa is on this.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of grape juice if boiled until two-thirds evaporate?
quduri.b: It is Halal even if it is potentially intoxicating.

quduri.f: What is the status of wine if it becomes or is made into vinegar?
quduri.b: It is Halal to eat both cases.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of making it [i.e. wine] into vinegar?
quduri.b: Permissible.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of making Nabiz in Duba [bottle gourd], Hantam [green earthenware jar], Muzaffat [vessel coated with tar] and Naqir [hollowed palm]?
quduri.b: It was forbidden and then allowed. [In narration by Muslim.

quduri.f: What is Sayd?
quduri.b: It is the act of hunting and is applied to the hunted animal as well, i.e. a beast which refrains from humans, whether edible or not. Hunting wild beasts which are not in anyone's possession is permissible for non-Muhrims outside the Haram. Allaah says, "When you become Halal [you may] hunt."

quduri.f: How does a Muslim hunt?
quduri.b: Hunting is permissible by means of trained dogs, cheetahs, falcons and any other fanged or taloned trained beast or bird of prey. Allaah says, "Say: The pure things have been made permissible to you and that which you have trained of hunting beasts, you train them from what Allaah has taught you."

quduri.f: If the hunter sends out the trained dog or cheetah and it kills a beast, is it Halal?
quduri.b: If the animal is such an animal which is permissible to eat; the hunter recited the Name of Allaah when sending the trained animal; and the animal seized the prey and wounded it from which it died, then it is Halal to eat. Similarly if he sent a trained falcon or eagle and recited Allaah's Name, and the bird seized the animal and wounded it from which it died, then it is Halal.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated wounding and death? [i.e. when sending a trained animal or trained falcon/eagle]
quduri.b: The wound is necessary for the animal to be Halal. Through it Zakah Idtirari [forced slaughter] is established. It is to wound the animal in any part of its body. The stipulated of death means that if the dog or falcon seized and wounded the animal and then left it alive and the hunter reaches it then he must slaughter it. In such a situation Zakah Ikthiyari [voluntary slaughter] is stipulated. If he does not slaughter it and it dies, then it cannot be eaten.

quduri.f: You have stipulated that the animal be trained. What does its training entail?
quduri.b: The training of a dog and cheetah is that it is taught to seize an animal and not eat from it. When it is trained to do that and avoids eating thrice, it is deemed trained. The training of a falcon is that it returns when summoned. That is the difference in the ruling of a trained dog and trained falcon. If the dog eats from the prey, the meat may not be eaten. However, if the falcon eats from it, it may be eaten. The condition for the falcon's training is only that it obeys when summoned and not that it does not eat from the prey.

quduri.f: If the dog or cheetah strangles the animal and it dies before being slaughtered, can it be eaten?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: The hunter despatched his trained dog. Another dog joined it in killing. The second dog was either a non-trained dog, the Fire-worshipper's dog, or a dog upon which Allaah's Name had not been recited upon despatch. What is the status of the meat?
quduri.b: It is not Halal to eat.

quduri.f: You have mentioned hunting by birds and beasts of prey. Is there another method of hunting?
quduri.b: Yes, hunting by shooting arrows. If a Muslim shoots an arrow at an animal and mentions Allaah's Name at the time of shooting, the flesh of an animal the arrow strikes may be eaten if the arrow wounds it and kills it. If the hunter reaches the prey and it is still alive, he must slaughter it. If he does not, the animal is not Halal.

quduri.f: He shot an animal which then fell into water. The hunter then found it dead. Or it fell on a mountain or roof and then bounced down to the earth and died. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: It is Haram to eat.

quduri.f: Does the ruling change if it fell [i.e. the animal shot with an arrow] on the earth in the beginning and then died?
quduri.b: Yes, in that case it is Halal.

quduri.f: A man shot an animal. It bore the arrow and disappeared. The hunter then found it dead. Can he eat it?
quduri.b: If the hunter continuously pursued it until he found it dead, then it is Halal. If he paused in his chase and then found it dead then it cannot be eaten.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if when shooting an animal, an organ is cut off?
quduri.b: The animal can be eaten, not the cut off organ.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the animal got cut into two portions?
quduri.b: If cut into third portion and two-third portion, whereby the larger portion is the hind portion, then all may be eaten. In the major portion is the fore-portion then the major portion may be eaten and the rest abandonded.

quduri.f: The arrow was shot and its side struck the animal. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The animal may not be eaten unless the arrow had wounded it.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of hunting with Bunduqiyah [catapult]?
quduri.b: If the animal is killed with a catapult then it may not be eaten. If it is still alive after being struck and then is slaughtered, it may be eaten.

quduri.f: A man shot an animal. He neither wounded it nor demarcated it. A second man shot and killed it. Does it belong to the first man or the second? Can it be eaten?
quduri.b: It belongs to the second man and can be eaten.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if the first man wounded it [i.e. animal] and then the second shit and killed it? [i.e. does it belong to the first man or the second?]
quduri.b: The matter is reversed. It belongs to the first man and cannot be eaten. The second is liable to the first for the value of the prey less the value of the damage the first caused.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to hunt animals whose flesh cannot be eaten?
quduri.b: Yes, both animals which can be eaten and those which cannot be eaten, can be hunted.

quduri.f: Is there any category of person whose hunted animal cannot be eaten?
quduri.b:
The prey of the following cannot be eaten even if they mentioned Allaah's Name when shooting or sending the trained animal:
a Muhrim
a Fire-worshipper
an Apostate
an Idolater
The prey of a Muslim, Christian and Jew may be eaten if they recited Allaah's Name at the time of despatch.

quduri.f: What is slaughter? What are the conditions for the Zabihah [slaughtered animal] to be Halal for Muslims?
quduri.b: It is to cut the vessels which are between the throat and jaws of the animal. For the Zabihah to be Halal, the animal must also be such whose flesh can be eaten; the slaughterer must be a Muslim or Kitabi [Christian/Jew]; and the slaughterer must recite Allaah's Name at the time of slaughter. This is also called Zakah.

quduri.f: Which vessels must be slit at the time of slaughter?
quduri.b: There are four vessels to be slit - Hulqum [Windpipe], Mar-i [Foodpipe] and Wadajan [two Jugular veins]. When they are cut then it is Halal to eat or at least if most of them are cut according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى at least the food pipe, windpipe and one of the jugulars must be cut.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Zabihah if the slaughterer omitted Allaah's Name?
quduri.b: If he left it deliberately then the Zabihah is carrion and may not be eaten. If he left it forgetfully then it can be eaten.

quduri.f: Is it stipulated that slaughter can only be done with a knife?
quduri.b: No, if he slaughters with a bamboo, sharp stone, or anything which will make the blood flow the slaughter is valid. However, teeth and nails still attached to the body organ may not be used.

quduri.f: A sheep, cow or camel was slaughtered. A dead foetus was found in its belly. What is the status of the foetus?
quduri.b: It is carrion and may not be eaten, whether it has grown hair or not. If it emerges alive then it must be slaughtered and can be eaten. If it dies before slaughter it may not be eaten.

quduri.f: If a sheep is slaughtered from the nape, can it be eaten?
quduri.b: If the animal remains alive until the vessels are slaughtered then it can be eaten. The action however is Makruh. If it dies before the vessels are slaughtered then it is carrion and may not be eaten.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of slaughtering a wild animal which has been tamed and a domestic animal which has gone wild?
quduri.b: A tamed animal is slaughtered normally [Zakah]. A domestic animal gone wild is slaughtered by 'Aqr which is to wound it anywhere. This is called Zakah Idtirari [forced slaughter].

quduri.f: What is the status of the Zabihah of anyone besides Muslims and Kitabis?
quduri.b: The Zabihah of anyone besides these two categories cannot be eaten. The Zabihah of an Apostate, Fire-worshipper and Idolater may not be eaten, even if they recite Allaah's Name at the time of slaughter.

quduri.f: What is the status of the Muhrim's Zabihah?
quduri.b: If a Muhrim kills a prey, then it is carrion and may not be eaten. We had mentioned that in Kitabul Hajj. If he slaughters a cow, sheep, chicken or camel, they may be eaten.

quduri.f: Sundry Regulations
quduri.b:
It is Mustahabb for the slaughterer to sharpen his knife.
It is Makruh to let the knife reach the spine or to cut off the head. The Zabihah may nevertheless be eaten.
It is Mustahabb to make Nahr of the camel. If Nahr is made it is permissble but Makruh.
If an animal which cannot be eaten is slaughtered according to Shari'ah, its hide and flesh is clean, even if it cannot be eaten. The skin of humans and pigs will however not be regarded as pure because tanning and slaughter do not have effect upon them.

quduri.f: Are there animals which cannot be eaten?
quduri.b: Fanged beats, taloned birds, domestic donkeys, mules, hyenas, lizards and all forms of vermin may not be eaten.

quduri.f: What does Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى say about crow? [i.e. about eating it]
quduri.b: The omnivorous crow may be eaten, but not the spotted crow which eats carrion.

quduri.f: What does he say about horse meat?
quduri.b: It is Halal, but Makruh to eat lest the instruments of Jihad become scarce.

quduri.f: What is the status of rabbit meat?
quduri.b: There is no harm in eating it.

quduri.f: Can locust be eaten?
quduri.b: It is Halal. It need not be slaughtered.

quduri.f: What is the status of aquatic animals?
quduri.b: Aquatic animals are not Halal except for fish. That which died naturally and floats on the water is Makruh. There is no harm in eating the Jirrith fish and eel.

quduri.f: What is the status of Udhiyah in Islaam?
quduri.b:
It is Wajib upon every Muslim who is free, sane and well-off100 and resident. It is thus not Wajib upon the poor, slaves and travellers.

100 Well-off refers to those upon whom Sadaqatul Fitr is Wajib as has been discussed.

quduri.f: What must be slaughtered to fulfil this duty? [i.e. of Udhiyah]
quduri.b: A sheep for one person, or seven can share in a cow or camel on condition that none of the seven's share is less than a seventh. Also, all seven must intend for the sacrifice. If even one of them merely wishes for the meat, then none of the sevens Udhiyah is made.

quduri.f: When does the time of Udhiyah begin?
quduri.b: From true dawn on the Day of Nahr. Also, the people of cities may not slaughter before the 'Id Salah.

quduri.f: If one of them slaughtered before the Salah, what should he do? [i.e. before the 'Id Salah]
quduri.b: He must slaughter again.

quduri.f: Are the people of villagers where there is no 'Id Salah allowed to slaughter immediately after true dawn?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Can Udhiyah only be done on the Day of Nahr?
quduri.b: Udhiyah can be done on that day, and on the two days thereafter. When the sun sets on that second day, its time has terminated. The best time is the first day, then the next, then the last day.

quduri.f: Can one slaughter during one of the two nights which fall between these days?
quduri.b: Yes, although it is Makruh due to the possibility that required vessels will not be slit.

quduri.f: Which animals cannot be slaughtered for Udhiyah?
quduri.b: Udhiyah is not permissible with animals which are blind, one-eyed, lame to the extent that it cannot walk to the sacrifice place, nor emaciated animals, which have no marrow in their bones, nor animals with cut ears or tails, nor that which most of the ear or tail is cut.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if most of the tail and ear is intact?101
quduri.b:
It may be slaughtered in Udhiyah.

101 The animal which has lost most of its sight is also not allowed. It is recognised by how it approaches offered fodder. The detail of this is in al-Hidayah. Refer to it.

quduri.f:
Can the following animals be slaughtered for Udhiyah?
Hornless
Castrated
Mad
Mangry
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Which animals can be slaughtered for Udhiyah?
quduri.b: Camels, goats and cattle and nothing else. In all these the animals must have completed at least a year except for a sheep in which case a Jaza' [six month old] is allowed. Goats of any of its three categories are allowed.

quduri.f: Can the meat of the Udhiyah be eaten and stored?
quduri.b: One may eat of it and feed rich and poor and store it. It is Mustahabb that at least a third be given in charity.

quduri.f: What must be done with the hide of the Udhiyah?
quduri.b: It can be given in charity or made into utensils such as sieves, water-bags etc.

quduri.f: Must one slaughter oneself or may one appoint an agent to slaughter?
quduri.b: It is best to slaughter by oneself if one is capable. It is also permissible for someone else to slaughter with one's permission.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if someone ordered a Kitabi to slaughter on his behalf?
quduri.b: It is Makruh, but the Wajib is fulfilled.

quduri.f: Two men each bought a sheep for Udhiyah. There was a mix up and each slaughtered the other's sheep. Have their Udhiyah been fulfilled?
quduri.b: Yes, there is no liability against them.

quduri.f: What is Ayman?
quduri.b: The plural of yamin [oath]. It literally means wound or strength. Technically it refers to strengthening one of two angels to some statement by means of an oath. This oath is called yamin because the one who takes the oath strengthens by oath to do something or leave something.

quduri.f: What are the types of oaths?
quduri.b:
There are three:
Ghamus [immersion]

Mu'aqidah [in effect]

Laghw [futile].

Al-Ghamus is to take an oath about a passed event and deliberately lying about it, e.g. "By Allah I did not do it," whereas he did do it. This is a major sin. It is called Ghamus because it immerses its perpretrator in sin and leads to Jahannum (Hell). Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The major sins are to associate partners with Allaah, disobey partners, and al-yamin al-ghamus."102 

There is no Kaffarah upon the perpretrator. Instead, he should repent and seek forgiveness.

Al-Mun'aqidah is to take an oath about a future action, either to do it, or to refrain from it. If the oath is broken Kaffarah is compulsory.

Al-Laghw is to take an oath about a passed event, believing the oath to be true, but the reality was different. We hope that Allaah will not take the perpretrator to account for this kind of oath.

102 Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitabul Ayman, Bab al-Yamin al-Ghamus.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that Kaffarah is payable in the event of al-Ghamus. Is this only when it was doen deliberately or in all scenarios?
quduri.b: It is payable in all scenarios, whether deliberately, absentmindedly or by force.

quduri.f: A man did not intend to take an oath, but was forced to. He then broke the oath. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He must still pay Kaffarah.

quduri.f: What are the circumstances in which it will be deemed that a Muslim made an oath?
quduri.b: It is an oath if he swore by Allaah or any of His Names, such as "ar-Rahman" and "ar-Rahim", or by an attribute of His Being, such as, "The Honour/Majesty/Greatness of Allaah". However, "By the Knowledge of Allaah", is not deemed an oath.

quduri.f: What is the status of swearing, "By the anger/displeasure of Allaah"?
quduri.b:
That is not deemed an oath.103

103 That is customarily not deemed an oath.

quduri.f: Has he taken an oath if he says, "If I did so, then may the anger/displeasure of Allaah be upon me."?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: How does one make an oath by Allaah and His Attributes?
quduri.b: By applying huruful qasm [letters of oath] upon what one swears by.

quduri.f: What are these letters of oath?
quduri.b: They are three Waw [wAllaahi]; Ba [billahi] and Ta [tAllaahi]. The letters can also be hidden if applied in the meaning, e.g. "Allaahi I shall do so."

quduri.f: Is it an oath if he says, "Wa Haqqillahi - by Allaah's Right"?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Au Hanifa رحمه الله تعالى no.

quduri.f: Which words constitute oaths?
quduri.b: "Uqsimu/Aqsimu billaghi" I swear by Allaah, "Ash-hadu/Ushhidu billah" I testify by Allaah, "Wa 'Ahidillah/Mithaqihi" by the pact/covenant of Allaah.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if he swears by Allaah and adds InshaAllaah [if Allaah wills]?
quduri.b:
If he said it immediately after the oath then does contrary then he has not violated the "oath".104

104 Ibn Umar رضي الله عنه narrates thar Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "He who swears an oath then adds Inshaallah will not have contravention of oath against him." [at-Tirmizi and Abu Dawud]

quduri.f: Is it an oath if he says, "If I do so then I am a Jew/Christian/Fire-worshipper/Polytheist"?
quduri.b: Yes, it is an oath. Kaffarah is liable if he breaks it.

quduri.f: Is it an oath if he says, "If I do so then I am an adulterer/wine-drinker/usurer"?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of swearing by anything besides Allaah, such as Rasulullaah ﷺ, the Quraan or the Ka'bah?
quduri.b: Swearing by any besides Allaah does not constitute a valid oath.

quduri.f: A man swore to sin, e.g. "By Allaah, I shall not pray Salah/I shall never speak to my father/I shall commit murder." What should he do?
quduri.b:
Resolve to sin is a sin in itself. He who swears to sin is amongst the worst sinners. Nevertheless he may not commit the sin he swore to. He should break the oath and pay Kaffarah.106

106 'Awf bin Malik narrates from his father: I said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ, what if I used to go to my cousin and ask him and he refused me and did not maintain ties with me. He then had a need and came to ask of me. I had vowed not to give or maintain ties with him." He ordered me to give what is good and pay Kaffarah for my oath. [an-Nasai and Ibn Majah]

quduri.f: A man declares forbidden upon himself something which he is capable of. Does it become Haram?
quduri.b: No, if he uses it he should pay Kaffarah.

quduri.f: What is covered by the saying, "Everything Halal is Haram upon me."?
quduri.b: In custom it covers food and drink, unless he intended something else.

quduri.f: A Kafir made an oath he then embraces Islaam. Does he have to pay Kaffarah if he broke the oath before or after embracing Islaam?
quduri.b:
The Shari'ah does not recognise his oath. There is no Kaffarah.107

107 An oath entails honouring Allah, which is lacking in a state of Kufr. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: A man vows to do an act which he is incapable of, e.g. "I shall climb up to the sky/I shall turn this rock into gold." Does this count as an oath? If so, when will the oath be regarded as violated?
quduri.b: The oath is established and immediately deemed violated.

quduri.f: A man vowed to go to al-Busrah and did not go until he died. At what point is the vow deemed violated?
quduri.b: At the last moment of his life.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak. He then recited the Quraan in Salah. Is the oath broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to someone for a Hin/Zaman [while]. How long is that?
quduri.b: Six months.

quduri.f: And if he vowed for a Dahr [era] [i.e. he vowed not to speak to someone for that duration]
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is also six months. Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى did not decide, and said, "I do not know what Dahr is."

quduri.f: And if he vowed not to speak for "days"?
quduri.b: It is three days if said as a common known. If however he made it a proper noun, "the days", then it is 10 days according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and the days of a week according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: What do the three Imams say about an oath not to speak for "months"?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is 10 months. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is 12 months.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to another. He then spoke to him at a distance where he would be able to hear, but was sleeping. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The oath has been violated.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to someone without his permission. He granted permission. The one making the vow did not know about the permission but spoke to him anyway. Is the oath broken?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to "the owner of this shawl". The owner then sold it and the man spoke to him. Has his vow been broken?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to, "this youngster". He then spoke to him when he became an old man. Has his vow been broken?
quduri.b: [author of the book left his empty]

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to a certain person's wife. That person then divorced her and he spoke to her. Has his vow been broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to speak to a certains person's slave or enter his house. The person then sold the slave and the man spoke to him, or he sold the house and the man entered it. Has his vow been broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat ghada, 'asha or suhur. What is meant by these?
quduri.b: Ghada is a meal from dawn until noon, 'asha is a meal from noon until half the night, and suhur is a meal from half the night until dawn.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat bread. What does "bread" entail?
quduri.b:
The vow will cover whatever bread the people of his land are used to. Thus if a man of Iraq eats Qataif [small triangular] or rice-bread, then his vow is not broken.108

109 If he however eats it in Tabaristan where it is usual, then it is violated. [al-Hidayah]

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat of "this wheat." He then ate the bread made from it. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
Not according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى, who says that it is only violated if he eats the actual wheat.109

109 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is violated because eating the bread is the understood meaning of eating the wheat. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى wheat is also directly consumed.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat of "this flour." He then ate the bread made from it. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
Yes.110

110 Because flour is not edible in itself. Hence the vew is interpreted to refer to the bread.

quduri.f: Is the oath violated if he swallows the flour? [i.e. after he vowed not to eat this flour]
quduri.b: No. [i.e. it was understood to mean he'll eat it as bread, because flour isn't eaten raw]

quduri.f: He vowed not to eat cooked food and ate cooked lentils or legumes. What is the ruling?
quduri.b:
The oat is only violated by eating cooked meat, nothing else.111 

111 Because that which is cooked refers to meat.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat heads. He then ate a sparrow's head. Is the vow broken.
quduri.b: No, because "heads" refer to that which is generally baked in ovens and sold in cities.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat roast. He then ate roast meat/eggplant/carrot. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The oath is violated by eating the roast meat, not the roast eggplant and carrot.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat of "this wheat foetus." The foetus then was born and grew into a ram. He then ate the ram. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat of "this date-tree." He then ate of its branches or roots. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: The vow is interpreted according to custom to refer to the fruits. If he eats any other part of the tree then the vow is not broken, only if he eats the fruit.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat of "this unripe dates." He then ate the dates after they ripened. Or he vowed not to eat unripe dates and ate ripe dates. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not eat unripe dates. He then ate unripe dates starting to ripen. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى his vow is broken.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to eat "meat". He then ate fish. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
No.112

112 Although according to the juristic principle of Qiyas it is violated because the Quran calls fish "meat", fish flesh is not meat in the sense of that which which is made from blood because fish do not have blood.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to drink from the Tigris River. He then drank its water from a vessel. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is not broken unless he places his mouth in the river.113

113 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is violated with or without a vessel.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to drink from the water of the Tigris River. He then drank its waters from a vessel. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to enter a dar [house]. He entered a ruin. Is his house broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to enter "this dar [house]." It was destroyed and completely levelled. He then entered the land. Is the vow broken?114
quduri.b:
Yes.

114 Dar includes the land.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to enter "this bayt [house]." It was destroyed and completely levelled. He then entered the land. Is the vow broken?
quduri.b:
No.115 

115 Bayt necessitates a building where the night can be spent. Thus if the roof has collapsed and the walls remain, the vow will be violated as one can spend the night there.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to enter a house in which he is. He does not leave immediately, but reamins standing or sitting there for a while. Is the vow broken?
quduri.b: No, it is only broken if he enters after exiting.

quduri.f: A man vows not to enter a house. He enters the Ka'bah, a Masjid, church or synagogue. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: [The author left this empty]

quduri.f: A man vowed not to enter "this house." He then stood on its roof or enters its Dhiliz [foyer]. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: Yes, however if he stood in the doorway in a manner whereby the door is closed he is outside, then he has not broken the vow.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to live in "this house." He himself left it, but left his family and goods behind in it. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
Yes.117

117 By custom he is said to be inhabiting the house if his family and goods are there.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to buy, sell or hire. He appointed an agent to do these acts for him. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to sit on the earth. He then sat on a mat or blanket. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
No.118

118 Since he is not regarded as sitting directly on the earth. However, if the only barrier is his clothing, then that is insufficient and his vow is broken. [al-Jawharah]

quduri.f: A man vowed not to sit on a seat. He then sat on a seat covered with a blanket. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b:
Yes.119

119 Because he is deemed sitting on the seat.

quduri.f: If he places another seat on top of the seat and sits on it?
quduri.b: His oath is not broken if he specified that he will not sit on that particular seat at the bottom.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to sleep on a bed. He then slept on the bed covered with a bed sheet. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: Yes, if however he had placed another bed on top of the vowed bed and slept on the top bed then the vow is kept.

quduri.f: He vowed that his wife may not leave without his permission. He granted her permission once. She left and returned. She then left a second time without explicit permission. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: Yes, his vow is broken if his words were as above. However if he had vowed whilst speaking to her, "By Allaah, you may not leave unless I permit you to", then if he permits her even once and she goes and returns and leaves again, his vow is intact.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to ride a certain person's mount. He then rode on that person's slave's mount that had been permitted to trade. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man vowed not to ride an animal he was riding at that moment, or not to wear attire he was dressed in at that moment. Is his vow broken?
quduri.b: If he immediately dismounts/disrobes that attire then the vow is kept. If however he stays on the beast or keeps that clothing on then the vow is broken. His continuation of riding/wearing is deemed a new ride/dressing.

quduri.f: A man vows to go to someone "if he is able to." What is meant by this?
quduri.b: It means his capability according to his health and removal of all obstacles. It does not entail whether Allaah decrees his coming or not.

quduri.f: A man vows: "I shall certainly pay him the debt owing today." He then finds the creditor and pays him. The creditor discovers that some of the coins are alloyed and some are rejected and some are genuine. Is the vow fulfilled?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: If they are lead or Suttuqah [copper covered silver]? [i.e. a man vows to pay the debt today and pays in coins made of this material]
quduri.b: His vow is broken.

quduri.f: What is meant if he vows to pay his debt "shortly" or "after a long time"?
quduri.b: Less than a month is "shortly". More than a month is "a long time."

quduri.f: A man vowed not to take his debt in instalments. He then took part payment. Is the vow broken?
quduri.b: Not bu just taking part payment. If however he takes the whole amount in instalments then it is broken.

quduri.f: He made the above oath [i.e. he vowed not to take his debt in instalments] and then took the amount whereby it was weighed in two weighings. What is the ruling?
quduri.b:
If he does not engage in any other act between the weighings besides weighing, then the oath is intact. If he does something else in between then it is broken.

NOTE: A ruler summons a man and makes him vow to inform the ruler of whatever corruption enters the land. This oath is specific to his rule. If the ruler loses his post the man's oath is not broken by not informing him.

WARNING: 
If a man vows, "By Allaah I shall do that act", his vow is fulfilled if he does so once in his life. If he sets a condition of time or place then it must be done according to that condition or else he has violated the oath. If he vows not to ride someone's animals and he rides it his oath is broken, but not if he rides someone else's animal.
If he vows not to do something, "I shall not do that act", then he must avoid it for the rest of his life. If he does it even once then his oath is broken.

quduri.f: A man says, "There is a nazr on me/for Allaah" He does not mention what he has pledged. What is the ruling?
quduri.b:
Although the words are nazr the meaning is yamin [oath]. Kaffarah of yamin is payable.120

120 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Kaffarah of nazr is the Kaffarah of yamin." [Abu Dawud]

quduri.f: What is the ruling if someone made nazr and mentioned what he pledged?
quduri.b: If he did not mention a condition fulfilling the nazr, then he must fulfil whatever he pledged to do, e.g. "For Allaah I shall fast a month/perform Hajj/pray two Rak'at."

quduri.f: If he attaches a condition to the nazr what is the ruling, e.g. "If Allaah cures me/if my son comes then I shall fast/pray/perform Hajj/free a slave", etc.
quduri.b:
It is Wajib to fulfil in this case also because the words of the ayah are general, "And they fulfil their nazr."
It is narrated that Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى said, "If someone makes nazr, 'if I do so then I have to make Hajj or fast a year', kaffarah of yamin will suffice him."This is also the view of Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: What if a man made a nazr to disobey Allaah?
quduri.b: He may not perform the sin because of the nazr. Instead he should pay kaffarah as in violated oaths.

quduri.f: A man made nazr to give his wealth in charity. What does he have to give?
quduri.b: He has to give whatever wealth category in which Zakah is compulsory upon him.

quduri.f: A man vows to give in charity whatever he owns. What must he give?
quduri.b: He must give whatever he owns but may retain an amount needed to maintain himself and his dependants until he can earn more money. Once he has earned more he must give an amount equivalent to the amount he had retained.

quduri.f: What is the Kaffarah for breaking an oath?
quduri.b:
Allaah has explained it in the Quraan as follows, "Allaah will not punish you for unintentional oaths, but will punish you for deliberate oaths. Its Kaffarah is that you feed ten poor people of the average food you feed your family, or clothe them, or freeing a slave. He who does not find, should fast three days. That is the Kaffarah of when you make oaths [you do not fulfil]. Guard your oaths. Thus Allaah explains your signs that you may be grateful." [al-Maidah:89]

Thus one has a choice between feeding ten poor people of the average food one feeds one's family, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. If one is unable to do any of these, then one must fast three consecutive days.

quduri.f: If one wishes to feed, how should it be done?
quduri.b: Feed ten poor people lunch and supper so that they are satiated; or give each of them half Sa' of wheat or a full Sa' of barley or dates.

quduri.f: Is the Kaffarah fulfilled if he gave each the value of a half Sa' of wheat or a full Sa' of barley or dates?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: How would he clothe them? [i.e. as Kaffarah]
quduri.b:
Give each of the ten poor at least that which wherein Salah would be valid.121 

121 According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى a trouser will not be enough as the wearer is still considered uncovered.

quduri.f: Which slave will suffice as Kaffarah?
quduri.b: A healthy, intact slave must be freed as described in kaffarah of Zhihar.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if he is incapable of paying the any of the above three [i.e. feeding poor people, clothing them or freeing a slave as kaffarah], he must fast three consecutive days. The Quraan does not stipulate that it be consecutive. What is your proof for that?
quduri.b: According to the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud رحمه الله تعالى it is, "... fasting of three consecutive days..."

quduri.f: A man made an oath and wished to break it. He first paid the kaffarah and then broke the oath. Is he still liable?
quduri.b: Yes, he is liable to pay it a second time after breaking the oath.

quduri.f: What is da'wa literally and in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: Etymologically it is on the scale of fa'la. It means to attribute something to oneself. In Shari'ah it refers to attribution of something to oneself at the time of a dispute. In grammar it is used on the scale of ifti'al.

quduri.f: Who is the mudda'i [claimaint]?
quduri.b: The party which cannot be forced to continue the dispute is abandonded.

quduri.f: Who is the mudda'a 'alayhi [defendant]?
quduri.b: The party which can be forced to continue the dispute [at court].

quduri.f: If a man makes a claim against another, will the court accept his mere claim?
quduri.b: No, the mudda'i must mention something about the type and quantity of the goods. If it is a specific item that he claims, then the mudda'a 'alayhi must present it at court where the mudda'i will point at it and make his claim. If the object is not present then the mudda'i will mention its value. If it is land he claims, he will define its boundaries and mention that it is in the hands of the mudda'a 'alayhi and that he is claiming it. If it is a right which the mudda'a 'alayhi must fulfil then he will mention it and say, "I am claiming this from him."

quduri.f: What will the judge do once the claim is established?
quduri.b: The judge will then question the mudda'a 'alayhi. If he confesses, then the judge will rule according to the mudda'i's claim. If he denies the claim, the judge will ask the mudda'i to produce evidence. If he can present the evidence and witnesses he will receive the ruling in his favour. If he is unable to present evidence, and demands an oath-taking, the judge will first make him take an oath. If the mudda'a 'alayhi takes an oath to the contrary the judge will refuse the claim. If the mudda'a 'alayhi refuses to take the oath the judge will rule in the mudda'i's favour. It is appropriate for the judge to first say, "I shall present the oath-taking to you thrice. If you take it, well and good. If you refuse to, I shall rule against you according to what he claims." If he then refuses after the presentations, the judge will rule against him.

quduri.f: The judge demands that the mudda'i present his evidence. He replies, "I have evidence, but I want you to take an oath from the mudda'a 'alayhi about it." Can the judge accept his request?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he may not demand the oath when he has evidence.

quduri.f: The mudda'a 'alayhi refused to take the oath. Will the mudda'i have to take the oath again?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Are there any matters about which the denier will not take an oath about?
quduri.b: The denier will not take an oath on the following claims - marriage, retracting a divorce, Fayy, Ila, slavery, being Ummul Walad, lineage, Wala, Hudud, Li'an.

quduri.f: Two men claimed the same item which is in the hands of a third party. Each claims to be the owner and presents evidence to that effect. What will the judge do?
quduri.b: He will allocate it to both of them.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if two men both claim to be married to the same woman and produce evidence to that effect?
quduri.b: He will accept neither of their evidence and will seek the woman's verification.

quduri.f: If two men both claim that they had bought a specific slave from a third party, and they produce evidence, what will the judge do?
quduri.b: Each may accept half the slave in exchange for half the price, or leave it. If the judge had ruled accordingly and one of the two says, "I do not want half a slave. I want to rescind the sale." then the other may not take the entire slave. If both claimants define a date of sale, then the slave is for whichever claimed the earlier date. If neither can produce a date but the slave is already in the possession of one of them, then the possessor keeps the slave.

quduri.f: One man claims to have bought from a third party and another claims that that was a gift to him from the third party. Both have taken possession from the third party. Neither can produce a date of sale or evidence. Who keeps the goods?
quduri.b: The one claiming a sale.

quduri.f: A man claims that he bought an item from another. A woman claims instead that he had married her for that as dowry. Both produce evidence. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both claims are equal. None will be preferred over the other.

quduri.f: The one claims an item is collateral from Zayd and the other that it is a gift from Zayd. They take possession and both produce evidence. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The claim of collateral will be given preference.

quduri.f: If two parties who have not taken possession, make a general claim of ownership and produce different dates of ownership, whose claim will be accepted?
quduri.b: The one with the earlier date.

quduri.f: If both claim to have bought it from a third party and both produce different dates, whose claim will be accepted?
quduri.b: The one with the earlier date.

quduri.f: If both claim to have bought it from a third party and both produce the same date, whose claim will be accepted?
quduri.b:
Both's claims will be equally valid. Neither will be preferred over the other.122 

122 I.e. they will share it 50-50 [Sharhul Kanz]

quduri.f: One claimant does not have the item in his possession. The other claimaint does. The first produces a date of ownership and the second produces an earlier date. Whose claim will be preferred?
quduri.b: The one with the earlier date.

quduri.f: Two men both claim to own a beast and produce evidence that they owned it from its bith. The one has it in his possession and the other does not. Whose claim will be preferred?
quduri.b: The one who has it in his possession.

quduri.f: Two men both claim to own a cloth and produce evidence that they owned it from its time of embroiding. The one has it in his possession and the other does not. Whose claim will be preferred?
quduri.b: The one who has it in his possession is preferred in cloths which are only embroided once. Similarly any item whose cause of ownership occurs only once is treated the same in the above scenario.

quduri.f: The one who does not have possession produces evidence of general ownership. The one who has it in his possession produces evidence that he bought it from him. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The one who has it keeps it.

quduri.f: Two men each claim to have bought an item from each other and produce evidence to that effect. They have no dates. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The court will not decide between them. Both evidences will be rejected.

quduri.f: One claimant produces two witnesses and the other produces four. Will the first be preferred?
quduri.b: No, both are still equal.

quduri.f: A man claims Qisas [retaliation] but the mudda'a 'alayhi denies it. How will this case be decided?
quduri.b: The mudda'a 'alayhi will be made to take an oath. If he refuses and the retaliation is for something besides life, he will be retaliated against. If it is in a case of life, then he will be detained until he either confesses or takes the oath. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he must pay Arsh in both cases.

quduri.f: The mudda'i says, "I have evidence in the city which I shall present InshaAllaah." What should the judge do?
quduri.b: The judge will order the defendant to give a kafil for his life for three days. if he does so, well and good, or failing which he will order the mudda'i to follow him, unless he is a traveller. In that case he will follow him for the duration of the court's session.

quduri.f: A man claims an item from another. The mudda'a 'alayhi says, "This item a third party left as Wadi'ah/Rahn by me/I usurped it from a third party." What is the ruling?
quduri.b: If the mudda'a 'alayhi can produce evidence to that effect then the dispute between them will no longer be entertained.

quduri.f: If the mudda'a 'alayhi however says, "I bought it from a third party", does the claim of the mudda'i remain?
quduri.b:
Yes.123 

123 Because the mudda'a 'alayhi has in effect acknowledged that the claimaint has ownership in the item.

quduri.f: A man claims, "He stole that item from me", and produces evidence for that. The mudda'a 'alayhi says, "He left it as Wadi'ah by me", and produces evidence for that. Is the case dropped by the defendant's evidence?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: A man has an item in his possession and claims that a certain person left it as Wadi'ah in his care. Another man claims that he bought it from the same man. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The case between them is dropped if there is no evidence.

quduri.f: A house is in the possession of a man. A second man claims that the entire house is his. A third man claims that half the house is his. Both produce evidence. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the second man gets three-quarters and the third man gets a quarter. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the second gets two-third and the third gets a third.

quduri.f: If the house is instead in the hands of the two claimants, with with their claims as above? [i.e. one man claims that the entire house is his, and the other man claims that half the house is his, and both produce evidence]
quduri.b: Half will be ruled for the claimant of the entire house by way of a court order, and the other half will be said to be his without a court order.

quduri.f: Two men claim an animal. Both produce evidence that the animal was born in their possession. They also produce dates. In whose favour will the court rule?
quduri.b: The one whose date corresponds with the age of the animal. If that's indeterminate then it will be shared between them.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if one disputant is mounted on the beast and the other grabbing the bridle? [i.e. both claim the animal]
quduri.b: The rider's claim will be given preference.

quduri.f: Two men claim a beast of burden. The one has a load on the beast and the other only has his claim. Whose claim is preferred?
quduri.b: The owner of the load.

quduri.f: Two men claim a shirt. One is wearing it and the other is grabbing onto the sleeve. Whose claim will be preferred?
quduri.b: The one wearing it.

quduri.f: How are disputes regarding price and commodity between buyers and sellers settled?
quduri.b:
There are various scenarios, with different rulings:
When the seller claims a higher price than the buyer admits to, or the buyer claims a greater quantity of the commodity that the seller admits to; whichever produces evidence will have the ruling in his favour.
If both produce evidence, then the ruling will be according to the greater amount.
If neither can produce evidence then the buyer will be told, "Either accept the price the seller claims or the sale is cancelled." The seller will be told,  "Either accept the quantity the buyer claims or the sale is cancelled." If neither wishes to concede, then each will have to take an oath concerning the other's claim. The buyer will begin taking the oath. Once both have taken their oaths, the court will rescind the sale. If one of them refuses to take the oath, the court will rule in favour of the other's claim.
If the dispute is about the time given for payment, or Shartul Khiyar then there is no mutual oath taking. The word of the one who denies the time given or the option of rescinding will be accepted, but he must take an oath.
If the commodity perishes and they dispute the price, then they will not take oaths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى. The price which the buyer claims will be accepted. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى both will take oaths and the sale will be cancelled based on the market value of the commodity.
If one of two slaves perished, and they dispute the price, they will not take oaths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى, unless the seller agrees to give up his claim on the perished slave. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى, both will take oaths. The sale with reference to the surviving sale is cancelled and the perished slave is valued at market price.

quduri.f: How are disputes between the spouses regarding dowry settled?
quduri.b:
There are different scenarios as follows:
The husband claims that the dowry is 1,000 and the wife claims that it is 2,000. The claim of whoever can produce evidence will be accepted.
If both produce evidence, then the wife's word will be taken.
If neither has evidence, then they will take oaths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. The marriage will not be cancelled. The ruling will be based on Mahr al-Mithl. If that is equal or less than the amount the husband stated, then the ruling will be according to his claim. If it is equal or more than what she said, then the ruling will be according to her claim. If Mahr al-Mithl is more than her amount and less than her amount then the ruling will be Mahr al-Mithl.

quduri.f: The couple disagree on household commodities. How will the dispute be settled?
quduri.b:
What is appropriate for men124 is for the husband and what is appropriate for women125 is for the wife. What is appropriate for both is for the man. This is if they dispute and both are still living. If one has died and the dispute is with the heirs, then what is appropriate for men and women is for the surviving one of the two. This is all according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the woman is given that which a woman like her prepares with, and the remainder goes to the husband under oath.

124 Such as turbans, horses, bows and weapons. 
125 Such as silken clothing.

quduri.f: How are disputes between the claims of the hirer and the hired resolved?
quduri.b:
There are several scenarios here as well:
If they dispute about the fee before the fulfilment of what was agreed upon, then both will take oaths and cancel the agreement.
If they disagree after the fulfilment then they will not take mutual oaths. The hirer's word will be taken under oath.
If they disagree after partial fulfilment, then both will take oaths and the remainder of the contract is cancelled. The past fulfilment will be according to the word of the hirer under oath.

quduri.f: The owner and the Mukatab dispute the amount payable for the Kitabah. Whose word is accepted?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى they will not both be put to oath. The Mukatab's word will be accepted under oath. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they will both be put to oath and the Kitabah cancelled.

quduri.f: A man sold a slave-girl. She gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession. The seller claims the child as his own. Will his claim be accepted?
quduri.b: If she gave birth within six months of her sale, the child is the seller's and she becomes his Ummul Walad. The sale is rescinded.

quduri.f: Whose child is it if the buyer also claims the child at the same time or after the seller if the child was born within six months of the sale? [i.e. a man sold a slave-girl and she gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession]
quduri.b: It is still the seller's.

quduri.f: And if the child was born after six months of the day of her sale? [i.e. a man sold a slave-girl and she gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession, and both the seller and buyer claim the child as their own]
quduri.b: If it was born after six months and less than two years from the date of sale, the seller's claim will not be accepted unless the buyer verifies it.

quduri.f: The child was born less than six months and died. The seller still claims its lineage after death. Will his claim be accepted? [i.e. a man sold a slave-girl whom give birth whilst in the buyer's possession and the seller claims the child as his own]
quduri.b: Neither the child's lineage nor the mother being his Ummul Walad will be accepted.

quduri.f: The slave-girl gave birth in less than six months and dies. The seller claims the child. [i.e. he sold her and she gave birth whilst in the buyer's possession]. Is the lineage recognised?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the seller will take the child and return the full price. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he will only return the proportion of the child.

quduri.f: A slave-girl gave birth to twins. Her owner claims only one of them. Is the lineage of the other negated?
quduri.b: No, the lineage of both is attributed to him.

quduri.f: How is the mudda'a 'alayhi put to oath?
quduri.b:
There are several details:
A Muslim may not be put to oath except in the name of Allaah. The oath may be emphasised with His Attributes. An oath may not be made severe by demanding a specific time or place.
A Jew will take an oath in the name of "God who revealed the Torah to Moses عليه السلام."
A Christian will take an oath in the name of "God who revealed the Gospel to Jesus عليه السلام."
A Fire-worshipper will take an oath in the name of "God who created fire."
Oaths will not be taken in their houses of worship.

quduri.f: Scenarios of oath taking
quduri.b:
Someone claims to have bought that man's slave for 1000. The seller disputed him and they were put to oath. He will say, "By Allaah, there is no established sale with you in this slave", and not "You did not sell."
A man accused of usurpation will say, "By Allaah I am not obligated to return this item, not to return its price." He will not say, "By Allaah I did not usurp it."
Concerning marriage the oath will be, "By Allaah, there is no established marriage between us at present."
The oath accepted in divorce is, "By Allaah, she has never been irrevocably divorced from me at any time." He will not say, "By Allaah, I did not divorce her."

quduri.f: What is the status of Arsh in Shari'ah?
quduri.b:
It is Fard for the witnesses to testify, in order that rights are obtained and not lost. They have no right to hide their Arsh when the owner of the right seeks it. Allaah says, "The witnesses should not refuse when called to testify." He also says, "Do not hide Arsh. He who hides it has indeed a sinful heart." This is with regards to rights.

Regarding Hudud, the witness may choose between exposing and hiding his Arsh. Hiding is preferred in matters regarding theft of wealth. In that case he should say, "He took the wealth", and not "He stole the wealth."

quduri.f: Are there degrees of Arsh?
quduri.b:
Yes:
Arsh of Zina requires four male witnesses. The Arsh of females will not be accepted.
Qisas and the remaining Hudud require two males. The Arsh of females will not be accepted.
Other rights require two male, or a male and two female witnesses, whether in a case of wealth or not e.g. marriage, divorce, agency and bequests.
The Arsh of one female is accepted in matters men may not investigate e.g. birth, virginity and defects in women.

quduri.f: Are there conditions for the acceptance of Arsh?
quduri.b: Yes, in all these the witness must be 'adil [just] and must use the words, "I testify." If he says, "I know/I am certain", then the Arsh is not accepted.

quduri.f: Will apparent 'adalah of the witness be accepted or must his public and private life be investigated?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى a Muslim is accepted as 'adil on face-value except in matters of Hudud and Qisas. In these cases he must be investigated just as the allegations of the disputants are investigated. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى a public and secret investigation must be held.

quduri.f: Are there people who's Arsh is not accepted?
quduri.b:
Yes, the Arsh of the following is not accepted:
A blind person.
Slave.
One lashed for slander, even if he has repented.
One may not testify for one's father or grandfather, or son or grandson.
A spouse may not testify for the other.
An owner may not testify for his freed-slave or Mukatab.
A partner may not testify in that which he shares with the partner.
Transsexual.
Professional mourner.
Songstress.
An addict who drinks besides wine.
One who plays with birds.
One who sings to people.
One involved in major sins, particularly those associated with a Hadd.
One who enters the bath without a lower garment.
A consumer of usury.
One who gambles with backgammon and chess.
One who perpretrates demeaning acts such as urinating in the road and eating while walking.
He who vilifies the pious predecessors.
A Kafir from the lands of the Kuffar may not testify against a Kafir living under Islaam.
Someone who has enmity against another for wordly reasons may not testify against him.

quduri.f: Whose Arsh is accepted?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
A man may testify for his brother and paternal uncle.
The Arsh of deviant sects is accepted126 except for the Khattabiyah.127 
A Zimmi may testify against a Zimmi.128 
A sinner whose good outweighs his evil, as long as he avoids major sins.
One with a cut penis, one castrated and one born out of wedlock may testify.
Hermaphrodite.
A Zimmi may testify against a Mustamin Harbi [Kafir who has obtained safety to enter the lands of Islaam] just as a Muslim may testify against both of them.
NOTE:

Arsh which accords with the claim is accepted. If they conflict it is rejected.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى regard is given if the testimonies of the two witnesses agree in word and meaning.129 
126 As long as their deviance is not such that they have become Kafir [az-Zayla'i in Sharhul Kanz]

127 Rafidi followers of Abul Khattab Muhammad bin Wahb al-Adja'. This man of al-Kufah claimed that 'Ali رضي الله عنه is the greatets god and Ja'far as-Sadiq رضي الله عنه the lesser god. Governor 'Isa bin Musa executed him by crucifixion.

128 Even if their religions differ i.e. amongst Christians, Jews and Magians who pay Jizyah are protected by the Islamic State.
