129 According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى only the meaning is paid attention to.

quduri.f: The witnesses give contradictory Arsh e.g. one testifies "1000" and the other "2000". How is this resolved?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى both testimonies are rejected. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى, "1000" is accepted.

quduri.f: One witness testified "1000", and the other "1500". The mudda'i claims 1500. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both testimonies will be accepted as 1000.

quduri.f: Both witnesses testified to 1000, but one added, "He did however pay 500 of that." What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both testimonies will be taken as 1000. The payment of 500 will be ignored unless the other also testifies to it. It is appropriate that if the witness does know that, that he does not testify to the 1000 until the mudda'i admits to receiving the 500.

quduri.f: Two witnesses testified that Zayd was killed on the Day of Nahr at Makkah. Another two testified that he was killed on the Day of Nahr at al-Kufah. They all testify at the same time. What will the court decide?
quduri.b: Both testimonies will be rejected.

quduri.f: The first pair testified [i.e. Two witnesses testified that Zayd was killed on the Day of Nahr at Makkah. Another two testified that he was killed on the Day of Nahr at al-Kufah] and the judge ruled accordingly. The next pair then arrives. Will the ruling be rescinded?
quduri.b: No, the second Arsh will not be accepted after a decision has been given on the first Arsh.

quduri.f: Can a witness testify to what he did not himself see?
quduri.b:
It is not permissible. However, if a reliable person has informed him of the following then he may convey it:
lineage,
death,
marriage,
intercourse,
and appointment of a judge.

quduri.f: Does Shari'ah recognise Arsh upon Arsh? What does it entail?
quduri.b:
A witness can give two forms of Arsh. The first is that by which a ruling can be established in itself. These include sale, hire, marriage, confession, usurpation, murder and a decision of a judge. If he hears or sees these matters he may testify to it if he does not make a secondary witness to it. He will say, "I testify that he sold..." and will not say, "I have been made witness ..."

The second is it does not establish a ruling in itself. This is Arsh upon Arsh. If he merely hears a witness testifying to something he cannot testify to it unless the primary witness makes him a secondary witness to the Arsh. Similarly if someone hears a primary witness making a secondary witness to a Arsh, the hearer cannot testify. Arsh upon Arsh is permissible in every right which does not become forfeit due to doubt. It is not accepted in Hudud and Qisas. The Arsh of two witnesses form two witnesses is acceptable, but not the Arsh of one from one.

quduri.f: Describe the procedure of making a secondary witness.
quduri.b: The primary witness will say to the secondary witness, for example, "Be witness to my Arsh that I testify that so-and-so confessed to me about that, and made me a witness against him." It is permissible if he omits, "He made me a witness against himself."

quduri.f: How will the secondary witness then testify? [i.e. in the procedure of making a secondary witness: The primary witness will say to the secondary witness, for example, "Be witness to my Arsh that I testify that so-and-so confessed to me about that, and made me a witness against him."]
quduri.b: He will say, "I testify that so-and-so confessed to him concerning ... and he then said to me, 'Testify according to my Arsh that ...' hence I testify to that."

quduri.f: Are there further conditions for the acceptance of secondary Arsh?
quduri.b: The secondary witness may only testify if the primary witness died; or has gone away the distance of three days' journey or more; or is too ill to attend the court.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of the secondary witnesses regarding the primary witnesses as 'adil?
quduri.b: If they regard them so it is permissible. If they remain silent about their 'adalah then it is also permissible but the judge will examine their state.

quduri.f: When the secondary witnesses intended to testify, the primary witnesses refuted their Arsh. Will the Arsh of the secondary witnesses still be accepted?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What does the judge do when witnesses retract their Arsh?
quduri.b:
There are details to this which you should pay attention to:
If the witnesses retract their Arsh before the court rules on it, then their Arsh is forfeit and they have no liability.
If the judge had ruled that the mudda'a 'alayhi had to pay money based on their Arsh, and they thereafter retract, the decision is cancelled and they are liable to compensate the mudda'a 'alayhi for his loss.
If one of the two retracts then he is liable for half.
Three witnesses testified to a money case. One witness retracts. he does not owe anything. If however two retract, then the two must jointly compensate him for half the amount.
A man and two women testified. If a woman retracts then she is liable for a quarter of the amount. If both women retract then they are liable for half.
A man and ten women testified. If eight women retract then there is no liability upon them. If a ninth woman retracts, then the retracting women owe a quarter. If the man and women all retract then the man owes a sixth and the women five-sixths according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he owes half the women half.
Two witnesses testified that a woman married with Mahrul Mithl or more. If they retract then they are not liable. If they testified to less than Mahrul Mithl and then retracted, they are not liable for the deficiency.
Two witnesses testified that a man married with Mahrul Mithl or less. If they retract then they are not liable. If they testified to more than Mahrul Mithl and then retracted, they are liable for the excess.
If they testify that a commodity was sold at market value or more and then they retract, they are not liable. If they testified to less than market value they are liable for the loss.
They testified that a man divorced his wife before intercourse. If they retract they are liable for half the dowry. If they retracted after intercourse there is no liability.
They testified that a man freed his slave. If they retract they are liable for the value of the slave.
They testified to Qisas. The mudda'a alayhi was executed. They then retracted. They are liable for Diyah not Qisas. 
When secondary witnesses retract they are liable.
If the primary witnesses retract and say, "We did not authorise any secondary witnesses", then they are not liable. If they admit "We authorised them to testify but committed an error", then they are liable.
If the secondary witnesses claim that the primary witnesses lied or are mistaken, these claims will be ignored.
Four witnesses testified to Zina. Two witnesses testified that the perpretrator has Ihsan i.e. he will be stoned and not lashed. If these two witnesses retract after the stoning they are not liable.
When those who have declared the witnesses reliable retract they are liable.
Two witnesses testify that an oath was taken. Another two testify that there was a condition as well. They then retract. Liability is only on the witnesses to the oath.

quduri.f: Sundry regulations
quduri.b:
The judge will not entertain claims of the defendant that the witnesses be rejected [after having made his own investigations] nor negative Arsh [unless it is relevant to the case e.g. he has no other heir besides this man] and he will not rule according to that.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى a false witness will be exposed in the market and not physically punished. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he will be beaten and imprisoned.
The witness is not allowed to read one's letter and testify except when he knows the testimony.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to join the judicial system?
quduri.b:
There is no harm in it if one can fulfil one's duty with justice. It is Makruh for one who fears that he will be weak in fulfilling the legal duties or that he will not be able to be impartial. It is not appropriate to desire or seek a judicial post. A judicial appointment is not valid if the appointee does not fulfil the prerequisites of Arsh130 and that he be capable of Ijtihad131.

130 Sanity, adulthood, freedom, Islam and justice.
131 This condition is one of preference [not obligatory] - al-Hidayah

quduri.f: When a judge is appointed, what does a judge do with those prisoners whom the previous judge had detained?
quduri.b: The register of the previous judge is given to him. He will examine the cases of the prisoners. Those who confess will continue their sentences. As for those who plead innocent the word of the previous judge will not be accepted without evidence. Even if there is no evidence, the new judge will not hasten to release them. He will make an announcement and examine the case just as he will, regarding Wadi'ah and Awqaf. He will then act according to the evidence at hand or he who has them in his possession admits to them. The mere word of the previous judge will not be accepted unless the one who holds them admits that the previous judge had handed them to him, in which case his word will be accepted.

quduri.f: Mention some of the characteristics the judge will adopt during his tenure.
quduri.b: He will sit openly for passing judgement in the Masjid. He may not accept gifts except from Mahram blood relatives or from such people with whom he used to have a relationship of exchanging gifts before being appointed. He may not accept invitations, except those which are general. He must attend funerals and visit the sick. He may not host one party of disputants and exclude the other. When both parties attend court, he will treat them equally in seating and in giving them attention. He will not speak secretly to one of them. He will not pass hints to him. He will not lead him on in presenting his proofs.

quduri.f: Will the judge detain the mudda'a 'alayhi if found guilty?
quduri.b: If the mudda'i demands his right the judge should not hasten to detain the mudda'a 'alayhi. He should order him to pay what he owes. If he refuses the judge will detain him for any liability which was incurred by acquiring wealth in his hands such as the price of goods or loans; as well as for any debt incurred by transaction, such as deferred dowry and Kafalah. He may not be detained for other liabilities if he says he is poor.

quduri.f: Will his mere claim of being poor be accepted or will his condition be investigated?
quduri.b: If his creditor can prove that he has wealth he will be detained for two to three months. Thereafter he will again be questioned. If no wealth is revealed he will be released. His creditors will not be prevented from approaching him.

quduri.f: Can a man be imprisoned for not paying his wife's maintenance?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Can a father be imprisoned for the debts of his son?
quduri.b: Only if he refused to pay the Wajib maintenance of his child.

quduri.f: The ruler appointed a female as a judge of a district. Is the appointment valid?
quduri.b: Yes, except in matters of Hudud and Qisas.

quduri.f: Can sentence be passed on someone who is absent?
quduri.b: No, unless a representative is present.

quduri.f: If the decision of one judge is taken to another, can he implement the decision?
quduri.b: He may, unless the decision conflicts with the Quraan, Sunnah or Consesus of the 'Ulama or is without proof.

quduri.f: Can the judge appoint a deputy in his absence?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the status of a judge's ruling concerning his parents, children and wives?
quduri.b: It is void.

quduri.f: Two men have a dispute. They appoint a third party as arbitrator between them. They accept his decision. Is this permissible?
quduri.b:
It is permissible if the arbitrator has the attributes of decisionmaking. Thus the following may not arbitrate:
a Kafir,
slave,
Zimmi,
one lashed for slander,
an open sinner,
and a minor.

quduri.f: They appointed an aribitrator. One or both of them wish to withdraw from the arbitration. Is this permissible?
quduri.b: They can withdraw before a decision has been passed. Once a decision is passed it is binding.

quduri.f: The arbitration decision was referred to the judge. Can he implement it?
quduri.b: If in accord with his views, or else he can annul it.

quduri.f: Can the arbitrator examine evidence and pronounce a decision if a party refuses to take an oath?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Two men appointed an arbitrator regarding an accidental murder. The arbitrator ruled that the 'Aqilah must pay Diyah. Will his decision be implemented.
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: If a judge writes to another, will the letter be accepted?
quduri.b: It is accepted in matters of rights if it was witnessed to in his presence. It is not accepted in Hudud and Qisas. If the witnesses testify against the party which is present, he may rule accordingly and write his decision. If they testified and the party is not present, he may not give a ruling but will write the Arsh for the addressed judge to make a ruling. It is Wajib for him to first read out the letter to the witnesses that they may know its contents. He will then seal it and hand it to the witnesses.

quduri.f: Will the addressed judge [i.e. if a judge writes to another] accept the letter when he receives it without further evidence?
quduri.b:
He may not accept it without the Arsh of two men or a man and two women, nor may he accept it without the disputant being present. When the witnesses hand the letter to him, he must examine the seal.
The witnesses must testify, "It is the letter of Judge so-and-so, he handed it to us during high court session, he read it to us and sealed it." The addressed judge will then open it and read it to the disputant. He will implement its contents.

quduri.f: A house, property etc. is jointly owned. The partners require that it be partitioned. Who will do it?
quduri.b: It is appropriate for the ruler to appoint a Qasim [partitioner]. He will receive a state salary and will perform to partitioning service to the public for free.

quduri.f: How will he operate [i.e. a Qasim (partitioner)] if the public treasury cannot support him?
quduri.b: He will render his service for fee payable by the partners. The Qasim must be just, trustworthy and knowledgeable in partitioning. The judge will not force a single Qasim upon the people, nor will he allow those in that profession to collaborate in partnership.

quduri.f: Do the partners pay equal fees? [i.e. the partners that require partition from a Qasim (partitioner)]
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the fee is divided equally amongst each partner. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the fee is split according to each one's share.

quduri.f: The partners request that the judge arrange for their house or property to be partitioned. They claim that they jointly inherited it. Will the judge order the partition just on their word or must he demand evidence?
quduri.b:
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he will not divide it until they produce evidence of the death and the amount of heirs.

According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى their word is accepted. This is in regards land. As regards other joint wealth, all agree that their word that they inherited it will be accepted.

quduri.f: Besides inheritance, what if they claim that they bought the land or claim ownership without specifying how they came to possess it?
quduri.b: it will be divided according to their claim.

quduri.f: Two heirs present evidence to the judge concerning the death and amount of heirs. They have the house in their hands and request a partition. There is however another absent heir. Will the judge agree to the partition based on the request of the present heirs?
quduri.b: Yes, he will appoint an agent to take possession of the share of the absent heir. This is if it is a jointly inherited house. If they bought it, it may not be partitioned in the absence of any partner, even if the others present proof of purchase.

quduri.f: A group inherits property. One of them is absent. He has the entire or part of the property in his possession. Those present seek partition. Will it be divided?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Only one partner comes and seeks partition. Will the judge comply?
quduri.b: If the shared substance is such that each partner will benefit from his share, then partition can occur at the request of one partner. If however one will benefit and the other be harmed due to the minimal nature of his share, partition can occur at the request of the major holder nad not at the request of the other.

quduri.f: If both partners will be harmed by partition?
quduri.b: It will only be divided if both partners agree to it.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of dividing commodities?
quduri.b: It is a single kind of good it can be divided at the request of any partner. If a mixture of several kinds then it cannot be divided except through mutual consent.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of dividing slaves and jewels?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى they may not be divided. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى jewels can be divided, not slaves.

quduri.f: Can baths and mills be divided?
quduri.b: Only if there is mutual consent.

quduri.f: Several houses are jointly owned in the same city, how will they be divided?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى each house will be separately divided. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammedd رحمه الله تعالى if it be more convenient for them, each may take his share in whole houses.

quduri.f: How will partition be done if they share a house and land, or house and shop?
quduri.b: Each will be separately divided.

quduri.f: How does partition take place?
quduri.b: It is appropriate for the Qasim to draw what he is going to divide. He should settle their shares and measure it. He will arrange the buildings in such a way that each partner has his own access to the road and water and that each share thus is independent of the other. The shares will then be allotted by means of lots. Monetary compensation will not be part of the partition unless the partners mutually agree.

quduri.f: After the partition, the one partner still had a waterway or pathway in the property of the other. The judge had not stipulated the right to use them. How will this be resolved?
quduri.b: If possible, move the path from his share, because he cannot use the path or flow water in the land of the other. If this is not possible then the partition is annulled due to the mixture.

quduri.f: How is partition done of a shared bottom floor, or a shared top floor, or bottom floor with a shared top floor?
quduri.b: Each is separetly divided. Division is baded on price, nothing else.

quduri.f: The one partner claims he did not receive his due share. The other partners claim that he did. Two Qasims testify that he did. Will their Arsh be accepted?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A partner claims that there has been a mistake, something of his is in the hands of another partners. However, he had previously testified that he had received his full share.
quduri.b: His claim will not be accepted unless he produces proof.

quduri.f: If he says, "I received my full share, then one of the partners took part of it." The other denies it. What will be done?
quduri.b: His opponent's word will be accepted under oath.

quduri.f: One partner says, "I was to receive until that spot, but my partner did not hand it over to me." He had not previously testified that he had received his share in full. The partner belies him. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: Both will take oaths and the partition will be anulled.

quduri.f: After partition a specific part of one of their shares is rightfully claimed by a third party.
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the partner who loses will claim his proportionate loss from the other partner's share. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى the partition is cancelled.

quduri.f: Under what circumstances is coercion established?
quduri.b: It is only established from a source capable of fulfilling threats, be it the legal ruler or a criminal.

quduri.f: A man was forced to sell his goods or to buy goods; or to confess that he owes someone 1000 Dirham; or to rent his house. He was threatened with death, beating or detention. He therefore agreed. The force was then removed. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: He may sanction the sale or he may cancel it and take back his goods. This is if he took the price under compulsion. If however he had freely given the goods or taken the price, then his action has sanctioned the sale.

quduri.f: He was forced to sell. [i.e. a man was forced to sell his goods because he was threatened with death, beating or detention] He took the price under duress. What is his duty?
quduri.b:
He must return the price if it is still intact in his possession.132 

132 If it has been destroyed then he is not liable. He had not taken the price as owner, but as trustee. One is not liable for trust if destroyed without neglect. [al-Kifayah]

quduri.f: The seller sold under duress. The buyer was not forced and the goods perished in his possession. Is he liable?
quduri.b: Yes, he must pay the market price of the goods to the seller.

quduri.f: Can the coerced hold the [third party] coercer liable?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man was threatened with jail, beating or chains if he does not eat carrion or drink wine. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: The carrion and wine are not Halal. If he is however threatened with loss of life or limb, then only may he comply with what he has been forced to.

quduri.f: Does he [i.e. a man who was threatened with jail, beating or chains if he does not eat carrion or drink wine] not have the option of persevering and on what he has been threatened with and undergo death or loss or limb?
quduri.b: No, and if the threat is actually implemented because he refused to eat, then he has committed a sin.

quduri.f: A man is threatened with chains, jail or beating unless he denies Allaah or vilifies Rasulullaah ﷺ. Is he considered forced?
quduri.b: No, only when threatened with death or loss of limb.

quduri.f: If he then fears for loss or life or limb [i.e. a man is threatened unless he denies Allaah or vilifies Rasulullaah ﷺ], can he then express disbelieve?
quduri.b: Yes, he may express with his tongue that which contradicts his heart. If he does so, but his heart has real Iman, then there is no sin against him. Allaah says that in Surah an-Nahl. However, he should attempt to use Tawriyah - words which have a double meaning, including the non-Kufr meaning.

quduri.f: Is he a sinner if he persevers and refuses to utter the words of Kufr until he is slain? [i.e. he is pressed to deny Allaah or vilify Rasulullaah ﷺ]
quduri.b: No, he will be rewarded.

quduri.f: Can he comply if forced by threat of loss of life or limb to destroy the possessions of a Muslim?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Can the owner of the destroyed goods hold the one who forced him liable? [i.e. someone is forced by threat of loss of life or limb to destroy the possessions of a Muslim]
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A man is threatened with death unless he kills another Muslim. Can he comply?
quduri.b: No. He must resist even if killed.

quduri.f: What is the status of the induced person who kills a Muslim? [i.e. a man is threatened with death unless he kills another Muslim]
quduri.b: He is a sinner.

quduri.f: If the killing is 'amad, upon who will retaliation be inflicted? [i.e. a man was threated with death unless he killed another Muslim]
quduri.b: The one who forced him to commit the murder.

quduri.f: A man divorced his wife or freed his slave under duress. Is the divorce and manumission valid?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: What then are his options for reimbursement of the Dowry or value of his slave? [i.e. a man divorced his wife or freed his slave under duress]
quduri.b: He will claim the value of the slave from the one who forced him, or half the dowry if he had not had sex with his wife. If they had had sex then there is no liability upon the inducer.

quduri.f: Will the Hadd be inflicted if a man was forced to commit Zina?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the Hadd will be inflicted unless it was the ruler who forced him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى the Hadd will not be inflicted.

quduri.f: A man was forced to leave Islaam and utter words of disbelief. Is his wife separated from him?
quduri.b: No, unless he apostatised in his heart as well.

quduri.f: What is Siyar?
quduri.b: It is the plural of Sirah, which literally means "way of affairs." In the terminology of the Jurists it refers to the military expeditions of Rasulullaah ﷺ. In Kitabus Siyar they mentioned the regulations of Jihad and related matters, such as distribution of booty, imposition of Jizyah, treatment of prisoners etc.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Jihad in Shari'ah?
quduri.b: It is Fard 'alal Kifayah. If a group of Muslims establish it, the obligation is lifted from the rest. If none establish it, all Muslims are sinners for abandoning it. Jihad is not a duty upon minors, slaves, females, blind men, cripples and those with lost limbs. However, if the enemy assaults a particular city of the Muslims, Jihad becomes Fard upon every individual Muslim. It becomes their duty to repel the enemy. A woman will in those circumstances go for battle without her husband's permission and a slave will fight without his owner's permission.

quduri.f: You have mentioned two stages of the obligation of Jihad. Explain Jihad which is Fard 'alal Kifayah. How is it implemented in every age?
quduri.b:
We shall strike at them first even if they do not commence hostilities against us. We shall continue to fight them until they either embrace Islaam or they render Jizyah in humilitation. When the Muslims abandonded Jihad and combat, they were conquered and became playthings of the enemy.133

133 Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "When a people abandon Jihad, Allah afflicts the mass of them with punishment." [at-Tabrani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat].

quduri.f: The Muslims set out for Jihad. They enter Darul Harb [the lands of hostile Kuffar] and besiege a city or fort. With what act should they commence?
quduri.b: They will first call them to Islaam. If they accept, the Muslims should desist from fighting. If they refuse then the Muslims should demand that they render Jizyah. If they comply then they will share the same rights and obligations as the Muslims. If they refuse, then the Muslims will seek Allaah's help against them and fight them. They will use catapults, fire and water against them. They may cut their trees and destroy their crops, but may not break their word or any agreement made. They may not mutilate their dead, kill a woman, child, madman, old man, blind man or cripple unless any of these was an advisor to the Kuffar in battle, or the woman was the queen of the Kuffar. A woman may not fight without her husband's permission and a slave may not fight without his owner's permission unless there is an enemy assault as already discussed.

quduri.f: Can the Muslim attack without offering them Islaam?
quduri.b: No, fighting is not permissible without presenting the enemy with Islaam first. Thereafter if facing a particular people to whom the call to Islaam had reached, it would be recommended but not obligatory to renew the call to Islaam first.

quduri.f: There may be Muslim prisoners or traders in the land of the Kuffar. If weapons such as arrows were to be used, we have no guarantee that they will not kill those Muslims. Should such weapons therefore not be used in such instances? Similarly what if the Kuffar use Muslim children or prisoners as shields, can the Muslims still shoot their arrows at them?
quduri.b: The Muslims should not desist from firing and should still shoot their arrows, intending the Kuffar and not Muslims.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to take women and copies of the Quraan with into enemy lands?
quduri.b: If the Muslim army is large enough that they are satisfied that they can protect the women and Manuscripts, they may do so. If they are small and cannot guarantee protection then it would be Makruh.

quduri.f: What is the status of buying weapons from the enemy?
quduri.b: It is not permissible to buy weapons from the enemy or to equip them in turn.

quduri.f: Is the Muslim ruler allowed to conclude peace with the enemy or a group amongst them?
quduri.b: It is permissible if there is some benefit to the Muslims in that.

quduri.f: He [i.e. the ruler] made a peace agreement for a specified time and then saw that terminating the agreement would be better for the Muslims. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: It is permissible, although he may not commence fighting until announcing the termination of the treaty. Allaah says, "If you fear treachery from a people then throw back [the treaty] that you may be on equal terms. Verily Allaah does not love the treacherous." [al-Anfal:58]

quduri.f: What will the Muslim ruler do if the enemy acts treacherously?
quduri.b: If the act was agreed upon amongst the enemy, the Muslims will attack without respite of announcement.

quduri.f: Can the Muslims accept peace with the enemy in exchange for receiving payment from them?
quduri.b: Yes, the money received will be used as Jizyah is used.

quduri.f: What is the status of Muslims granting the Kuffar amnesty?
quduri.b: If a free Muslim male or female grants a Kafir individual, group, fort or city amnesty it is valid. No Muslim may then fight them. If there will arise mischief from that, the ruler will announce to them its annulment.

quduri.f: Who may not grant amnesty?
quduri.b: The amnesty of a Zimmi is not valid and a prisoner or trader who is amongst the enemy may not grant amnesty. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى an incapacitated slave may not grant amnesty unless his owner permits him to fight. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى his amnesty is valid.

quduri.f: A land has been conquered by force. What will be done with its land and people?
quduri.b: The ruler may either share it amongst the Muslims; or leave it in the hands of its people and impose Jizyah on the people and Khiraj on the land.

quduri.f: If the booty has been collected, how will it be divided?
quduri.b:
It will not be shared until it has been taken out of Darul Harb. Once it is in Darul Islaam the state's fifth is taken out and the remaining four-fifths is divided amongst those who have earned the booty.  According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى each horseman receives two shares and each infantryman receives one share. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى horsemen receive three and infantrymen one. Rid134 and fighters are equal. Even if the fighters meet the reinforcements in Darul Harb before the booty is taken to Darul Islaam then they will share with them in it. Foreign and Arabian horses are the same. Each horseman only gets shares for one horse. Camels and mules are not counted.

134 Those who entered enemy lands, witnessed the participants, assisted by means of their numbers and equipment but did not get the opportunity to physically fight.

quduri.f: A man set out for battle on horse and entered enemy lands thus. His horse then perished. Does he receive the share of a horseman or infantryman?
quduri.b: Horseman.

quduri.f: A man entered enemy land on foot and bought a horse there. What share does he receive?
quduri.b: Infantry.

quduri.f: A man in the Muslim army died in Darul Harb before the booty could be taken to Darul Islaam. Does his estate receive his share?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: And if he died after the booty reached Darul Islaam? [i.e. a man in the Muslim army died, does his estate receive his share?]
quduri.b: His heirs will receive his share.

quduri.f: Traders met up with the Muslim army to buy and sell in the camp. Do they receive booty?
quduri.b: Only if they actually fight.

quduri.f: Can the booty be divided in Darul Harb?
quduri.b: No, it must be taken to Darul Islaam and shared there. If there is no means of transport, the booty will be divided amongst the fighters in Darul Harb as Wadi'ah. They will then return it to Darul Islaam where the state's fifth will be taken and the remainder divided.

quduri.f: Can booty be sold in Darul Harb before distribution?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Can the fighters use the booty whilst still in Darul Harb?
quduri.b: If there is any fodder it can be used to feed the animals, the food can be eaten, firewood lit, oil used on themselves and the horses' hooves and the weapons used for fighting. All these are permissible before the division. It is not permissible to sell any of that or to enrich oneself with it. Whoever has leftover fodder and food must return it to the booty. Once the booty leaves Darul Harb it is not permissible to consume the food and fodder there from.

quduri.f: A slave, woman, child, madman or Zimmi participated in the Jihad. Do they receive shares?
quduri.b: They do not receive formal shares from the booty, although the commander may award them a nominal amount as per his discretion.

quduri.f: How is the Fifth spent?
quduri.b: Three parts are for the orphans, one for the poor and one for travellers.

quduri.f: Allaah says, "Know that the booty you earn a fifth is for Allaah, the Rasul, his relatives, the orphans, the poor and the travellers." You have omitted the first three. Why is that? [i.e. in question 2307: "How is the Fifth spent?"]
quduri.b:
According to Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنه the mention of Allaah at the beginning is for blessings. The share of the Rasul ﷺ dropped upon his passing away just as Safi135 was dropped. His relatives were entitled during his lifetime because of their assistance to him. After his death they are only entitled by way of poverty. They are more entitled than other poor people. Their wealthy will receive nothing.

135 His right to award himself something from the booty e.g. armour, a sword, a slave-girl etc.

quduri.f: An individual or two entered Darul Harb without the ruler's permission and conducted a raid. What is the satus of the Fifth of their booty?
quduri.b: A fifth will be taken from what they had acquired by force, even if the ruler had not authorised them.

quduri.f: The Muslims wish to return to Darul Islaam. They have beasts whcih they cannot bring back with them. What should they do?
quduri.b: The must slaughter them and burn the bodies. Nothing should be left for the enemy. The animals should not be wounded.

quduri.f: Can the fighters receive amounts in addition to their booty shares?
quduri.b:
It is permissible for the commander to reward them during fighting and may announce, "He who slays an enemy may keep his spoils."

He may also tell a particular expeditionary force, "I set aside for you a quarter after the fifth is taken out."

This is before the booty is taken to Darul Islaam. Once there, rewards may not be given except from the Fifth.

quduri.f: What are the "spoils"? [i.e. when a commander says, "He who slays an enemy may keep his spoils."]
quduri.b: That which is on the slain, such as his clothing and weapons; his mount and that which is on it such as the saddle and equipment; that which he had with him on an animal such as wealth in a bag or on it. All those are spoils. Anything else is not.

quduri.f: What is the status of the spoils if the commander had not announced them for the killer?
quduri.b: It will be included in the general booty. The killer and everyone else has equal rights to it.

quduri.f: What will the Muslim army do with the Kuffar prisoners they capture?
quduri.b: The commander may execute them, enslave them or free them as Zimmis. It is not permissible to return them to Darul Harb; nor release them; nor offer them in ransom according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they may be exchanged for Muslim prisoners.

quduri.f: A Kafir embraces Islaam in Darul Harb. Does his Islaam guarantee his life, etc?
quduri.b: His life, that of his minor children, the wealth in his possession, and any Wadi'ah he may have of a Muslim or Zimmi will all be respected.

quduri.f: A Kafir embraces Islaam. He has land, a wife or adult children in Darul Harb. What is their status if we conquer them?
quduri.b: His land, wife, her foetus and his adult children will all be Fay. Any of his slaves who fought will also be Fay.

quduri.f: A man embraced Islaam in Darul Harb. He had money which a Harbi, Muslim or Zimmi usurped. What is its status?
quduri.b:
The wealth in the hands of the Harbi is Fay, be it usurped wealth or Wadi'ah. The usurped wealth in the hands of a Muslim or Zimmi is Fay according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Muhammed136 رحمه الله تعالى it is not Fay.

136 And according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى.

quduri.f: Upon which lands is 'Ushr and Khiraj imposed?
quduri.b:
'Ushr is imposed on the following lands:
All of Arabia which is defined as the area between 'Uzayb and the ends of Hajar in Yemen, from Mahrah in Yemen to the border of Syria.
A land whose people embraced Islaam.
A land conquered by force and divided as booty.
The land of al-Basrah, according to us, per the unanimous decision of the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم.
Khiraj is imposed upon these lands:

The land of al-'Iraq, which is defined as between al-'Uzayb and the mountain-pass of Hulwan, and from al-'Alth to 'Abadan. It is the property of its inhabitants who may buy and transact in it.
Land conquered by force and the people left to it.
A man cultivates dead land. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is classified according to the adjacent land. If it is Khiraj land then his is also Khiraj. If it is 'Ushr land, then his is also 'Ushr. According to Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى if he cultivated it by a well he dug or a spring he let gush out, or with the Tigris, Euphrates or any other large river which nobody owns then it is 'Ushr land. If by means of canals which the non-Arabs had dug e.g. The Imperial Canal or the Yazdgird Canal then it is Khiraj land.

quduri.f: What are the details of paying 'Ushr?
quduri.b: It has been explained it Kitabuz-Zakah, refer to it.

quduri.f: Explain the quantity of Khiraj.
quduri.b: The Khiraj which 'Umar رضي الله عنه imposed upon the people of al-'Iraq is as follows: -for every Jarib [land measure] which water reaches and is capable of having crops grown 1 Hashimi Faqiz which equals a Sa' and a Dirham. 5 Dirhams for every Jarib of Rutab. 10 Dirhams for every Jarib of joined grapes or joined date trees. Besides that will be according to capability.

quduri.f: The ruler imposed Khiraj upon a land which cannot sustain it, what will be done?
quduri.b: It will be reduced to an amount appropriate to its condition.

quduri.f: Khiraj was flooded, or could not be watered, or the crops was afflicted by some calamity. Is the Khiraj forgiven?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: If the owner leaves it fallow [i.e. the Khiraj], what is the ruling of the Khiraj?
quduri.b: He must still pay it.

quduri.f: The Zimmi owner of Khiraj lands embraces Islaam or sells the land to a Muslim. Does the status of the land change?
quduri.b: No, it remains Khiraj land.

quduri.f: Is 'Ushr taken in addition from Khiraj lands?
quduri.b: No, the two are not joined. There is no 'Ushr on Khiraj land.

quduri.f: Is Khiraj multiply charged if the crop grows more than once in the same year?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is Jizyah?
quduri.b: Jizyah is what is taken from the Zimmis to protect their lives and wealth. There are two kinds - Jizyah which is given by consent at the time of a peace treaty, the amount is determined by mutual consent, and Jizyah which imposed on those conquered by force and left to live in their lands.

quduri.f: What are the details of the Jizyah imposed on the conquered Kuffar?
quduri.b:
The one who is apparently rich must pay 48 Dirham annually, each month 4 Dirhams will be taken.
The middleclass person will pay 24 Dirham annually, each month 2 Dirham will be taken.
A poor working class person will pay 12 Dirham annually. Each month 1 Dirham will be taken.

quduri.f: Are there Zimmis exempt from Jizyah?
quduri.b: Women, minors, chronically ill, poor who do not have steady work and monks who do not associate with the people are exempt from Jizyah.

quduri.f: Do all Kuffar pay Jizyah or are there sects which are exempted?
quduri.b: Jizyah is imposed upon the People of the Book, Fire-Worshippers and Idolaters who are not 'Arab. 'Arab Idolaters and Apostates do not have the option of Jizyah. Their only choice is between Islaam and the sword.

quduri.f: A Zimmi with outstanding Jizyah embraces Islaam. Is the amount forfeit?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: A Zimmi has two years of outstanding Jizyah. Will he be pardoned?
quduri.b: Yes, he will only pay one year's Jizyah.

quduri.f: Are there people who instead pay double the Zakah Muslims pay?
quduri.b: Yes, the Christians of Banu Taghlib will pay double the Zakah Muslims would pay. This applies to their men and women but not children.

quduri.f: What is Fay? What is the difference between it and Ghanimah [booty]?
quduri.b: Fay is on the same syntax scale as Shay. The verb is read as fa-a yafiu and means to return. Ghanimah is that which is taken by force from the Kuffar. That which is taken without fighting is Fay. The forms of fay the jurists have mentioned include Jizyah, Khiraj, and what has been acquired from the Kuffari in lieu of peace. Some of these we have covered, we shall discuss the rest inshaAllaah.

quduri.f: On what is Khiraj, Jizyah and Fay spent?
quduri.b: What the ruller collects from Khiraj, Jizyah, the payments of Banu Taghlib, and the gifts from Darul Harb, he will spend for the benefit of the Muslims. He will build harbours, canals and bridges and pay the judges and 'Ulama that which suffices them. He will provide for the soldiers and their children from it.

quduri.f: What are the special regulations pertaining to the Zimmis living in Darul Islaam?
quduri.b: They may not build churches and synagogues in Darul Islaam. The ruler may permit them to restore those places of worship which fell into ruin before Islaam gained dominance. They will be ordered to distinguish themselves from the Muslims by means of their attire, mounts, saddles, and headgear. They may not mount horses and may not carry weapons.

quduri.f: A Zimmi refused to pay Jizyah, killed a Muslim, committed Zina with a Muslim lady, or abused Rasulullaah ﷺ. Is his covenant terminated?
quduri.b: No. It is terminated if he leaves for Darul Harb or the Zimmis overpower a region and wage war against us.

quduri.f: The Kuffar have need to enter our lands in safety just as Muslim often enter their lands. Explain the relevant rules.
quduri.b:
The jurists have explained this as follows:
If a Muslim enters Darul Harb with their guarantee of safety, for the purpose of trade, he may not violate their wealth or blood. If he deceives them and takes anything of theirs to Darul Islaam, his ownership thereof is ilicit and he must give those goods away in charity.
If a Harbi enters Darul Islaam with our guarantee of safety he may not stay a full year. He will be warned, "If you remain here for a year, Jizyah will become liable upon you." If he does remain for a year, Jizyah will be taken from him. He becomes a Zimmi and may not return to Darul Harb.
If he does return to Darul Harb and has left a Wadi'ah by a Muslim or Zimmi, or they are indebted to him, his blood has become permissible to shed because of his returning to Darul Harb, and his wealth in Darul Islaam is in jeopardy. If he is captured or appears in Darul Islaam and is killed then the debts owing to him is forgiven and his Wadi'ah becomes Fay. If he was killed without appearing in Darul Islaam then his loans and Wadi'ah are for his heirs.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of Muslims conquering Kuffar, Kuffar conquering Muslims, and some conquering each other?
quduri.b:
The jurists have written several Masail in this regard:
If a group of Kuffar conquer another group of Kuffar, and capture them and take their wealth, they become the owners. If we then conquer them, what we find of that is Halal for us.
If the Kuffar capture our wealth and take it to Darul Harb, they become the owners. If the Muslims then recapture it and the previous owners find it before being shared, then they may reclaim it without compensation. If they found it after the booty was divided, they may claim it but must pay the market value.
A trader enters Darul Harb and buys that wealth which the Kuffar plundered. He takes it back to Darul Islaam. The previous owner has first right. He may buy it from the trader at the price he paid the Kuffar, or he may leave it.
If a camel of Muslims runs wild and the Kuffar take it, they own it.

quduri.f: What is the ruling if one of our slaves flees to the Kuffar with goods; or they capture him?
quduri.b:
There are several Masail in this scenario:
If the Kuffar captured a slave of a Muslim. One of them bought him and returned him to Darul Islaam. One of his eyes was put out and he claimed Arsh. The old owner can claim him at the price the man paid the enemy but will not take the Arsh.
The Kuffar captured a slave of a Muslim. A man bought him for 1000 Dirham. He was captured a second time and taken to Darul Harb. Another man bought him for 1000 Dirham. The old owner cannot claim him from the second buyer. The first buyer can claim him from the second buyer for 1000. If the old owner then wishes he can claim him from the first buyer for 2000.
When the Kuffar captures a Mudabbar, Ummul Walad or Mukatab belonging to the Muslims, their ownership is not recognised, as when they capture a free person of us. On the other hand, we will own whichever of the above we capture.
A slave belonging to a Muslim flees to the Kuffar and they take him. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى they do not own him. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they own him.
A slave belonging to a Muslim flees with a horse and goods to the Kuffar. The Kuffar take all that. A man buys these items and takes them to Darul Islaam. The original owner can take the slave back without compensation and the horse and goods at the price the man paid. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى if he wants them back he must pay, including for the slave.
A Harbi enters Darul Islaam with aman and buys a Muslim slave. He takes him to Darul Harb. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى the slave is free. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى he is not.
A slave of a Harbi embraces Islaam and flees to us or is captured in their lands. He is now free as any of their slaves who flees to the Muslim camp.

quduri.f: What are the regulations of Muslims who abandon Islaam?
quduri.b:
They are as follows:
When a man abandons Islaam he will be presented with an opportunity to re-embrace it. If he has nay doubts, these should be explained to him. He will be imprisoned for three days. If he accepts, well and good. If he refuses he will be killed.
It is Makruh to kill him before offering him Islaam. Nevertheless there is neither Qisas nor Diyah upon his killer.
If a woman abandons Islaam, she will not be killed. She will be imprisoned until she embraces Islaam, even if forever.
The apostate's ownership of his wealth is suspended. If he returns to Islaam his wealth returns to him. If he is executed or dies upon his apostasy, the wealth he earned during his Islaam goes to his Muslim heirs. What he earned after apostasy is Fay and will be deposited in the public treasury.
If the apostate flees to Darul Harb and the judge declares it official, his Mudabbar and Ummul Walad are free and his debts are absolved. His earnings as a Muslim are distributed amongst his Muslim heirs. His debts which he incurred as a Muslim will be paid from his wealth earned as Muslim. His debts which he incurred as an Apostate will be paid from his wealth earned as an Apostate.
All his buying, selling and transacting as an apostate are suspended. If he returns to Islaam they are valid, if he dies, is killed or flees as an apostate to Darul Harb then they are void.
If he returns to Darul Islaam as a Muslim after the court had declared his going to Darul Harb official, then he may claim what remains of his wealth in the hands of his heirs.
The transactions of a female apostate during her apostasy are valid.

quduri.f: What should the ruler do if a people withdraw from the obedience of Islaam and overwhelm a region?
quduri.b: The ruler should calll them to return and will attempt to answer their grievances. He will not commence hostilities until they do so first. Once they attakc he should endeavour to split their ranks asunder. If they have a group they flee to, he should swiftly slay their wounded and pursue those who flee. If they do not have such a group, he should not kill their wounded nor pursue those who flee. Their children will not be captured and their wealth will not be plundered.

quduri.f: The ruler's army captured rebel weapons. Can they use them?
quduri.b: If the Muslims are in need, they may do so.

quduri.f: The ruler's army captured wealth of the rebels. What should he do with them?
quduri.b: He will impound it and will not return it to them until they repent.

quduri.f: The rebels have collected Khiraj and 'Ushr from the lands they control. The ruler then reconquers those lands. Will he collect the taxed a second time?
quduri.b: No. If the rebels had spent it correctly then it suffices on behalf of those who had paid. If they had not, then it is the personal responsibility of the people of that land in their relation with Allaah to pay a second time.

quduri.f: What is the meaning of Hazhr and Ibahah?
quduri.b: Hazhr is literally "prohibition". Mahzhur is prohibited. Ibahah is the right of the Mukallaf [one answereable in Shari'ah] to do or to omit certain acts without entitlement of either reward or punishment.

quduri.f: Which attire is permissible and which are prohibited for men and women?
quduri.b:
There are details to this question:
Neither a man nor a woman may imitate the Kuffar in clothing, apparel and appearence. Men may not imitate women and women may not imitate men.137 
Extravagance and waste are not allowed.
Men may not wear silk. Women may.
Men may wear silk and brocade in war according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. It is Makruh according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى.
There is no harm in men wearing a silken garment if the lengthwise thread is cotton.
It is Haram for men to wear their loin-cloths, trousers, shirts etc. to below the ankles.138
137 Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allah curse the men who imitate women and women who imitate men." [al-Bukhari]

138 Abu Hurayrah رضي الله عنه narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "That which falls below the ankles of the loin-cloth is in Jahannum (Hell)." [al-Bukhari]

quduri.f: What is the status of silken pillows?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى there is no harm. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى it is Makruh.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of using gold and silver?
quduri.b:
The rules are as follows:
Men may not adorn themselves with gold and silver. Women may.
It is not permissible to dress a child in gold and silk.
There is no harm in a man wearing a silver ring as long as it does not reach a Mithqal. Anything besides silver is not allowed.
Gold and silver vessels may not be used for eating, drinking, oiling or perfuming. Thus neither men nor women may use gold and silver spoons or antimony sticks.
There is no harm in using glass, lead, crystal and carnelian vessels.
According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is permissible to drink from a silver plated vessel, sit on a silver plated saddle or seat, as long as one avoids the actual silvered area.
There is no harm in decorating the Manuscripts of the Quraan, engraving the Masjid and beautifying it with gold water.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a man looking at a strange woman?
quduri.b:
It is not permissible for him to look at her, except her face and hands.139 If he is not safe from lust, then he should not look at her face even, except under dire necessity. He may not touch her face or hand, even if it is without lust.

139 That is not a license for women to roam about displaying their faces to all in this age of sin and rebellion. What security is there that the men are not gazing at them with lust?

quduri.f: What is a valid reason to look at her face? [i.e. a man looking at a strange woman]
quduri.b: A witness has a valid reason to look at her when giving Arsh on her, as does the judge when ruling about her. They may look even if they fear that they will feel lust.

quduri.f: A woman has a sore on her thigh. The doctor needs to examine it. What should he do?
quduri.b: He may examine the place of the sore only. He should not look at the rest of the thigh.

quduri.f: What is the law of men looking at man and women looking at women?
quduri.b: A man may look at another man's body except the region from the navel to the knees, as may a woman look at another woman except from the navel to the knees.

quduri.f: Which parts of a man may a woman look at?
quduri.b: She may see of a man whatever a man may see of a man.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a man looking at his slave-girl and wife?
quduri.b:
He may see the entire body of his permitted140 slave-girl and wife.

140 I.e. a slave-girl who is a Fire-worshipper, Mukatabah, married to another, or forbidden unto him by way of breastfeeding or Musaharah is just like a strange woman unto him in terms of what he may see or her.

quduri.f: What may a man see of his Mahram women?
quduri.b:
He may see her face, head, chest and calves.141 He may not see her back, thighs and stomach. There is no harm in him touching that which he may see.

141 This is also on condition that both parties are safe from lust.

quduri.f: What is the ruling of a man looking at a slave-girl not belonging to him?
quduri.b: He may see the same parts which are permissible for him to look at from his female Mahram relatives. There is no harm if he touches those parts if he intends purchasing her, even if he fears lust will arise.

quduri.f: Can a male slave look at his female owner?
quduri.b: No, he may only look at those parts which are permissible for a strange man to look at as per the previously mentioned conditions.

quduri.f: What is the status of hoarding essential foods?
quduri.b: It is not permissible to hoard foods essential to men and beasts in a land where its hoarding harms its people.

quduri.f: A man kept back the grain of his farm, or the grain he imported. Is this deemed prohibited hoarding as well?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: What is the status of the government fixing prices?
quduri.b: It is not appropriate. The government should leave the people to trade as they wish.

quduri.f: Sundry regulations
quduri.b:
It is Makruh to divide the Quraanic ayat in groups of ten [Ruku'] and to place dots and diacritical marks therein.142 
It is Makruh to use eunuchs.
There is no harm in castrating animals.
There is no harm in mating a horse and donkey to breed a mule.
It is permissible to accept the word of a slave or minor that the owner or adult had allowed the guest to enter or had given the recipient a gift.
The word of an open sinner will be accepted in transactions.
In matters of Din only an 'adil [does not openly sin] is accepted.
An eunuch gazing at a strange woman is the same as a normal man's regulations.
A man may practice coitus interuptus with his slave-girl without her permission. He may not do so with his wife, except with her permission.
It is Makruh to sell weapons during times of strife.143 
There is no harm in selling juice to one whom knowns will make wine of it.
142 Because the 'Arabs could read the Quran without them. Putting the dots and marks these helps ensure correct reading.

143 To those known to cause strife and rebellion.

quduri.f: What is Wasiyah and what is its status?
quduri.b:
Literally it is a request that someone perform some act, whether during the life or after the death of the one requesting. In the terminology of the jurists it is the transfer of ownership to someone upon the one's death, whether it be of a physical item or of a benefit,

Its status is that if the Musi [one making the bequest] has obligations upon him to Allaah e.g. unpaid Zakah, he did not perform Hajj when it became compulsory upon him, etc. then it is Wajib upon him to make a bequest that these be fulfilled on his behalf. It is also Wajib upon him to leave a bequest for the fulfilment of rights of people against him and debts he owes them. He must also leave instructions for the return of trusts and Wadi'ah he has by him.

If he does not have any outstanding rights of Allaah or humans or debts to be paid, then it is Mustahhab for him to leave a bequest that some of his wealth be spent in good avenues.

If his debts encompass his entire estate, then he may not make a bequest for anyone. If he does make a bequest, it is not valid and will not be implemented unless the creditors agree out of their kindness.

quduri.f: Can a Muslim leave a bequest for a Kafir? Can a Kafir leave a bequest for a Muslim?
quduri.b: Both are permissible.

quduri.f: Is a minor's bequest valid?
quduri.b: No.

quduri.f: Are there people for whom one's bequest is void?
quduri.b: A bequest for one's murderer is void, be the murder deliberate or accidental, if he was directly involved in the slaying.

quduri.f: Are there other people for whom bequests are not valid?
quduri.b: One cannot make a bequest for one's heir, unless all the other sane, adult heirs agree.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated that the bequest be of "some of his wealth"? Can he not make a bequest with all his wealth?
quduri.b: A bequest is only valid up to a third of the estate, not more, unless the heirs agree after the death of the one making the bequest. Their consent during his life is disregarded. It is Mustahabb that one keeps the bequest to less than a third.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for another. The recipient accepted or rejected it during the bequest maker's life. What is the status of his acceptance or rejection?
quduri.b: It is of no effect. Once the bequest maker actually dies, the recipient may then accept or reject.

quduri.f: Does ownership transfer with acceptance?
quduri.b: The one for whom the bequest was made assumes ownership upon acceptance, except in one scenario. If the one making the bequest dies and the one for whom the bequest was made dies before acceptance, the bequest is immediately transferred to the ownership of the beneficiary's heirs.

quduri.f: A man appointed an executor i.e. someone who will fulfil his bequest. He accepted in the presence of the one making the bequest and then rejected it in his absence. Has his status changed?
quduri.b: The status has changed if he refuses in his presence and the bequest is void. If he refuses in his absence then it does not change.

quduri.f: A man appoints a Kafir, slave or open sinner as executor. Is this valid?
quduri.b: The judge will replace them with another executor.

quduri.f: Can one appoint one's own slave as executor?
quduri.b: If there are adults amongst the heirs then it is not valid, otherwise it is.

quduri.f: If a man appoints an executor who is unable to implement the bequest, what happens?
quduri.b: The Judge will appoint someone with him.

quduri.f: A man appointed two executors. Must they transact together?
quduri.b: Yes, according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى none may transact without the other, except for purchasing funeral cloth and making funeral arrangements for the deceased; feeding and clothing his minor children; returning trusts; implementing specific instructions of the bequest; freeing specific slaves; fulfilling debts; and representing the deceased in legal disputes.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that bequests cannot exceed a third of the estate. A man makes a bequest for a man for a third of his estate and another third for another man. The heirs do not consent. How will this bequest be implemented?
quduri.b: A third of the estate will be equally divided between the two.

quduri.f: And if he bequeathed a third for one and a sixth for the other? [i.e. a man makes a bequest for two men, but the heirs do not consent (for it to be above the maximum one third)]
quduri.b: The first will get two-thirds of a third of the estate and the other will get a sixth of a third.

quduri.f: He bequeathed his entire estate to one man and a third to another. The heirs do not consent. What is the ruling?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى a third will be shared equally between them. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى they will share a third between them in quarters. Three for the first man and one for the second.

quduri.f: Is there any scenario according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى where the beneficiary can receive more than a third?
quduri.b:
It is not allowed except in three cases - Mahabah [partiality]144, Si'ayah [striving]145 and Darahim Mursalah146 [unrestricted dirhams].

144 For example, a man has two slaves. One is worth 1,100 and the other is 600. He leaves a bequest that the one be sold to someone for 100 and the other to someone else for 100. The first has thus gained 1000 and the second 500. If there is no other wealth in the estate and the heirs do not consent, they will share in a third of 1500 as follows - the first gets paid 100 plus two-thirds of 1000 and the other 100 plus two-thirds of 500.
145 A man has two slaves, nothing else. He bequests that they be freed. The one is worth 1000 and the other 2000. If the heirs agree they will be freed in total, if not then from one third which is worth 1000. The one worth 2000 will be freed from the estate to the extent of two-thirds of 1000 and will earn to reimburse the rest of his 2000. The one worth 1000 will be freed from the estate to the extent of a third of 1000 and will earn to reimburse the extent for the rest of his 1000.
146 A man leaves a bequest of 2000 Dirhams for one man and 1000 for another. One third of his known estate is 1000. Each is entitled to his full share on the possibility that there is more to the estate, although at the moment each will only get two thirds of 1000 and a third of 1000 respectively.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest of a third of his Dirhams or goats for a man. Two thirds of it perished. Only a third remains. What will the beneficiary receive?
quduri.b: If all that remains equals a third of the estate the beneficiary takes everything.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for another for a third of his clothing. Two-third got destroyed. The remaining third equals a third of the estate. What is the beneficiary entitled to?
quduri.b:
A third of the remaining clothing.147

147 If they are of different kinds. If they are all the same then the ruling is the same as in Dirhams.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest of 1000 Dirhams to the beneficiary. His estate consists of wealth at hand and debts owing to the deceased. How will the beneficiary be paid out?
quduri.b: If a third of the wealth at hand covers the 1000, it should be handed to him. If not, he will be given a third of the cash at hand and every time the debts are colllected, a third will be given to him until he gathers his 1000.

quduri.f: Can a bequest be made in favour of a foetus?
quduri.b: Yes.

quduri.f: Can a bequest of a foetus be made?
quduri.b: Yes, if it is born in less than six months from the day of the bequest.

quduri.f: A man bequethed his slave-girl to someone and excepted her foetus she was carrying. What is the status of the bequest?
quduri.b: The bequest and the exception are both valid.

quduri.f: A man bequeathed his pregnant slave-girl to a man and made no mention of the foetus. She gave birth after the bequest maker died. Only then did the beneficiary accept the bequest. Does he receive the slave only or her child as well?
quduri.b: If both are covered by a third of the estate then they are both his. If not, then they are valued over the third and he will take both of them in that proportion according to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى he will first claim his proportion from the mother. If there is anything remaining then he will take it from the child.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for the children of a man or for the heirs of a man. How will they share the bequest?
quduri.b: In the first case they share equally and the second as per inheritance i.e. a male gets double the share of a female.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest for Zayd and 'Amr of a third of his wealth. 'Amr  dies. How will the bequest be shared?
quduri.b: Zayd gets the entire amount.

quduri.f: If he left a third of his estate to be shared between 'Amr and Zayd and Zayd dies?
quduri.b: 'Amr gets half of the third.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest of a third of his wealth. He has no wealth. He then earns some wealth. What is the beneficiary entitled to?
quduri.b: A third of whatever he owned at the time of death.

quduri.f: The beneficiary dies before the one who made the bequest. What is the status of the bequest?
quduri.b: It is void.

quduri.f: What is the status of a bequest, "equal to the share of my son"?
quduri.b: It is valid, for example if he had two sons, they get two third and the beneficiary a third.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest of a "share" and did not stipulate what the share is.
quduri.b: The beneficiary is entitled to the least share of the heirs. If that is less than a sixth he is entitled to a sixth.

quduri.f: And if the bequest was for a "part" of the estate? [i.e. a man left a bequest and did not stipulate what the share is]
quduri.b: The heirs may give whatever they wish to.

quduri.f: A bequest was made in favour of the neighbours. Who are entitled?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it refers to the adjacent neighbours.

quduri.f: Who are entitled if the bequest was for "ashar" [in-laws] and "akthan" [sons-in-law]?
quduri.b: A bequest for Ashar is for every Mahram blood relative of his wife. Akthan are all the husbands of his female blood relatives.

quduri.f: And if he bequeathed to his Aqarib [family]?
quduri.b: It includes his blood relative Mahrams from the closest then the next closest and so on. Parents and children are not included. It includes two individuals and more.

quduri.f: A man made a bequest for his family. He has two paternal uncles and two maternal uncles.
quduri.b: The bequest is interpreted for the paternal uncles.

quduri.f: And if he has one paternal uncle and two maternal? [i.e. a man made a bequest for his family]
quduri.b: The paternal uncle gets half and the maternal uncles share the other half. This is according to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى a bequest for Aqarib covers all whose lineage is attributed to the furthest male ancestor in Islaam.

quduri.f: Is it permissible to free one's slave, sell on Muhabah or grant a gift on one's deathbed?
quduri.b: These are all permissible, but must be taken from the third of the estate. The beneficiaries are treated just as the beneficiaries of an explicit bequest.

quduri.f: A man manumitted then made Muhabah; or made Muhabah then manumitted. Which will be implemented first?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى if Muhabah is made first it has preference, if second then both are equal. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى and Imaam Muhammed رحمه الله تعالى both are equal in both scenarios.

quduri.f: A man made several bequests for the pleasure of Allaah. Which will be implemented first?
quduri.b: His Fard obligations must first be attended to, whether he put them first or last, e.g. outstanding Hajj, Zakah and Kaffarah. That which is not Fard will be implemented as per his instructions.

quduri.f: A man left a bequest that his Fard Hajj be fulfilled. What is the duty of the heirs?
quduri.b: A man of his city should perform the Hajj on his behalf. He will do it with conveyance. If he did not leave sufficient funds to have the Hajj performed from his city, someone will be appointed from where the funds will suffice.

quduri.f: A man died on his way for Hajj. He left a bequest that Hajj be performed on his behalf. From where must the Hajj be performed?
quduri.b: According to Imaam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله تعالى it is from his city. According to Imaam Abu Yusuf رحمه الله تعالى it is from where he died.

quduri.f: Sundry regulations
quduri.b:
A Mukatab's bequest is not implemented even if he left sufficient funds.
One may annul one's bequest, but the cancellation must be explicit.
One may make a bequest of the services of one's slave or residence of one's house for a specified time, just as one may do it for an indefinite time. If the value of the slave is within the third, the slave will be handed to the beneficiary for service. If the slave is the entire estate, he will serve the heirs two days and the beneficiary one day. When the beneficiary dies then the slave is entirely for the heirs.

quduri.f: What is Faraid?
quduri.b:
It is the plural of Faridah, which is applied to that which Allaah has written upon His salves. He ordered us to do it, with emphasis, and there is no escape from fulfilling it. The one who does not do it and has no Shari' excuse is a Fasiq [open sinner].

In common usage it has come to refer to the shares of inheritance Allaah has stipulated for males and females from the estate of the deceased. He says, "Allaah instructs you regarding your children, the male will receive double the share of the female."148

148 An-Nisa: 11-12

quduri.f: Explain the order of Inheritance.
quduri.b:
The estate of the deceased will first be used to cover his burial and funeral expenses which should neither be extravagant nor unduly frugal. Whatever is left will be used to pay his debts. After the payment of his debts a third of the remainder is used to fulfil any bequests he made. Thereafter the remainder will be divided amongst the heirs as per Allaah's instructions in His Book or what He conveyed via the tongue of His Rasul ﷺ.

One begins with the Ashabul Faraid, who are those whose shares have been defined in the Quraan. Then the 'Asabat will receive what the Ashabul Faraid have left. If there are no Ashabul Faraid, the 'Asabat will take everything. If there are no 'Asabat then the remainder returns to those Ashabul Faraid who have the same lineage as per their shares.

If there are neither Ashabul Faraid nor 'Asabat, or there are no Ashabul Faraid to whom the remainder can return, then the Ulul Arham receive. If there are no Ulul Arham also, then the Mawlal Muwalah is entitled. If there are none then the beneficiary of the bequest is entitled to everything. If there are none then the estate is given to the public treasury.

quduri.f: Which males inherit from the deceased?
quduri.b:
There are ten:
Son
Son's son and descending
Father
Father's father and ascending
Brother
Brother's son
Father's brother
Father's brother's son
Husband
Mawlan Ni'mah i.e. the one who holds the Wala of freeing a slave.

quduri.f: Which females inherit from the deceased?
quduri.b:
There are seven:
Daughter
Sons' daughter
Mother
Grandmother, paternal and maternal
Sister
Wife
Mawlan Ni'mah

quduri.f: What are the causes of disinheritance?
quduri.b:
There are four:
Slavery
Murder
If the deceased and the heir are of different religions.
If one party lives in Darul Islaam and the other in Darul Harb.
An Apostate and a slave thus do not inherit from anyone. A murderer cannot inherit from his victim. A Muslim cannot inherit from a Kafir, a Kafir cannot inherit from a Muslim. A Harbi cannot inherit from a Zimmi, a Zimmi cannot inherit from a Harbi. Two Harbis cannot inherit from each other if they are in different Dars.

quduri.f: What are the shares Allaah has stipulated in the Quraan?
quduri.b:
They are six:
Half
Quarter
Eight
Two-thirds
A third
A sixth

quduri.f: Who is entitled to a half? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b:
There are five such parties:
Daughter.
Son's daughter if there is no direct daughter.
Full sister.
A sister on the father's side if there is no full sister.
A wife if there is no son of the deceased or son's child and descending.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to the quarter? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: The husband if his late wife has no children or son's children whether from him or another man. Similarly the wife of the deceased, if he had no children or son's children whether from her or another woman. If there are several wives they all share in the quarter.

quduri.f: Who is entiteld to the eight? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: The wife if the late husband had a child or son's child. If there are several wives they share in the eight.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to two-thirds? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: Two or more daughters if the deceased does not have a son. Also, two or more daughters of a son if the deceased has no direct children or son's son. Also two sisters if they have the same parents as the deceased or at least the same father, and the deceased has no child, male or female. The father is also entitled to two-thirds if the deceased leaves behind both parents, but no son or daughter.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to the third? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: The mother if the deceased did not leave behind a child, nor a child of the son, nor two or more brothers or sisters. Also entitled are if there are two or more children of the mother if the deceased has neither child, nor son's child, nor father, nor grandfather. In this case the males and females and males are equal in shares and entitlement.

quduri.f: Who is entitled to the sixth? [i.e. of inheritance]
quduri.b: Each of the parents if the deceased has a child or son's child and descending. Also the mother if two or more brothers or sisters, irrespective from which side. Grandfathers and grandmothers if there is a child and son's child. The son's daughters with the daughter if they have no brother. Children of the mother if the deceased has no child or son's child and descending, male or female, and no father or grandfather.

quduri.f: Are there certain relatives who nullify the shares of others?
quduri.b:
Yes, there are several which nullify others:
Maternal and paternal grandmothers are nullified if there is a mother.
The father nullifies the grandfathers and brothers.
A mother's child is nullified by any of these four - a child, son's child, father and grandfather nullify.
When daughters acquire two-thirds the son's daughters are dropped, unless there is equal to them or lower than them a son's son, in which case they inherit as 'Asabat.149 
When the full sisters acquire two-thirds the sisters who share only a father with the deceased are dropped, unless they have a brother, in which case they inherit as 'Asabat.
149 A male gets double the share of each female.

quduri.f: What is the order of inheritance of the 'Asabat?
quduri.b:
The closest 'Asabat are the sons; then their sons; then the father; then the grandfather; then the father's sons i.e. brothers'; then the grandfather's sons i.e. paternal uncles; then the sons of the grandfather's father.

If the father's sons are equal in rank, then the full brothers have preference. Sons, sons' sons and brothers share with their respective sisters on the basis of double share for each male and single for each female. The other 'Asabat are exclusively male, without females.

These 'Asabat are by way of lineage. There is also the Mawlal 'Itaqah i.e. the ex-owner who had freed a slave who has now died. These are 'Asabah by way of cause. Next entitled are the closest then the next closest 'Asabat of the ex-owner. The ex-owner is only entitled after the 'Asabat by lineage, but before the Zawil Arham.

quduri.f: What is Hajb?
quduri.b: It is the deprivation of certain heirs from inheriting by the presence of other heirs. If the heir is entirely deprived it is termed Hajb al-Hurman. If his allotment is reduced, it is termed Hajb an-Nuqsan.

quduri.f: Explain both kinds [i.e. Hajb al-Hurman and Hajb an-Nuqsan].
quduri.b:
A mother's share is reduced from a third to a sixth by the presence of a child, a son's child and descending. Two brothers or sisters, from whichever parent they may be, reduce the husband's share from half to quarter when the deceased has a child, just as a wife is reduced from quarter to eight when her late husband has a child. These are Hajb an-Nuqsan.

Hajb al-Hurman is enacted when there are two daughters and a son's daughter. The son's daughter is completely deprived in their presence. If however he left one daughter and a son's daughter, the daughter gets half and the son's daughter gets a sixth to combine as two-thirds. If he left two full sisters and a sister with a common father, the half-sister is completely deprived. If there is one full sister and with a sister with a common father, the altter gets a sixth adding up with the other to two-thirds.

quduri.f: You had mentioned that if there are no 'Asabat then the remainder of the inheritance after the Ashabul Faraid get their shares the remainder gets shared amongst the Ashabul Faraid. Is this when both categories of 'Asabat are not to be found i.e. 'Asabat by lineage and 'Asabat by cause or only if the 'Asabat by lineage are not found.
quduri.b: It applies to both. Thus if the deceased has a Mawlal 'Itaq the remainder goes to him, not the Ashabul Faraid.

quduri.f: Why have you stipulated 'Asabat by lineage?
quduri.b: Because the remainder will not go to the husband or wife.

quduri.f: You have mentioned that if there are no Ashabul Faraid and no'Asabat, the Ulul Arham will inherit the estate. Who are the Ulul Arham?
quduri.b:
They are ten:
Daughter's child
Sister's child
Brother's daughter
Paternal uncle's daughter
Maternal uncle
Maternal aunt
Mother's father
Mother's father's brother
Paternal aunt
Son of brother with common mother.
The closest of these are more entitled than the further ones.

quduri.f: Is there an order to their entitlement or are they all equal?
quduri.b: There is an order to their entitlement to inheritance as follows - the most entitled is the one from the child of the deceased i.e. the daughter's child. Then the descendants of the parents or one of them i.e. brother's daughters and sister's children. Then the child of the parents of the parents or one of them i.e. maternal uncles, maternal aunts and paternal aunts.
