qatr.f: Give an example of an offer/invitation (العرض) causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
qatr.b: أَلَا تَدْنُو فَتُبْصِرَ مَا قَدْ حَدَّثُوكَ — فَتُبْصِرَ is subjunctive after an offer.

qatr.f: What restriction does Ibn Hishām place on the "request" (الطلب) that licenses subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة?
qatr.b: The request must be expressed by a verb. Nouns functioning as commands (e.g. نَزَالَ, صَهْ) do not qualify according to the preferred view.

qatr.f: After what preceding context is أَنْ obligatorily omitted after وَاوُ الْمَعِيَّة?
qatr.b: After pure negation (النفي المحض) or a verbal request (الطلب بالفعل).

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example of وَاوُ الْمَعِيَّة after pure negation requiring an omitted أَنْ.
qatr.b: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ — يَعْلَمَ is subjunctive with an omitted أَنْ.

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example of وَاوُ الْمَعِيَّة after a verbal request requiring an omitted أَنْ.
qatr.b: ﴿يَا لَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (reading of Ḥamzah, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ).

qatr.f: How is the verb interpreted in the sentence: لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبَ اللَّبَنَ?
qatr.b: تَشْرَبَ is subjunctive if the meaning is: Do not combine eating fish with drinking milk.

qatr.f: How is the verb interpreted in the sentence: لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبِ اللَّبَنَ? (jussive reading)
qatr.b: تَشْرَبْ is jussive if the meaning is: Do not eat fish, and do not drink milk.

qatr.f: How is the verb interpreted in the sentence: لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبُ اللَّبَنَ? (indicative reading)
qatr.b: تَشْرَبُ is indicative if only eating fish is prohibited while drinking milk remains permitted.

qatr.f: When is a present verb jussive after a request (الطلب) without فَاء?
qatr.b: When the فَاء is omitted and the speaker intends the verb to express the result (الجزاء) of the request.

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example of a present verb becoming jussive after a request because فَاء is omitted.
qatr.b: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ﴾ — أَتْلُ is jussive because it is the consequence of the command تَعَالَوْا.

qatr.f: What condition must be satisfied for a present verb after a prohibition to be jussive as the result of the prohibition?
qatr.b: The sentence must accept the substitution of إِنْ لَا ("if not"), making the prohibition function like a conditional.

qatr.f: Give an example where a present verb is jussive after a prohibition because the conditional meaning is valid.
qatr.b: لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ تَسْلَمْ — meaning: If you do not approach the lion, you will be safe.

qatr.f: Why is the verb not jussive in a sentence like: لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ يَأْكُلُكَ?
qatr.b: Because the conditional interpretation (إِنْ لَا) is not valid; the second verb is not the intended consequence of obeying the prohibition.

qatr.f: Which particles each jussive a single present verb (تجزم فعلًا واحدًا)?
qatr.b: They are: لَمْ, لَمَّا, لَامُ الْأَمْرِ, and لَا النَّاهِيَة (in addition to the special case of a request expressing a conditional meaning).

qatr.f: Give examples of the jussive particles لَمْ, لَمَّا, لَامُ الْأَمْرِ, and لَا النَّاهِيَة.
qatr.b: لَمْ يَلِدْ; وَلَمَّا يَقْضِ; لِيُنْفِقْ

qatr.f: Which particles make two present verbs jussive (تجزم فعلين)?
qatr.b: إِنْ، إِذْمَا، أَيْنَ، أَنَّى، أَيَّانَ، مَتَى، مَهْمَا، مَنْ، مَا، حَيْثُمَا.

qatr.f: What are the two verbs called in a conditional sentence introduced by a particle that jussives two verbs?
qatr.b: The first is the verb of the condition (فعل الشرط), and the second is the answer/result (جواب الشرط أو الجزاء).

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example of a conditional particle jussiving two verbs.
qatr.b: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ — both verbs are jussive.

qatr.f: Give another Qurʾānic example of a conditional particle jussiving two verbs.
qatr.b: ﴿مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنْسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا﴾.

qatr.f: When must the answer of a conditional sentence be preceded by فَاء?
qatr.b: When it is not suitable to follow the conditional particle directly (i.e., it cannot function as a plain jussive answer).

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example where the answer of the condition is introduced by فَاء.
qatr.b: ﴿وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾.

qatr.f: When must the answer of a conditional sentence be preceded by إِذَا الفُجَائِيَّة?
qatr.b: When the answer is one of the constructions that require إِذَا الفُجَائِيَّة rather than a simple jussive verb.

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example where the answer of the condition is introduced by إِذَا الفُجَائِيَّة.
qatr.b: ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ﴾.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical rule for jussive (جزم) of a present verb that follows a request (الطَّلَب) without فَاء, and what conditions must be met?
qatr.b: A present verb becomes majzūm (jussive) when it follows a request (such as a command, prohibition, question, wish, etc.) without the conjunction فَاء, provided that the verb is intended as the result (جَزَاء) of the request. The request therefore carries the meaning of a conditional clause. Example: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ﴾ ("Come, and I shall recite..."), meaning: "If you come, I shall recite." The verb أَتْلُ is jussive by deleting its final weak letter.

qatr.f: Give examples of present verbs becoming jussive as the result of a preceding request (الطَّلَب).
qatr.b: Examples include: ائْتِنِي أُكْرِمْكَ ("Come to me and I will honour you."); هَلْ تَأْتِينِي أُحَدِّثْكَ؟ ("Will you come to me so that I may speak to you?"); لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ ("Do not disbelieve and you will enter Paradise."). In each case the second verb is jussive because it is the result of the first request.

qatr.f: Does a present verb become jussive after a negative statement or an affirmative statement?
qatr.b: No. If what precedes is merely a negative statement or an affirmative statement, the following present verb remains indicative (مرفوع). Examples: مَا تَأْتِينَا تُحَدِّثُنَا ("You do not come to us and speak to us.") and أَنْتَ تَأْتِينَا تُحَدِّثُنَا ("You come to us and speak to us."). In both cases تُحَدِّثُنَا must be indicative.

qatr.f: Why is the verb يَغْفِرْ in the verse ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ... يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾ jussive?
qatr.b: In ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجَاهِدُونَ... يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾, the verbs تُؤْمِنُونَ and تُجَاهِدُونَ carry the meaning of an imperative ("Believe" and "Strive"), so يَغْفِرْ is the jussive result of that implied command, not the result of the preceding interrogative expression.

qatr.f: When does a present verb following a request not become jussive?
qatr.b: If the following verb is not intended as the result of the request but merely describes or qualifies something, it remains indicative. Example: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ﴾. Here تُطَهِّرُهُمْ describes the charity ("a charity that purifies them") rather than expressing the consequence of taking it.

qatr.f: Why can the verb يُحِبُّ in the sentence ائْتِنِي بِرَجُلٍ يُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ not be jussive?
qatr.b: In ائْتِنِي بِرَجُلٍ يُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ, the verb يُحِبُّ is a descriptive relative clause modifying رَجُلٍ ("a man who loves Allah and His Messenger"), not the consequence of bringing the man. Therefore it cannot be jussive.

qatr.f: What condition must be satisfied for a verb after a prohibition (النَّهْي) to become jussive as its result?
qatr.b: The sentence must accept an equivalent conditional construction with إِنْ لَا while preserving the meaning. Examples: لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ ("If you do not disbelieve, you will enter Paradise.") and لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ تَسْلَمْ ("If you do not approach the lion, you will be safe.").

qatr.f: Give examples where a verb after a prohibition cannot be jussive and explain why.
qatr.b: Examples include لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلُ النَّارَ and لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ يَأْكُلُكَ. They cannot be interpreted with إِنْ لَا, so the second verb is not a conditional result and therefore cannot be jussive.

qatr.f: Why is تَسْتَكْثِرُ in the verse ﴿وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ indicative rather than jussive?
qatr.b: The phrase does not mean "If you do not give, you will seek more." Rather, تَسْتَكْثِرُ functions as a circumstantial clause (حال): "Do not give while seeking more in return." Therefore the verb is indicative rather than the jussive answer to the prohibition.

qatr.f: How did Ibn Hishām explain the jussive reading تَسْتَكْثِرْ reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī?
qatr.b: He mentioned three possible explanations: (1) it is a substitute for تَمْنُنْ, meaning "Do not regard what you give as abundant."; (2) it reflects pausal pronunciation carried into connected speech; or (3) the final consonant was made silent to match the endings of neighbouring Qurʾānic verses.

qatr.f: What is the particle لَمْ, and what are its grammatical effects?
qatr.b: لَمْ is a particle that negates a present verb, changes its meaning to the past, and makes the verb jussive. Examples: لَمْ يَقُمْ, لَمْ يَقْعُدْ, ﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ﴾.

qatr.f: What are the similarities between لَمْ and لَمَّا?
qatr.b: Both are particles that: (1) are used only with present verbs; (2) make the present verb jussive; (3) shift its meaning to the past; and (4) are indeclinable particles.

qatr.f: How does لَمَّا differ from لَمْ?
qatr.b: لَمَّا usually indicates that the negation continues up to the present and often implies that the action is still expected later. Example: ﴿بَلْ لَمَّا يَذُوقُوا عَذَابِ﴾ ("They have not yet tasted My punishment."). لَمْ merely negates a past occurrence without implying future expectation.

qatr.f: Can a verb be omitted after لَمَّا? Can it be omitted after لَمْ?
qatr.b: Yes. After لَمَّا, the verb may be omitted when understood from context. Example: هَلْ دَخَلْتَ الْبَلَدَ؟ — قَارَبْتُهَا وَلَمَّا ("I came near it, but not yet [entered]."). This omission is not permitted after لَمْ.

qatr.f: Can لَمَّا be preceded by a conditional particle?
qatr.b: No. Expressions such as إِنْ لَمَّا تَقُمْ are not permitted. By contrast, إِنْ لَمْ تَقُمْ is valid.

qatr.f: What is لَامُ الطَّلَبِ (the imperative lām), and what meanings can it express?
qatr.b: لَامُ الطَّلَبِ is a particle that makes the present verb jussive. It may express a command, as in ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾, or a supplication, as in ﴿لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ﴾.

qatr.f: What is لَا الطَّلَبِيَّة (the prohibitive لَا), and what meanings can it express?
qatr.b: لَا الطَّلَبِيَّة is the prohibitive لَا, which makes the present verb jussive. It may express prohibition, as in ﴿لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ﴾, or supplication, as in ﴿لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا﴾.

qatr.f: Which particles make two present verbs (فِعْلَانِ مُضَارِعَانِ) jussive (مَجْزُوم), and what are they called?
qatr.b: There are eleven conditional particles (أَدَوَاتُ الشَّرْطِ) that make two present verbs jussive: إِنْ، أَيْنَمَا، أَيٌّ، مَنْ، مَا، مَهْمَا، مَتَى، أَيَّانَ، حَيْثُمَا، إِذْمَا، أَنَّى. The first verb is called فِعْلُ الشَّرْطِ (the conditional verb), and the second is called جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ or جَزَاءُ الشَّرْطِ (the apodosis or result clause).

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle إِنْ function, and give an example?
qatr.b: إِنْ is a conditional particle that makes both the conditional verb and its answer jussive. Example: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ — "If He wills, He will remove you." Both يَشَأْ and يُذْهِبْ are jussive.

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle أَيْنَمَا function, and give an example?
qatr.b: أَيْنَمَا means "wherever." It makes both verbs jussive. Example: ﴿أَيْنَمَا تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ — "Wherever you may be, death will reach you."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle أَيٌّ function, and give an example?
qatr.b: أَيٌّ (when used conditionally and followed by مَا) means "whichever." Example: ﴿أَيًّا مَا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ — "Whichever Name you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle مَنْ function, and give an example?
qatr.b: مَنْ means "whoever." It makes both verbs jussive. Example: ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ — "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle مَا function, and give an example?
qatr.b: مَا means "whatever." It makes both verbs jussive. Example: ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ﴾ — "Whatever good you do, Allah knows it."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle مَهْمَا function, and give an example?
qatr.b: مَهْمَا means "whatever." Example: مَهْمَا تَأْمُرِي الْقَلْبَ يَفْعَلْ — "Whatever you command the heart, it will do." Both verbs are jussive.

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle مَتَى function, and give an example?
qatr.b: مَتَى means "whenever." Example: مَتَى أَضَعِ الْعِمَامَةَ تَعْرِفُونِي — "Whenever I remove my turban, you will recognize me."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle أَيَّانَ function, and give an example?
qatr.b: أَيَّانَ means "whenever" or "at whatever time." Example: فَأَيَّانَ مَا تَعْدِلْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ تَنْزِلْ — "Wherever the wind carries it, it comes down."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle حَيْثُمَا function, and give an example?
qatr.b: حَيْثُمَا means "wherever." Example: حَيْثُمَا تَسْتَقِمْ يُقَدِّرْ لَكَ اللَّهُ نَجَاحًا — "Wherever you remain upright, Allah will decree success for you."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle إِذْمَا function, and give an example?
qatr.b: إِذْمَا is a conditional particle meaning "whenever." Example: وَإِنَّكَ إِذْمَا تَأْتِ مَا أَنْتَ آمِرٌ بِهِ تَلْقَ مِنْ إِيَّاهُ تَأْمُرُ آتِيًا — "Whenever you do what you command, you will find those whom you command complying."

qatr.f: How does the conditional particle أَنَّى function, and give an example?
qatr.b: أَنَّى means "wherever" or "however." Example: فَأَصْبَحْتُ أَنَّى تَأْتِهَا تَسْتَجِرْ بِهَا تَجِدْ — "Wherever you come to it seeking protection, you will find it."

qatr.f: What are the names of the two verbs governed by a conditional particle (أَدَاةُ الشَّرْطِ)?
qatr.b: The first jussive verb is called فِعْلُ الشَّرْطِ (the conditional verb), while the second jussive verb is called جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ or جَزَاءُ الشَّرْطِ (the answer or result clause).

qatr.f: When must the answer to a conditional sentence (جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ) be preceded by the particle فَاء?
qatr.b: The answer must be introduced by فَاءُ الْجَوَابِ whenever it is not suitable to function directly as a conditional answer. This occurs when the answer is: (1) a nominal sentence (جُمْلَةٌ اسْمِيَّةٌ), (2) a verbal sentence beginning with a command, prohibition, request, or other imperative expression, (3) headed by a frozen (non-conjugating) verb (فِعْلٌ جَامِدٌ), (4) negated by لَنْ or مَا, (5) introduced by قَدْ, or (6) introduced by a future particle such as سَ or سَوْفَ.

qatr.f: Give examples of conditional answers that require فَاءُ الْجَوَابِ.
qatr.b: Examples include: ﴿وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ (nominal sentence); ﴿قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي﴾ (imperative); ﴿إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا فَعَسَى رَبِّي﴾ (frozen verb عَسَى); ﴿وَمَا يَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ﴾ (negated by لَنْ); ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ (preceded by سَوْفَ).

qatr.f: When may the answer to a conditional sentence be introduced by إِذَا الْفُجَائِيَّة instead of فَاء?
qatr.b: If the answer is a nominal sentence, it may be introduced by إِذَا الْفُجَائِيَّة ("suddenly"). Example: ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ﴾ — "If a calamity befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, suddenly they despair."

qatr.f: What is the definition of an indefinite noun (النَّكِرَةُ) according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: An indefinite noun (النَّكِرَةُ) is a noun that applies generally to any member of an existing genus or a mentally conceivable genus. Existing genus: رَجُلٌ ("a man"), which applies to any individual man. Conceivable genus: شَمْسٌ ("a sun"), whose genus could apply to multiple individuals if they existed, even though only one exists in reality.

qatr.f: Why does Ibn Hishām classify شَمْسٌ as an indefinite noun although only one sun exists?
qatr.b: Because indefiniteness depends on how the word was coined, not on the number of existing individuals. The noun شَمْسٌ was coined as the name of a genus, not as a proper name like زَيْدٌ. If multiple suns existed, the same noun would naturally apply to all of them.

qatr.f: Into how many categories are nouns divided with respect to definiteness (التَّعْرِيفُ وَالتَّنْكِيرُ)?
qatr.b: Nouns are divided into two categories: النَّكِرَةُ (indefinite nouns) and الْمَعْرِفَةُ (definite nouns). Indefiniteness is the original state, while definiteness is secondary.

qatr.f: Into how many categories are definite nouns (الْمَعَارِفُ) divided according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Definite nouns are divided into six categories (سِتَّةُ أَقْسَامٍ), beginning with the pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ).

qatr.f: What is the definition of a pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ)?
qatr.b: A pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ) is a definite noun that refers to a speaker (مُتَكَلِّم), an addressee (مُخَاطَب), or an absent person or thing (غَائِب).

qatr.f: Into what two major categories are Arabic pronouns (الضَّمَائِرُ) divided?
qatr.b: Arabic pronouns are divided into hidden (مُسْتَتِر) and overt (بَارِز) pronouns.

qatr.f: What is the difference between a obligatorily hidden pronoun (ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ وُجُوبًا) and a permissibly hidden pronoun (ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ جَوَازًا)?
qatr.b: An obligatorily hidden pronoun must remain unexpressed, such as in أَقُومُ ("I stand") and نَقُومُ ("We stand"). A permissibly hidden pronoun may remain hidden, such as in زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ, where the hidden pronoun refers back to زَيْدٌ.

qatr.f: Into what two categories are overt pronouns (الضَّمَائِرُ الْبَارِزَةُ) divided?
qatr.b: Overt pronouns are divided into attached pronouns (مُتَّصِلَة), such as تَاءُ قُمْتُ, كَافُ أَكْرَمَكَ, and هَاءُ غُلَامُهُ, and detached pronouns (مُنْفَصِلَة), such as أَنَا، هُوَ، إِيَّايَ.

qatr.f: When is it permissible to use a detached pronoun instead of an attached pronoun?
qatr.b: The rule is not to separate (detach) a pronoun when attachment is possible, except in certain specific constructions mentioned by Ibn Hishām, such as سَلْنِيهِ (where separation is less preferred) and ظَنَنْتُكَهُ or كُنْتُهُ (where separation is preferred according to the grammarians).

qatr.f: What is the first category of definite nouns (المعارف), and why is it mentioned first?
qatr.b: The first category is the pronoun (الضَّمِير). It is mentioned first because it is considered the most definite (أَعْرَفُ المَعَارِفِ) of the six categories of definite nouns.

qatr.f: What is the definition of a pronoun (الضَّمِير)?
qatr.b: A pronoun is a word that indicates a speaker (مُتَكَلِّم), an addressee (مُخَاطَب), or an absent person or thing (غَائِب).Examples:• Speaker: أَنَا• Addressee: أَنْتَ• Absent: هُوَ

qatr.f: Into what two categories are pronouns divided?
qatr.b: Pronouns are divided into:1. Hidden (ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ) — having no explicit form in speech.2. Overt (ضَمِيرٌ بَارِزٌ) — having an explicit spoken form.

qatr.f: What is an overt pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ البَارِزُ)? Give an example.
qatr.b: An overt pronoun is one that has an explicit form in pronunciation.Example: the تَاءُ الفَاعِلِ in قُمْتُ.

qatr.f: What is a hidden pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ المُسْتَتِرُ)? Give an example.
qatr.b: A hidden pronoun is one that has no explicit spoken form but is understood.Example: the hidden subject in قُمْ ("Stand!"), whose subject is understood as أَنْتَ.

qatr.f: Into what two categories is the hidden pronoun divided?
qatr.b: The hidden pronoun is divided into:1. Obligatorily hidden (وَاجِبُ الِاسْتِتَارِ).2. Permissibly hidden (جَائِزُ الِاسْتِتَارِ).

qatr.f: What is an obligatorily hidden pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ الوَاجِبُ الِاسْتِتَارِ)?
qatr.b: It is a hidden pronoun whose place cannot be taken by an explicit noun.Examples are the subjects of imperfect verbs beginning with:• أَ: أَقُومُ• نَ: نَقُومُ• تَ: تَقُومُThus one cannot say: أَقُومُ زَيْدٌ or نَقُومُ عَمْرٌو.

qatr.f: What is a permissibly hidden pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ الجَائِزُ الِاسْتِتَارِ)?
qatr.b: It is a hidden pronoun whose place may be taken by an explicit noun.Example:زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ → One may also say زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ غُلَامُهُ.

qatr.f: Into what two categories is the overt pronoun divided?
qatr.b: Into:1. Attached (مُتَّصِل).2. Detached (مُنْفَصِل).

qatr.f: What is an attached pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ المُتَّصِلُ)?
qatr.b: An attached pronoun is one that cannot stand independently, such as the تَاء in قُمْتُ.

qatr.f: What is a detached pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ المُنْفَصِلُ)?
qatr.b: A detached pronoun is one that can stand independently, such as أَنَا، أَنْتَ، هُوَ.

qatr.f: Into what categories are attached pronouns divided according to grammatical function?
qatr.b: Attached pronouns are divided into:1. Nominative (مَرْفُوع).2. Accusative (مَنْصُوب).3. Genitive (مَخْفُوض).

qatr.f: Give examples of nominative, accusative, and genitive attached pronouns.
qatr.b: Nominative: قُمْتُ (the تَاء is the subject).Accusative: أَكْرَمَكَ (the كَاف is the direct object).Genitive: غُلَامُهُ (the هَاء is the genitive by possession).

qatr.f: Into what categories are detached pronouns divided according to grammatical function?
qatr.b: Detached pronouns are divided into:1. Nominative only.2. Accusative only.There are no detached genitive pronouns.

qatr.f: List the detached nominative pronouns.
qatr.b: أَنَا، نَحْنُ، أَنْتَ، أَنْتِ، أَنْتُمَا، أَنْتُمْ، أَنْتُنَّ، هُوَ، هِيَ، هُمَا، هُمْ، هُنَّ.

qatr.f: List the detached accusative pronouns.
qatr.b: إِيَّايَ، إِيَّانَا، إِيَّاكَ، إِيَّاكِ، إِيَّاكُمَا، إِيَّاكُمْ، إِيَّاكُنَّ، إِيَّاهُ، إِيَّاهَا، إِيَّاهُمَا، إِيَّاهُمْ، إِيَّاهُنَّ.

qatr.f: Can detached nominative pronouns be used in the accusative, or detached accusative pronouns in the nominative?
qatr.b: No. Each set is restricted to its grammatical function. Thus one says:أَنَا مُؤْمِنٌ (not إِيَّايَ مُؤْمِنٌ).إِيَّاكَ أَكْرَمْتُ (not أَنْتَ أَكْرَمْتُ).

qatr.f: What is the general rule regarding the use of attached and detached pronouns?
qatr.b: Whenever an attached pronoun is possible, it must be used, and one should not replace it with a detached pronoun.

qatr.f: Give examples where detached pronouns are required because attachment is impossible.
qatr.b: Examples:مَا قَامَ إِلَّا أَنَامَا أَكْرَمْتُ إِلَّا إِيَّاكَThe particle إِلَّا prevents the use of attached pronouns.

qatr.f: What is the first exception in which a detached pronoun may be used even though an attached pronoun is possible?
qatr.b: When the pronoun is the second of two pronouns, the first is more definite, and it is not nominative.Examples:سَلْنِيهِ / سَلْنِي إِيَّاهُخِلْتُكَهُ

qatr.f: Why is the first pronoun in expressions such as سَلْنِيهِ considered more definite than the second?
qatr.b: Because the order of definiteness among pronouns is:Speaker (المُتَكَلِّم) > Addressee (المُخَاطَب) > Absent (الغَائِب).

qatr.f: What is the second exception allowing separation of a pronoun?
qatr.b: When the pronoun is the predicate (خبر) of كَانَ or one of its sisters, whether preceded by another pronoun or not.Examples:الصَّدِيقُ كُنْتُهُ / كُنْتُ إِيَّاهُالصَّدِيقُ كَانَهُ زَيْدٌ

qatr.f: According to Ibn Hishām, which form is generally preferred: attachment or separation?
qatr.b: In non-mental verbs (e.g., سَلْنِيهِ، أَعْطِنِيهِ), attachment is preferred. With mental verbs and with كَانَ, scholars differed. The majority preferred separation in many of these cases, while Ibn Mālik often preferred attachment.

qatr.f: What is the definition of a proper noun (العَلَم)?
qatr.b: A proper noun is a noun assigned to a specific individual and not applicable to others resembling it.

qatr.f: Into what two categories are proper nouns divided according to what they denote?
qatr.b: They are divided into:1. Personal proper nouns (عَلَمُ شَخْصٍ) — e.g., زَيْدٌ.2. Generic proper nouns (عَلَمُ جِنْسٍ) — e.g., أُسَامَةُ (lion).

qatr.f: What is a generic proper noun (عَلَمُ الجِنْسِ)? Give examples.
qatr.b: It is a proper noun denoting the essence of an entire species rather than one individual.Examples:أُسَامَةُ (lion)ثُعَالَةُ (fox)ذُؤَالَةُ (wolf).

qatr.f: Into what categories are proper nouns divided according to their structure?
qatr.b: Into:1. Simple (مُفْرَد).2. Compound (مُرَكَّب).

qatr.f: What are the three kinds of compound proper nouns?
qatr.b: 1. Genitive compound (تَرْكِيبُ إِضَافَة) — e.g., عَبْدُ اللَّهِ.2. Blended compound (تَرْكِيبُ مَزْج) — e.g., بَعْلَبَكَّ، سِيبَوَيْهِ.3. Sentential compound (تَرْكِيبُ إِسْنَاد) — e.g., شَابَ قَرْنَاهَا.

qatr.f: How are genitive compounds (المركب الإضافي) declined?
qatr.b: The first part is declined according to its grammatical role, while the second part is always genitive as the second term of an iḍāfah.

qatr.f: How are blended compounds (المركب المزجي) declined?
qatr.b: If not ending in ـوَيْهِ, they behave like diptotes: ḍammah in the nominative and fatḥah in both the accusative and genitive.If ending in ـوَيْهِ, such as سِيبَوَيْهِ, they are indeclinable on kasrah.

qatr.f: How are sentential compounds (المركب الإسنادي) treated grammatically?
qatr.b: They are quoted unchanged (محكيّ), and grammatical factors do not alter their original form.

qatr.f: Into what three categories are proper nouns divided according to usage?
qatr.b: Into:1. Name (اِسْم).2. Kunyah (كُنْيَة).3. Laqab (لَقَب).

qatr.f: What is a kunyah (كُنْيَة)?
qatr.b: A proper noun beginning with أَبُو or أُمُّ, such as:أَبُو بَكْرٍأَبُو عَمْرٍوأُمُّ كُلْثُومٍ

qatr.f: What is a laqab (لَقَب)?
qatr.b: A descriptive title that conveys praise or blame.Examples:زَيْنُ العَابِدِينَ (praise)قُفَّةٌ (blame).

qatr.f: What is an ism (اِسْم) in this classification?
qatr.b: A proper noun that is neither a kunyah nor a laqab, such as زَيْدٌ and عَمْرٌو.

qatr.f: When a personal name and a laqab occur together, what is the preferred order?
qatr.b: The personal name comes first, followed by the laqab.

qatr.f: When are the name and laqab treated as apposition (بدل أو عطف بيان)?
qatr.b: When:• Both are in iḍāfah.• The first is simple and the second is in iḍāfah.• The first is in iḍāfah and the second is simple.In these cases the laqab follows the grammatical case of the name.

qatr.f: If both the name and the laqab are simple nouns (e.g., زَيْدٌ قُفَّةٌ), what are the two grammatical opinions? Which does Ibn Hishām prefer?
qatr.b: The Kufans and al-Zajjāj allow:1. Apposition (الإِتْبَاع).2. Making the name an iḍāfah to the laqab (الإِضَافَة).Most Basrans require the iḍāfah. Ibn Hishām considers apposition stronger by analogy (أَقْيَس), although iḍāfah is more common in usage (أَكْثَر).

qatr.f: What is the third type of maʿrifah (definite noun)?
qatr.b: Ism al-Ishārah (اسم الإشارة), the demonstrative pronoun.

qatr.f: What demonstrative is used for the masculine singular?
qatr.b: ذا (dhā). Usually appears as هذا with هاء التنبيه.

qatr.f: What demonstratives are used for the feminine singular?
qatr.b: There are ten reported forms: ذي، ذهي، ذه، ذهْ، ذات، تي، تهي، تيه، تهْ، تا. The most common in usage is هذه.

qatr.f: Which feminine demonstrative form is considered the rarest?
qatr.b: ذات as a demonstrative.

qatr.f: What are the three uses of ذات?
qatr.b: (1) Meaning "owner/possessor" (e.g., ذات جمال), (2) meaning "the one which (التي)" in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, and (3) as a rare feminine demonstrative.

qatr.f: What are the demonstratives for the masculine dual?
qatr.b: ذان (nominative) and ذين (accusative/genitive).

qatr.f: What are the demonstratives for the feminine dual?
qatr.b: تان (nominative) and تين

qatr.f: What demonstrative is used for both masculine and feminine plurals?
qatr.b: أولاء (commonly هؤلاء when preceded by هاء التنبيه).

qatr.f: How are demonstratives divided according to the referent?
qatr.b: Into those referring to a singular, dual, and plural; each has masculine and feminine forms where applicable.

qatr.f: How is a demonstrative used for a nearby object?
qatr.b: It is used without the kāf (ك) of distance. هاء التنبيه (ها) may optionally precede it, e.g., هذا or ذا.

qatr.f: How is a demonstrative used for a distant object?
qatr.b: It must take the كاف البعد (ك), either alone (e.g., ذاك) or together with لام البعد (ل) (e.g., ذلك).

qatr.f: When is لام البعد prohibited?
qatr.b: In three cases: (1) with the dual (ذانك، تانك), (2) with the plural in the dialect that uses أولاء, and (3) whenever هاء التنبيه precedes the demonstrative (e.g., هذاك, not هذالك).

qatr.f: What is the fourth type of maʿrifah?
qatr.b: Ism al-Mawṣūl (الاسم الموصول), the relative pronoun.

qatr.f: What are the specific (specialized) relative pronouns?
qatr.b: الذي، التي، اللذان، اللتان، الذين، الأولى، اللائي، اللاتي.

qatr.f: How are اللذان and اللتان declined?
qatr.b: They take الألف in the nominative and الياء in the accusative and genitive.

qatr.f: How is الذين declined?
qatr.b: It remains with الياء in all grammatical cases.

qatr.f: Which tribes used الذون in the nominative?
qatr.b: Hudhayl (هذيل) and ʿAqīl (عقيل).

qatr.f: Which forms are used for the feminine plural relative pronoun?
qatr.b: اللائي and اللاتي, with the option of retaining or omitting the final ياء.

qatr.f: What are the common (shared) relative pronouns?
qatr.b: من، ما، أي، أل، ذو، ذا.

qatr.f: Why are these called common relative pronouns?
qatr.b: Because they can refer to the singular, dual, or plural, masculine or feminine, depending on context.

qatr.f: Under what condition is أل considered a relative pronoun rather than the definite article?
qatr.b: When it is attached to a clear descriptive adjective (وصف صريح) that is not a comparative (اسم التفضيل).

qatr.f: Which descriptive forms can take relative أل?
qatr.b: اسم الفاعل, اسم المفعول, and الصفة المشبهة (e.g., الضارب، المضروب، الحسن).

qatr.f: When is أل merely the definite article rather than a relative pronoun?
qatr.b: When attached to a noun (e.g., الرجل), a noun-like adjective (e.g., الصاحب), or a comparative adjective (e.g., الأفضل، الأعلى).

qatr.f: In whose dialect is ذو used as a relative pronoun?
qatr.b: The dialect of Ṭayyiʾ (طيء).

qatr.f: Under what condition is ذا considered a relative pronoun?
qatr.b: Only when preceded by ما or من used interrogatively, e.g., ماذا or من ذا.

qatr.f: Give an example of ذا functioning as a relative pronoun.
qatr.b: ماذا أنزل ربكم؟ = "What is it that your Lord sent down?" (ما الذي).

qatr.f: What is the grammatical analysis of ماذا in this usage?
qatr.b: It means ما الذي, where ذا functions as the relative pronoun.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical analysis of من ذا قالها؟
qatr.b: It means من الذي قالها؟, where ذا functions as the relative pronoun.

qatr.f: Can ذا be a relative pronoun without preceding ما or من?
qatr.b: No. In that case it is an ism al-ishārah (demonstrative pronoun) according to the Basran grammarians.

qatr.f: What was the Kufan argument for allowing ذا as a relative pronoun without ما or من?
qatr.b: They cited poetic evidence where ذا appeared to function as a relative pronoun.

qatr.f: How did Ibn Hishām answer the Kufan argument?
qatr.b: He interpreted ذا as a demonstrative pronoun, with the following clause functioning as a circumstantial clause (حال), not as a relative clause.

qatr.f: What evidence supports Ibn Hishām's interpretation that ذا is a demonstrative rather than a relative pronoun?
qatr.b: The presence of هاء التنبيه, which only enters demonstrative pronouns, not relative pronouns.

qatr.f: What two elements must every relative pronoun have?
qatr.b: A صلة (relative clause) and an عائد (resumptive pronoun).

qatr.f: What kinds of clauses can serve as the صلة?
qatr.b: (1) A declarative sentence containing a matching عائد, (2) a complete adverbial phrase (ظرف), or (3) a complete prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور) attached to an omitted استقر.

qatr.f: What is the عائد?
qatr.b: The pronoun inside the relative clause that refers back to the relative pronoun.

qatr.f: Can the عائد ever be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes, in certain cases, such as أيهم أشد and similar constructions mentioned by Ibn Hishām.

qatr.f: What forms can the ṣilah (صلة الموصول) of a relative pronoun take?
qatr.b: It may be either a sentence (جملة) or a quasi-sentence (شبه جملة).

qatr.f: Into what two types is a sentence (جملة) divided when serving as a ṣilah?
qatr.b: Into a nominal sentence (جملة اسمية) and a verbal sentence (جملة فعلية).

qatr.f: What are the two conditions for a sentence to qualify as a ṣilah?
qatr.b: (1) It must be declarative (خبرية), and (2) it must contain a matching ʿāʾid (عائد) referring back to the relative pronoun.

qatr.f: What does it mean for the ṣilah to be خبرية?
qatr.b: It must be capable of being true or false (i.e., a statement), not an imperative or other non-declarative sentence.

qatr.f: Why is جاء الذي اضربه invalid as a relative clause?
qatr.b: Because اضربه is an imperative (إنشاء), not a declarative sentence.

qatr.f: Give examples of valid relative clauses.
qatr.b: جاء الذي أبوه قائم and جاء الذي ضربته, because both are declarative.

qatr.f: What must the ʿāʾid (resumptive pronoun) agree with?
qatr.b: It must agree with the relative pronoun in number (singular, dual, plural) and gender (masculine or feminine).

qatr.f: Give examples showing agreement of the ʿāʾid with the relative pronoun.
qatr.b: الذي أكرمته، التي أكرمتها، اللذان أكرمتهما، اللتان أكرمتهما، الذين أكرمتهم، اللاتي أكرمتهن.

qatr.f: Can the ʿāʾid ever be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes. It may be omitted in certain permitted cases.

qatr.f: Can a nominative ʿāʾid be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes, as in أيهم أشد, meaning الذي هو أشد.

qatr.f: Can an accusative ʿāʾid be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes, as in the Qur'anic reading وما عملت أيديهم, meaning عملته.

qatr.f: Can a genitive ʿāʾid attached through iḍāfah be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes, as in فاقض ما أنت قاض, meaning ما أنت قاضيه.

qatr.f: Can a genitive ʿāʾid governed by a preposition be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes, as in يشرب مما تشربون, meaning منه.

qatr.f: What three things count as shibh al-jumlah (شبه الجملة) in a relative clause?
qatr.b: (1) An adverb (ظرف), (2) a prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور), and (3) a clear adjective (صفة صريحة) when أل is relative.

qatr.f: Give an example of a ẓarf used as a ṣilah.
qatr.b: الذي عندك.

qatr.f: Give an example of a jār wa-majrūr used as a ṣilah.
qatr.b: الذي في الدار.

qatr.f: Under what condition may a ẓarf or jār wa-majrūr function as the ṣilah?
qatr.b: They must be complete (تامّان).

qatr.f: Why is جاء الذي بك invalid?
qatr.b: Because the prepositional phrase is incomplete and therefore cannot serve as a valid ṣilah.

qatr.f: Why is جاء الذي أمس invalid?
qatr.b: Because the adverb is incomplete and therefore cannot serve as a valid ṣilah.

qatr.f: What exceptional usage did al-Kisāʾī report?
qatr.b: نزلنا المنزل الذي البارحة, meaning الذي نزلناه البارحة.

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām classify the usage reported by al-Kisāʾī?
qatr.b: He regards it as irregular (شاذ).

qatr.f: When a ẓarf or jār wa-majrūr serves as the ṣilah, to what is it attached?
qatr.b: To an obligatorily omitted verb whose implied meaning is استقر ("settled/existed").

qatr.f: What happens to the hidden pronoun when استقر is omitted?
qatr.b: The hidden pronoun transfers from the omitted verb to the ẓarf or jār wa-majrūr.

qatr.f: What is the fifth type of maʿrifah (definite noun)?
qatr.b: A noun made definite by أل (ذو الأداة).

qatr.f: According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, what is the definite article?
qatr.b: أل, not merely لام by itself.

qatr.f: What was al-Akhfash's view regarding the definite article?
qatr.b: He held that the defining element is لام alone.

qatr.f: What opinion did Ibn Mālik defend regarding the disagreement?
qatr.b: He argued that both al-Khalīl and Sībawayh agreed that the definite article is أل, differing only over whether the همزة is original or added.

qatr.f: What are the three major functions of أل?
qatr.b: (1) العهد, (2) الجنس, and (3) الاستغراق.

qatr.f: Into what two kinds is أل العهد divided?
qatr.b: العهد الذكري (previously mentioned) and العهد الذهني (mentally known).

qatr.f: What is العهد الذكري?
qatr.b: Referring back to something already mentioned, e.g., اشتريت فرسًا ثم بعت الفرس.

qatr.f: What is العهد الذهني?
qatr.b: Referring to something already known to both speaker and listener, e.g., جاء القاضي when a specific judge is understood.

qatr.f: What is أل الجنسية?
qatr.b: It denotes the essence or species of something, not a particular individual.

qatr.f: Give an example of أل الجنسية.
qatr.b: الرجل أفضل من المرأة or أهلك الناس الدينار والدرهم.

qatr.f: Why does الرجل أفضل من المرأة not mean every individual man is superior to every individual woman?
qatr.b: Because أل refers to the genus (الجنس), not every individual.

qatr.f: What other names are given to أل الجنسية?
qatr.b: أل لبيان الماهية and أل لبيان الحقيقة.

qatr.f: Into what two types is أل الاستغراق divided?
qatr.b: (1) Exhausting all individuals, and (2) exhausting all qualities/attributes.

qatr.f: Give an example of أل denoting exhaustive inclusion of individuals.
qatr.b: وخلق الإنسان ضعيفًا, meaning every human being is weak.

qatr.f: Give an example of أل denoting exhaustive inclusion of qualities.
qatr.b: أنت الرجل, meaning "You possess all the praiseworthy qualities of a man."

qatr.f: How can you identify أل that exhausts all individuals?
qatr.b: It can genuinely be replaced by كل, e.g., خلق كل إنسان ضعيفًا.

qatr.f: How can you identify أل that exhausts all qualities?
qatr.b: It can be replaced by كل only figuratively, e.g., أنت كل الرجل (hyperbolically).

qatr.f: What famous prophetic expression illustrates figurative كل?
qatr.b: كل الصيد في جوف الفرا.

qatr.f: What linguistic feature characterizes the dialect of Ḥimyar (حمير)?
qatr.b: They replace the لام of أل with ميم.

qatr.f: Give the prophetic example of the Ḥimyarite substitution.
qatr.b: ليس من أمبر أمصيام في أمسفر, corresponding to ليس من البر الصيام في السفر.

qatr.f: What is the sixth and final category of maʿrifah?
qatr.b: The noun annexed (المضاف) to one of the previous definite nouns.

qatr.f: How does a noun become definite through iḍāfah (الإضافة)?
qatr.b: By being annexed to one of the previously mentioned definite nouns; its degree of definiteness follows that of what it is annexed to.

qatr.f: What is the exception regarding nouns annexed to pronouns?
qatr.b: A noun annexed to a pronoun (ضمير) has the same level of definiteness as a proper noun (العلم).

qatr.f: What is the sixth category of المعارف (definite nouns)?
qatr.b: The sixth category is المضاف (the construct noun), i.e., a noun added (مضاف) to one of the five previously mentioned definite nouns, such as غلامي, غلام هذا, غلام الذي في الدار, and غلام القاضي.

qatr.f: How is the degree of definiteness (رتبة التعريف) of a المضاف determined?
qatr.b: A المضاف takes the same rank of definiteness as the noun to which it is added (المضاف إليه). Thus, a noun added to a proper noun has the rank of a proper noun, one added to a demonstrative has the rank of a demonstrative, and so on.

qatr.f: What is the exception regarding a المضاف attached to a pronoun (المضمر)?
qatr.b: A المضاف attached to a pronoun does not take the rank of a pronoun. Instead, it has the rank of a proper noun (العلم).

qatr.f: What evidence does Ibn Hishām give that a المضاف إلى الضمير has the rank of a proper noun rather than a pronoun?
qatr.b: One says مررت بزيد صاحبك ("I passed by Zayd, your companion"), where صاحبك describes the proper noun زيد. If صاحبك had the higher rank of a pronoun, the adjective would be more definite than the noun it describes, which is considered incorrect according to the preferred opinion.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical ruling (حكم) of both المبتدأ and الخبر?
qatr.b: Both المبتدأ and الخبر are مرفوع (nominative).

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām define المبتدأ?
qatr.b: المبتدأ is a noun free from overt grammatical governors (العوامل اللفظية) and introduced for predication (للإسناد).

qatr.f: Can a المبتدأ be an explicit noun or an interpreted expression (مؤول)?
qatr.b: Yes. It may be an explicit noun, such as زيد in زيد قائم, or an interpreted clause, such as أن تصوموا in وأن تصوموا خير لكم.

qatr.f: Why is زيد in كان زيد عالماً not a مبتدأ?
qatr.b: Because it is not free from overt grammatical governors; it is governed by كان.

qatr.f: Why are isolated numerals such as واحد، اثنان، ثلاثة not considered مبتدأ?
qatr.b: Although they are free from overt governors, they are not used for predication (إسناد).

qatr.f: Can the المبتدأ be either the subject or the predicate in relation to what follows?
qatr.b: Yes. It may be the noun to which the following predicate is ascribed (e.g. زيد قائم) or the noun to which the following subject is ascribed (e.g. أقائم الزيدان؟).

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām define الخبر?
qatr.b: الخبر is the predicate (المسند) through which, together with the المبتدأ, a complete meaning is achieved.

qatr.f: Why is the noun following أقائم الزيدان؟ not a خبر?
qatr.b: Because الزيدان is the subject (المسند إليه), not the predicate (المسند), even though the sentence is complete.

qatr.f: Why is قام in قام زيد not considered a خبر?
qatr.b: Because it is not predicated together with a مبتدأ.

qatr.f: What is the normal rule regarding definiteness for the المبتدأ?
qatr.b: The المبتدأ is normally definite (معرفة), since making a judgment about an unknown indefinite noun usually provides no useful information.

qatr.f: When may a المبتدأ be indefinite (نكرة)?
qatr.b: It may be indefinite if it conveys either generality (عموم) or specificity (خصوص).

qatr.f: How can an indefinite المبتدأ convey generality (عموم)?
qatr.b: By occurring in the context of negation or interrogation, such as ما رجل في الدار or أإله مع الله؟

qatr.f: How can an indefinite المبتدأ convey specificity (خصوص)?
qatr.b: By being described or being in an إضافة, such as ولعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك and خمس صلوات كتبهن الله.

qatr.f: According to Ibn Hishām, to what do all the many cases permitting an indefinite مبتدأ ultimately return?
qatr.b: They all ultimately return to either خصوص (specificity) or عموم (generality).

qatr.f: When the خبر is a sentence (جملة), what must connect it to the مبتدأ?
qatr.b: It must contain a رابط (connecting element) linking it to the مبتدأ, unless the sentence itself is identical in meaning to the مبتدأ.

qatr.f: What are the four connectors (روابط) between a sentence خبر and its مبتدأ?
qatr.b: 1. A pronoun (الضمير). 2. A demonstrative (الإشارة). 3. Repetition of the مبتدأ. 4. Generality (العموم).

qatr.f: How does a pronoun serve as the connector in زيد أبوه قائم?
qatr.b: The pronoun ـه in أبوه refers back to زيد, connecting the predicate sentence to the مبتدأ.

qatr.f: How does a demonstrative serve as the connector in ولباس التقوى ذلك خير?
qatr.b: The demonstrative ذلك refers back to لباس التقوى, connecting the predicate sentence to the original مبتدأ.

qatr.f: How does repetition function as a connector in الحاقة ما الحاقة?
qatr.b: The repeated word الحاقة links the predicate sentence back to the original المبتدأ.

qatr.f: How does generality (العموم) function as the connector in زيد نعم الرجل?
qatr.b: The أل in الرجل denotes generality, and since Zayd is included among "men," the sentence is connected to the مبتدأ.

qatr.f: When is no connector (رابط) required between the خبر sentence and the مبتدأ?
qatr.b: When the sentence itself is identical in meaning to the مبتدأ, such as قل هو الله أحد, where هو means "the matter" or "the affair."

qatr.f: Can an adverb (ظرف) function as a خبر?
qatr.b: Yes. A ظرف may serve as a خبر, such as والركب أسفل منكم.

qatr.f: Can a جار ومجرور function as a خبر?
qatr.b: Yes. A جار ومجرور may function as a خبر, such as الحمد لله.

qatr.f: To what are a ظرف and جار ومجرور attached when functioning as خبر?
qatr.b: They are attached to an obligatory omitted element estimated as either مستقر or استقر.

qatr.f: Which omitted word do the majority of the Basran grammarians prefer when a ظرف or جار ومجرور serves as the خبر?
qatr.b: They prefer مستقر, because they regard the omitted predicate as essentially a noun.

qatr.f: Which omitted word do al-Akhfash, al-Fārisī, and al-Zamakhsharī prefer?
qatr.b: They prefer استقر, because they regard the omitted governing element as fundamentally a verb.

qatr.f: Can a temporal adverb (ظرف زمان) normally be the predicate of a concrete entity (ذات)?
qatr.b: No. A temporal adverb normally predicates only events or qualities (أعراض), not concrete entities.

qatr.f: Can a spatial adverb (ظرف مكان) be the predicate of both concrete entities and qualities?
qatr.b: Yes. A spatial adverb may predicate both substances and qualities, such as زيد أمامك and الخير أمامك.

qatr.f: Why is زيد اليوم generally considered invalid?
qatr.b: Because a temporal adverb cannot normally be predicated directly of a concrete entity (ذات).

qatr.f: How is the expression الليلة الهلال interpreted?
qatr.b: It is understood through an omitted مضاف, meaning الليلة طلوع الهلال ("Tonight is the rising of the crescent").

qatr.f: When may a raised noun governed by a descriptive word (وصف) eliminate the need for a separate خبر?
qatr.b: When the descriptive word depends on either negation or interrogation, such as أقائم الزيدان؟ or ما قائم الزيدان.

qatr.f: Why is no separate خبر needed in أقائم الزيدان؟
qatr.b: Because the descriptive word قائم functions with the meaning of a verb (أيقوم), and الزيدان serves as its subject, making the sentence complete.

qatr.f: Does this rule apply whether the descriptive word raises a فاعل or a نائب فاعل?
qatr.b: Yes. There is no difference whether the descriptive word raises a فاعل or a نائب فاعل, as illustrated by examples such as قاطن and مضروب.

qatr.f: Can a مبتدأ have more than one خبر?
qatr.b: Yes. Although the original rule is to have one predicate (e.g. زيد قائم), it is permissible to have multiple predicates, as in ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾, where all are predicates of the same subject.

qatr.f: What opinion denied the multiplicity of the خبر?
qatr.b: Some grammarians held that a مبتدأ cannot have multiple predicates and interpreted the additional descriptions as separate omitted clauses, e.g. "وهو الودود"، "وهو ذو العرش".

qatr.f: In which expressions is there no real multiplicity of the خبر, despite appearances?
qatr.b: 1. زيد شاعر وكاتب (the second is merely coordinated to the first predicate). 2. الزيدان شاعر وكاتب (each individual has only one predicate). 3. هذا حلو حامض (the two adjectives together express one combined meaning, i.e. sweet-and-sour).

qatr.f: May the خبر precede the مبتدأ?
qatr.b: Yes. It may precede either permissibly (جوازًا) or obligatorily (وجوبًا).

qatr.f: Give examples where the خبر may optionally precede the مبتدأ.
qatr.b: في الدار زيد; سلام هي; وآية لهم الليل. In such cases the preposed element remains the predicate because otherwise a definite predicate would be predicated of an indefinite subject.

qatr.f: When is advancing the خبر obligatory?
qatr.b: It is obligatory in three situations: (1) when delaying it would make it resemble an adjective, e.g. في الدار رجل; (2) when the predicate contains an interrogative that must come first, e.g. أين زيد؟; (3) when delaying it would make a pronoun refer forward to something later both in wording and rank, e.g. على التمرة مثلها زبدًا.

qatr.f: Why must the predicate precede the subject in في الدار رجل?
qatr.b: Because if delayed (رجل في الدار), في الدار could be mistaken for an adjective describing رجل rather than the predicate.

qatr.f: Why must the predicate precede the subject in أين زيد؟
qatr.b: Because أين is an interrogative word, and interrogatives must occupy the beginning of the sentence.

qatr.f: Can the مبتدأ or خبر be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes. Either one, or both (one after the other), may be omitted when there is contextual evidence indicating the omission.

qatr.f: Give examples where the مبتدأ is omitted.
qatr.b: ﴿قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكُمُ النَّارُ﴾ — i.e. هي النار. ﴿سُورَةٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهَا﴾ — i.e. هذه سورة.

qatr.f: Give examples where the خبر is omitted.
qatr.b: ﴿أُكُلُهَا دَائِمٌ وَظِلُّهَا﴾ — i.e. وظلها دائم. ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ﴾ — i.e. أم الله أعلم.

qatr.f: Give an example where both the مبتدأ and خبر are omitted (one in each clause).
qatr.b: ﴿سَلَامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ﴾. The first means سلام عليكم (predicate omitted), while the second means أنتم قوم منكرون (subject omitted).

qatr.f: In which four situations must the خبر be omitted?
qatr.b: 1. Before the answer to لولا. 2. Before the answer to an explicit oath (القسم الصريح). 3. Before a حال that cannot itself function as the predicate. 4. After the explicit واو المصاحبة.

qatr.f: Why is the predicate omitted before the answer to لولا?
qatr.b: Because the omitted predicate is understood from the context, e.g. ﴿لَوْلَا أَنْتُمْ لَكُنَّا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, meaning: "Had you not prevented us from guidance..."

qatr.f: Why is the predicate omitted before the answer to an explicit oath?
qatr.b: Because the omitted predicate is understood as "my oath" or "my covenant," e.g. لعمرك means لعمرك يميني or قسمي.

qatr.f: Why must the predicate be omitted before a حال that cannot serve as a predicate?
qatr.b: Because the حال cannot logically be predicated of the subject. For example, ضربي زيدًا قائمًا means ضربي زيدًا حاصل إذا كان قائمًا, not "My striking is standing."

qatr.f: Why is the predicate omitted after the explicit واو المصاحبة?
qatr.b: Because the meaning of accompaniment supplied by واو implies an omitted predicate such as مقرونان, e.g. كل رجل وضيعته = "Every man together with his estate are paired."

qatr.f: What are the three types of نواسخ (abrogating particles/verbs) affecting the مبتدأ and خبر?
qatr.b: 1. Those that raise the مبتدأ and accusative the خبر (كان وأخواتها). 2. Those that accusative the مبتدأ and raise the خبر (إن وأخواتها). 3. Those that accusative both (ظن وأخواتها).

qatr.f: Which verbs belong to كان وأخواتها according to Ibn Hishām here?
qatr.b: كان، أمسى، أصبح، أضحى، ظل، بات، صار، ليس، ما زال، ما فتئ، ما انفك، ما برح، ما دام.

qatr.f: What effect do كان وأخواتها have on the مبتدأ and خبر?
qatr.b: They raise the مبتدأ (called اسم كان) and accusative the خبر (called خبر كان). Example: ﴿وكان ربك قديرًا﴾.

qatr.f: What does the word ناسخ mean linguistically?
qatr.b: It comes from النسخ, meaning removal or abrogation, as in نسخت الشمس الظل ("The sun removed the shadow").

qatr.f: What is the technical definition of a ناسخ?
qatr.b: A grammatical element that changes the original ruling of the مبتدأ and خبر.

qatr.f: What are the grammatical names of the two complements of كان وأخواتها?
qatr.b: The first is called اسم كان (also فاعل by some grammarians), and the second is called خبر كان (also مفعول by some grammarians).

qatr.f: What are the grammatical names of the complements of إن وأخواتها?
qatr.b: The first complement is اسم إن, and the second is خبر إن.

qatr.f: What are the grammatical names of the complements of ظن وأخواتها?
qatr.b: They are called المفعول الأول and المفعول الثاني.

qatr.f: What are the three categories of kāna and its sisters according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: They are divided into: (1) those that work unconditionally (كان، أمسى، أصبح، أضحى، ظل، بات، صار، ليس); (2) those that require a preceding negation or something similar (زال، برح، فتئ، انفك); and (3) دام, which only works when preceded by the temporal-source particle ما (ما المصدرية الظرفية).

qatr.f: Which verbs of kāna work without any condition?
qatr.b: كان، أمسى، أصبح، أضحى، ظل، بات، صار، ليس.

qatr.f: Which verbs only function as kāna's sisters after negation or something similar?
qatr.b: زال، برح، فتئ، انفك require a preceding negation, prohibition, or supplication.

qatr.f: What counts as "something similar to negation" (شبه النفي) for زال، برح، فتئ، انفك?
qatr.b: Prohibition (النهي), such as ولا تزل ذاكراً الموت; and supplication (الدعاء), such as ولا زال منهلاً....

qatr.f: Which verb only functions as a nāqiṣ verb after ما المصدرية الظرفية?
qatr.b: دام, as in: ما دمت حياً.

qatr.f: Why is ما before دام called both maṣdariyyah and ẓarfiyyah?
qatr.b: It is maṣdariyyah because it is interpreted as the verbal noun (دوام), and ẓarfiyyah because it conveys the meaning of a time period (مدة).

qatr.f: May the predicate of kāna and its sisters come between the verb and its subject?
qatr.b: Yes. The predicate may intervene between the verb and its subject, e.g. فليس سواء عالم وجهول.

qatr.f: Is it permissible to advance the predicate before kāna and its subject?
qatr.b: Yes, for most of the sisters, e.g. عالماً كان زيد.

qatr.f: Which two sisters generally do not allow the predicate to precede the verb?
qatr.b: ليس and دام.

qatr.f: Why may the predicate of دام not precede it?
qatr.b: Because ما is a particle introducing a verbal noun, and advancing the predicate would improperly separate or precede the relative construction (صلة الموصول الحرفي).

qatr.f: What is the preferred opinion regarding advancing the predicate of ليس?
qatr.b: The preferred opinion is that it is not permitted because ليس is a frozen (جامد) verb, and no direct evidence exists for such usage.

qatr.f: What evidence did those who permit advancing the predicate of ليس use?
qatr.b: They cited: ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفاً عنهم, arguing that the complement preceding ليس indicates the permissibility of advancing the predicate.

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām answer the proof for advancing the predicate of ليس?
qatr.b: He says the preceding element is a ظرف, and Arabic permits greater flexibility with adverbials than with other complements.

qatr.f: Which five verbs may be used with the meaning of ṣāra (became)?
qatr.b: كان، أمسى، أصبح، أضحى، ظل.

qatr.f: Give examples of kāna and its sisters meaning "became."
qatr.b: Examples include: فكانت هباءً منبثاً, فأصبحتم بنعمته إخواناً, ظل وجهه مسوداً, أمست خلاء, and أضحى يمزق أثوابي.

qatr.f: Which of kāna's sisters may also be used as complete (تامّة) verbs?
qatr.b: All except ليس، زال، فتئ. Thus كان، أمسى، أصبح، أضحى، ظل، بات، صار، دام، برح، انفك may be complete according to this discussion, while ليس، زال، فتئ may not.

qatr.f: What is meant by a verb being complete (تام)?
qatr.b: It is complete when it requires only a subject and no predicate.

qatr.f: According to Ibn Hishām, what is the correct meaning of a complete verb (الفعل التام)?
qatr.b: A complete verb is one that dispenses with a predicate, not merely one that indicates both action and time.

qatr.f: Why are the verbs called defective (ناقصة) according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Because they do not suffice with the subject alone and require a predicate to complete the meaning.

qatr.f: Into what three usages does كان itself fall?
qatr.b: It may be defective (ناقصة), complete (تامّة), or redundant (زائدة).

qatr.f: What is the function of a defective كان?
qatr.b: It raises its subject and assigns accusative to its predicate.

qatr.f: What is the function of a complete كان?
qatr.b: It takes only a subject and does not require a predicate.

qatr.f: What is meant by a redundant (زائدة) كان?
qatr.b: It is inserted without serving as the predicate-bearing verb of the sentence, though it still contributes meaning.

qatr.f: Under what two conditions may كان occur redundantly?
qatr.b: (1) It must be in the past tense, and (2) it must occur between two closely connected elements that are not a preposition and its object.

qatr.f: Does a redundant كان have absolutely no meaning?
qatr.b: No. It still conveys meaning, but it is not used for predication (الإسناد).

qatr.f: When may the final nūn of the jussive imperfect of كان be omitted?
qatr.b: When it is in the imperfect, jussive, connected in speech (not paused upon), not followed by an attached object pronoun, and not followed by a consonant.

qatr.f: Why is the nūn omitted in لم أكُ بغياً?
qatr.b: The jussive removes the ḍammah, the wāw is deleted to avoid two consecutive sukūns, and the nūn is optionally omitted for lightness.

qatr.f: When may the nūn of يكن not be omitted?
qatr.b: When followed by a consonant, attached to an object pronoun, or when stopping (waqf) on the word.

qatr.f: Why is omission not allowed in لم يكن الذين كفروا?
qatr.b: Because يكن is followed by a consonant, giving the nūn a supporting vowel that prevents its deletion.

qatr.f: Why is omission not allowed in إن يكنه?
qatr.b: Because an attached object pronoun restores the word to its original form.

qatr.f: Why is omission not allowed when stopping on يكن?
qatr.b: Because stopping after deleting the nūn would require adding a pause letter, whereas restoring the original letter is preferable.

qatr.f: What are the two ways in which كان itself may be omitted?
qatr.b: (1) كان alone is omitted while its subject and predicate remain, with ما compensating for it; (2) كان and its subject are both omitted, leaving only the predicate.

qatr.f: In what construction is كان omitted while ما compensates for it?
qatr.b: After أن in causal constructions, as in أما أنت ذا نفر.

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām derive the expression أما أنت?
qatr.b: From لأن كنت..., then the preposition is omitted, كان is deleted, ما is inserted as compensation, and assimilation produces أما.

qatr.f: In which two constructions may kāna and its subject be omitted together while the predicate remains?
qatr.b: After the conditional particles إن and لو.

qatr.f: Give examples where kāna and its subject are omitted after إن.
qatr.b: Examples include: إن سيفاً فسيف، وإن خيراً فخير، وإن شراً فشر، وإن ظالماً، وإن مظلوماً.

qatr.f: What is the underlying meaning of إن سيفاً فسيف?
qatr.b: It means: إن كان ما قُتل به سيفاً فالذي يُقتل به سيف ("If what he was killed with was a sword, then he will be killed with a sword.").

qatr.f: What is the underlying meaning of إن خيراً فخير، وإن شراً فشر?
qatr.b: It means: إن كان عملهم خيراً فجزاؤهم خير، وإن كان عملهم شراً فجزاؤهم شر.

qatr.f: What is the underlying meaning of إن ظالماً وإن مظلوماً?
qatr.b: It means: إن كنت ظالماً وإن كنت مظلوماً ("Whether you are an oppressor or oppressed.").

qatr.f: Give examples where kāna and its subject are omitted after لو.
qatr.b: Examples include: التمس ولو خاتماً من حديد and ولو ملكاً.

qatr.f: What is the underlying meaning of ولو خاتماً من حديد?
qatr.b: It means: ولو كان ما تلتمسه خاتماً من حديد ("Even if what you seek is only an iron ring.").

qatr.f: What is the underlying meaning of ولو ملكاً?
qatr.b: It means: ولو كان الباغي ملكاً ("Even if the oppressor were a king.").

qatr.f: Which three negative particles may function like laysa?
qatr.b: ما، لا، لات.

qatr.f: Which dialect gives mā the grammatical function of laysa?
qatr.b: The dialect of the Ḥijāzīs.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical effect of mā when it functions like laysa?
qatr.b: It raises its subject and assigns the accusative to its predicate.

qatr.f: What are the three conditions for mā to function like laysa?
qatr.b: (1) Its subject must precede its predicate; (2) it must not be followed by the extra إن; and (3) its predicate must not be introduced by إلا.

qatr.f: Give Qur'anic examples of mā functioning like laysa.
qatr.b: ما هذا بشراً and ما هن أمهاتهم.

qatr.f: Why is mā not operative in ما مسيء من أعتب?
qatr.b: Because the predicate precedes the subject.

qatr.f: Why is mā not operative in ما إن أنتم ذهب?
qatr.b: Because it is followed by the extra particle إن.

qatr.f: Why is mā not operative in وما محمد إلا رسول?
qatr.b: Because its predicate is accompanied by إلا.

qatr.f: How do the Banū Tamīm treat negative mā?
qatr.b: They never make it function like laysa; they leave it inoperative even when the conditions are met.

qatr.f: Which particle may function like laysa only in poetry?
qatr.b: لا النافية.

qatr.f: What are the four conditions for lā to function like laysa?
qatr.b: (1) The subject must precede the predicate; (2) the predicate must not be accompanied by إلا; (3) both subject and predicate must be indefinite; and (4) the usage must occur in poetry, not prose.

qatr.f: Give a poetic example of lā functioning like laysa.
qatr.b: فلا شيء على الأرض باقياً ولا وزر مما قضى الله واقياً.

qatr.f: Why does lā not function like laysa in لا أفضل منك أحد?
qatr.b: Because the predicate precedes the subject.

qatr.f: Why does lā not function like laysa in لا أحد إلا أفضل منك?
qatr.b: Because the predicate is accompanied by إلا.

qatr.f: Why does lā not function like laysa in لا زيد قائم?
qatr.b: Because its subject is definite rather than indefinite.

qatr.f: Why does Ibn Hishām regard al-Mutanabbī's line فلا الحمد مكسوباً ولا المال باقياً as incorrect?
qatr.b: Because لا is made to function like laysa although its subject (الحمد) is definite, violating the condition that both subject and predicate must be indefinite.

qatr.f: Why did Ibn Hishām omit mentioning the condition that lā's subject must not be accompanied by إن?
qatr.b: Because the subject of lā is never accompanied by إن, making the condition unnecessary.

qatr.f: What is لات according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: It is لا with an added tāʾ, functioning like laysa under restricted conditions.

qatr.f: What are the two conditions for لات to function like laysa?
qatr.b: (1) Its subject and predicate must involve the word حين (or a word meaning "time"), and (2) one of the two parts must be omitted.

qatr.f: Which part is usually omitted after لات?
qatr.b: The subject is usually omitted.

qatr.f: Give the Qur'anic example of لات functioning like laysa.
qatr.b: ولات حين مناص.

qatr.f: What is the estimated meaning of ولات حين مناص?
qatr.b: It means: ليس الحين حين فرار ("Now is not the time for escape.").

qatr.f: Is it possible for the predicate of لات to be omitted instead of the subject?
qatr.b: Yes. Although uncommon, the predicate may be omitted while the subject remains, as in the reading ولات حينُ (with حين in the nominative).

qatr.f: How many particles belong to إن وأخواتها?
qatr.b: Six: إن، أن، لكن، كأن، ليت، لعل.

qatr.f: What effect do إن وأخواتها have on the mubtadaʾ and khabar?
qatr.b: They make the mubtadaʾ accusative (their noun) and the khabar nominative (their predicate).

qatr.f: What is the meaning of إن and أن?
qatr.b: They express emphasis (التوكيد).

qatr.f: What is the difference between إن and أن?
qatr.b: إن begins a statement directly, whereas أن normally follows preceding speech such as بلغني ("it reached me") or أعجبني ("it pleased me").

qatr.f: What is the meaning of لكن?
qatr.b: Istidrāk (exception/correction): removing a mistaken assumption created by the previous statement.

qatr.f: Give examples illustrating لكن.
qatr.b: زيد عالم لكنه فاسق ("Zayd is learned, but he is immoral.") and ما زيد شجاعًا لكنه كريم ("Zayd is not brave, but he is generous.").

qatr.f: What are the meanings of كأن?
qatr.b: It denotes comparison/similitude (التشبيه) or supposition/probability (الظن).

qatr.f: Give examples of كأن for both meanings.
qatr.b: Comparison: كأن زيدًا أسد ("Zayd is like a lion."); supposition: كأن زيدًا كاتب ("It seems Zayd is a writer.").

qatr.f: What is the meaning of ليت?
qatr.b: Wish (التمني).

qatr.f: What kinds of wishes does ليت express?
qatr.b: A wish for something impossible or unattainable, or something very difficult to attain.

qatr.f: Give examples of ليت.
qatr.b: ليت الشباب يعود يوماً ("If only youth would return.") and ليت لي قنطارًا من الذهب ("If only I had a talent of gold.").

qatr.f: What are the meanings of لعل?
qatr.b: Hope (الترجي), fear/apprehension (الإشفاق), or purpose/cause (التعليل).

qatr.f: Give examples of the meanings of لعل.
qatr.b: Hope: لعل زيدًا قادم; fear: لعل زيدًا هالك; purpose: فقولا له قولًا لينًا لعله يتذكر ("...so that he may remember.").

qatr.f: When do إن وأخواتها lose their grammatical effect?
qatr.b: When they are followed by ما الحرفية (the extra particle ما), except for ليت.

qatr.f: What happens when ما الحرفية follows إن وأخواتها?
qatr.b: Their grammatical operation is cancelled, and they may precede verbal sentences.

qatr.f: Give Qurʾānic examples where ما cancels the action of these particles.
qatr.b: إنما يوحى إلي and كأنما يساقون إلى الموت.

qatr.f: Which particle is the exception regarding ما الحرفية?
qatr.b: ليت.

qatr.f: What is special about ليتما?
qatr.b: It may either retain its grammatical operation or lose it.

qatr.f: Why is ليت treated differently from its sisters after ما?
qatr.b: Because ليت still remains restricted to nominal sentences, unlike the others.

qatr.f: What is the evidence that ليتما may be operative or inoperative?
qatr.b: The verse قالت ألا ليتما هذا الحمام لنا... is transmitted with both رفع and نصب of الحمام.

qatr.f: Does ما الاسمية cancel the action of إن?
qatr.b: No. Only ما الحرفية cancels it.

qatr.f: Explain إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر according to Ibn Hishām.
qatr.b: Here ما is a relative pronoun (الذي), so إن remains operative: إن الذي صنعوه كيد ساحر.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of إن when it is lightened (إن المخففة)?
qatr.b: Both operation and non-operation are permissible, though non-operation is preferred.

qatr.f: Which is preferred with إن المخففة?
qatr.b: Neglecting its grammatical action (الإهمال) is preferred.

qatr.f: Give examples of إن المخففة being neglected and operative.
qatr.b: Neglected: إن زيد لمنطلق; operative: إن زيدًا منطلق.

qatr.f: What Qurʾānic examples show إن المخففة?
qatr.b: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ and إن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of لكن when lightened (لكن المخففة)?
qatr.b: It is always inoperative (مهملة).

qatr.f: Why is لكن المخففة always inoperative?
qatr.b: Because it no longer remains exclusive to nominal sentences and may enter verbal sentences.

qatr.f: Give Qurʾānic examples of لكن المخففة.
qatr.b: ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين and لكن الراسخون في العلم.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of أن المخففة?
qatr.b: It remains operative even when lightened.

qatr.f: What must the omitted noun of أن المخففة be?
qatr.b: An omitted pronoun of the matter (ضمير الشأن).

qatr.f: What three conditions apply to the noun of أن المخففة?
qatr.b: It must be a pronoun, refer to the matter (الشأن), and be omitted.

qatr.f: What must the predicate of أن المخففة be?
qatr.b: It must be a complete sentence, not a single word.

qatr.f: When does أن المخففة require no separator before its predicate?
qatr.b: If its predicate is a nominal sentence, a sentence with a static verb, or a supplicatory verb.

qatr.f: Give examples where no separator is required after أن المخففة.
qatr.b: أن الحمد لله; أن عسى أن يكون; أن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى; أن غضب الله عليها.

qatr.f: When must a separator come after أن المخففة?
qatr.b: When the predicate is a sentence beginning with a conjugated verb that is not a supplication.

qatr.f: What four separators may follow أن المخففة before such a verbal sentence?
qatr.b: قد, a future particle (سوف/السين), a negation particle, or لو.

qatr.f: Give an example of separation by قد.
qatr.b: أن قد صدقتنا or ليعلم أن قد أبلغوا.

qatr.f: Give an example of separation by a future particle.
qatr.b: علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى.

qatr.f: Give an example of separation by negation.
qatr.b: أن لا يرجع إليهم قولًا.

qatr.f: Give an example of separation by لو.
qatr.b: وأن لو استقاموا.

qatr.f: Can أن المخففة ever be followed directly by a conjugated verb without a separator?
qatr.b: Yes, but only rarely in poetry.

qatr.f: Can أن المخففة ever be followed directly by a conjugated verb without a separator?
qatr.b: Yes, but only rarely in poetry, e.g. علموا أن يؤملون....

qatr.f: In poetic necessity, may the noun of أن المخففة be an explicit noun instead of the omitted pronoun of the matter?
qatr.b: Yes. In poetic necessity its noun may be explicitly stated rather than being the omitted pronoun of the matter.

qatr.f: When the noun of أن المخففة is explicitly mentioned in poetry, what may its predicate be?
qatr.b: It may be either a single word (مفرد) or a sentence (جملة).

qatr.f: Give the poetic example where both a nominal and verbal predicate occur with an explicit noun of أن المخففة.
qatr.b: بأنك ربيع وغيث مربع، وأنك هناك تكون الثمالا.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of كأن المخففة?
qatr.b: It remains operative (عاملة) when lightened, just as أن المخففة does.

qatr.f: Is the noun of كأن المخففة usually omitted?
qatr.b: No. Its noun is mentioned more frequently than the noun of أن المخففة.

qatr.f: Must the noun of كأن المخففة be the pronoun of the matter?
qatr.b: No. It may be an explicit noun.

qatr.f: Give the poetic example of كأن المخففة with an explicit noun.
qatr.b: كأن ظبية تعطو إلى وارق السلم.

qatr.f: How is ظبية analyzed in the accusative reading?
qatr.b: It is the noun of كأن, the following sentence is its adjective, and the predicate is omitted.

qatr.f: How is ظبية analyzed in the nominative reading?
qatr.b: The noun of كأن is omitted (i.e. كأنها), and ظبية is the predicate.

qatr.f: When does كأن المخففة not require a separator?
qatr.b: When its predicate is a single word or a nominal sentence.

qatr.f: Give an example of كأن المخففة with a single-word predicate.
qatr.b: كأن ظبية (according to the nominative reading).

qatr.f: Give an example of كأن المخففة with a nominal-sentence predicate.
qatr.b: كأن ثدياه حقان.

qatr.f: If the predicate of كأن المخففة is a verbal sentence, what must separate it from كأن?
qatr.b: Either لم or قد.

qatr.f: Give a Qurʾānic example of separation by لم after كأن المخففة.
qatr.b: كأن لم تغن بالأمس.

qatr.f: Give a poetic example of separation by لم after كأن المخففة.
qatr.b: كأن لم يكن بين الحجون إلى الصفا أنيس....

qatr.f: Give an example of separation by قد after كأن المخففة.
qatr.b: وكأن قد زالت (with the verb omitted).

qatr.f: May the predicate of إن وأخواتها normally come between the particle and its noun?
qatr.b: No.

qatr.f: What are the only exceptions allowing the predicate of إن وأخواتها to intervene?
qatr.b: When it is an adverb (ظرف) or a prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور).

qatr.f: Why is the predicate not freely movable with إن وأخواتها as it is with كان?
qatr.b: Because verbs are stronger governors than particles and therefore allow greater flexibility.

qatr.f: Give Qurʾānic examples where an intervening adverb or prepositional phrase is allowed.
qatr.b: إن لدينا أنكالًا and إن في ذلك لعبرة.

qatr.f: Does permitting an intervening adverb or prepositional phrase also permit placing it before إن?
qatr.b: No. Permission for intervention does not imply permission for complete fronting.

qatr.f: In which four places must إن be written with a kasrah (إن) rather than a fatḥah (أن)?
qatr.b: At the beginning of a sentence, after an oath, after verbs of saying (quoted speech), and before the emphatic لام.

qatr.f: Give an example of إن at the beginning of a sentence.
qatr.b: إنا أنزلناه or إنا أعطيناك الكوثر.

qatr.f: Give an example of إن after an oath.
qatr.b: والكتاب المبين إنا أنزلناه.

qatr.f: Give an example of إن after a verb of saying.
qatr.b: قال إني عبد الله.

qatr.f: Give an example of إن before the emphatic لام.
qatr.b: والله يعلم إنك لرسوله.

qatr.f: Why is إن broken (مكسورة) in والله يعلم إنك لرسوله but opened (مفتوحة) in علم الله أنكم...?
qatr.b: Because the first contains the لام الابتداء, whereas the second does not.

qatr.f: Upon which four elements may لام الابتداء enter after إن المكسورة?
qatr.b: (1) The delayed predicate, (2) the delayed noun, (3) an intervening complement of the predicate, and (4) the separating pronoun (ضمير الفصل).

qatr.f: Give an example of the لام entering the predicate.
qatr.b: وإن ربك لذو مغفرة.

qatr.f: Give an example of the لام entering the noun.
qatr.b: إن في ذلك لعبرة.

qatr.f: Give an example of the لام entering a complement of the predicate.
qatr.b: إن زيدًا لطعامك آكل.

qatr.f: Give an example of the لام entering the separating pronoun.
qatr.b: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق or وإنا لنحن الصافون.

qatr.f: When is the لام الفارقة obligatory?
qatr.b: When إن is lightened, inoperative, and the affirmative meaning would otherwise be unclear.

qatr.f: Why is the لام الفارقة obligatory in that case?
qatr.b: To distinguish affirmative إن from the negative particle إن.

qatr.f: Why is this لام called لام الفارقة?
qatr.b: Because it distinguishes between affirmation and negation.

qatr.f: When is the لام الفارقة merely permissible rather than obligatory?
qatr.b: If one of the three conditions is absent: (1) إن is heavy, (2) it is lightened but still operative, or (3) it is lightened, inoperative, and the meaning is already clear.

qatr.f: Give an example where the لام is optional because إن is heavy.
qatr.b: إن زيدًا قائم.

qatr.f: Give an example where the لام is optional because إن is lightened but still operative.
qatr.b: إن زيدًا قائم.

qatr.f: Give an example where the لام is optional because the meaning is already clear despite إن being lightened and inoperative.
qatr.b: وإن مالك كانت كرام المعادن.

qatr.f: What is the function of ظن وأخواتها among the grammatical "nawāsikh" (abrogating verbs)?
qatr.b: They are the third category of nawāsikh. They enter upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar, making both accusative as the first and second objects (مفعول أول، مفعول ثانٍ).

qatr.f: Which verbs are included among ظن وأخواتها mentioned by Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: ظن، رأى (the cognitive "to consider"), حسب، درى، خال، زعم، وجد، علم (the verbs of the heart).

qatr.f: Why are these verbs called أفعال القلوب (verbs of the heart)?
qatr.b: Because they express inner mental acts such as thinking, believing, knowing, supposing, or considering rather than physical actions.

qatr.f: What grammatical effect do ظن وأخواتها have?
qatr.b: They make the subject of the original nominal sentence the first object (مفعول أول) and the predicate the second object (مفعول ثانٍ).

qatr.f: Give an example of ظن governing two objects.
qatr.b: وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّكَ يَا فِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا ("Indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.").

qatr.f: Give an example of رأى used as a verb of the heart.
qatr.b: رَأَيْتُ اللَّهَ أَكْبَرَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ("I considered Allah greater than everything.").

qatr.f: Give an example of حسب governing two objects.
qatr.b: لَا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكُمْ ("Do not consider it evil for you.").

qatr.f: Give an example of درى governing two objects.
qatr.b: دَرَيْتُ الْوَفِيَّ الْعَهْدَ ("I knew the one faithful to his covenant.").

qatr.f: Give an example of خال governing two objects.
qatr.b: يَخَالُ بِهِ رَاعِي الْحَمُولَةِ طَائِرًا ("The camel driver imagines it to be a bird.").

qatr.f: Give an example of زعم governing two objects.
qatr.b: زَعَمْتَنِي شَيْخًا ("You claimed me to be an old man.").

qatr.f: Which verbs besides ظن are counted among the verbs of the heart according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: رأى، حسب، درى، خال، زعم، وجد، and علم.

qatr.f: What is الإلغاء (cancellation) with the verbs of the heart?
qatr.b: It is leaving the verb without grammatical effect despite its presence, so the following nominal sentence remains in its original nominative form.

qatr.f: When is الإلغاء more likely (راجحًا) with the verbs of the heart?
qatr.b: When the verb comes after the entire nominal sentence.

qatr.f: Give an example of الإلغاء when the verb comes last.
qatr.b: الْقَوْمُ فِي أَثَرِي ظَنَنْتُ ("The people are behind me, I thought.").

qatr.f: When is الإلغاء equally permissible with normal governance?
qatr.b: When the verb occurs in the middle of the sentence (توسُّط).

qatr.f: Give an example where the verb is in the middle and both governance and cancellation are possible.
qatr.b: وَفِي الْأَرَاجِيزِ خِلْتُ اللُّؤْمَ وَالْخَوَرَ.

qatr.f: What is التعليق (suspension) with the verbs of the heart?
qatr.b: It is when the verb is prevented from governing its objects in pronunciation because something follows it that requires the following clause to remain independent, although the verb still governs semantically.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical effect of التعليق?
qatr.b: The verb's governance is suspended only in wording (في اللفظ), not in meaning.

qatr.f: Which particles cause obligatory تعليق when they immediately follow a verb of the heart?
qatr.b: ما (negative), لا (negative), إن (negative), لام الابتداء, an oath (القسم), and an interrogative (الاستفهام).

qatr.f: Why does an interrogative after a verb of the heart cause التعليق?
qatr.b: Because the interrogative must remain at the beginning of its clause and cannot be governed directly by the preceding verb.

qatr.f: Give the Qur'ānic example of التعليق with an interrogative.
qatr.b: لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى ("That We may know which of the two parties is more accurate...").

qatr.f: When ما، لا، إن النافية، لام الابتداء، القسم، or الاستفهام follow a verb of the heart, what happens?
qatr.b: The verb's grammatical operation is suspended obligatorily (التعليق), though its meaning remains intact.

qatr.f: Give an example of وجد functioning as one of the verbs of the heart (أفعال القلوب).
qatr.b: تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا ("You will find it with Allah to be better and greater in reward.").

qatr.f: Give an example of علم functioning as one of the verbs of the heart.
qatr.b: فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ ("If you know them to be believing women.").

qatr.f: What are the two special grammatical rulings associated with the verbs of the heart?
qatr.b: They permit both الإلغاء (cancellation) and التعليق (suspension).

qatr.f: What is الإلغاء (cancellation) with the verbs of the heart?
qatr.b: It is cancelling the verb's grammatical operation both in wording and syntactic position (اللفظ والمحل), when the verb is between its two objects or comes after them.

qatr.f: When may الإلغاء occur?
qatr.b: When the verb is placed between the two objects (توسط) or after both objects (تأخر).

qatr.f: Give an example of الإعمال when the verb comes between its two objects.
qatr.b: زَيْدًا ظَنَنْتُ عَالِمًا ("I considered Zayd knowledgeable.").

qatr.f: Give an example of الإلغاء when the verb comes between its two objects.
qatr.b: زَيْدٌ ظَنَنْتُ عَالِمٌ ("Zayd—I thought—is knowledgeable.").

qatr.f: Give the poetic example of الإلغاء with the verb in the middle.
qatr.b: وَفِي الْأَرَاجِيزِ خِلْتُ اللُّؤْمُ وَالْخَوَرُ.

qatr.f: In the verse وفي الأراجيز خلت اللؤم والخور, why is خلت considered cancelled?
qatr.b: Because it comes between the mubtadaʾ (اللؤم) and its khabar (في الأراجيز), so the nominal sentence remains grammatically independent.

qatr.f: When the verb of the heart comes between its two objects, which is stronger according to one opinion: governance or cancellation?
qatr.b: There are two opinions: some consider both equally permissible, while others prefer governance (الإعمال).

qatr.f: Give an example of الإلغاء when the verb comes after both objects.
qatr.b: زَيْدٌ عَالِمٌ ظَنَنْتُ ("Zayd is knowledgeable, I thought.").

qatr.f: Give an example of الإعمال when the verb comes after both objects.
qatr.b: زَيْدًا عَالِمًا ظَنَنْتُ.

qatr.f: When the verb of the heart comes after both objects, which is preferred?
qatr.b: Cancellation (الإلغاء) is preferred by consensus.

qatr.f: Give the poetic example where ظننت comes after both objects.
qatr.b: الْقَوْمُ فِي أَثَرِي ظَنَنْتُ.

qatr.f: When the verb of the heart comes before both objects, may it be cancelled?
qatr.b: No. Cancellation is not allowed when the verb precedes both objects.

qatr.f: What example illustrates that cancellation is not permitted when the verb comes first?
qatr.b: One may not say ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ with nominatives; instead the verb must govern its objects.

qatr.f: Which grammarians disagreed by allowing cancellation even when the verb comes first?
qatr.b: The Kufan grammarians (الكوفيون).
