qatr.f: What is التعليق (suspension) with the verbs of the heart?
qatr.b: It is suspending the verb's grammatical operation in wording only—not in syntactic position—because something that must occupy the beginning of a clause intervenes between the verb and its objects.

qatr.f: What kinds of expressions trigger التعليق?
qatr.b: Expressions that have the right to stand at the beginning of a clause (ما له صدر الكلام), such as negative particles, the introductory lām, and interrogatives.

qatr.f: Does التعليق cancel the verb's grammatical effect completely?
qatr.b: No. It cancels the effect only in wording (اللفظ), while the verb still governs the clause syntactically (في المحل).

qatr.f: Give an example of التعليق caused by ما negative.
qatr.b: عَلِمْتُ مَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ.

qatr.f: Give the Qur'ānic example of التعليق caused by ما negative.
qatr.b: لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ.

qatr.f: In لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون, why are هؤلاء and ينطقون not the two objects of علمت?
qatr.b: Because ما triggers suspension (التعليق), leaving هؤلاء as the mubtadaʾ and ينطقون as its khabar.

qatr.f: Give an example of التعليق caused by لا negative.
qatr.b: عَلِمْتُ لَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ وَلَا عَمْرٌو.

qatr.f: Give the Qur'ānic example of التعليق caused by إن negative.
qatr.b: وَتَظُنُّونَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا.

qatr.f: In the verse وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا, what does إن mean?
qatr.b: It is a negative particle meaning ما ("You thought that you had stayed only a little.").

qatr.f: Give an example of التعليق caused by لام الابتداء.
qatr.b: عَلِمْتُ لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ.

qatr.f: Give the Qur'ānic example of التعليق caused by لام الابتداء.
qatr.b: وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ.

qatr.f: Give an example of التعليق caused by the lām of oath (لام القسم).
qatr.b: وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ لَتَأْتِيَنَّ مَنِيَّتِي.

qatr.f: Give an example of التعليق caused by an interrogative sentence.
qatr.b: عَلِمْتُ أَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ؟

qatr.f: Does an interrogative noun anywhere in the clause trigger التعليق?
qatr.b: Yes, whether it is one of the two main parts of the clause or an additional element (فضلة).

qatr.f: Give the Qur'ānic example where the interrogative is one of the main parts of the clause.
qatr.b: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى.

qatr.f: Give the Qur'ānic example where the interrogative is an additional element (فضلة).
qatr.b: وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ.

qatr.f: In وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أي منقلب ينقلبون, what is the grammatical role of أيَّ منقلب?
qatr.b: It is the cognate accusative (مصدر) of ينقلبون, not the object of يعلم.

qatr.f: Why is it incorrect to parse أيَّ in وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أي منقلب ينقلبون as the object of يعلم?
qatr.b: Because interrogatives have the right to stand at the beginning of their clause, preventing the preceding verb from governing them directly.

qatr.f: Why is this type of cancellation called تعليق ("suspension")?
qatr.b: Because the verb is simultaneously operative in syntactic position but inoperative in wording, resembling a "suspended" state.

qatr.f: To what does Ibn Hishām compare a suspended verb?
qatr.b: To a woman who is suspended (المعلقة): neither fully married nor divorced.

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām define the woman who is suspended (المعلقة)?
qatr.b: She is a woman whose husband mistreats her so that she is neither properly married nor divorced.

qatr.f: What evidence shows that the suspended verb still governs the clause syntactically?
qatr.b: A coordinated noun may be joined to the syntactic position of the suspended clause in the accusative.

qatr.f: Which poetic example proves that a suspended verb still governs syntactically?
qatr.b: وَمَا كُنْتُ أَدْرِي قَبْلَ عَزَّةَ مَا لِبُكْيِ وَلَا مُوجِعَاتِ الْقَلْبِ حَتَّى تَوَلَّتْ.

qatr.f: In the verse وما كنت أدري قبل عزة ما لبكي ولا موجعات القلب, why is موجعات accusative?
qatr.b: Because it is coordinated to the syntactic position (محل) of the suspended clause governed by أدري, proving that the verb still governs in syntactic position though not in wording.

qatr.f: According to Ibn Hishām, what is the definition of the فاعل (subject) in Arabic grammar?
qatr.b: The فاعل is an explicit noun, or something interpreted as a noun, to which a verb (or something interpreted as a verb) is primarily attributed before it, with the action either issuing from it or subsisting in it.

qatr.f: What grammatical case is the فاعل (subject) always in?
qatr.b: The فاعل is always nominative (مرفوع).

qatr.f: Give two examples of a فاعل that illustrate that it is nominative.
qatr.b: قام زيدٌ ("Zayd stood.") and مات عمروٌ ("ʿAmr died.").

qatr.f: Does the definition of فاعل require that the verb (or its equivalent) precede the subject?
qatr.b: Yes. The verb (or what is interpreted as a verb) must precede the فاعل.

qatr.f: Can the فاعل be something other than an explicit noun?
qatr.b: Yes. It may be an explicit noun or something interpreted as a noun (مؤول بالاسم).

qatr.f: Can a verbal expression interpreted as a noun function as the فاعل? Give an example.
qatr.b: Yes. In ﴿ألم يأن للذين آمنوا أن تخشع قلوبهم﴾, أن تخشع is interpreted as الخشوع and functions as the فاعل.

qatr.f: Can something interpreted as a verb govern a فاعل? Give an example.
qatr.b: Yes. In مختلف ألوانه, مختلف is interpreted as يختلف, making ألوانه the فاعل.

qatr.f: Why is زيد in زيد قام not considered a فاعل?
qatr.b: Because the verb comes after زيد. The sentence is nominal: زيد is the مبتدأ, while قام and its hidden subject form the predicate.

qatr.f: Why is زيد in قائم زيد not considered a فاعل?
qatr.b: Because قائم is a predicate that is only notionally before the subject; زيد is not the subject of a preceding verb.

qatr.f: Why is زيد in ضُرب زيد not considered a فاعل?
qatr.b: Because the action is done to Zayd, not by him; he is the recipient of the action, not the doer.

qatr.f: Does being called a فاعل necessarily mean the noun actually performs the action?
qatr.b: No. A فاعل is the noun to which the verb is grammatically attributed, even if it did not actively perform the action.

qatr.f: Why is عمرو in مات عمرو still called a فاعل although he did not cause his own death?
qatr.b: Because the verb مات is grammatically attributed to عمرو, even though he did not perform the act of dying upon himself.

qatr.f: May the governing verb come after the فاعل in a verbal sentence?
qatr.b: No. The governing verb must precede the فاعل in a verbal sentence.

qatr.f: Why is أخواك قام grammatically incorrect as a verbal sentence?
qatr.b: Because it places the فاعل before the verb. If أخواك comes first, it becomes a مبتدأ, making the sentence nominal.

qatr.f: How should أخواك be expressed if it precedes the verb?
qatr.b: One should say أخواك قاما, where أخواك is the مبتدأ and قاما is the verbal sentence serving as the predicate.

qatr.f: When a dual or plural subject follows its verb, does Classical Arabic normally attach dual or plural markers to the verb?
qatr.b: No. The verb normally remains singular.

qatr.f: How are the sentences "Two men stood," "Men stood," and "Women stood" normally expressed in Classical Arabic?
qatr.b: قام رجلان، قام رجال، قام نساء.

qatr.f: Is it standard Classical Arabic to say قاما رجلان or قاموا رجال?
qatr.b: No. The standard language keeps the verb singular before a following subject.

qatr.f: Did some Arabs use dialects that attached dual or plural markers to the verb before the subject?
qatr.b: Yes. Some dialects allowed forms such as يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة.

qatr.f: When is the feminine marker attached to a past-tense verb whose subject is feminine?
qatr.b: It is attached according to the rules governing feminine subjects, either obligatorily or optionally depending on the situation.

qatr.f: Give an example where feminine agreement with the subject is obligatory.
qatr.b: قامت هند.

qatr.f: Is feminine agreement obligatory with a figuratively feminine noun such as الشمس?
qatr.b: No. Both masculine and feminine verb forms are permissible, although the feminine is preferred.

qatr.f: Which is more eloquent with the figuratively feminine noun الشمس: طلعت الشمس or طلع الشمس?
qatr.b: طلعت الشمس is more eloquent, though both are permissible.

qatr.f: What is meant by a figuratively feminine noun (مجازي التأنيث)?
qatr.b: It is a noun treated grammatically as feminine but not referring to a biologically female being, such as الشمس.

qatr.f: In how many situations is feminine agreement with the verb optional according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: In four situations.

qatr.f: When the subject is an explicit figuratively feminine noun, is feminine agreement obligatory or optional?
qatr.b: It is optional, though feminine agreement is preferred.

qatr.f: When a truly feminine subject is separated from its verb by words other than إلا, is feminine agreement obligatory or optional?
qatr.b: It is optional, though feminine agreement is more eloquent.

qatr.f: Give an example where a truly feminine subject is separated from the verb and both agreements are allowed.
qatr.b: حضرت القاضي امرأة and حضر القاضي امرأة.

qatr.f: When the governing word is نعم or بئس, is feminine agreement with a feminine subject obligatory?
qatr.b: No. Both masculine and feminine agreement are permissible.

qatr.f: Give an example showing optional feminine agreement with نعم.
qatr.b: نعمت المرأة هند and نعم المرأة هند.

qatr.f: When the subject is a non-sound plural, is feminine agreement obligatory?
qatr.b: No. Both masculine and feminine agreement are permissible.

qatr.f: Why may non-sound plurals take either masculine or feminine agreement?
qatr.b: The feminine treats the noun as a collective (الجماعة), while the masculine treats it as a grammatical plural (الجمع).

qatr.f: Do sound masculine and sound feminine plurals follow the same agreement rule as broken plurals?
qatr.b: No. They follow the same agreement rules as their singular forms.

qatr.f: How should the verb agree with a sound masculine plural subject?
qatr.b: As with a singular masculine noun, e.g. قام الزيدون.

qatr.f: How should the verb agree with a sound feminine plural subject?
qatr.b: As with a singular feminine noun, e.g. قامت الهندات.

qatr.f: In which two situations is feminine agreement with the verb obligatory?
qatr.b: (1) When the subject is a truly feminine noun that is adjacent to the verb and not after نعم or بئس. (2) When the subject is a connected feminine pronoun.

qatr.f: Give an example where a truly feminine noun requires feminine agreement because it immediately follows the verb.
qatr.b: إذ قالت امرأة عمران.

qatr.f: Give an example where a connected feminine pronoun requires feminine agreement.
qatr.b: الشمس طلعت.

qatr.f: Why is ما قامت إلا هند considered incorrect in ordinary prose according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Because the true grammatical subject is an omitted masculine noun such as أحد, while هند is a substitute (بدل) after إلا.

qatr.f: What is the implied underlying sentence behind ما قام إلا هند?
qatr.b: ما قام أحدٌ إلا هند.

qatr.f: Why is the verb masculine in ما قام إلا هند even though هند is feminine?
qatr.b: Because the verb agrees with the omitted masculine subject (أحد), not with هند.

qatr.f: Name one context in which Arabic regularly permits omission of the فاعل.
qatr.b: After إلا, as in ما قام إلا هند, where the omitted subject is understood to be أحد.

qatr.f: Name another context in which Arabic regularly permits omission of the فاعل.
qatr.b: With a verbal noun (المصدر), such as أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيماً.

qatr.f: What are the four cases in which the subject (فاعل) is obligatorily omitted according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: The subject is obligatorily omitted in four cases: (1) the subject of a verbal noun (فاعل المصدر), e.g. ﴿أو إطعامٌ في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيماً﴾, meaning or that he feeds an orphan; (2) in the passive voice (باب النيابة), e.g. ﴿وقضي الأمر﴾, whose original form is وقضى الله الأمر; (3) the subject of أفعل in the exclamatory construction when indicated by a preceding expression, e.g. ﴿أسمع بهم وأبصر﴾, where the omitted phrase is بهم; and (4) the case mentioned previously of ما قام إلا هند, whose true subject is an omitted masculine noun (أحد).

qatr.f: What is the basic word order of the verb, subject, and object?
qatr.b: The basic order is verb → subject → object, because the verb and its subject are treated almost as a single unit.

qatr.f: When may the subject come after the object?
qatr.b: The subject may follow the object either permissibly (جوازًا) or obligatorily (وجوبًا).

qatr.f: When is postponing the subject after the object merely permissible?
qatr.b: It is permissible when no ambiguity or grammatical problem results, such as ﴿ولقد جاء آلَ فرعونَ النذرُ﴾, where النذر (the subject) follows آل فرعون (the object).

qatr.f: Why is the word order in ﴿ولقد جاء آلَ فرعونَ النذرُ﴾ permissible?
qatr.b: Because if the order were reversed to جاء النذرُ آلَ فرعونَ, the pronoun would still refer to something preceding it in wording and rank, which is grammatically acceptable.

qatr.f: When is postponing the subject after the object obligatory?
qatr.b: It is obligatory when advancing the subject would create an invalid grammatical construction, such as an unacceptable backward pronoun reference or separation of an attached pronoun from its verb.

qatr.f: Why must the subject remain after the object in ﴿وإذ ابتلى إبراهيمَ ربُّه﴾?
qatr.b: Because changing it to ابتلى ربُّه إبراهيمَ would make the pronoun in ربه refer forward to إبراهيم, which is not allowed.

qatr.f: Why must the subject follow the attached object pronoun in ضربني زيدٌ?
qatr.b: Because changing it to ضرب زيدٌ إياي would unnecessarily separate the object pronoun from the verb even though an attached pronoun is possible.

qatr.f: When must the object be postponed after the subject?
qatr.b: The object must be postponed when advancing it would create ambiguity about which noun is the subject and which is the object.

qatr.f: Why must the object follow the subject in ضرب موسى عيسى?
qatr.b: Because without any contextual clue, advancing عيسى would make it impossible to determine which noun is the subject and which is the object.

qatr.f: What kinds of clues permit either the subject or the object to come first?
qatr.b: Either semantic clues (قرينة معنوية), such as أرضعت الصغرى الكبرى or أكل الكمثرى موسى, or grammatical clues (قرينة لفظية), such as ضربت موسى سلمى or ضرب موسى العاقل عيسى, remove ambiguity and allow either order.

qatr.f: Why is أرضعت الصغرى الكبرى unambiguous despite the object preceding the subject?
qatr.b: Because the meaning itself makes it clear that the younger one nurses the older one, identifying the grammatical roles.

qatr.f: Why is ضربت موسى سلمى unambiguous despite the order?
qatr.b: Because the verb ending -تُ identifies the speaker as the subject, leaving موسى as the object.

qatr.f: Why may the object not precede both the verb and the subject in ambiguous sentences like ضرب موسى عيسى?
qatr.b: Because beginning with the object could make it appear to be the subject (or an initial noun with the verb containing an implied pronoun), leading to ambiguity.

qatr.f: When may the object precede the verb itself?
qatr.b: The object may precede the verb when there is no ambiguity, as in ﴿فريقًا هدى﴾.

qatr.f: When must the object precede the verb?
qatr.b: It must precede the verb when it has something that requires sentence-initial position, such as a conditional or interrogative noun.

qatr.f: Why must أيًّا come before the verb in ﴿أيًّا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى﴾?
qatr.b: Because أيًّا is a conditional noun, and conditional nouns must occupy the beginning of the clause.

qatr.f: What three forms may the subject of نِعم and بِئس take?
qatr.b: The subject may be: (1) a noun with the generic definite article أل, (2) a noun annexed to a word containing أل, or (3) an implied pronoun explained by a following accusative specification (تمييز).

qatr.f: Give an example of a subject of نعم or بئس that is a noun with أل.
qatr.b: نعم العبد.

qatr.f: Give an example of a subject of نعم or بئس that is annexed to a noun containing أل.
qatr.b: ﴿ولنعم دار المتقين﴾.

qatr.f: Give an example of a hidden pronoun subject explained by a تمييز after بئس.
qatr.b: ﴿بئس للظالمين بدلاً﴾, whose underlying meaning is بئس هو بدلاً.

qatr.f: What comes after نعم or بئس once their subject has been completed?
qatr.b: The noun specifically praised or blamed (المخصوص بالمدح أو الذم), e.g. نعم الرجل زيد or نعم رجلاً زيد.

qatr.f: How is the مخصوص in نعم الرجل زيد parsed?
qatr.b: It is a postponed subject (مبتدأ), while the preceding clause is its predicate, linked by the general meaning conveyed by أل.

qatr.f: May the مخصوص precede the subject of نعم or بئس?
qatr.b: No. By consensus it may not precede the subject. Therefore نعم زيد الرجل is incorrect.

qatr.f: May the مخصوص precede the تمييز after نعم or بئس?
qatr.b: No, according to the majority. Thus نعم زيد رجلاً is not accepted, though the Kufans allowed it.

qatr.f: May the مخصوص precede the entire نعم/بئس clause?
qatr.b: Yes. It may precede both the verb and its subject, as in زيد نعم الرجل.

qatr.f: May the مخصوص be omitted?
qatr.b: Yes, if the context clearly identifies it.

qatr.f: Give an example where the مخصوص is omitted after نعم.
qatr.b: ﴿إنا وجدناه صابرًا نعم العبد إنه أواب﴾, where the omitted مخصوص is هو (i.e., Ayyūb).

qatr.f: When the original subject (الفاعل) is omitted, what normally becomes the نائب الفاعل (deputy subject)?
qatr.b: The direct object (المفعول به) normally becomes the نائب الفاعل and takes all the grammatical rulings of the original subject.

qatr.f: What grammatical properties does the نائب الفاعل inherit from the omitted subject?
qatr.b: It becomes nominative (مرفوع), becomes an essential sentence element (عمدة), must follow the verb, and the verb agrees with it in gender where applicable.

qatr.f: Besides the direct object, what elements may become the نائب الفاعل if no direct object exists?
qatr.b: A qualifying adverb (ظرف مختص متصرف), a qualifying prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور), or a qualifying verbal noun (مصدر مختص متصرف) may become the نائب الفاعل.

qatr.f: What are the three reasons for omitting the original subject (الفاعل)?
qatr.b: The subject may be omitted because it is unknown, for a stylistic purpose (such as preserving rhyme), or for a rhetorical or semantic purpose where mentioning it serves no benefit.

qatr.f: In the passive sentence سُرِقَ المتاعُ, why is the original subject omitted?
qatr.b: The subject is omitted because it is unknown (the thief is not known).

qatr.f: In the saying من طابت سريرته حُمِدت سيرته, why is the original subject omitted?
qatr.b: The subject is omitted for a stylistic purpose, because mentioning الناس would spoil the rhetorical style or rhyme (السجع).

qatr.f: In the Qur'anic verse ﴿إذا قيل لكم تفسحوا في المجالس﴾, why is the original subject omitted?
qatr.b: The subject is omitted because the identity of the speaker is irrelevant to the intended meaning.

qatr.f: How is the active sentence ضرب زيدٌ عمراً converted into the passive?
qatr.b: It becomes ضُرِبَ عمروٌ, where عمرو changes from the direct object to the نائب الفاعل.

qatr.f: How is the active sentence ضرب زيدٌ هندًا converted into the passive?
qatr.b: It becomes ضُرِبَتْ هندٌ, where هند becomes the نائب الفاعل and the verb is feminine because the deputy subject is feminine.

qatr.f: Under what conditions may an adverb (ظرف) become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: It may become the نائب الفاعل only if there is no direct object and the adverb is both specific (مختص) and declinable (متصرف).

qatr.f: What is an example of an adverb serving as نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: سِيرَ فرسخٌ ("A farsakh was travelled.").

qatr.f: Under what conditions may a verbal noun (مصدر) become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: It may become the نائب الفاعل only if there is no direct object and the verbal noun is both specific (مختص) and declinable (متصرف).

qatr.f: What is an example of a verbal noun serving as نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: جُلِسَ جلوسُ الأميرِ ("The ruler's manner of sitting was performed.").

qatr.f: Under what conditions may a prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور) become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: It may become the نائب الفاعل only when there is no direct object available to take its place.

qatr.f: What is an example of a prepositional phrase serving as نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: مُرَّ بزيدٍ ("Zayd was passed by.").

qatr.f: What three conditions must an adverb or verbal noun satisfy before it may become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: It must be (1) specific (مختص), (2) declinable (متصرف), and (3) used in a sentence that contains no direct object.

qatr.f: Why can the verbal noun in ضُرِبَ ضربٌ not become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: Because ضرب is indefinite and not specific (غير مختص).

qatr.f: How can the verbal noun in ضُرِبَ ضربٌ شديدٌ become eligible to serve as نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: By being qualified with an adjective (شديد), which makes it specific (مختص).

qatr.f: Why can the adverb in صِيمَ زمنٌ not become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: Because زمن is indefinite and not specific.

qatr.f: How can the adverb in صِيمَ زمنٌ طويلٌ become eligible to serve as نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: By adding a descriptive adjective (طويل) that makes it specific.

qatr.f: Why can the noun in اعتُكِفَ مكانٌ not become the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: Because مكان is indefinite and not specific.

qatr.f: How can the noun in اعتُكِفَ مكانٌ حسنٌ become eligible to serve as نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: By adding the adjective حسن, making it a specific location.

qatr.f: Why can سبحان not serve as the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: Because it is non-declinable (غير متصرف) and is permanently used as a verbal noun.

qatr.f: Why can إذا not serve as the نائب الفاعل?
qatr.b: Because it is non-declinable (غير متصرف) and permanently functions as an adverb of time.

qatr.f: According to the majority of grammarians, may an adverb, verbal noun, or prepositional phrase become the نائب الفاعل if a direct object is present?
qatr.b: No. If a direct object exists, it alone should become the نائب الفاعل.

qatr.f: Which grammarians allowed a non-direct-object to become the نائب الفاعل even when a direct object is present?
qatr.b: Al-Akhfash and the Kufan grammarians.

qatr.f: Which Qur'anic reading did Al-Akhfash and the Kufans cite as evidence that a prepositional phrase may become the نائب الفاعل despite the presence of a direct object?
qatr.b: They cited the reading ﴿ليجزى قوماً بما كانوا يكسبون﴾, where بما appears to function as the نائب الفاعل despite the presence of قوماً.

qatr.f: How did Ibn Hishām respond to the evidence from the reading ﴿ليجزى قوماً بما كانوا يكسبون﴾?
qatr.b: He replied that the reading is irregular (شاذة), or that the true نائب الفاعل is an omitted pronoun referring to الغفران, understood from the previous verse.

qatr.f: How is a regular past-tense verb changed when converting it to the passive voice?
qatr.b: The first letter takes ḍammah (ضمة) and the penultimate letter takes kasrah (كسرة), e.g. ضَرَبَ → ضُرِبَ.

qatr.f: How is a regular present-tense verb changed when converting it to the passive voice?
qatr.b: The first letter takes ḍammah (ضمة) and the penultimate letter takes fatḥah (فتحة), e.g. يَضرِبُ → يُضرَبُ.

qatr.f: How is a Form V verb such as تعلَّم changed into the passive?
qatr.b: The first letter and the second root letter both receive ḍammah, giving تُعُلِّمَ according to the classical rule described by Ibn Hishām.

qatr.f: How is a verb beginning with hamzat al-waṣl, such as انطلق, changed into the passive?
qatr.b: The hamzah and the following consonant both receive ḍammah, producing اُنطُلِقَ.

qatr.f: Which Qur'anic example illustrates the passive pattern for a verb beginning with hamzat al-waṣl?
qatr.b: ﴿فمن اضطُرَّ﴾, where the initial hamzah and the following consonant are both pronounced with ḍammah at the beginning of the word.

qatr.f: What are the three permissible passive pronunciations of hollow triliteral verbs such as قال and باع?
qatr.b: (1) Pure kasrah before the weak letter (قِيلَ، بِيعَ), (2) ishmām (a pronunciation between kasrah and ḍammah), and (3) pure ḍammah (قُولَ، بُوعَ).

qatr.f: Which passive pronunciation of hollow triliteral verbs is considered the most eloquent (أفصح)?
qatr.b: The pronunciation with pure kasrah before the weak letter, such as قِيلَ and بِيعَ.

qatr.f: What is ishmām in the passive pronunciation of hollow triliteral verbs?
qatr.b: Ishmām is pronouncing the vowel primarily as kasrah while slightly indicating ḍammah to reflect the verb's original form.

qatr.f: Which passive pronunciation of hollow triliteral verbs is considered rare?
qatr.b: The pronunciation with pure ḍammah, producing forms such as قُولَ and بُوعَ.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical definition of باب الاشتغال (the chapter of Ishtighāl)?
qatr.b: Ishtighāl occurs when a noun precedes a verb, and that verb is occupied by working on a pronoun referring back to the noun (or on a noun connected to that pronoun), such that if the pronoun or related noun were removed, the verb could govern the preceding noun directly. Example: زيدًا ضربته ("Zayd—I struck him").

qatr.f: In the construction زيدًا ضربته, what are the two permissible analyses of زيد?
qatr.b: زيد may be raised as a mubtadaʾ, with ضربته as its khabar, or accusative through an obligatorily omitted verb (e.g. ضربت زيدًا) explained by the following verb.

qatr.f: Why must the omitted verb in the accusative analysis of Ishtighāl be omitted?
qatr.b: Because the following verb serves as its interpreter (مفسر), making its explicit mention unnecessary and grammatically impermissible.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical status of the following sentence when the preceding noun is parsed as a mubtadaʾ?
qatr.b: The following sentence is the predicate (khabar) of the mubtadaʾ.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical status of the following sentence when the preceding noun is parsed with an omitted verb?
qatr.b: The sentence has no syntactic position (لا محل لها) because it merely explains the omitted verb.

qatr.f: Why is the omitted verb in زيدًا مررت به estimated as جاوزت rather than مررت?
qatr.b: Because مررت cannot govern a noun directly without a preposition, whereas the omitted verb must be capable of governing the accusative noun directly.

qatr.f: Why is the omitted verb in زيدًا ضربت أخاه estimated as أهنت rather than ضربت?
qatr.b: Because the explicit verb ضربت governs أخاه, not زيدًا; therefore another suitable verb, such as أهنت, must be supplied for the omitted verb.

qatr.f: Into how many categories does the ruling on the preceding noun in Ishtighāl fall?
qatr.b: Five: (1) accusative preferred, (2) accusative obligatory, (3) nominative preferred, (4) nominative obligatory, and (5) both equally permissible.

qatr.f: When is the accusative preferred in Ishtighāl because the following verb is a verb of request?
qatr.b: When the following verb is an imperative, prohibition, or supplication, e.g. زيدًا اضربه، زيدًا لا تهنه، اللهم عبدك ارحمه.

qatr.f: Why is the accusative preferred when the following verb is a verb of request?
qatr.b: Because raising the noun would make a declarative sentence consist of a predicate that is a request, and request sentences do not naturally function as informative predicates since they are neither true nor false.

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām explain the Qur'anic nominative in والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما despite the following imperative?
qatr.b: He explains that السارق والسارقة are mubtadaʾs whose predicate is omitted (e.g. "their ruling is..."), while فاقطعوا begins a new independent sentence.

qatr.f: What alternative explanation does al-Mubarrad give for والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما?
qatr.b: He holds that أل has the meaning of الذي, and the فاء is the fāʾ of consequence, which prevents the following verb from governing what precedes it.

qatr.f: When is the accusative preferred because of stylistic parallelism?
qatr.b: When the noun follows a conjunction preceded by a verbal sentence, e.g. قام زيد وعمراً أكرمته, so that both coordinated clauses remain verbal.

qatr.f: Why is the accusative preferred in قام زيد وعمراً أكرمته?
qatr.b: Because it preserves parallelism by coordinating one verbal sentence with another instead of mixing a verbal sentence with a nominal sentence.

qatr.f: Why is والأنعام خلقها parsed with the accusative according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Because it follows the verbal sentence خلق الإنسان, so the accusative preserves stylistic correspondence between coordinated verbal clauses.

qatr.f: When is the accusative preferred because of the preceding particle?
qatr.b: When the noun is preceded by a particle that usually introduces verbs, such as the interrogative hamzah or ما, e.g. أزيدًا ضربته؟ and ما زيدًا رأيته.

qatr.f: When is the accusative obligatory in Ishtighāl?
qatr.b: When the noun is preceded by a particle restricted to entering verbs, such as conditional or exhortative particles, e.g. إن زيدًا رأيته فأكرمه and هلا زيدًا أكرمته.

qatr.f: Why is the accusative obligatory after conditional or exhortative particles?
qatr.b: Because these particles only govern verbal constructions, requiring an implied governing verb before the noun.

qatr.f: When is the nominative obligatory in Ishtighāl?
qatr.b: When the noun is preceded by a particle that only enters nominal sentences, such as إذا الفجائية, e.g. خرجت فإذا زيدٌ يضربه عمرو.

qatr.f: Why is the nominative obligatory after إذا الفجائية?
qatr.b: Because إذا الفجائية only introduces nominal sentences, whereas the accusative analysis requires an implied verb, producing a verbal construction.

qatr.f: When are both the nominative and accusative equally permissible in Ishtighāl?
qatr.b: When the noun follows a conjunction preceded by a larger sentence whose beginning is nominal and whose ending is verbal, e.g. زيد قام أبوه وعمراً أكرمته.

qatr.f: Why are both analyses equally valid in زيد قام أبوه وعمراً أكرمته?
qatr.b: Because the preceding sentence may be viewed either as nominal (favoring the nominative) or as verbal in its latter part (favoring the accusative), giving equal syntactic correspondence.

qatr.f: When is the nominative preferred in Ishtighāl?
qatr.b: In all ordinary cases where no stronger factor favors the accusative, e.g. زيد ضربته.

qatr.f: Why is the nominative preferred in ordinary Ishtighāl constructions?
qatr.b: Because the nominative analysis is the default grammatical principle unless another factor outweighs it.

qatr.f: Why is وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر not an example of Ishtighāl?
qatr.b: Because the intended meaning is not "they did everything," but "everything they did is recorded in the scriptures," so the verb cannot logically govern the preceding noun.

qatr.f: Why is the nominative obligatory in وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر?
qatr.b: Because the delayed verb functions as a descriptive clause (صفة) rather than a governing verb, so it cannot govern the preceding noun.

qatr.f: Why is أزيد ذهب به not considered an example of Ishtighāl?
qatr.b: Because even if the verb were redirected, it could not govern زيد in the accusative, so the defining condition of Ishtighāl is absent.

qatr.f: What is التنازع (Tanāzuʿ) in Arabic grammar?
qatr.b: Tanāzuʿ is the construction in which two or more governing words (usually verbs) precede one or more delayed dependents, and each governor is capable of governing the same dependent. It is also called باب الإعمال.

qatr.f: What is the general rule regarding governance in باب التنازع?
qatr.b: Either of the competing governors may be allowed to govern the shared dependent; the disagreement among grammarians concerns only which choice is preferable, not which is permissible.

qatr.f: Which school prefers assigning the shared dependent to the first governor in باب التنازع?
qatr.b: The Kufans prefer assigning the shared dependent to the first governor because it comes first.

qatr.f: Which school prefers assigning the shared dependent to the second (nearest) governor in باب التنازع?
qatr.b: The Basrans prefer assigning the shared dependent to the last (nearest) governor because of its proximity to the shared dependent.

qatr.f: Give an example of two verbs competing for one shared object in باب التنازع.
qatr.b: Allah's statement: آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا. Both آتوني and أفرغ seek an object, while قطرًا comes after both and could theoretically belong to either.

qatr.f: Give an example of two verbs competing for more than one dependent in باب التنازع.
qatr.b: ضرب وأكرم زيدٌ عمرًا. The verbs compete over the delayed subject and object.

qatr.f: Give an example of more than two governors competing for one shared dependent in باب التنازع.
qatr.b: صليت وباركت وترحمت على إبراهيم. The prepositional phrase على إبراهيم is sought by all three verbs.

qatr.f: Give an example of more than two governors competing for more than one shared dependent in باب التنازع.
qatr.b: In the hadith: تسبحون وتحمدون وتكبرون دبر كل صلاة ثلاثًا وثلاثين. Both دبر كل صلاة and ثلاثًا وثلاثين are shared among the three verbs.

qatr.f: If the first governor is made operative in باب التنازع, what must be supplied for the second governor?
qatr.b: Every argument required by the second governor (subject, object, or prepositional complement) must be represented by an appropriate pronoun.

qatr.f: Why is it permissible for the pronoun to refer back to a noun that comes later in wording when the first governor is operative?
qatr.b: Because the disputed noun is considered to occupy its original intended position before the verbs in the underlying structure, making it conceptually earlier even though it appears later in wording.

qatr.f: If the second governor is made operative in باب التنازع, what is supplied for the first governor?
qatr.b: Only its required subject is supplied as a pronoun; required objects or prepositional complements are omitted rather than replaced with pronouns.

qatr.f: When the second governor is operative, why is only the omitted subject represented by a pronoun?
qatr.b: Because the subject cannot simply be omitted, whereas objects and prepositional complements may be omitted if understood from the context.

qatr.f: Why should one not say ضربتهما وضربني أخواك when the second verb is operative?
qatr.b: Because this would require a pronoun object referring to a noun that is later both in wording and rank, which is not permitted for objects.

qatr.f: Why should one not say مررت بهما ومر بي أخواك when the second verb is operative?
qatr.b: Because a delayed antecedent is only tolerated for the indispensable subject pronoun, not for object or prepositional pronouns.

qatr.f: Why is the verse ولو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة كفاني ولم أطلب قليلًا من المال not an example of باب التنازع?
qatr.b: Because the two verbs are not genuinely seeking the same object; making both govern قليلًا would produce a contradiction in meaning.

qatr.f: What essential condition must exist for a construction to qualify as باب التنازع?
qatr.b: All competing governors must genuinely seek the same dependent in meaning as well as in grammar.

qatr.f: Why would making كفاني and أطلب both govern قليلًا corrupt the meaning of the verse?
qatr.b: Because لو reverses the polarity of the clauses, making the interpretation imply both the affirmation and negation of seeking a small amount of wealth simultaneously.

qatr.f: How does Ibn Hishām explain the omitted object of أطلب in the verse ولم أطلب قليلًا من المال?
qatr.b: He explains that its omitted object is something like الملك ("kingship"), not قليلًا من المال, thereby preserving the intended meaning.

qatr.f: Why cannot the second clause in that verse simply be treated as an independent sentence to preserve باب التنازع?
qatr.b: Because Tanāzuʿ requires a grammatical connection between the competing governors, whereas treating the second clause as independent removes that required connection.

qatr.f: What is the general grammatical case of the مفعول (object)?
qatr.b: Every mafʿūl is accusative (منصوب).

qatr.f: Why is the subject always nominative while the object is accusative according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Because there is normally only one subject but there may be many objects; therefore the heavier case (nominative) is reserved for the less frequent element, while the lighter case (accusative) is used for the more frequent one.

qatr.f: According to the correct opinion, how many categories of mafʿūl are there?
qatr.b: Five: المفعول به، المفعول المطلق، المفعول فيه (الظرف)، المفعول له، المفعول معه.

qatr.f: What are the five accepted categories of mafʿūl?
qatr.b: (1) Direct object (المفعول به), (2) Absolute object (المفعول المطلق), (3) Adverbial object/time-place (المفعول فيه), (4) Object of purpose (المفعول له), and (5) Accompaniment object (المفعول معه).

qatr.f: How did al-Zajjāj classify المفعول معه?
qatr.b: He did not recognize it as a separate category and instead analyzed it as a direct object with an implied verb.

qatr.f: How did the Kufans classify المفعول له?
qatr.b: They treated it as a type of المفعول المطلق, not as an independent category.

qatr.f: What sixth category did al-Sīrāfī add to the objects?
qatr.b: He added المفعول منه, as in واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلاً, interpreting the meaning as "from his people."

qatr.f: What additional category did al-Jawharī call a mafʿūl?
qatr.b: He referred to the exception (المستثنى) as a type of mafʿūl.

qatr.f: What is the definition of المفعول به (the direct object)?
qatr.b: It is the noun upon which the action of the subject falls, such as زيدًا in ضربت زيدًا.

qatr.f: How did Ibn al-Ḥājib answer the objection that the definition of المفعول به does not fit negative or future sentences such as ما ضربت زيدًا or لا تضرب زيدًا?
qatr.b: He explained that "the action falling upon it" means the object's grammatical dependence on the verb for its meaning, not the actual occurrence of the action.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical origin of the vocative (المنادى) according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: The vocative is originally a direct object (مفعول به). For example, يا عبد الله is originally أدعو عبدَ الله, where the verb is omitted and يا takes its place.

qatr.f: In which three cases is the vocative noun accusative (منصوب) in form?
qatr.b: It is accusative when it is: (1) an iḍāfah (مضاف), (2) similar to an iḍāfah (شبيه بالمضاف), or (3) an indefinite noun not intended to refer to a specific person (نكرة غير مقصودة).

qatr.f: When is a vocative noun considered an iḍāfah (مضاف), and how is it declined?
qatr.b: When it is annexed to another noun, such as يا عبدَ الله or يا رسولَ الله. It is declined in the accusative.

qatr.f: What is a "similar to an iḍāfah" (شبيه بالمضاف) in the chapter of the vocative?
qatr.b: It is a noun completed in meaning by something attached to it, even though it is not formally an iḍāfah. It is treated like an iḍāfah and is accusative.

qatr.f: How can a vocative noun be similar to an iḍāfah through a following subject?
qatr.b: When a nominative complement completes its meaning, e.g. يا محمودًا فعلُه ("O one whose actions are praiseworthy").

qatr.f: How can a vocative noun be similar to an iḍāfah through a following object?
qatr.b: When it is completed by an accusative object, e.g. يا طالعًا جبلًا ("O climber of a mountain").

qatr.f: How can a vocative noun be similar to an iḍāfah through a prepositional phrase?
qatr.b: When it is completed by a preposition and its object, e.g. يا رفيقًا بالعباد or يا خيرًا من زيد.

qatr.f: How can coordination make a vocative noun similar to an iḍāfah?
qatr.b: If it is coordinated with another word before the vocative, such as يا ثلاثةً وثلاثين used as a proper name.

qatr.f: When is an indefinite noun (نكرة) accusative in the vocative?
qatr.b: When it is not intended to refer to a particular individual, such as يا رجلًا خذ بيدي ("O man, take my hand").

qatr.f: What two conditions make a vocative noun indeclinable (مبني)?
qatr.b: It must be single (not an iḍāfah or similar to one) and definite (or intended to refer to a particular person).

qatr.f: What does "single" (مفرد) mean in the chapter of the vocative?
qatr.b: It means the noun is neither an iḍāfah nor similar to an iḍāfah.

qatr.f: What does "definite" (معرفة) mean in the chapter of the vocative?
qatr.b: It means either originally definite (e.g. زيد) or made definite by directly addressing a particular person (e.g. يا رجل intending one specific man).

qatr.f: How is a singular definite vocative noun declined?
qatr.b: It is built (مبني) on the case sign it would have if it were nominative, e.g. يا زيدُ.

qatr.f: How is a dual definite vocative noun declined?
qatr.b: It is built on the alif, e.g. يا زيدانِ.

qatr.f: How is a sound masculine plural definite vocative noun declined?
qatr.b: It is built on the wāw, e.g. يا زيدونَ.

qatr.f: How is an originally indefinite noun treated when a particular individual is intended in the vocative?
qatr.b: It becomes definite by the act of direct address and is built, e.g. يا رجلُ addressing one specific man.

qatr.f: How many accepted forms are there when a vocative noun is annexed to the first-person possessive suffix (ياء المتكلم)?
qatr.b: There are six accepted forms.

qatr.f: What is the first accepted form of a vocative noun annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: Retain the silent ياء, e.g. يا غلامي.

qatr.f: What is the second accepted form of a vocative noun annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: Omit the ياء but retain the kasrah indicating it, e.g. يا غلامِ.

qatr.f: What is the third accepted form of a vocative noun annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: Replace the kasrah with a ḍammah, e.g. يا غلامُ. This is a weak dialect.

qatr.f: What is the fourth accepted form of a vocative noun annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: Retain the ياء and open it, e.g. يا غلامَي.

qatr.f: What is the fifth accepted form of a vocative noun annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: Change the preceding kasrah to a fatḥah so that the yāʾ becomes an alif, e.g. يا غلاما.

qatr.f: What is the sixth accepted form of a vocative noun annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: Omit the resulting alif while leaving the fatḥah as its indicator, e.g. يا غلامَ.

qatr.f: How many forms are permitted for vocative أب and أم when annexed to ياء المتكلم?
qatr.b: They have ten forms: the previous six plus four additional forms using تاء instead of ياء.

qatr.f: What are the four additional forms for يا أب and يا أم in the vocative?
qatr.b: (1) يا أبتِ, (2) يا أبتَ, (3) يا أبتا, and (4) يا أبتي. The last two are considered ugly (قبيح), especially the last.

qatr.f: When the vocative is annexed to another noun that is itself annexed to ياء المتكلم (e.g. يا غلام غلامي), which forms are allowed?
qatr.b: Only keeping the final ياء, either open or silent, is permitted.

qatr.f: Which four forms are allowed for the vocatives ابن أم and ابن عم?
qatr.b: (1) فتح الميم, (2) كسر الميم, (3) retaining the ياء, and (4) changing the ياء into an alif. The last two are uncommon.

qatr.f: How are adjectives, emphatic words, appositives, and coordinated nouns following a built vocative treated when they begin with ال?
qatr.b: They may follow either the surface form (اللفظ) or the syntactic position (المحل) of the vocative.

qatr.f: How are adjectives or appositives without ال treated after a built vocative?
qatr.b: They follow the syntactic position (المحل) of the vocative rather than its surface form.

qatr.f: How is a coordinated noun without ال treated after a built vocative?
qatr.b: It is treated like an independent vocative noun and follows the rules of vocative coordination.

qatr.f: When a vocative noun is built (مبني), which types of dependents are discussed in this chapter?
qatr.b: The chapter discusses the rules for the vocative's adjective (نعت), emphatic word (توكيد), apposition (بيان), coordination (نسق), and later substitution (بدل).

qatr.f: When a built vocative is followed by a singular dependent or a dependent annexed to a noun containing ال, how may the dependent be declined?
qatr.b: It may either be raised according to the vocative's surface form (اللفظ) or accusative according to its syntactic position (المحل).

qatr.f: How may the adjective following a built vocative be declined when it is singular or annexed to a noun containing ال?
qatr.b: Both are permissible, e.g. يا زيدُ الظريفُ or يا زيدُ الظريفَ.

qatr.f: How may an emphatic word (توكيد) following a built vocative be declined?
qatr.b: It may either be nominative following the surface form or accusative following the syntactic position, e.g. يا تميمُ أجمعون or أجمعين.

qatr.f: How may an apposition (بيان) following a built vocative be declined?
qatr.b: It may either be nominative following the surface form or accusative following the syntactic position, e.g. يا سعيدُ كرزُ or كرزًا.

qatr.f: How may a coordinated noun joined by و followed by ال be declined after a built vocative?
qatr.b: It may either be nominative or accusative, e.g. يا زيدُ والضحاكُ or والضحاكَ.

qatr.f: What is the ruling when the dependent of a built vocative is an annexed noun (مضاف) that does not contain ال?
qatr.b: It must be accusative according to the syntactic position (المحل).

qatr.f: Give an example of an annexed dependent without ال that must be accusative after a built vocative.
qatr.b: Examples include يا زيدَ صاحبَ عمرو, يا زيدَ أبا عبد الله, and يا تميمَ كلكم.

qatr.f: How is the adjective of أي in expressions such as يا أيها الناس declined?
qatr.b: It must be nominative following the surface form, e.g. يا أيها الناس and يا أيها النبي.

qatr.f: How is a substitute (بدل) after a vocative declined?
qatr.b: It takes whatever form it would have if it were itself the vocative.

qatr.f: How is a definite substitute after a vocative declined?
qatr.b: It is built on what it would normally be built upon if directly called, e.g. يا سعيدُ كرزُ just as يا كرزُ.

qatr.f: How is an annexed substitute after a vocative declined?
qatr.b: It is accusative because an annexed vocative is accusative, e.g. يا سعيدَ أبا عبد الله.

qatr.f: How is a coordinated noun without ال declined after a vocative?
qatr.b: It receives the ruling it would have if independently addressed, e.g. يا زيدُ وعمروُ or يا زيدَ وأبا عبد الله.

qatr.f: Do substitution (بدل) and coordination (نسق) follow the same rule whether the original vocative is built or declinable?
qatr.b: Yes. They receive the form they would have if they themselves were the vocative.

qatr.f: When the same vocative proper noun is repeated in an annexed construction (e.g. يا زيد زيد اليعملات), what are the two possible forms of the first noun?
qatr.b: The first noun may either be nominative (ضم) or accusative (فتح).

qatr.f: If the first repeated vocative noun is nominative in expressions like يا زيد زيد اليعملات, how is it analyzed?
qatr.b: It is treated as an independent built vocative, while the second may be another vocative with the particle omitted, an apposition, or an object of an implied verb such as أعني.

qatr.f: If the first repeated vocative noun is accusative in expressions like يا زيد زيد اليعملات, what is the underlying analysis?
qatr.b: The original expression is understood as يا زيد اليعملات زيد اليعملات, with one occurrence of the annexed phrase omitted according to different grammatical analyses.

qatr.f: What is tarkhīm (ترخيم) in Arabic grammar?
qatr.b: Tarkhīm is shortening a vocative by deleting its final letter to make pronunciation lighter.

qatr.f: When may a definite vocative noun ending with tāʾ (ة) be shortened by tarkhīm?
qatr.b: It may always be shortened, regardless of whether it is a proper noun or how many letters it contains.

qatr.f: Is a proper noun required for tarkhīm when the noun ends in tāʾ (ة)?
qatr.b: No. Proper-noun status is not required if the noun ends in ة.

qatr.f: Must a noun ending with tāʾ (ة) have more than three letters to undergo tarkhīm?
qatr.b: No. The condition of having more than three letters does not apply to nouns ending with ة.

qatr.f: Give examples of tarkhīm for nouns ending in tāʾ (ة).
qatr.b: عائشة → يا عائش and ثبة → يا ثب.

qatr.f: What three conditions must a noun not ending in tāʾ meet in order to undergo tarkhīm?
qatr.b: It must (1) be built on ḍammah as a vocative, (2) be a proper noun, and (3) contain more than three letters.

qatr.f: Why can جعفر be shortened to يا جعف but زيد cannot?
qatr.b: جعفر satisfies all three conditions, while زيد has only three letters and therefore does not.

qatr.f: Why can عبد الله not undergo tarkhīm?
qatr.b: Because it is an annexed vocative (مضاف), not a built vocative on ḍammah.

qatr.f: Why can يا إنسان referring to a specific person not undergo tarkhīm?
qatr.b: Because it is not a proper noun (علم), even if a specific individual is intended.

qatr.f: What opinion did al-Farrāʾ hold regarding tarkhīm of three-letter proper names such as حكم and حسن?
qatr.b: He allowed their tarkhīm by analogy, although the standard view does not.

qatr.f: What are the two methods of pronouncing a shortened vocative after tarkhīm?
qatr.b: The language of one who ignores the omitted letters (لغة من لا ينظر) and the language of one who considers the omitted letters (لغة من ينتظر).

qatr.f: What is the language of one who ignores the omitted letters (لغة من لا ينظر) in tarkhīm?
qatr.b: The remaining letters are treated as a complete word and receive a new ending, usually a final ḍammah, e.g. يا جعفُ.

qatr.f: What is the language of one who considers the omitted letters (لغة من ينتظر) in tarkhīm?
qatr.b: The remaining letters keep the vowel they had before the omitted letters were removed, e.g. يا جعفَ.

qatr.f: How is جعفر pronounced under the two methods of tarkhīm?
qatr.b: In لغة من لا ينظر: يا جعفُ. In لغة من ينتظر: يا جعفَ.

qatr.f: How is مالك pronounced under the two methods of tarkhīm?
qatr.b: In لغة من لا ينظر: يا مالُ. In لغة من ينتظر: يا مالِ.

qatr.f: How is منصور pronounced under the two methods of tarkhīm?
qatr.b: In لغة من لا ينظر: يا منصُ. In لغة من ينتظر: يا منصُ while retaining the original vowel before deletion.

qatr.f: How is هرقل pronounced under the two methods of tarkhīm?
qatr.b: In لغة من لا ينظر: يا هرقُ. In لغة من ينتظر: يا هرقْ with the original final consonant remaining quiescent.

qatr.f: What is the default rule for how much is deleted when performing tarḫīm (truncation) of a vocative noun?
qatr.b: Normally, one letter is deleted from the end of the noun.

qatr.f: When are two letters deleted instead of one in tarḫīm?
qatr.b: Two letters may be deleted if all four conditions are met: (1) the penultimate letter is extra (zāʾid), (2) it is a weak letter (ḥarf ʿillah), (3) it is quiescent (sākin), and (4) it is preceded by at least three letters.

qatr.f: Give examples of nouns from which two letters are deleted in tarḫīm.
qatr.b: Examples: سلمان → يا سلم, منصور → يا منص, مسكين (as a proper name) → يا مسك.

qatr.f: What are the four conditions required for deleting two letters in tarḫīm?
qatr.b: (1) The penultimate letter must be extra, (2) it must be a weak letter, (3) it must be quiescent, and (4) it must be preceded by three or more letters.

qatr.f: What poetic example illustrates deleting two letters in tarḫīm?
qatr.b: The poet says: يا مرو intending يا مروان.

qatr.f: What other poetic example illustrates deleting two letters in tarḫīm?
qatr.b: The poet says: يا أسم intending يا أسماء.

qatr.f: Why is only one letter deleted in the tarḫīm of مختار?
qatr.b: Because its weak letter is original, not extra; therefore only the final letter may be deleted.

qatr.f: What was al-Akhfash's opinion regarding tarḫīm of مختار?
qatr.b: He allowed deleting the weak letter as well by analogy with extra weak letters.

qatr.f: Why is only one letter deleted in the tarḫīm of دلامص?
qatr.b: Although the mīm is extra, it is a consonant, not a weak letter, so the conditions for deleting two letters are not fulfilled.

qatr.f: Why is only one letter deleted in the tarḫīm of سعيد، عماد، and ثمود?
qatr.b: Because the weak letter is not preceded by three letters, so the required condition is missing.

qatr.f: What opinion did al-Farrāʾ hold regarding names such as سعيد and عماد?
qatr.b: He allowed deleting the weak letter as well, contrary to the majority.

qatr.f: What evidence did Sibawayh cite for al-Farrāʾ's opinion?
qatr.b: The poetic expression لمى, intended as a tarḫīm of لميس.

qatr.f: Why is only one letter deleted in the tarḫīm of هبيخ and قنور?
qatr.b: Because the weak letter is vowelled (moving) rather than quiescent.

qatr.f: What is the third type of deletion in tarḫīm besides deleting one or two letters?
qatr.b: Deleting an entire word in a compound proper name (murakkab mazjī).

qatr.f: Give examples where an entire word is deleted in tarḫīm.
qatr.b: معدي كرب → يا معدي, حضرموت → يا حضر.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical definition of المستغاث به (the object of appeal)?
qatr.b: It is a noun called upon to provide help in removing hardship or assisting in overcoming difficulty.

qatr.f: Which vocative particle is used with المستغاث به?
qatr.b: Only يا is used.

qatr.f: What is the normal preposition used before the noun being appealed to (المستغاث به)?
qatr.b: It is normally preceded by a lām with fatḥah (لَ).

qatr.f: According to Ibn Jinnī, what does the lām of the المستغاث به attach to?
qatr.b: It attaches to يا, because يا carries the meaning of a verb.

qatr.f: According to Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh and Ibn ʿUṣfūr, what does the lām of the المستغاث به attach to?
qatr.b: It attaches to an omitted verb.

qatr.f: What was Ibn Khurūf's opinion regarding the lām of the المستغاث به?
qatr.b: He held that it is extra (zāʾidah) and attaches to nothing.

qatr.f: How is the المستغاث له (the one for whose benefit help is sought) introduced?
qatr.b: It is always preceded by a lām with kasrah (لِ).

qatr.f: What is the function of the lām before the المستغاث له?
qatr.b: It is the lām of purpose (taʿlīl) attached to an omitted verb, such as أدعوك لكذا ("I call upon you for such-and-such").

qatr.f: What is the parsing of the phrase: يا لله للمسلمين?
qatr.b: The first lām (لَ) belongs to the object appealed to (الله), while the second (لِ) introduces the beneficiary (المسلمين).

qatr.f: What happens to the lām of a coordinated المستغاث به if يا is repeated?
qatr.b: It takes fatḥah: e.g. يا لقومي ويا لأمثال قومي.

qatr.f: What happens to the lām of a coordinated المستغاث به if يا is not repeated?
qatr.b: It takes kasrah: e.g. يا للكهول وللشبان.

qatr.f: What is the first alternative construction of the المستغاث به besides the usual lām construction?
qatr.b: An alif is added to the end of the noun, and the initial lām is omitted: e.g. يا يزيدا.

qatr.f: What is the second alternative construction of the المستغاث به besides the usual lām construction?
qatr.b: Neither the initial lām nor the final alif is used, and the noun follows the ordinary rules of the vocative: e.g. يا زيد لعمرو, يا عبد الله لزيد.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical definition of the mandūb (المندوب) in Arabic grammar?
qatr.b: The mandūb is a vocative noun used either to lament someone who has died or suffered a loss, or to express grief or pain over oneself or one's condition.

qatr.f: What are the two types of mandūb (المندوب)?
qatr.b: (1) One lamented over (المتفجع عليه), and (2) one through whom the speaker expresses pain or grief (المتوجع منه).

qatr.f: Give an example of a mandūb used to lament a deceased person.
qatr.b: يا عمرا in the elegy for ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz رضي الله عنه.

qatr.f: Give an example of a mandūb used to express personal grief or pain.
qatr.b: واحر قلباه in al-Mutanabbī's verse.

qatr.f: Which vocative particles may be used with the mandūb?
qatr.b: Only وا (the normal and characteristic particle) and يا when confusion with an ordinary vocative will not occur.

qatr.f: Which vocative particle is specifically associated with the mandūb?
qatr.b: وا is the characteristic and most common particle of lamentation.

qatr.f: Does the mandūb follow the same grammatical rules as the ordinary vocative (المنادى)?
qatr.b: Yes. Its grammatical rulings are the same as those of the ordinary vocative.

qatr.f: How is a singular definite mandūb inflected?
qatr.b: It is built on ḍammah, e.g. وازيدُ.

qatr.f: How is an annexed (muḍāf) mandūb inflected?
qatr.b: It is accusative (manṣūb), e.g. واعبدَ الله.

qatr.f: May an alif be added to the end of the mandūb?
qatr.b: Yes. A final alif may be added, e.g. وازيدا and واعمرا.

qatr.f: May a final hāʾ be added to the mandūb when pausing (waqf)?
qatr.b: Yes. At pause, a final hāʾ may be added, e.g. وازيداه and واعمراه.

qatr.f: What happens to the final hāʾ of the mandūb when speech continues (waṣl)?
qatr.b: It is normally omitted, except in poetic necessity.

qatr.f: When may the final hāʾ of the mandūb be retained in connected speech?
qatr.b: It may be retained only in cases of poetic necessity.

qatr.f: How may the final hāʾ of the mandūb be pronounced when retained?
qatr.b: It may be pronounced with ḍammah by analogy with the pronoun hāʾ, or with kasrah to resolve the meeting of two sukūns.

qatr.f: What does Ibn Hishām mean by the expression "والنادب" in the matn?
qatr.b: It means "the one lamenting says...", introducing the forms of lamentation.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical definition of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (المفعول المطلق)?
qatr.b: It is a supplementary verbal noun (maṣdar) governed by an agent derived either from the same wording or from the same meaning.

qatr.f: What are the two kinds of governing agents for the mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: An agent from the same wording (lafẓ) or from the same meaning (maʿnā).

qatr.f: Give an example of a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governing agent is from the same wording.
qatr.b: ضربت ضربًا or وكلم الله موسى تكليمًا.

qatr.f: Give an example of a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governing agent is from the same meaning.
qatr.b: قعدت جلوسًا, because قعود and جلوس have the same meaning.

qatr.f: Why is جلوسًا in قعدت جلوسًا considered a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: Because جلوس has the same meaning as the verb قعد.

qatr.f: Why is حلفة in تأليت حلفة considered a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: Because الحلف is synonymous with التألّي (swearing an oath).

qatr.f: Why must the mafʿūl muṭlaq be described as a supplementary element (فضلة)?
qatr.b: To exclude verbal nouns that are essential sentence elements rather than optional complements.

qatr.f: Why is كلام in كلامك كلام حسن not a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: Because it is not a supplementary element; it functions as the predicate, not as a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

qatr.f: Why is جده in جد جده not considered a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: Because it is not functioning as a supplementary verbal noun governed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

qatr.f: Can something other than a verbal noun substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: Yes. Certain words may stand in place of the verbal noun (niyābah ʿan al-maṣdar).

qatr.f: Which words meaning "all" or "part" may substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: كل and بعض, when annexed to the verbal noun, e.g. فلا تميلوا كل الميل and ولو تقول علينا بعض الأقاويل.

qatr.f: How may numbers substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: A number may replace the verbal noun, e.g. فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة, where ثمانين is the mafʿūl muṭlaq and جلدة is its tamyīz.

qatr.f: In the verse فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة, which word is the mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: ثمانين is the mafʿūl muṭlaq.

qatr.f: In the verse فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة, what is the grammatical function of جلدة?
qatr.b: It is tamyīz (specification).

qatr.f: How may instrument nouns substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: Instrument nouns such as سوطًا, عصًا, or مقرعةً may stand in place of the verbal noun.

qatr.f: Give examples of instrument nouns substituting for a mafʿūl muṭlaq.
qatr.b: ضربته سوطًا, ضربته عصًا, and ضربته مقرعةً.

qatr.f: According to Ibn Hishām, does an adjective of the verbal noun substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq?
qatr.b: No. He rejects that analysis.

qatr.f: How did some grammarians analyze رغدًا in وكلا منها رغدًا?
qatr.b: They considered it the adjective of an omitted verbal noun: أكلًا رغدًا.

qatr.f: How did Sibawayh analyze رغدًا in وكلا منها رغدًا?
qatr.b: He considered it a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) describing the implied verbal noun, not a substitute for it.

qatr.f: What evidence does Sibawayh use to show that رغدًا is a ḥāl rather than a substituted verbal noun?
qatr.b: Arabs say سير عليه طويلًا, allowing the prepositional phrase to become deputy subject, but they do not raise طويل, showing it is a ḥāl, not a verbal noun.

qatr.f: Why does Sibawayh reject treating رغدًا as a substituted verbal noun?
qatr.b: Because if it were a true verbal noun, it could assume the grammatical properties of a verbal noun, such as serving as deputy subject, which it does not.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical definition of the mafʿūl lahu (المفعول له
qatr.b: It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) that expresses the reason or cause for an action while sharing the same time and the same doer (agent) as that action.

qatr.f: What are the conditions for a noun to be a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: It must be (1) a verbal noun (maṣdar), (2) express the cause of the action, (3) share the same time as the action, and (4) share the same doer (agent) as the action.

qatr.f: Why is إجلالًا in قمت إجلالًا لك considered a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: Because إجلال is a verbal noun expressing the reason for standing, and it shares both the same time and the same doer as the action.

qatr.f: What happens if one of the conditions of the mafʿūl lahu is missing?
qatr.b: It must be preceded by the lām of causation (لام التعليل) and become genitive.

qatr.f: What is an example where the mafʿūl lahu loses the condition of being a verbal noun?
qatr.b: خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعًا, where لكم is introduced by lām because the pronoun is not a verbal noun.

qatr.f: Why is لكم in خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعًا introduced by the lām of causation?
qatr.b: Because the cause is expressed by a pronoun rather than a verbal noun, so one of the conditions of the mafʿūl lahu is absent.

qatr.f: Why is لأدنى in ولو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة not a mafʿūl lahu in the accusative?
qatr.b: Because أدنى is a comparative adjective (اسم تفضيل), not a verbal noun, so it is preceded by lām.

qatr.f: What is an example where the mafʿūl lahu loses the condition of sharing the same time as the action?
qatr.b: فجئت وقد نضت لنوم ثيابها, because removing the clothes occurred before the sleep itself.

qatr.f: Why is لنوم in فجئت وقد نضت لنوم ثيابها preceded by the lām?
qatr.b: Because the time of sleeping differs from the time of removing the clothes, so the condition of simultaneous time is missing.

qatr.f: What is an example where the mafʿūl lahu loses the condition of sharing the same doer?
qatr.b: وإني لتعروني لذكراك هزة.

qatr.f: Why is لذكراك in وإني لتعروني لذكراك هزة preceded by the lām?
qatr.b: Because the doer of "remembering" is the speaker, while the doer of "overtaking" is the trembling, so the agents differ.

qatr.f: Why is لتركبوها in ولتركبوها وزينة introduced by the lām?
qatr.b: Because the creator is Allah, whereas the riders are human beings, so the doers are different.

qatr.f: Why is زينة in ولتركبوها وزينة in the accusative rather than preceded by lām?
qatr.b: Because the doer of both creating and beautifying is Allah, so the condition of a shared doer is fulfilled.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical definition of the mafʿūl fīhi (المفعول فيه
qatr.b: It is a noun of time or place governed by an agent with the implied meaning of "in" (في).

qatr.f: What are the two categories of the mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Nouns of time (ظرف الزمان) and nouns of place (ظرف المكان).

qatr.f: Give an example of a temporal mafʿūl fīhi.
qatr.b: صمت يوم الخميس ("I fasted on Thursday").

qatr.f: Give an example of a locative mafʿūl fīhi.
qatr.b: جلست أمامك ("I sat in front of you").

qatr.f: What is the essential semantic condition for a noun to function as a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: The governing verb must apply to it with the implied meaning of "in" (في).

qatr.f: Why is يومًا in إنا نخاف من ربنا يومًا عبوسًا قمطريرًا not a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because the meaning is they fear the Day itself, not merely something occurring "on" that day; therefore it is a mafʿūl bihi.

qatr.f: Why is حيث in الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته not a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because Allah knows the place itself deserving revelation, not merely something occurring "in" it; therefore حيث is a mafʿūl bihi.

qatr.f: How is حيث analyzed in الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته?
qatr.b: It is the object of an understood verb implied by أعلم, i.e. يعلم حيث يجعل رسالته.

qatr.f: Why is أن تنكحوهن in وترغبون أن تنكحوهن not a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because although it conveys a meaning similar to في, it is neither a noun of time nor of place.

qatr.f: Can every noun of time function as a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Yes. All nouns of time may be accusative as adverbials, whether definite, counted, or indefinite.

qatr.f: What are the three categories of temporal nouns accepted as mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Specific (مختص), counted (معدود), and indefinite (مبهم) nouns of time.

qatr.f: What is a specific noun of time (اسم زمان مختص)?
qatr.b: A time noun answering the question "When?" (متى), such as يوم الخميس.

qatr.f: What is a counted noun of time (اسم زمان معدود)?
qatr.b: A measurable period answering "How much time?" (كم), such as week, month, or year.

qatr.f: What is an indefinite noun of time (اسم زمان مبهم)?
qatr.b: A general time expression such as حين or وقت.

qatr.f: Can every noun of place function as a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: No. Only indefinite nouns of place (المبهم) may function as adverbials of place.

qatr.f: What are the three categories of indefinite nouns of place that may function as mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: (1) Direction nouns, (2) distance/measurement nouns, and (3) place nouns derived from the same verbal root as their governing verb.

qatr.f: Which six principal direction nouns are treated as adverbials of place?
qatr.b: Above, below, in front, behind, right, and left (and equivalent expressions).

qatr.f: Give examples of direction nouns functioning as mafʿūl fīhi.
qatr.b: فوق، تحت، أمام، وراء، يمين، شمال، ذات اليمين، ذات الشمال.

qatr.f: Which nouns resemble the six directions in functioning as adverbials?
qatr.b: Indefinite location words such as عند and لدى.

qatr.f: What kinds of measurement nouns may function as mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Nouns measuring distance, such as فرسخ، ميل، بريد.

qatr.f: How can a noun derived from the same verbal root as its governing verb function as a mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: It may function as an adverb of place when its root matches that of the governing verb, e.g. جلست مجلس زيد.

qatr.f: Why is مجلس in جلست مجلس زيد a valid mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because مجلس is derived from the same root as جلست (جلس).

qatr.f: Why is مقاعد in وأنا كنا نقعد منها مقاعد للسمع a valid mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because مقاعد is derived from the same root as نقعد (قعد).

qatr.f: Why is مجلس in ذهبت مجلس زيد not a valid mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because مجلس is derived from جلس, while the governing verb is ذهب, so their roots differ.

qatr.f: Why is مذهب in جلست مذهب عمرو not a valid mafʿūl fīhi?
qatr.b: Because مذهب is derived from ذهب, while the governing verb is جلس, so their roots differ.

qatr.f: In Arabic grammar (Qaṭr al-Nadā), what is the definition of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose/cause)?
qatr.b: The mafʿūl lahu is a verbal noun (maṣdar) that states the reason for an action and shares the same doer and the same time as the action it explains.

qatr.f: In Arabic grammar, what three conditions must a mafʿūl lahu satisfy in order to be accusative (manṣūb) without a preposition?
qatr.b: It must (1) be a verbal noun (maṣdar), (2) explain the reason for another action, and (3) share both the same doer and the same time as that action.

qatr.f: Why is "حذرَ الموت" in "يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم من الصواعق حذرَ الموت" considered a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: Because ḥadhar is a verbal noun expressing the reason for putting fingers in the ears, and it shares the same doer and time as the action.

qatr.f: What happens in Arabic grammar if a mafʿūl lahu loses one of the required conditions?
qatr.b: It must be preceded by the preposition لِـ (the lām of purpose).

qatr.f: When the reason for an action is not expressed by a verbal noun, how is it normally expressed according to Qaṭr al-Nadā?
qatr.b: It is expressed with لِـ (the lām of purpose).

qatr.f: Why is "لكم" in "خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعًا" introduced with the preposition لِ instead of being a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: Because لكم is a pronoun, not a verbal noun (maṣdar).

qatr.f: Why is "لأدنى معيشة" in the verse "ولو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة..." not a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: Because أدنى is a comparative adjective (ism tafḍīl), not a verbal noun.

qatr.f: Why is "لنوم" in "فجئت وقد نضت لنوم ثيابها" preceded by لِ instead of being accusative as a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: Because the time of sleeping is different from the time of removing the clothes, so the condition of sharing the same time is missing.

qatr.f: Why is "لذكراك" in "وإني لتعروني لذكراك هزة" introduced with لِ instead of being a mafʿūl lahu?
qatr.b: Because the doer of remembering is the speaker, whereas the doer of trembling is the trembling itself, so the doer is not the same.

qatr.f: Why is "لتركبوها" in "والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة" preceded by لِ according to Qaṭr al-Nadā?
qatr.b: Because the creator is Allah, while the riders are human beings, so the doer differs.

qatr.f: Why is "زينة" in "والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة" accusative without لِ?
qatr.b: Because both creating and adorning are attributed to Allah, so the doer is the same.

qatr.f: In Arabic grammar (Qaṭr al-Nadā), what is the definition of the mafʿūl fīh (adverbial object/ẓarf)?
qatr.b: It is a noun of time or place upon which the governing word operates with the meaning of "in" (fī).

qatr.f: What kinds of nouns can function as a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: Nouns of time and certain indefinite nouns of place.

qatr.f: Can every noun of time be used as a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: Yes. Specific, counted, and indefinite nouns of time may all function as adverbials.

qatr.f: Can every noun of place function as a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: No. Only indefinite nouns of place (asmāʾ al-makān al-mubhamah) may function as adverbials.

qatr.f: What are the three categories of indefinite place nouns that may function as a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: (1) Direction words (e.g. أمام، فوق، تحت), (2) measures of distance (e.g. فرسخ، ميل), and (3) place nouns derived from the same root as their governing verb (e.g. مقعد، مجلس).

qatr.f: Why is "يوم" in "إنا نخاف من ربنا يومًا عبوسًا" not a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: Because the meaning is "we fear that Day itself," not "during that day," so it is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi).

qatr.f: Why is "حيث" in "الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته" not a mafʿūl fīh according to Qaṭr al-Nadā?
qatr.b: Because Allah knows the place itself, not merely what occurs in that place, so it is treated as a direct object.

qatr.f: Why is "أن تنكحوهن" in "وترغبون أن تنكحوهن" not considered a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: Because although it has the meaning of "in," it is neither a noun of time nor a noun of place.

qatr.f: Why is "مجلس" in "جلست مجلس زيد" a valid mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: Because it is a place noun derived from the same root as its governing verb (جلس).

qatr.f: Why is "مذهب" in "جلست مذهب عمرو" invalid as a mafʿūl fīh?
qatr.b: Because its governing verb (جلس) does not share the same root as the place noun (مذهب from ذهب).

qatr.f: In Arabic grammar (Qaṭr al-Nadā), what is the definition of the mafʿūl maʿahu (comitative object)?
qatr.b: It is an extra noun occurring after a wāw that explicitly denotes accompaniment (maʿiyyah) and is preceded by a verb or something containing both the meaning and letters of a verb.

qatr.f: What conditions must a noun satisfy to be considered a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: It must be (1) a noun, (2) extra to the sentence, (3) follow a wāw meaning accompaniment rather than coordination, and (4) be preceded by a verb or something containing the meaning and letters of a verb.

qatr.f: Why is the verb in "لا تأكل السمك وتشرب اللبن" not an example of a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because the word after the wāw is a verb, whereas a mafʿūl maʿahu must be a noun.

qatr.f: Why is "الشمس طالعة" in "جاء زيد والشمس طالعة" not a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because what follows the wāw is a complete sentence, not a noun.

qatr.f: Why is "عمرو" in "اشترك زيد وعمرو" not a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because it is an essential argument of the verb rather than an extra element.

qatr.f: Why is "عمرو" in "جاءني زيد مع عمرو" not a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because accompaniment is expressed by the preposition مع, not by the special wāw of accompaniment.

qatr.f: Why is "النيل" in "سرت والنيل" a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because it is a noun after the wāw of accompaniment and is preceded by a verb.

qatr.f: Can a mafʿūl maʿahu follow something other than a finite verb?
qatr.b: Yes. It may follow something that contains both the meaning and letters of a verb, such as أنا سائر والنيل.

qatr.f: Why is "وضيعته" in "كل رجل وضيعته" not considered a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because it is not preceded by a verb or something containing the meaning and letters of a verb.

qatr.f: When is the accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu obligatory?
qatr.b: When coordination with the wāw is impossible because of a semantic or grammatical obstacle.

qatr.f: Why must "إتيانه" in "لا تنه عن القبيح وإتيانه" be parsed as a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because coordination would produce the contradictory meaning "Do not forbid evil and do not forbid committing it."

qatr.f: Why is "زيدًا" in "قمت وزيدًا" preferably parsed as a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because coordinating with an attached subject pronoun is grammatically weak without an explicit detached pronoun.

qatr.f: Why is "زيدًا" in "مررت بك وزيدًا" preferably parsed as a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because coordination with an attached object of a preposition normally requires repeating the preposition.

qatr.f: When is parsing as a mafʿūl maʿahu preferred over coordination?
qatr.b: When coordination would weaken or distort the intended meaning, even though it is grammatically possible.

qatr.f: Why is "زيدًا" in "كن أنت وزيدًا كالأخ" preferably a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: Because only the listener is being commanded, not Zayd.

qatr.f: How should the predicate after a mafʿūl maʿahu agree in "كن أنت وزيدًا كالأخ"?
qatr.b: It agrees only with the person addressed (كالأخ), not with both nouns.

qatr.f: When is coordination preferred over parsing a noun as a mafʿūl maʿahu?
qatr.b: When coordination is grammatically and semantically straightforward, as in قام زيد وعمرو.

qatr.f: In Arabic grammar (Qaṭr al-Nadā), what is the definition of the ḥāl (circumstantial accusative)?
qatr.b: The ḥāl is a descriptive extra element that answers the question "How?" about the state of its possessor.

qatr.f: What three characteristics define a valid ḥāl?
qatr.b: It must be descriptive, extra to the sentence, and answer the question "How?".

qatr.f: Why is "مكتوفًا" in "ضربت اللص مكتوفًا" considered a ḥāl?
qatr.b: Because it is descriptive, extra, and answers the question "How did you strike the thief?"

qatr.f: Why is "ثبات" in "فانفروا ثبات" considered a ḥāl although it is not formally an adjective?
qatr.b: Because it is interpreted as meaning متفرقين, making it descriptive in meaning.

qatr.f: What does "extra" (faḍlah) mean in the definition of the ḥāl?
qatr.b: It means that it comes after the sentence is complete, not that it can always be omitted without affecting the meaning.

qatr.f: Does the standard definition of ḥāl include both explanatory and emphatic circumstantial expressions?
qatr.b: No. It is intended for the explanatory (mubayyinah) ḥāl, not the emphatic one.

qatr.f: What is the normal definiteness requirement for a ḥāl?
qatr.b: A ḥāl should normally be indefinite (nakirah).

qatr.f: How are apparently definite ḥāls interpreted?
qatr.b: They are interpreted as indefinite in meaning.

qatr.f: What four conditions allow the possessor (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) of a ḥāl to be indefinite?
qatr.b: Specification, generality, postponement after the ḥāl, or another context making it sufficiently identifiable.

qatr.f: Why is the pronoun in "خشعًا أبصارهم يخرجون" a valid possessor of the ḥāl?
qatr.b: Because pronouns are definite.

qatr.f: Why is "أربعة" in "في أربعة أيام سواءً للسائلين" allowed as the possessor of the ḥāl?
qatr.b: Because it is specified by the genitive phrase أيام.

qatr.f: Why is "قرية" in "وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا لها منذرون" allowed as the possessor of the ḥāl despite being indefinite?
qatr.b: Because it is general through occurring in a negative context.

qatr.f: Why is "طلل" in "لمية موحشًا طلل" allowed as the possessor of the ḥāl?
qatr.b: Because the indefinite noun comes after the ḥāl, satisfying the condition of postponement.

qatr.f: What is التَّمْيِيز (tamyīz)?
qatr.b: It is a noun that is extra (فضلة), indefinite (نكرة), and a concrete noun (جامد), which clarifies something whose meaning is ambiguous among entities.

qatr.f: How many conditions does Ibn Hishām mention for التمييز?
qatr.b: Five conditions: 1) It must be a noun, 2) it must be extra (not an essential part of the sentence), 3) it must be indefinite, 4) it must be a concrete noun (جامد), 5) it must clarify something ambiguous among entities.

qatr.f: How does التمييز resemble الحال?
qatr.b: They both are nouns that are extra, indefinite, and come after a complete meaning.

qatr.f: How does التمييز differ from الحال?
qatr.b: الحال is derived (مشتق) and describes states/conditions, while التمييز is a concrete noun (جامد) and clarifies entities.

qatr.f: What are the two types of التمييز?
qatr.b: 1) تمييز المفرد (clarifying a single word), and 2) تمييز النسبة (clarifying a relationship or sentence meaning).

qatr.f: What are the common places where تمييز المفرد occurs?
qatr.b: After quantities (المقادير), numbers (العدد), words indicating similarity, and words indicating difference.

qatr.f: What are the three types of quantities (المقادير) that commonly take tamyīz?
qatr.b: 1) Measurement of area, 2) measurement of volume/capacity, 3) measurement of weight.

qatr.f: Give an example of tamyīz after an area measurement.
qatr.b: جريب نخلاً — "a field measure of palm trees."

qatr.f: Give an example of tamyīz after a volume measurement.
qatr.b: صاع تمراً — "a ṣāʿ of dates."

qatr.f: Give an example of tamyīz after a weight measurement.
qatr.b: منوان عسلاً — "two manns of honey."

qatr.f: What is the ruling of tamyīz after numbers from 11 to 99?
qatr.b: It is منصوب and singular (مفرد).

qatr.f: Give a Quranic example of tamyīz after a number.
qatr.b: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا — "I saw eleven stars."

qatr.f: What is the ruling of tamyīz after 100 and above?
qatr.b: It is singular and genitive (مجرور), e.g. مائة عبدٍ.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of tamyīz after 3–10?
qatr.b: It is plural and genitive, e.g. ثلاثة أعبدٍ.

qatr.f: What are the two meanings of كم in Arabic?
qatr.b: كم الاستفهامية (asking "how many?") and كم الخبرية (meaning "many/a great number").

qatr.f: What is the ruling of tamyīz after كم الاستفهامية?
qatr.b: It is منصوب and singular: كم عبدًا ملكت؟

qatr.f: What is the ruling of tamyīz after كم الخبرية?
qatr.b: It is always مجرور. It may be plural like the tamyīz of 3–10, or singular like the tamyīz of 100+.

qatr.f: Give an example of tamyīz after كم الخبرية with a plural noun.
qatr.b: كم عبيدٍ ملكت — similar to عشرة أعبدٍ ملكت.

qatr.f: Give an example of tamyīz after كم الخبرية with a singular noun.
qatr.b: كم عبدٍ ملكت — similar to مائة عبدٍ ملكت.

qatr.f: What happens to the tamyīz of كم الاستفهامية when preceded by a preposition?
qatr.b: It may be مجرور or منصوب: بكم درهمٍ اشتريتَ or بكم درهمًا اشتريتَ.

qatr.f: According to Ibn Hishām, what causes the jarr in بكم درهمٍ?
qatr.b: It is بسبب حرف جر مقدر, not because of iḍāfah (contrary to al-Zajjāj).

qatr.f: Give an example of tamyīz after something indicating similarity.
