qatr.b: أزيد عندك أم عمرو؟ — "Is Zayd with you or is it Amr?"

qatr.f: Why is the answer to a question with أم not answered by نعم or لا?
qatr.b: Because the question asks for identification of which option is correct, not whether the whole statement is true or false.

qatr.f: Why is this type of أم called معادلة?
qatr.b: Because it balances the interrogative hamzah by placing two equal alternatives under consideration.

qatr.f: Why is this type of أم called متصلة?
qatr.b: Because what comes before and after it cannot be separated; both parts depend on the other.

qatr.f: What is the function of لا as a conjunction?
qatr.b: It rejects an incorrect assumption after an affirmative statement and directs the judgment to what follows it.

qatr.f: Give an example of لا correcting a mistaken assumption.
qatr.b: جاءني زيد لا عمرو — "Zayd came, not Amr."

qatr.f: What is the function of لكن as a conjunction?
qatr.b: It rejects an incorrect assumption after a negative statement and affirms what follows it.

qatr.f: Give an example of لكن correcting a mistaken assumption.
qatr.b: ما جاءني زيد لكن عمرو — "Zayd did not come, rather Amr came."

qatr.f: What is the function of بل after a negative statement?
qatr.b: It rejects the previous judgment and affirms the opposite judgment.

qatr.f: Give an example of بل after negation.
qatr.b: ما جاءني زيد بل عمرو — "Zayd did not come; rather, Amr came."

qatr.f: What is the function of بل after an affirmative statement?
qatr.b: It transfers the judgment from what precedes it to what follows it, leaving the first as though no judgment was made about it.

qatr.f: Give an example of بل after affirmation.
qatr.b: جاءني زيد بل عمرو — "Zayd came; rather, Amr came."

qatr.f: Is إما considered a conjunction according to the stronger opinion?
qatr.b: No. Al-Fārisi held that إما is not a conjunction, and al-Jurjānī considered counting it among conjunctions an obvious mistake.

qatr.f: What is the definition of بدل (substitution/apposition)?
qatr.b: A dependent word that is intended by the ruling without an intermediary.

qatr.f: Why is بدل considered a type of تابع?
qatr.b: Because it follows another word grammatically.

qatr.f: How does بدل differ from a naʿt (صفة), emphasis (توكيد), and conjunction?
qatr.b: In بدل, the second word itself is intended by the ruling, unlike naʿt and emphasis, and unlike conjunction it has no connecting particle.

qatr.f: How many types of بدل are there?
qatr.b: Six types: بدل كل من كل, بدل بعض من كل, بدل الاشتمال, بدل الإضراب, بدل الغلط, and بدل النسيان.

qatr.f: What is بدل كل من كل?
qatr.b: A replacement where the second term is identical in meaning to the first term.

qatr.f: Give an example of بدل كل من كل.
qatr.b: جاءني محمد أبو عبد الله — "Muhammad, Abu Abdullah, came." Abu Abdullah is the same person as Muhammad.

qatr.f: Give a Qur’anic example of بدل كل من كل.
qatr.b: فمفازًا حدائق — "Gardens are the same thing intended by the expression of success."

qatr.f: What is بدل بعض من كل?
qatr.b: A replacement where the second term is a part of the first term.

qatr.f: Give an example of بدل بعض من كل.
qatr.b: أكلت الرغيف ثلثه — "I ate the loaf, a third of it."

qatr.f: Give a Qur’anic example of بدل بعض من كل.
qatr.b: ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا — according to the famous view, من استطاع is بدل from الناس because it refers to a portion of them.

qatr.f: What is بدل الاشتمال?
qatr.b: A replacement where there is a connection between the two words, but the second is not a physical part of the first.

qatr.f: Give an example of بدل الاشتمال.
qatr.b: أعجبني زيد علمه — "I admired Zayd, his knowledge." Knowledge belongs to Zayd but is not a physical part of him.

qatr.f: Give a Qur’anic example of بدل الاشتمال.
qatr.b: يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه — "They ask you about the sacred month, fighting in it." Fighting is related to the month but not part of it.

qatr.f: Can بدل and the word it replaces both be indefinite or definite?
qatr.b: Yes. They can both be indefinite, both definite, or differ in definiteness.

qatr.f: What are the three final types of بدل?
qatr.b: بدل الإضراب, بدل الغلط, and بدل النسيان.

qatr.f: Give an example that could represent the three types of بدل.
qatr.b: تصدقت بدرهم دينار — "I gave charity with a dirham, a dinar."

qatr.f: How is بدل الإضراب understood in تصدقت بدرهم دينار?
qatr.b: The speaker intended to mention the dirham first, then changed his intention and intended the dinar.

qatr.f: How is بدل الغلط understood in تصدقت بدرهم دينار?
qatr.b: The speaker intended to say dinar but his tongue mistakenly said dirham.

qatr.f: How is بدل النسيان understood in تصدقت بدرهم دينار?
qatr.b: The speaker intended the dirham, but after saying it realized that intention was wrong and corrected himself.

qatr.f: What is the difference between بدل الغلط and بدل النسيان?
qatr.b: The mistake in بدل الغلط occurs on the tongue, while in بدل النسيان the mistake occurs in the mind/intention.

qatr.f: What is the fourth type of تابع discussed after emphasis and conjunction?
qatr.b: عطف البيان (the explanatory apposition).

qatr.f: What is the definition of عطف البيان?
qatr.b: A جامد تابع that clarifies or specifies another word without being interpreted as a derived adjective.

qatr.f: How does عطف البيان differ from a naʿt?
qatr.b: A naʿt is derived (مشتق) and describes a quality, while عطف البيان is جامد and identifies or clarifies.

qatr.f: Give an example of عطف البيان.
qatr.b: أقسم بالله أبو حفص عمر — Umar رضي الله عنه is عطف بيان explaining Abu Hafs.

qatr.f: Can عطف البيان be a noun after a noun?
qatr.b: Yes, according to the correct view, it may follow another indefinite noun.

qatr.f: What is عطف النسق?
qatr.b: A تابع connected to its preceding word by one of the conjunction particles.

qatr.f: What are examples of conjunction particles used in عطف النسق?
qatr.b: الواو، الفاء، ثم، أو، أم، لا، لكن، بل، حتى.

qatr.f: What does the conjunction واو indicate?
qatr.b: It indicates simple combination (الجمع) without implying order.

qatr.f: Does واو العطف indicate sequence?
qatr.b: No. It only indicates participation in the ruling; order must be understood from another evidence.

qatr.f: Give an example where واو indicates only combination.
qatr.b: جاء زيد وعمرو — both came, but it does not specify who came first.

qatr.f: Give an example where context gives order with واو.
qatr.b: إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها وقال الإنسان ما لها — the events are understood sequentially from context.

qatr.f: What does فاء العطف indicate?
qatr.b: It indicates sequence and immediate succession (الترتيب والتعقيب).

qatr.f: Give an example of فاء indicating sequence.
qatr.b: جاء زيد فعمرو — Amr came immediately after Zayd.

qatr.f: What additional meaning can فاء have?
qatr.b: It can indicate causation (التسبب), especially between sentences.

qatr.f: Give an example of فاء meaning causation.
qatr.b: سرق فقطع — "He stole, so his hand was cut."

qatr.f: Why is فاء used in conditional answers?
qatr.b: Because it indicates that the consequence follows from the condition.

qatr.f: Give an example of فاء in a conditional answer.
qatr.b: من يأتيني فإني أكرمه — "Whoever comes to me, then I honor him."

qatr.f: What does ثمّ indicate?
qatr.b: Sequence with delay (الترتيب والتراخي).

qatr.f: What is the difference between فاء and ثمّ?
qatr.b: فاء indicates immediate succession, while ثمّ indicates succession after a period of delay.

qatr.f: What does حتى indicate in conjunction?
qatr.b: It indicates reaching an endpoint (غاية) and gradual progression (تدريج).

qatr.f: Why must what comes after حتى be part of what precedes it?
qatr.b: Because حتى indicates that the action continues progressively until reaching that final part.

qatr.f: Give an example of حتى showing a real part.
qatr.b: أكلت السمكة حتى رأسها — "I ate the fish, even its head."

qatr.f: Give an example of حتى showing a figurative part.
qatr.b: ألقى الصحيفة كي يخفف رجله والزاد حتى نعله — the shoe is considered part of what burdens him.

qatr.f: Does حتى indicate sequence like ثمّ and فاء?
qatr.b: No. According to Ibn Hisham, حتى indicates general combination, not sequence.

qatr.f: What evidence shows that حتى does not indicate sequence?
qatr.b: The hadith: كل شيء بقضاء وقدر حتى العجز والكيس — there is no sequence between divine decree and these matters.

qatr.f: What is the sixth category of the topics of the dependent words (التوابع) discussed in Sharḥ Qaṭr al-Nadā?
qatr.b: The sixth category is the chapter of numbers (باب العدد).

qatr.f: How do the numbers from three to nine behave with masculine and feminine nouns?
qatr.b: Numbers from three to nine oppose the gender of the counted noun: they are feminine with masculine nouns and masculine with feminine nouns.

qatr.f: Give examples of numbers three to nine with masculine nouns.
qatr.b: One says: سبعة أيام (seven days) and ثمانية أيام (eight days).

qatr.f: Give examples of numbers three to nine with feminine nouns.
qatr.b: One says: سبع ليالٍ (seven nights).

qatr.f: How does the number ten behave when it is not compound?
qatr.b: The number ten (عشرة) follows the same rule as three to nine when it is not compounded: it opposes the gender of the counted noun.

qatr.f: How do the numbers one and two behave regarding gender?
qatr.b: The numbers one and two follow the normal pattern: they agree with the counted noun in gender.

qatr.f: How do ordinal numbers (أسماء العدد على وزن فاعل) behave regarding gender?
qatr.b: Ordinal numbers such as ثالث، رابع، خامس follow the normal rule: they are masculine with masculine nouns and feminine with feminine nouns.

qatr.f: What are the three categories of number expressions according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Number expressions are divided into: 1. Those that always follow the normal gender rule. 2. Those that always oppose the gender rule. 3. Those that have two different cases.

qatr.f: Which numbers always follow the normal gender rule?
qatr.b: The numbers one, two, and ordinals on the pattern فاعل always follow the normal gender rule.

qatr.f: Give examples of one and two with masculine and feminine nouns.
qatr.b: Masculine: واحد، اثنان. Feminine: واحدة، اثنتان.

qatr.f: Give examples of ordinal numbers with masculine and feminine nouns.
qatr.b: Masculine: ثانٍ، ثالث، رابع، عاشر. Feminine: ثانية، ثالثة، رابعة، عاشرة.

qatr.f: Which numbers always oppose the normal gender rule?
qatr.b: The numbers three to nine always oppose the gender of the counted noun.

qatr.f: Give Quranic evidence for the gender opposition of numbers.
qatr.b: Allah says: ﴿سخرها عليهم سبع ليال وثمانية أيام حسوما﴾. "Seven nights" uses the feminine form with the feminine noun "nights", while "eight days" uses the masculine form with the masculine noun "days".

qatr.f: What special case does the number ten have?
qatr.b: The number ten has two states: when compounded it follows the normal rule, and when independent it opposes the normal rule.

qatr.f: How does ten behave when compounded?
qatr.b: In compound numbers (11–19), the first part follows normal gender agreement. Example: ثلاثة عشر عبداً and ثلاث عشرة أمةً.

qatr.f: How does ten behave when independent?
qatr.b: When independent, it opposes gender: عشرة رجال and عشر إماء.

qatr.f: What are the four possible forms of ordinal numbers (فاعل)?
qatr.b: They are: 1. Used independently. 2. Added to the noun from which they are derived. 3. Added to a number less than it. 4. Having a noun less than it in the accusative.

qatr.f: What does an ordinal number mean when used independently?
qatr.b: It means one person described by that ordinal quality, such as ثالث meaning "the third one".

qatr.f: What does ثالث اثنين mean?
qatr.b: ثالث اثنين means "one of two who is the third (making three)" according to the context.

qatr.f: Give Quranic examples of ordinal numbers added to what they are derived from.
qatr.b: Allah says: ﴿إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين﴾ meaning "the second of two"; and ﴿لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة﴾ meaning "the third of three".

qatr.f: What does an ordinal number mean when added to something below it?
qatr.b: It means the person who completes the number by adding himself. Example: ثالث اثنين = the one who makes two become three.

qatr.f: Give a Quranic example of an ordinal number added to what is below it.
qatr.b: Allah says: ﴿ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم﴾.

qatr.f: What is the fourth usage of ordinal numbers?
qatr.b: The ordinal is used with the noun after it in the accusative: رابع ثلاثةً.

qatr.f: What does رابع ثلاثة mean?
qatr.b: It means "the one who makes three become four."

qatr.f: Is it permissible to use this accusative construction with a number derived from itself?
qatr.b: No. It is not permitted with a number followed by what it is derived from, contrary to the opinions of al-Akhfash and Thaʿlab.

qatr.f: How many things prevent a noun from accepting tanwīn (صرف)?
qatr.b: There are nine causes (موانع الصرف).

qatr.f: What is the basic principle regarding declinable nouns?
qatr.b: The original state of Arabic nouns is that they accept full declension (صرف). They become diptotes only when two causes of منع الصرف exist, or one cause that replaces two.

qatr.f: What poetic line summarizes the nine causes of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: اجمع وزن عادلا أنث بمعرفة ركب وزد عجمة فالوصف قد كملا.

qatr.f: What are the nine causes of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: They are: 1. وزن الفعل (verb pattern). 2. التركيب (compound construction). 3. العجمة (foreign origin). 4. التعريف (proper noun). 5. العدل (change from original form). 6. الوصف (adjectival quality). 7. الجمع (plural pattern). 8. التأنيث (feminization). 9. ألف التأنيث.

qatr.f: What is the first cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The first cause is the pattern of a verb (وزن الفعل).

qatr.f: When does a noun have the cause of وزن الفعل?
qatr.b: When it is on a pattern specific to verbs, or when it begins with an extra letter like verbs and shares the same pattern.

qatr.f: Give examples of nouns on verb-only patterns.
qatr.b: Examples include names like قُتِّل، ضُرِب، انطلق when used as names.

qatr.f: Give examples of proper names resembling verb patterns.
qatr.b: Examples: أحمد، يزيد، يشكر، تغلب، نرجس when used as names.

qatr.f: What is the second cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The second cause is composition (التركيب).

qatr.f: What type of composition causes منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It refers to compound blending (التركيب المزجي) that is not built (not ending in بويه).

qatr.f: Why is iḍāfah (possessive construction) not considered the composition that causes منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Because iḍāfah already causes the noun to take kasrah when governed, so it cannot be a reason for taking fatḥah instead of kasrah.

qatr.f: Why is تركيب الإسناد not considered the intended composition?
qatr.b: Because compounds like شاب قرناها and تأبط شراً are treated as quoted expressions (محكيّات), not normal declined nouns.

qatr.f: Why are compounds ending in بويه excluded from this rule?
qatr.b: Because they are built nouns (مبني), and منع الصرف applies only to declinable nouns (المعرب).

qatr.f: What examples are given of compound nouns that cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Examples include بعلبك، حضرموت، معد يكرب.

qatr.f: What is the third cause of منع الصرف (preventing a noun from taking tanwīn)?
qatr.b: The third cause is foreignness (العجمة).

qatr.f: What does العجمة mean as a cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It means that the word originates according to foreign (non-Arabic) linguistic patterns.

qatr.f: Give examples of foreign proper nouns that are diptotes because of العجمة.
qatr.b: Examples include إبراهيم، إسماعيل، إسحاق، يعقوب.

qatr.f: Are all prophets' names foreign and therefore diptotes?
qatr.b: No. Most prophets' names are foreign, but four are Arabic: محمد ﷺ، صالح، شعيب، هود عليهم السلام.

qatr.f: What two conditions are required for a foreign word to cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Two conditions are required: 1. It must be a proper noun in the foreign language. 2. It must have more than three letters.

qatr.f: Why is a foreign word that was originally a common noun not prevented from declension?
qatr.b: Because foreignness is only considered when the word was a proper noun in the foreign language. If it was a common noun and later made into a proper noun in Arabic, it is declined normally.

qatr.f: Give an example of a foreign common noun that would not cause منع الصرف if made a proper noun.
qatr.b: Naming someone لجام (bridle) or ديباج (silk brocade) would not cause منع الصرف.

qatr.f: Why are نوح and لوط fully declinable despite being foreign names?
qatr.b: Because they have fewer than four letters, so the condition of foreignness is not fulfilled.

qatr.f: What Quranic examples show the declension of نوح and لوط?
qatr.b: Allah says: ﴿إلا آل لوط نجيناهم﴾ and ﴿إنا أرسلنا نوحًا إلى قومه﴾.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of the grammarians who say short foreign names may either be declined or not declined?
qatr.b: Ibn Hishām says this opinion is incorrect. The correct view is that names like نوح and لوط are declined.

qatr.f: What is the fourth cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The fourth cause is definiteness (التعريف).

qatr.f: What type of definiteness causes منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It refers specifically to proper noun definiteness (العلمية).

qatr.f: Why are pronouns, demonstratives, and relative pronouns not included under definiteness as a cause?
qatr.b: Because they are all indeclinable (مبنيات), while منع الصرف applies only to declinable nouns.

qatr.f: Why does definiteness through the definite article (الـ) not cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Because if a diptote receives الـ, it becomes capable of taking kasrah in the genitive, so it no longer behaves as a diptote.

qatr.f: Why does definiteness through iḍāfah not cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Because adding the noun to another noun also allows kasrah in the genitive, removing the reason for taking fatḥah instead.

qatr.f: What is the fifth cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The fifth cause is عدل (deviation/change from an original form while retaining the original meaning).

qatr.f: What does عدل mean linguistically in grammar?
qatr.b: It means transferring a noun from one form to another while keeping the original meaning.

qatr.f: How many types of عدل are there?
qatr.b: There are two types: 1. عدل occurring in proper nouns. 2. عدل occurring in adjectives.

qatr.f: What are examples of عدل in proper nouns?
qatr.b: Examples include عمر، زفر، زحل، جمع.

qatr.f: On what pattern do masculine proper nouns with عدل usually occur?
qatr.b: They occur on the pattern فُعَل and are changed from another form such as فاعل.

qatr.f: What is عمر considered عدل from?
qatr.b: عمر is considered changed from عامر.

qatr.f: What is the second pattern of عدل in proper nouns?
qatr.b: The pattern فعال in feminine proper nouns.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine names with عدل on the pattern فعال.
qatr.b: Examples include حذام، قطام، رقاش.

qatr.f: Who uses the diptote pronunciation of names like حذام and قطام?
qatr.b: The people of Tamīm make them diptotes.

qatr.f: How do the people of the Hijaz treat names like حذام and قطام?
qatr.b: They make them indeclinable on kasrah (مبني على الكسر).

qatr.f: Give a poetic example containing حذام.
qatr.b: إذا قالت حذام فصدقوها فإن القول ما قالت حذام.

qatr.f: What happens if an عدل name ends with راء, such as سفار or حضار?
qatr.b: Most grammarians agree with the Hijazi dialect and build it on kasrah, though some Tamimīs keep declension with منع الصرف.

qatr.f: What is the issue regarding أمس (yesterday)?
qatr.b: Some Tamimīs consider أمس diptote when referring specifically to the previous day because it is considered changed from الأمس.

qatr.f: How is أمس treated in the accusative and genitive according to this view?
qatr.b: It is built on kasrah: اعتكف أمس and ما رأيته مذ أمس.

qatr.f: What is another opinion regarding أمس?
qatr.b: Some grammarians treat it as a normal diptote in all cases.

qatr.f: Under what conditions is سحر prevented from declension?
qatr.b: It is prevented from declension when: 1. It is used as a ظرف (time adverb). 2. It refers to a specific day.

qatr.f: Give an example of سحر being diptote.
qatr.b: جئتك يوم الجمعة سحر ("I came to you on Friday at dawn").

qatr.f: Why is سحر prevented from declension in this case?
qatr.b: Because it is considered changed from السحر.

qatr.f: When is سحر fully declinable?
qatr.b: When it does not refer to a specific day, such as in Allah's statement: ﴿نجيناهم بسحر﴾.

qatr.f: What is the sixth cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The sixth cause is description/adjectival quality (الوصف).

qatr.f: Give examples of adjectives that cause منع الصرف.
qatr.b: Examples include أحمر، أفضل، سكران، غضبان.

qatr.f: What two conditions must exist for an adjective to cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: 1. The adjective must be originally adjectival. 2. It must not accept feminine تاء التأنيث.

qatr.f: Why does a word that only became an adjective later not cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Because the adjectival quality is accidental, not original.

qatr.f: Give examples of words that became adjectives but remain fully declinable.
qatr.b: صفوان originally meaning smooth stone, and أرنب originally meaning rabbit, if used to mean "hard-hearted" and "weak/cowardly".

qatr.f: Why is صفوان declined when used as an adjective meaning "hard"?
qatr.b: Because its original meaning was a noun (a smooth stone), and the adjective meaning is later acquired.

qatr.f: Why is أرنب declined when used as an adjective meaning "weak/cowardly"?
qatr.b: Because the adjectival meaning is not original.

qatr.f: What is the second condition for adjectival منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The adjective must not accept tāʾ of femininity (تاء التأنيث).

qatr.f: Why is عريان fully declinable?
qatr.b: Because its feminine form is عريانة, which accepts the feminine tāʾ.

qatr.f: Why is أرمل fully declinable?
qatr.b: Because its feminine form is أرملة, which accepts the feminine tāʾ.

qatr.f: Why are سكران and أحمر prevented from declension?
qatr.b: Because their feminine forms are سكرى and حمراء, which do not take feminine tāʾ.

qatr.f: What is the seventh cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The seventh cause is the plural pattern (الجمع).

qatr.f: What condition must a plural fulfill to cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The plural must be on a pattern that does not exist for singular nouns.

qatr.f: What type of plural causes منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It refers to broken plurals (جمع التكسير) on certain patterns known as صيغة منتهى الجموع.

qatr.f: How many types of plural patterns cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: There are two main types: مفاعل and مفاعيل.

qatr.f: Give examples of the مفاعل pattern.
qatr.b: Examples: مساجد، دراهم.

qatr.f: Give examples of the مفاعيل pattern.
qatr.b: Examples: مصابيح، طواويس.

qatr.f: What is the eighth cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The eighth cause is extra letters (الزيادة).

qatr.f: What is meant by الزيادة as a cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It means the presence of an additional alif and nūn at the end of the noun.

qatr.f: Give examples of nouns prevented from declension because of extra alif and nūn.
qatr.b: Examples: سكران and عثمان.

qatr.f: What is the ninth cause of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The ninth cause is femininity (التأنيث).

qatr.f: How many types of femininity are there?
qatr.b: Femininity has three types: 1. Feminine by alif. 2. Feminine by tāʾ. 3. Feminine by meaning.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine nouns by alif.
qatr.b: Examples: حبلى and صحراء.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine nouns by tāʾ.
qatr.b: Examples: طلحة and حمزة.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine nouns by meaning only.
qatr.b: Examples: زينب and سعاد.

qatr.f: Does feminine alif always cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Yes. Feminine alif always prevents declension without any additional condition.

qatr.f: What condition is required for feminine tāʾ to cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It requires the noun to also be a proper noun (علم).

qatr.f: How does feminine-by-meaning affect منع الصرف?
qatr.b: It has the same ruling as feminine tāʾ: it usually requires proper noun status, but sometimes allows both declension and non-declension.

qatr.f: When does feminine-by-meaning definitely cause منع الصرف?
qatr.b: When one of three conditions exists: 1. More than three letters. 2. The middle letter is vowelled. 3. It is foreign.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine-by-meaning nouns with more than three letters.
qatr.b: Examples: سعاد، زينب.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine-by-meaning nouns with a moving middle letter.
qatr.b: Examples: سقر، لظى.

qatr.f: Give examples of feminine-by-meaning foreign names.
qatr.b: Examples: ماء، جور، حمص، بلخ.

qatr.f: When is feminine-by-meaning allowed to be fully declined or diptote?
qatr.b: When none of the three conditions are present, such as هند، دعد، جمل.

qatr.f: Give an example where a feminine name can be declined or not declined.
qatr.b: The poet said: لم تتلفع بفضل مئزرها دعدٌ ولم تسق دعدَ في العلب. The name دعد appears once declined and once diptote.

qatr.f: How are all the causes of منع الصرف divided into categories?
qatr.b: They are divided into three categories.

qatr.f: What is the first category of causes of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Causes that work by themselves without needing another cause.

qatr.f: Which causes work alone to prevent declension?
qatr.b: Two causes: the special plural pattern (الجمع) and the two feminine alifs (ألفا التأنيث).

qatr.f: What is the second category of causes of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Causes that work only when combined with proper noun status (العلمية).

qatr.f: Which causes require العلمية to prevent declension?
qatr.b: Three causes: femininity without alif, composition, and foreignness.

qatr.f: Give examples of femininity requiring العلمية.
qatr.b: فاطمة، زينب.

qatr.f: Give examples of composition requiring العلمية.
qatr.b: معد يكرب.

qatr.f: Give examples of foreignness requiring العلمية.
qatr.b: إبراهيم.

qatr.f: Why is صنجة declined despite being a foreign feminine noun?
qatr.b: Because it lacks the required proper noun status in this discussion.

qatr.f: Why is صولجان declined despite being foreign and having extra letters?
qatr.b: Because it is not a proper noun.

qatr.f: Why is مسلمة declined despite being feminine and adjectival?
qatr.b: Because it lacks proper noun status.

qatr.f: What is the third category of causes of منع الصرف?
qatr.b: Causes that work when combined with either proper noun status (العلمية) or description (الوصفية).

qatr.f: Which causes belong to the third category?
qatr.b: Three causes: عدل، وزن، زيادة.

qatr.f: Give examples of عدل, وزن, and زيادة with proper nouns.
qatr.b: عمر (عدل), أحمد (وزن الفعل), سلمان (زيادة الألف والنون).

qatr.f: Give examples of these causes with adjectives.
qatr.b: ثلاث (عدل), أحمر (وزن), سكران (زيادة الألف والنون).

qatr.f: What is the seventh topic discussed after منع الصرف?
qatr.b: The chapter of exclamation (باب التعجب).

qatr.f: How many standard forms of Arabic exclamation are there?
qatr.b: There are two forms: ما أفعله and أفعل به.

qatr.f: What is the first exclamation form?
qatr.b: ما أفعل زيدًا.

qatr.f: How is ما in ما أفعل زيدًا analyzed?
qatr.b: It is a مبتدأ meaning "something عظیم (something great)" according to one interpretation.

qatr.f: How is أفعل in ما أفعل زيدًا analyzed?
qatr.b: It is a past tense verb (فعل ماض).

qatr.f: What is the subject of أفعل in this construction?
qatr.b: The subject is a hidden pronoun referring back to ما.

qatr.f: What is زيدًا in ما أفعل زيدًا?
qatr.b: It is the direct object (مفعول به).

qatr.f: What is the grammatical structure of the sentence ما أفعل زيدًا?
qatr.b: ما is the مبتدأ, the verb phrase is its خبر, and زيدًا is the object of the verb.

qatr.f: What is the second exclamation form?
qatr.b: أفعل به.

qatr.f: What is the meaning of أفعل به?
qatr.b: It has the same meaning as ما أفعله ("How wonderful/remarkable is he!").

qatr.f: What is the original form of أفعل به according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: Its original form was أفعل, meaning "became possessing such a quality".

qatr.f: Give an example of this original meaning.
qatr.b: أغدّ البعير means "the camel became one possessing a swelling (غدة)."

qatr.f: Why was the structure changed in أفعل به?
qatr.b: The wording was altered and the letter بـ was added to improve the expression.

qatr.f: Why is the bāʾ in أفعل به fixed and necessary?
qatr.b: Because it became part of the established exclamation form, unlike the bāʾ in other constructions such as the subject of كفى.

qatr.f: From what type of verbs are exclamation forms and اسم التفضيل derived?
qatr.b: They are derived from a three-letter verb that is: 1. Affirmative. 2. Variable in degree. 3. Complete. 4. Active voice. 5. Not already on the pattern أفعل as a normal adjective.

qatr.f: Does Arabic have only two ways of expressing amazement?
qatr.b: No. Arabic has many expressions of amazement, but only two are formally categorized in grammar.

qatr.f: Give examples of non-standard expressions of amazement.
qatr.b: Examples include: ﴿كيف تكفرون بالله﴾, سبحان الله إن المؤمن لا ينجس حيًا ولا ميتًا, and لله دره فارسًا.

qatr.f: What are the two recognized grammatical forms of التعجب?
qatr.b: ما أفعله and أفعل به.

qatr.f: What is the grammatical status of ما in ما أفعل according to the first opinion?
qatr.b: It is a complete indefinite noun (نكرة تامة) meaning "something".

qatr.f: Why is it permissible to begin a sentence with ما in this construction?
qatr.b: Because it contains the meaning of amazement, which allows it to function as an introductory noun.

qatr.f: What is the meaning of عطف البيان in the example "أنا ابن التارك البكري بشر" and why is "بشر" not a بدل?
qatr.b: "بشر" is عطف بيان for "البكري". It cannot be بدل because a بدل is considered as if it replaces the first word completely. Saying "أنا ابن التارك بشر" would be incorrect because a word containing ال (التارك) cannot be annexed to a proper noun without ال (بشر).

qatr.f: Why is "عبد شمس ونوفلا" in "يا أخوينا عبد شمس ونوفلا" considered عطف بيان rather than بدل?
qatr.b: Because replacing the first word with the second would make the phrase incorrect. If "عبد شمس ونوفلا" were بدل, it would be like saying "يا عبد شمس ونوفلا". A vocative attached to a name without ال should be in the form of a direct call, so it should be "يا نوفل" not "يا نوفلا".

qatr.f: What is عطف النسق?
qatr.b: عطف النسق is a تابع (dependent word) that has one of the conjunction particles between it and the word it follows. It includes conjunction with و, ف, ثم, أو, أم, بل, لا, لكن, and others.

qatr.f: What does the conjunction و (waaw) indicate?
qatr.b: The conjunction و indicates absolute combination (مطلق الجمع). It means the two things share in the ruling, without necessarily indicating order.

qatr.f: Does و indicate chronological order?
qatr.b: No. The majority of grammarians hold that و does not indicate order. Any order understood from a sentence comes from another indication, not from و itself.

qatr.f: What are the three possible meanings of "جاء زيد وعمرو"?
qatr.b: It may mean: 1. Zayd and Amr came together. 2. Zayd came before Amr. 3. Amr came before Zayd. The context determines which meaning is intended.

qatr.f: Give an example where و indicates accompaniment (togetherness).
qatr.b: Allah's statement: ﴿وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ﴾. The context indicates Ibrahim عليه السلام and Ismail عليه السلام were both involved.

qatr.f: Give an example where و indicates order due to external evidence.
qatr.b: Allah's statement: ﴿إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا ۝ وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا ۝ وَقَالَ الْإِنسَانُ مَا لَهَا﴾. The events occur in sequence, but this comes from reality, not from the و.

qatr.f: What did some Kufan grammarians claim about و?
qatr.b: Some Kufans claimed that و indicates order. The majority rejected this because examples such as "اختصم زيد وعمرو" show that no order is intended.

qatr.f: What does فَ (fa) indicate in conjunction?
qatr.b: فَ indicates order and immediate succession (الترتيب والتعقيب).

qatr.f: What does "جاء زيد فعمرو" mean?
qatr.b: It means Amr came after Zayd immediately or without a significant delay.

qatr.f: Is immediate succession always absolute with فَ?
qatr.b: No. The meaning of immediate succession depends on the nature of the action. For example, travelling from Basrah to Baghdad after three days may still count as immediate succession because that is normal for travel.

qatr.f: What other meaning does فَ have besides succession?
qatr.b: فَ can indicate causation (التسبب), especially when connecting sentences.

qatr.f: Give examples where فَ indicates causation.
qatr.b: Examples: "سها فسجد" (he forgot, so he prostrated), "زنى فرجم" (he committed adultery, so he was stoned), "سرق فقطع" (he stole, so his hand was cut).

qatr.f: Why is فَ used in conditional answers?
qatr.b: Because it indicates that the second matter results from the first. Example: "من يأتيني فإني أكرمه" means whoever comes to me, I will honour him.

qatr.f: What does ثمّ indicate?
qatr.b: ثمّ indicates order with delay (الترتيب والتراخي).

qatr.f: What does "جاء زيد ثم عمرو" mean?
qatr.b: It means Amr came after Zayd with a period of delay between them.

qatr.f: What does حتى indicate as a conjunction?
qatr.b: حتى indicates reaching a limit and gradual progression (الغاية والتدريج).

qatr.f: Why must what follows حتى be part of what precedes it?
qatr.b: Because حتى indicates that the previous thing continues gradually until reaching the final part. The object after حتى is therefore a part of what came before, either literally or by estimation.

qatr.f: Give an example where the thing after حتى is literally part of what precedes.
qatr.b: "أكلت السمكة حتى رأسها" — the head is literally part of the fish.

qatr.f: Give an example where the thing after حتى is considered part of the previous thing by estimation.
qatr.b: "ألقى الصحيفة كي يخفف رجله والزاد حتى نعله ألقاها" — the sandal is not literally part of the load, but it is considered part of what burdens him.

qatr.f: Does حتى indicate order?
qatr.b: No. Some claimed it does, but the correct view is that it indicates general combination like و.

qatr.f: What example shows that حتى does not indicate order?
qatr.b: The hadith: "كل شيء بقضاء وقدر حتى العجز والكيس" because there is no order between divine decree and destiny and human qualities.

qatr.f: What meanings does أو have?
qatr.b: أو can indicate one of two or more things. After commands it may indicate choice or permission; after statements it may indicate doubt or deliberate ambiguity.

qatr.f: What is the difference between تخيير and إباحة with أو?
qatr.b: Takhyīr means choosing one and not combining them. Ibāḥah allows combining both.

qatr.f: Give an example of أو for choice (تخيير).
qatr.b: "تزوج هندًا أو أختها" — marry Hind or her sister; marrying both is not allowed.

qatr.f: Give an example of أو for permission (إباحة).
qatr.b: "جالس الحسن أو ابن سيرين" — sit with Hasan or Ibn Sirin; sitting with both is allowed.

qatr.f: What is the meaning of أو in "جاء زيد أو عمرو" when the speaker does not know who came?
qatr.b: It indicates doubt (شك).

qatr.f: What is the meaning of أو when the speaker knows but hides the information?
qatr.b: It indicates deliberate ambiguity (تشكيك).

qatr.f: What does أم indicate?
qatr.b: أم is used for requesting specification (طلب التعيين) after a hamzah of questioning when one of two equal possibilities must be identified.

qatr.f: Why is أم called معادلة?
qatr.b: Because it balances the two alternatives in the question. Example: "أزيد عندك أم عمرو؟" Both possibilities are treated equally.

qatr.f: Why is أم called متصلة?
qatr.b: Because what comes before and after it are connected and neither can stand independently in the intended question.

qatr.f: What is the function of لا as a conjunction?
qatr.b: لا rejects the previous assumption and affirms the opposite after an affirmative statement. Example: "جاءني زيد لا عمرو."

qatr.f: What is the function of لكن and بل after negation?
qatr.b: They correct an incorrect assumption by affirming what comes after them. Example: "ما جاءني زيد لكن عمرو" or "بل عمرو".

qatr.f: What is the difference between لا and بل/لكن?
qatr.b: لا can be used after affirmation and negation and can indicate correction. بل and لكن are mainly used after negation for correction, while بل after affirmation shifts the ruling away from the first and to the second.

qatr.f: What does بل mean after an affirmative statement?
qatr.b: It removes the ruling from the first thing and establishes it for the second. Example: "جاءني زيد بل عمرو" means Amr came, not Zayd.

qatr.f: Is إمّا a conjunction?
qatr.b: No. Although some included it among conjunctions, the correct view is that it is not a conjunction.

qatr.f: What is the definition of بدل?
qatr.b: بدل is a تابع (dependent) that is itself intended by the ruling without an intermediary.

qatr.f: Why is بدل different from adjective, emphasis, and عطف البيان?
qatr.b: Because those complete or clarify the first word, whereas the بدل itself is the intended object of the ruling.

qatr.f: Why is بدل different from عطف النسق?
qatr.b: Because عطف النسق requires a conjunction particle, while بدل does not.

qatr.f: What are the six types of بدل?
qatr.b: 1. بدل كل من كل. 2. بدل بعض من كل. 3. بدل اشتمال. 4. بدل الإضراب. 5. بدل الغلط. 6. بدل النسيان.

qatr.f: What is بدل كل من كل?
qatr.b: It is when the second word is identical in meaning and reference to the first. Example: "جاء محمد أبو عبد الله".

qatr.f: Why does Ibn Hisham avoid saying "بدل الكل من الكل"?
qatr.b: Because some grammarians objected to adding ال to both words in this phrase.

qatr.f: What is بدل بعض من كل?
qatr.b: It is when the second word is a part of the first. Example: "أكلت الرغيف ثلثه".

qatr.f: In "ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا", what type of بدل is "من استطاع"?
qatr.b: It is بدل بعض من كل because those capable are a part of mankind.

qatr.f: What is بدل اشتمال?
qatr.b: It is when the second word is related to the first but is not a physical part of it. Example: "أعجبني زيد علمه".

qatr.f: In "يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه", what is "قتال" grammatically?
qatr.b: "قتال" is بدل اشتمال from "الشهر الحرام". Fighting is associated with the month but is not part of it.

qatr.f: What are the three kinds of بدل involving speech correction?
qatr.b: بدل الإضراب, بدل الغلط, and بدل النسيان.

qatr.f: What is بدل الإضراب?
qatr.b: The speaker first intends one statement, then changes to another. Example: "تصدقت بدرهم دينار" meaning he first mentioned a dirham then changed to a dinar.

qatr.f: What is بدل الغلط?
qatr.b: The tongue makes a mistake and says something other than what was intended.

qatr.f: What is بدل النسيان?
qatr.b: The speaker intended one thing, but after saying it he realizes that intention was wrong.

qatr.f: What is the difference between بدل الغلط and بدل النسيان?
qatr.b: The mistake in بدل الغلط occurs on the tongue, while in بدل النسيان the mistake occurs in the intention or thought.

qatr.f: What is the general rule for stopping (الوقف) on words ending with تاء التأنيث?
qatr.b: If the تاء التأنيث is silent (ساكنة), it remains unchanged when stopping, such as قامت and قعدت. If it is vowelled, its pronunciation changes depending on the type of word.

qatr.f: How is الوقف done on a singular feminine noun ending in تاء التأنيث?
qatr.b: The most eloquent way is to replace the تاء with هاء when stopping. Example: هذه رحمة and هذه شجرة.

qatr.f: Is stopping on تاء التأنيث itself ever used?
qatr.b: Yes. Some Arabs stop with the تاء, and some Qur'an reciters did so in verses such as ﴿إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ and ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ﴾.

qatr.f: What is the correct stopping method for plurals ending in ألف وتاء (ـات)?
qatr.b: The preferred method is stopping with the تاء, such as مسلماتْ. Some also stop with هاء.

qatr.f: Why did Ibn Hisham mention that the rules may be reversed?
qatr.b: Because although the standard is stopping on singular feminine nouns with هاء and plurals with تاء, some Arabs reversed these patterns.

qatr.f: What is a المنقوص noun?
qatr.b: A المنقوص is a noun whose final letter is a ياء preceded by a kasrah, such as قاضٍ and القاضي.

qatr.f: How is الوقف performed on a المنقوص noun when it is indefinite and in the nominative or genitive case?
qatr.b: The preferred way is to remove the ياء. Example: هذا قاضٍ → هذا قاضْ, مررت بقاضٍ → مررت بقاضْ.

qatr.f: Is it permissible to keep the ياء when stopping on an indefinite المنقوص noun?
qatr.b: Yes. Some reciters, such as Ibn Kathir, stopped with the ياء in words like هادي, والي, and واقي.

qatr.f: How is الوقف performed on a definite المنقوص noun?
qatr.b: The preferred way is to keep the ياء. Example: هذا القاضي, مررت بالقاضي.

qatr.f: Is it permissible to delete the ياء when stopping on a definite المنقوص noun?
qatr.b: Yes. Some Arabs did so, and some Qur'an reciters stopped on words like المتعال and التلاق without the final ياء.

qatr.f: What does Ibn Hisham mean by "وقد يعكس فيهن" regarding الوقف?
qatr.b: It means that some forms may be stopped in the opposite way: رحمة with تاء, مسلمات with هاء, قاض with ياء, and القاضي by deletion.

qatr.f: How is الوقف done on a المنقوص noun in the accusative case?
qatr.b: The ياء must always remain. If it is indefinite, the tanwin becomes an ألف. Example: رأيت قاضيًا → قاضيا.

qatr.f: How is الوقف done on a definite المنقوص noun in the accusative?
qatr.b: The ياء remains. Example: رأيت القاضي.

qatr.f: What are the three cases where a silent نون becomes an ألف in writing/pronunciation when stopping?
qatr.b: 1. The particle إذن. 2. The light emphatic نون (نون التوكيد الخفيفة). 3. Tanwin of an accusative noun.

qatr.f: How is الوقف performed on إذن?
qatr.b: The correct view is that it is stopped with an ألف: إذًا.

qatr.f: What did Ibn ʿUsfur claim about stopping on إذن?
qatr.b: He claimed it should be stopped with the نون and therefore written with نون, but Ibn Hisham rejects this view.

qatr.f: How do all Qur'an reciters stop on the light نون of emphasis?
qatr.b: They stop on it with an ألف. Example: لنسفعا and ليكونا.

qatr.f: What is the original form of "فاعبدا" in poetry?
qatr.b: Its original form is فاعبدن with the light نون of emphasis, but when stopping it becomes an ألف.

qatr.f: How is الوقف performed on accusative tanwin?
qatr.b: The Arabs stop on it with an ألف. Example: رأيت زيدًا → رأيت زيدا.

qatr.f: Who differed regarding stopping on accusative tanwin?
qatr.b: The tribe of Rabīʿah stopped by deleting the ألف, saying forms like زيد instead of زيدا.

qatr.f: Why did Ibn Hisham discuss the writing of these words after discussing stopping?
qatr.b: Because the written form often follows the pronunciation used when stopping.

qatr.f: How are the three cases (إذن, نون التوكيد, accusative tanwin) written according to some scholars?
qatr.b: Some write the نون as an ألف according to the stopping pronunciation, while others preserve the original نون.

qatr.f: What are the three opinions regarding writing إذن?
qatr.b: 1. Always write it with ألف: إذا. 2. Always write it with نون: إذن. 3. Differentiate: write it with ألف when it is the particle and with نون in other cases.

qatr.f: How is the ألف after واو الجماعة written?
qatr.b: An ألف is added after واو الجماعة, such as قالوا, to distinguish it from an original واو.

qatr.f: Why is an ألف added after واو الجماعة?
qatr.b: To distinguish between واو الجماعة (قالوا) and an original واو, such as the واو in يدعو.

qatr.f: Is an ألف written after an original واو?
qatr.b: No. An original واو is not followed by an additional ألف. Example: زيد يدعو.

qatr.f: When is a final ألف written as ياء (ألف مقصورة)?
qatr.b: When the ألف is beyond three letters, such as استدعى and المصطفى, or when it originates from a ياء, such as رمى and الفتى.

qatr.f: When is a final ألف written as ألف?
qatr.b: When it is third in the word and originates from واو, such as دعا, عفا, العصا, and القفا.

qatr.f: How can one know whether the final ألف of a verb comes from واو or ياء?
qatr.b: Attach the verb to the تاء of the speaker or add the مخاطب form. The revealed letter shows the origin. Example: رمى → رميت (ياء origin), دعا → دعوت (واو origin).

qatr.f: How can one know the origin of the final ألف in a noun?
qatr.b: Look at its dual form. Example: فتى → فتيان shows ياء origin, while عصا → عصوان shows واو origin.

qatr.f: What poetic principle did Ibn Hisham mention about determining the origin of ألف?
qatr.b: The dual form reveals the origin of nouns, and returning a verb to its conjugated form reveals the origin of verbs.

qatr.f: What advice did al-Hariri give for determining the spelling of a verb with a problematic final ألف?
qatr.b: If the spelling of a verb is unclear, attach the تاء of خطاب. If it appears as ياء, write it with ياء; otherwise write it with ألف.

qatr.f: What is Hamzat al-Waṣl (همزة الوصل)?
qatr.b: It is a hamzah that is pronounced when beginning speech but dropped when connecting it with what precedes it.

qatr.f: In which types of words does Hamzat al-Waṣl occur?
qatr.b: It occurs in certain nouns, certain verbs, and the definite article الـ.

qatr.f: How many categories of nouns contain Hamzat al-Waṣl?
qatr.b: Two categories: specific memorized nouns and verbal nouns (maṣdars) of five- and six-letter verbs.

qatr.f: Which nouns have Hamzat al-Waṣl as a memorized exception?
qatr.b: اسم، است، ابن، ابنة، ابنم، امرؤ، امرأة، اثنان، اثنتان (and their dual forms).

qatr.f: Why is the hamzah in "أسماء" not Hamzat al-Waṣl?
qatr.b: Because it is a regular noun and its hamzah is Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ.

qatr.f: Are the plurals of nouns with Hamzat al-Waṣl also written with Hamzat al-Waṣl?
qatr.b: No. Their plurals generally have Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ, such as أبناء and أسماء.

qatr.f: Which verbal nouns contain Hamzat al-Waṣl?
qatr.b: The maṣdars of five-letter verbs, such as الانطلاق and الاقتداء, and six-letter verbs, such as الاستخراج.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of Hamzat al-Waṣl in present tense verbs?
qatr.b: Present tense verbs always begin with Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ, such as أستغفر and أحمد.

qatr.f: What is the ruling of Hamzat al-Waṣl in past tense verbs?
qatr.b: Only five-letter and six-letter past verbs have Hamzat al-Waṣl, such as انطلق and استخرج.

qatr.f: What type of hamzah does three-letter past verbs have?
qatr.b: Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ, such as أخذ and أكل.

qatr.f: What type of hamzah does four-letter past verbs have?
qatr.b: Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ, such as أخرج and أعطى.

qatr.f: What type of hamzah does the imperative of four-letter verbs have?
qatr.b: Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ, such as أكرم and أجب.

qatr.f: What type of hamzah does the imperative of three-letter verbs have?
qatr.b: Hamzat al-Waṣl, such as اقتل، اضرب، اذهب.

qatr.f: What is the only particle that contains Hamzat al-Waṣl?
qatr.b: The definite article الـ, such as الغلام and الفرس.

qatr.f: According to al-Khalīl, is the hamzah of الـ originally Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ or Hamzat al-Waṣl?
qatr.b: Al-Khalīl considered it originally Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ that was treated like Hamzat al-Waṣl due to frequent usage.

qatr.f: How many types of Hamzat al-Waṣl are there regarding its vowel?
qatr.b: Four: those pronounced with kasrah, fatḥah, ḍammah, and those with more than one possible vowel.

qatr.f: What vowel does the Hamzat al-Waṣl of most nouns take?
qatr.b: Kasrah, with some weak dialects allowing ḍammah.

qatr.f: What vowel does the Hamzat al-Waṣl of the definite article take?
qatr.b: Fatḥah.

qatr.f: What vowel does the Hamzat al-Waṣl in "أيمن الله" take?
qatr.b: Usually fatḥah: أَيْمُن الله, although kasrah is also reported.

qatr.f: What is "أيمن الله" used for?
qatr.b: It is used in oaths, meaning "By Allah".

qatr.f: What is the origin of "أيمن" according to Ibn Hishām?
qatr.b: It is a singular noun derived from اليُمن (blessing), not the plural of يمين (oath/right hand).

qatr.f: When is Hamzat al-Waṣl pronounced with ḍammah?
qatr.b: In the imperative of three-letter verbs when the third letter has an original ḍammah, such as اُقتل and اُكتب.

qatr.f: Why does "اغزي" begin with kasrah despite being from a verb with ḍammah?
qatr.b: Its original form is اغزوي; the wāw was removed, and the preceding letter received kasrah to match the remaining yā’.

qatr.f: Why does "امشوا" begin with kasrah?
qatr.b: Its original form was امشيوا; the yā’ was removed and the shīn was given kasrah because the original vowel was kasrah.

qatr.f: Why is "اذهب" pronounced with kasrah rather than fatḥah?
qatr.b: To avoid confusion with a present tense verb beginning with hamzah, such as أذهب.

burda.b: O my Lord, bless and grant peace always and forever
Upon Your beloved one, the Best of all Creation
Is it the memory of neighbours in Dhu Salam

burda.f: مَزَجْتَ دَمْعًا جَرَى مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ بِدَمِ
burda.b: That has left your eyes so red with tears?

burda.f: أَمْ هَبَّتِ الرِّيحُ مِنْ تِلْقَاءِ كَاظِمَةٍ
burda.b: Or is it the wind blowing from the direction of Kāẓima

burda.f: وَأَوْمَضَ البَرْقُ فِي الظَّلْمَاءِ مِنْ إِضَمِ
burda.b: And the lightning flashing in the black night from Mount Iḍam?

burda.f: فَمَا لِعَيْنَيْكَ إِنْ قُلْتَ اكْفُفَا هَمَتَا
burda.b: What is the matter with your eyes, that when you tell them to refrain,

burda.f: وَمَا لِقَلْبِكَ إِنْ قُلْتَ اسْتَفِقْ يَهِمِ
burda.b: They only weep more? And your heart – when you try to rouse it, It only becomes more bewildered
Does the one in love suppose his love can be concealed
Between pouring tears and a blazing heart?

burda.f: لَوْلاَ الهَوَى لَمْ تُرِقْ دَمْعًا عَلَى طَلَلٍ
burda.b: If not for love, your tears would not pour forth over traces left by your beloved,
Nor would you be sleepless remembering the willow tree and the mountain
So how can you deny this love when such honest witnesses
as weeping and looking gaunt have testified to it against you?
The agony of love has inscribed two lines of tears and grief
Upon your cheeks, pale as bahār4 and red as canam

burda.f: نَعَمْ سَرَى طَيْفُ مَنْ أَهْوَى فَأَرَّقَنِي
burda.b: Yes, a vision of the one I love came to me by night, and I could not sleep,
Oh, how love hinders the tasting of delight with its suffering!

burda.f: يَا لَائِمِي فِي الهَوَى العُذْرِيِّ مَعْذِرَةً
burda.b: O you who would rebuke me for this pure love, accept my excuse.

burda.f: مِنِّي إِلَيْكَ وَلَوْ أَنْصَفْتَ لَمْ تَلُمِ
burda.b: If you were truly fair, you would not reproach me at all
May you be spared a state such as mine! My secret cannot be concealed
From my detractors, nor will there ever be an end to my malady
You gave me sincere good counsel, but I did not hear it,

burda.f: إِنَّ المُحِبَّ عَنِ العُذَّالِ فِي صَمَمِ
burda.b: The lover is quite deaf to those who blame him

burda.f: إِنِّي اتَّهَمْتُ نَصِيحَ الشَّيْبِ فِي عَذَلِي
burda.b: I even suspected the counsel of my own grey hairs rebuking me,

burda.f: وَالشَّيْبُ أَبْعَدُ فِي نُصْحٍ عَنِ التُّهَمِ
burda.b: When I knew the counsel of old age and grey hair to be above suspicion
My foolish reckless self refused to heed the warning
Heralded by the onset of grey hair and old age

burda.f: وَلاَ أَعَدَّتْ مِنَ الفِعْلِ الجَمِيلِ قِرَى
burda.b: And it had not prepared any good deeds to properly welcome
This guest who had turned up on my head unannounced

burda.f: لَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ أَنِّي مَا أُوَقِّرُهُ
burda.b: If I had known that I could not receive him with honour,
I would have hidden my secret from him with dye

burda.f: مَنْ لِي بِرَدِّ جِمَاحٍ مِنْ غَوَايَتِهَا
burda.b: Who can hold back my headstrong soul from the error of its ways,
Just as wild horses are restrained with bridles and reins?
Do not aim to break the desires by plunging further into sin,
The glutton’s greed is only increased by [the sight of] food

burda.f: وَالنَّفْسُ كَالطِّفْلِ إِنْ تُهْمِلْهُ شَبَّ عَلَى
burda.b: The self is like an infant, if you neglect its proper care, It will grow up still loving to suckle;
But once you wean it, it will be weaned
So dismiss its passions, beware of letting them take over, For when passion gets the upper hand,

burda.f: إِنَّ الهَوَى مَا تَوَلَّى يُصْمِ أَوْ يَصِمِ
burda.b: It will either kill or bring dishonour
Keep a watchful eye on it as it grazes in the field of actions,

burda.f: وَإِنْ هِيَ اسْتَحْلَتِ المَرْعَى فَلاَ تُسِمِ
burda.b: And if it finds the pasture too delightful, do not let it graze unchecked
How often a pleasure that is in fact deadly has seemed good,

burda.f: مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَنَّ السُّمَّ فِي الدَّسَمِ
burda.b: To one who does not know there may be poison in the fat

burda.f: وَاخْشَ الدَّسَائِسَ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَمِنْ شِبَعٍ
burda.b: Beware the snares of hunger and satiety,
For an empty stomach may be worse than over-eating

burda.f: وَاسْتَفْرِغِ الدَّمْعَ مِنْ عَيْنٍ قَدِ امْتَلَأَتْ
burda.b: Dry the tears from eyes that have had their fill of forbidden things,
And henceforth let your only diet be regret
Oppose the self and shaytan – and defy them,
If they try to offer you advice, treat it with suspicion

burda.f: وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمَا خَصْمًا وَلاَ حَكَمًا
burda.b: Never obey them, whether they oppose or come to arbitrate,
For you know by now the tricks of both opponents and arbitrators

burda.f: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ مِنْ قَوْلٍ بِلاَ عَمَلٍ
burda.b: I beg Allah’s forgiveness for saying things I do not do,

burda.f: لَقَدْ نَسَبْتُ بِهِ نَسْلاً لِذِي عُقُمِ
burda.b: As though I were ascribing progeny to one who was barren

burda.f: أَمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ لَكِنْ مَا ائْتَمَرْتُ بِهِ
burda.b: I ordered you to be good, but then didn’t heed my own advice,

burda.f: وَمَا اسْتَقَمْتُ فَمَا قَوْلِي لَكَ اسْتَقِمِ
burda.b: I was not myself upright, so what of my telling you, ‘Be upright!’
I have not made much provision of voluntary prayer Before death comes to take me,

burda.f: وَلَمْ أُصَلِّ سِوَى فَرْضٍ وَلَمْ أَصُمِ
burda.b: Neither have I prayed nor fasted more than was obligatory

burda.f: ظَلَمْتُ سُنَّةَ مَنْ أَحْيَا الظَّلاَمَ إِلَى
burda.b: I have done injustice to the path of the one who prayed at night

burda.f: أَنِ اشْتَكَتْ قَدَمَاهُ الضُّرَّ مِنْ وَرَمِ
burda.b: Until his feet complained of pain and swelling
While he bound up his insides against the extremity of his hunger,
Hiding his delicate skin beneath the stone tied round his waist
The high mountains of gold sought to entice him,
But he showed them in return the true meaning of elevation
His situation of austerity and need only confirmed His indifference to worldly concerns,

burda.f: إِنَّ الضَّرُورَةَ لاَ تَعْدُو عَلَى العِصَمِ
burda.b: For even dire need cannot assail such impeccable virtue

burda.f: وَكَيْفَ تَدْعُو إِلَى الدُّنْيَا ضَرُورَةُ مَنْ
burda.b: How could the dire need of such a person draw him towards the world,

burda.f: لَوْلاَهُ لَمْ تُخْرَجِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ العَدَمِ
burda.b: When were it not for him, the world would never have emerged From non-existence?
Muhammad is the master of the two worlds, master of the jinn and men,

burda.f: ـنِ وَالفَرِيقَيْنِ مِنْ عُرْبٍ وَمِنْ عَجَمِ
burda.b: And master of the two groups, Arabs and non-Arabs
Our Prophet, who commands the good and forbids the wrong,

burda.f: أَبَرَّ فِي قَوْلِ لاَ مِنْهُ وَلاَ نَعَمِ
burda.b: There is no one truer to his word, whether it be ‘yes’ or ‘no’
He is the beloved one, whose intercession is hoped for
Against all the terrifying things that take us by storm
He has called people to Allah, so those who cling to him
Are clinging to a rope which will never break

burda.f: فَاقَ النَبِيِّينَ فِي خَلْقٍ وَفِي خُلُقٍ
burda.b: He surpassed the other prophets both in form and noble character,

burda.f: وَلَمْ يُدَانُوهُ فِي عِلْمٍ وَلاَ كَرَمِ
burda.b: And none has come close to him in knowledge or in pure generosity
They all petition the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for just a handful of water

burda.f: غَرْفًا مِنَ البَحْرِ أَوْ رَشْفًا مِنَ الدِّيَمِ
burda.b: From his ocean, or a draught from his never-ending rain
They all come to a halt before him according to their measure,

burda.f: مِنْ نُقْطَةِ العِلْمِ أَوْ مِنْ شَكْلَةِ الحِكَمِ
burda.b: As diacritical points upon his knowledge, or vowel marks upon his wisdom
He is the one in whom meaning and form were perfected,
And then the One who created all mankind Chose him as His beloved
He is far from having any equal in his virtues,
For in him, the essence of perfection is indivisible

burda.f: دَعْ مَا ادَّعَتْهُ النَّصَارَى فِي نَبِيِّهِمِ
burda.b: Abandon what the Christians have claimed about their Prophet,

burda.f: وَاحْكُمْ بِمَا شِئْتَ مَدْحًا فِيهِ وَاحْتَكِمِ
burda.b: Beyond that you may say whatever you wish in praise of him

burda.f: وَانْسُبْ إِلَى ذَاتِهِ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ شَرَفٍ
burda.b: You may ascribe whatever you wish of nobility to his essence,

burda.f: وَانْسُبْ إِلَى قَدْرِهِ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ عِظَمِ
burda.b: And to his rank, whatever you wish of greatness

burda.f: فَإِنَّ فَضْلَ رَسُولِ اللهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ
burda.b: Indeed, the high merit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has no furthest limit
Which could be expressed by the tongue of a human being
Were his miracles to be as mighty as his rank,

burda.f: أَحْيَا اسْمُهُ حِينَ يُدْعَى دَارِسَ الرِّمَمِ
burda.b: Just the sound of his name would bring dead bones to life

burda.f: لَمْ يَمْتَحِنَّا بِمَا تَعْيَا العُقُولُ بِهِ
burda.b: He did not test us with things that would exhaust our intellects,

burda.f: حِرْصًا عَلَيْنَا فَلَمْ نَرْتَبْ وَلَمْ نَهِمِ
burda.b: Out of concern for us, so we did not fall into doubt or bewilderment

burda.f: أَعْيَا الوَرَى فَهْمُ مَعْنَاهُ فَلَيْسَ يُرَى
burda.b: Mankind is unable to comprehend his true essence,

burda.f: فِي القُرْبِ وَالبُعْدِ فِيهِ غَيْرُ مُنْفَحِمِ
burda.b: Near and far, they are dumbfounded
Like the sun, which from afar appears small to the naked eye,
Whereas up close, it would dim and dazzle the vision
How can people who are asleep perceive his true reality
In this world, while they are distracted from him by their dreams?
The extent of the knowledge we have of him is that he is a man,
And that he is the best of all Allah’s creation

burda.f: وَكُلُّ آيٍ أَتَى الرُّسْلُ الكِرَامُ بِهَا
burda.b: Every miracle brought by the Noble Messengers
Was only connected to them through his light
Surely he is a sun of bounty and they are its planets,
Manifesting their lights for people in the darkness
How generous the creation of a Prophet Adorned with excellent character!
So graced with beauty, and radiant of face

burda.f: كَالزَّهْرِ فِي تَرَفٍ وَالبَدْرِ فِي شَرَفٍ
burda.b: Like a flower in freshness and a full moon in eminence,

burda.f: وَالبَحْرِ فِي كَرَمٍ وَالدَّهْرِ فِي هِمَمِ
burda.b: Like an ocean in pure generosity and like Time itself In strength of resolution
Just from his majestic bearing, even when he was alone,

burda.f: فِي عَسْكَرٍ حِينَ تَلْقَاهُ وَفِي حَشَمِ
burda.b: He seemed as if amongst a great army and entourage
It was as if shining pearls, protected in their shells,
Emerged from both his speech and his radiant smile

burda.f: لاَ طِيبَ يَعْدِلُ تُرْبًا ضَمَّ أَعْظُمَهُ
burda.b: No perfume could ever match that of the earth that holds his noble form,
What bliss for the one who smells that blessed earth or kisses it!
His birth made clear the purity of his origin,
O how pure his beginning and his end!
On that day, the Persians realized they had been warned
Of the onset of misery and disasters
That very night a crack appeared in the Arch of Chosroes,
Just as the unity and cohesion of his people was forever lost
The fire, out of grief for the loss, breathed its last,

burda.f: عَلَيْهِ وَالنَّهْرُ سَاهِي العَيْنِ مِنْ سَدَمِ
burda.b: And the river was distracted from its course by sorrow
Sawa was troubled as the waters of its lake receded,
And the one who came to drink from it returned raging with thirst

burda.f: كَأَنَّ بِالنَّارِ مَا بِالمَاءِ مِنْ بَلَلٍ
burda.b: It was as though, from grief, the fire took on water’s wetness,

burda.f: حُزْنًا وَبِالمَاءِ مَا بِالنَّارِ مِنْ ضَرَمِ
burda.b: And water took on the blazing dryness of the fire
The jinn were shrieking, and the lights were flashing out,

burda.f: وَالحَقُّ يَظْهَرُ مِنْ مَعْنىً وَمِنْ كَلِمِ
burda.b: As the truth was made manifest in both meaning and word
But blind and deaf, the Persians did not hear the happy tidings,
Neither did they see the flash of warning signs

burda.f: مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَخْبَرَ الأَقْوَامَ كَاهِنُهُمْ
burda.b: Even after the people’s own soothsayers had told them
That their crooked old religion could not last

burda.f: وَبَعْدَمَا عَايَنُوا فِي الأُفْقِ مِنْ شُهُبٍ
burda.b: And after they had seen shooting stars away on the horizon,

burda.f: مُنْقَضَّةٍ وَفْقَ مَا فِي الأَرْضِ مِنْ صَنَمِ
burda.b: Falling from the heavens, just as the idols were falling on earth

burda.f: حَتَّى غَدَا عَنْ طَرِيقِ الوَحْيِ مُنْهَزِمٌ
burda.b: Until even the devils were routed, fleeing from the path of revelation,
Following after others as they fled
They were fleeing just like Abraha’s warriors,

burda.f: أَوْ عَسْكَرٍ بِالحَصَى مِنْ رَاحَتَيْهِ رُمِي
burda.b: Or like the army scattered by pebbles thrown From the Prophet’s ﷺ own hand
Thrown by him after glorifying God in the palm of his hand,
As the one who glorified his Lord was thrown out From the belly of the whale
Trees came to him when he called, prostrating,

burda.f: تَمْشِي إِلَيْهِ عَلَى سَاقٍ بِلاَ قَدَمِ
burda.b: Walking towards him on trunks that had no feet
As though they had written lines of beautiful calligraphy
With their branches all along the path
Like the cloud that moved with him wherever he went,
Protecting him from the fierce oven of the midday heat
I swear by the [Lord of the] moon that was split in two,
Surely it has a connection with his heart, A true and blessed oath

burda.f: وَمَا حَوَى الغَارُ مِنْ خَيْرٍ وَمِنْ كَرَمِ
burda.b: And by the excellence and nobility encompassed in the cave,

burda.f: وَكُلُّ طَرْفٍ مِنَ الكُفَّارِ عَنْهُ عَمِي
burda.b: While every glance of the unbelievers was quite blind to it

burda.f: فَالصِّدْقُ فِي الغَارِ وَالصِّدِّيقُ لَمْ يَرِمَا
burda.b: The true one and the truthful one remained in the cave,

burda.f: وَهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا بِالغَارِ مِنْ أَرِمِ
burda.b: As those outside said to one another, ‘There is no one in this cave.’
They did not suspect that a dove would hover giving protection,

burda.f: خَيْرِ البَرِيَّةِ لَمْ تَنْسُجْ وَلَمْ تَحُمِ
burda.b: Or that a spider would spin its web to help the Best of Creation
Allah’s solicitude and shelter freed him from the need to resort

burda.f: مِنَ الدُّرُوعِ وَعَنْ عَالٍ مِنَ الأُطُمِ
burda.b: To coats of armour and fortresses for his protection

burda.f: مَا سَامَنِي الدَّهْرُ ضَيْمًا وَاسْتَجَرْتُ بِهِ
burda.b: Whenever the times have treated me unjustly, and I have turned to him

burda.f: إِلاَّ وَنِلْتُ جِوَارًا مِنْهُ لَمْ يُضَمِ
burda.b: For refuge, I always found security with him, unharmed

burda.f: وَلاَ الْتَمَسْتُ غِنَى الدَّارَيْنِ مِنْ يَدِهِ
burda.b: And never have I sought the wealth of the two worlds from his hand,

burda.f: إِلاَّ اسْتَلَمْتُ النَّدَى مِنْ خَيْرِ مُسْتَلَمِ
burda.b: Without receiving open-handed generosity from the best of givers

burda.f: لاَ تُنْكِرِ الوَحْيَ مِنْ رُؤْيَاهُ إِنَّ لَهُ
burda.b: Do not deny the revelations he received in his dreams,

burda.f: قَلْبًا إِذَا نَامَتِ العَيْنَانِ لَمْ يَنَمِ
burda.b: For surely, though his eyes would sleep, he had a heart that never slept
That was from the time when he attained to prophethood,
For the dreams of the one who has come of age cannot be denied
God be praised! Revelation is not something acquired,
Nor is a prophet’s knowledge of the unseen to be suspected
How many sick people have been healed at the touch of his hand,
And how many, driven almost mad by the noose of their sins, Have been set free
His supplication brought new life in the year of barren dryness,

burda.f: حَتَّى حَكَتْ غُرَّةً فِي الأَعْصُرِ الدُّهُمِ
burda.b: So that it stood out among the dark years Like the beautiful white blaze on a horse’s forehead

burda.f: بِعَارضٍ جَادَ أَوْ خِلْتَ البِطَاحَ بِهَا
burda.b: The clouds poured down rain, until you would have thought

burda.f: سَيْبًا مِنَ اليَمِّ أَوْ سَيْلاً مِنَ العَرِمِ
burda.b: The valley was flowing with water from the open sea, Or from the burst dam of ‘Arim
Allow me to describe to you the signs that appeared to him,

burda.f: ظُهُورَ نَارِ القِرَى لَيْلاً عَلَى عَلَمِ
burda.b: Clearly visible like beacons lit at night On the high hills to welcome guests
Although a pearl’s beauty is increased when strung among others,
Its value is not lessened when alone, unstrung
What hope can the one who tries to praise it have

burda.f: مَا فِيهِ مِنْ كَرَمِ الأَخْلاَقِ وَالشِّيَمِ
burda.b: Of doing justice to its noble traits and qualities?
Verses of truth from the Merciful — revealed in time,
Yet Eternal — the attribute of the Pre-eternal One
They are not bound by time, and bring us tidings

burda.f: عَنِ المَعَادِ وَعَنْ عَادٍ وَعَنْ إِرَمِ
burda.b: Of the Last Day, and also of ‘Ad and Iram
They have lasted to our time, and outstripped

burda.f: مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ إِذْ جَاءَتْ وَلَمْ تَدُمِ
burda.b: Every miracle brought by other prophets, Which came, but did not last
Verses so clear that no obscurity can remain

burda.f: لِذِي شِقَاقٍ وَمَا تَبْغِينَ مِنْ حَكَمِ
burda.b: For the wrangler, nor do they require any judge

burda.f: مَا حُورِبَتْ قَطُّ إِلاَّ عَادَ مِنْ حَرَبٍ
burda.b: No implacable enemy has ever attacked them
Without retreating at last from the battle, begging for peace
Their very eloquence refutes the claim of one opposing them,

burda.f: رَدَّ الغَيُورِ يَدَ الجَانِي عَنِ الحُرَمِ
burda.b: As an honourable man wards off the assailant’s hand From what is sacred

burda.f: لَهَا مَعَانٍ كَمَوْجِ البَحْرِ فِي مَدَدٍ
burda.b: They contain meanings like the sea’s never-ending waves,
And go far beyond its jewels in their beauty and value
Their wonders are numberless and incalculable,
Nor does their constant repetition ever result in weariness or boredom

burda.f: قَرَّتْ بِهَا عَيْنُ قَارِيهَا فَقُلْتُ لَهُ
burda.b: The one who recited them was filled with delight, and I said to him,
“Truly you have seized the rope of Allah — so hold on to it.”

burda.f: إِنْ تَتْلُهَا خِيفَةً مِنْ حَرِّ نَارِ لَظَى
burda.b: If you recite them fearing the heat of the blazing Fire,

burda.f: أَطْفَأْتَ حَرَّ لَظَى مِنْ وِرْدِهَا الشَّبِمِ
burda.b: You have extinguished the heat of the blaze by their cool sweet water
Like the Ḥawḍ, which makes bright the faces of the disobedient,
When they had arrived with faces black as coal
Like the Ṣirāṭ and like the Balance Scales in justice,

burda.f: فَالقِسْطُ مِنْ غَيْرِهَا فِي النَّاسِ لَمْ يَقُمِ
burda.b: True justice among men cannot be established from any other
Do not be surprised if an envious person refuses to acknowledge them,
Affecting ignorance, even though perfectly able to understand

burda.f: قَدْ تُنْكِرُ العَيْنُ ضَوْءَ الشَّمْسِ مِنْ رَمَدٍ
burda.b: For the eye may reject the sun’s light when it is inflamed,

burda.f: وَيُنْكِرُ الفَمُ طَعْمَ المَاءِ مِنْ سَقَمِ
burda.b: And when the body is unwell, The mouth may shun even the taste of sweet water

burda.f: يَا خَيْرَ مَنْ يَمَّمَ العَافُونَ سَاحَتَهُ
burda.b: O best of those to whose courtyards repair the seekers of blessings,
On foot and on the backs of laden camels
O you who are the greatest sign for the one able to perceive,
And the most sublime blessing for the one desiring benefit

burda.f: سَرَيْتَ مِنْ حَرَمٍ لَيْلاً إِلَى حَرَمٍ
burda.b: You travelled by night from one sacred place to yet another,

burda.f: كَمَا سَرَى البَدْرُ فِي دَاجٍ مِنَ الظُّلَمِ
burda.b: Just as the full moon travels across the pitch-black sky

burda.f: وَبِتَّ تَرْقَى إِلَى أَنْ نِلْتَ مَنْزِلَةً
burda.b: That night you ascended until you reached a station of nearness,

burda.f: مِنْ قَابِ قَوْسَيْنِ لَمْ تُدْرَكْ وَلَمْ تُرَمِ
burda.b: Only two bows-lengths distant, A station never before attained or even hoped for
Thus all the Prophets and Messengers gave precedence to you,
The precedence of a master over those who serve him
You traversed the Seven Heavens with them,

burda.f: فِي مَوْكِبٍ كُنْتَ فِيهِ صَاحِبَ العَلَمِ
burda.b: And you were the standard bearer – leading their procession

burda.f: حَتَّى إِذَا لَمْ تَدَعْ شَأْوًا لِمُسْتَبِقٍ
burda.b: Until you left no greater goal for the seeker of eminence and proximity,
Nor any higher station for the one seeking elevation
All other stations seemed lower in comparison with yours,
Since you were proclaimed in the highest terms – the unique one
So that you would achieve a station of perfect proximity,
Hidden from the eyes, And obtain a secret concealed from all creation
So you attained to every excellence without equal,
And you passed alone through every station, far from all others

burda.f: وَجَلَّ مِقْدَارُ مَا وُلِّيتَ مِنْ رُتَبٍ
burda.b: Sublime indeed is the measure of the ranks you have been granted,

burda.f: وَعَزَّ إِدْرَاكُ مَا أُولِيتَ مِنْ نِعَمِ
burda.b: Beyond comprehension the blessings bestowed upon you

burda.f: بُشْرَى لَنَا مَعْشَرَ الإِسْلَامِ إِنَّ لَنَا
burda.b: Glad tidings for us, O assembly of Muslims,
For truly we have a pillar of support and solicitude That can never be destroyed
When God named the one who called us to obey Him,
The noblest of Messengers, Henceforward we became the noblest of peoples
News of his marching out cast fear into the hearts of the enemy,
Just as heedless goats are startled at a sudden noise

burda.f: مَا زَالَ يَلْقَاهُمُ فِي كُلِّ مُعْتَرَكٍ
burda.b: He continued to meet them on every battleground,

burda.f: حَتَّى حَكَوْا بِالقَنَا لَحْمًا عَلَى وَضَمِ
burda.b: Until they were cut to pieces by spears, Like meat upon a butcher’s block
They were longing to flee, almost envying
The corpses carried off by the eagles and vultures
The nights passed, without them being able to keep count,

burda.f: مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنْ لَيَالِي الأَشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ
burda.b: Except if they were the nights of the Sacred Months
As if the religion were a guest that had arrived at their courtyards,

burda.f: بِكُلِّ قَرْمٍ إِلَى لَحْمِ العِدَا قَرِمِ
burda.b: With every brave chieftain ready to rend the flesh of their enemies
Bringing in its wake a sea of armed men upon fast horses,
Hurling forth waves of brave warriors in clashing tumult
Each responding to Allah’s summons, seeking His good pleasure,
Mounting a fierce assault, to tear out unbelief by its roots

burda.f: حَتىَّ غَدَتْ مِلَّةُ الإِسْلاَمِ وَهْيَ بِهِمْ
burda.b: Until the religion of Islam, thanks to them,
After banishment from her homeland, Was once again united with her kin
Ever protected from her enemies by the best father

burda.f: وَخَيْرِ بَعْلٍ فَلَمْ تَيْتَمْ وَلَمْ تَئِمِ
burda.b: And most excellent husband, So that she was neither orphaned nor widowed
They were mountains — ask those who fought against them,

burda.f: مَاذَا رَأَى مِنْهُمُ فِي كُلِّ مُصْطَدَمِ
burda.b: Just what they saw of them on every battlefield

burda.f: وَسَلْ حُنَيْنًا وَسَلْ بَدْرًا وَسَلْ أُحُدًا
burda.b: Ask Hunayn, ask Badr, ask Uhud — seasons of death and destruction,

burda.f: فُصُولَ حَتْفٍ لَهُمْ أَدْهَى مِنَ الوَخَمِ
burda.b: More calamitous for them than fatal epidemics

burda.f: المُصْدِرِي البِيضِ حُمْرًا بَعْدَ مَا وَرَدَتْ
burda.b: Their burnished swords returned quenched and bloody,

burda.f: مِنَ العِدَا كُلَّ مُسْوَدٍّ مِنَ اللِّمَمِ
burda.b: After drinking deep beneath black locks on their enemies’ heads
Like writers wielding reed pens for spears,
Their pens left no part of the bodies unpointed or unmarked
Bristling with arms, yet a special quality distinguished them,
Just as a rose differs by its fragrance From the thorny salam tree
The winds of victory would present to you their fragrance,

burda.f: فَتَحْسَبُ الزَّهْرَ فِي الأَكْمَامِ كُلَّ كَمِي
burda.b: So that you imagine each valiant one of them To be a beautiful flower in bud

burda.f: كَأَنَّهُمْ فِي ظُهُورِ الخَيْلِ نَبْتُ رُبًا
burda.b: As if, riding their steeds, they were flowers blooming upon a height,

burda.f: مِنْ شِدَّةِ الحَزْمِ لاَ مِنْ شَدَّةِ الحُزُمِ
burda.b: Held there not by the tautness of their saddles, But by the firmness of their resolve

burda.f: طَارَتْ قُلُوبُ العِدَا مِنْ بَأْسِهِمْ فَرَقًا
burda.b: The enemy hearts in turmoil, terrified at their mighty power,
Could hardly tell brave warriors from herds of sheep
Those whose help comes from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ —

burda.f: إِنْ تَلْقَهُ الأُسْدُ فِي آجَامِهَا تَجِمِ
burda.b: Even lions encountering them in their dens would be struck dumb with fear

burda.f: وَلَنْ تَرَى مِنْ وَليٍّ غَيْرِ مُنْتَصِرٍ
burda.b: You would never see a friend of his unaided by him,

burda.f: بِهِ وَلاَ مِنْ عَدُوٍّ غَيْرِ مُنْقَصِمِ
burda.b: Nor yet an enemy of his undefeated
He established his community within the fortress of his religion,

burda.f: كَاللَّيْثِ حَلَّ مَعَ الأَشْبَالِ فِي أَجَمِ
burda.b: As the lion settles down with its cubs in its lair

burda.f: كَمْ جَدَّلَتْ كَلِمَاتُ اللهِ مِنْ جَدِلٍ
burda.b: How often have the words of Allah

burda.f: فِيهِ وَكَمْ خَصَمَ البُرْهَانُ مِنْ خَصِمِ
burda.b: Thrown down those who contended with him! How often has the Clear Proof defeated his opponents in argument!
Enough of a miracle for you — such knowledge found
In someone unlettered, living in the Age of Ignorance, And such refinement in an orphan!
I have served him with my praise, seeking pardon

burda.f: ذُنُوبَ عُمْرٍ مَضَى فِي الشِّعْرِ وَالخِدَمِ
burda.b: For the sins of a life spent in poetry and the service of others
Garlanded with these two sins, the consequences of which I dread
It is as though I were now a sacrificial animal

burda.f: أَطَعْتُ غَيَّ الصِّبَا فِي الحَالَتَيْنِ وَمَا
burda.b: In both these errors I followed only the reckless delinquency of youth
Achieving nothing in the end but wrong action and regret
Alas for a soul that has met with only loss in its transactions!

burda.f: لَمْ تَشْتَرِ الدِّينَ بِالدُّنْيَا وَلَمْ تَسُمِ
burda.b: It did not use this world to help secure the Next, Nor even to embark upon negotiations
Whoever sells his Hereafter in exchange for this world,

burda.f: يَبِنْ لَهُ الغَبْنُ فِي بَيْعٍ وَفِي سَلَمِ
burda.b: Soon discovers he has been cheated, both in present and future gains

burda.f: إِنْ آتِ ذَنْبًا فَمَا عَهْدِي بِمُنْتَقِضٍ
burda.b: If I were to commit a sin, it would not break
My contract with the Prophet ﷺ, Nor cut off my connection to him
For I have a covenant of protection from him
By my being named Muhammad, and he is the most faithful Of all mankind in keeping trusts

burda.f: إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي مَعَادِي آخِذًا بِيَدِي
burda.b: On the Day of Rising, if he does not take me by the hand

burda.f: فَضْلاً وَإِلاَّ فَقُلْ يَا زَلَّةَ القَدَمِ
burda.b: Out of pure kindness, then just say, “What a terrible end!”
Far be it from him to ever deprive the hopeful one Of his generous gifts,

burda.f: أَوْ يَرْجِعَ الجَارُ مِنْهُ غَيْرَ مُحْتَرَمِ
burda.b: Or to turn back someone seeking refuge Without treating him honourably
For ever since I have devoted all my thoughts to his praise,
I have found him to be the best guarantor of my salvation

burda.f: وَلَنْ يَفُوتَ الغِنَى مِنْهُ يَدًا تَرِبَتْ
burda.b: His bounty will not fail even a hand that is dusty and poor,

burda.f: إِنَّ الحَيَا يُنْبِتَ الأَزْهَارَ فِي الأَكَمِ
burda.b: For surely the rain may bring forth flowers even on the rockiest of slopes

burda.f: وَلَمْ أُرِدْ زَهْرَةَ الدُّنْيَا الَّتِي اقْتَطَفَتْ
burda.b: Indeed, I have no more desire for the flowers of this world,

burda.f: يَدَا زُهَيْرٍ بِمَا أَثْنَى عَلَى هَرِمِ
burda.b: Like those gathered in by the hands of Zuhayr For his praise of Ḥarim

burda.f: يَا أَكْرَمَ الخَلْقِ مَالِي مَنْ أَلُوذُ بِهِ
burda.b: O most Noble of all Creation, whose protection can I seek
But yours, when the Great Catastrophe overtakes us?

burda.f: وَلَنْ يَضِيقَ رَسُولَ اللهِ جَاهُكَ بِي
burda.b: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, your great rank Will not be lessened by my petition,
If the Generous One appears as the Avenger
For surely this world and its companion the Next Are from your generosity.
And part of your knowledge Is knowledge of the Preserved Tablet and of the Pen

burda.f: يَا نَفْسُ لاَ تَقْنَطِي مِنْ زَلَّةٍ عَظُمَتْ
burda.b: O my soul, do not despair over an error which may appear immense,
For surely even grave sins, with divine forgiveness, Are more like minor lapses
It may be that my Lord’s mercy, when He distributes it,

burda.f: تَأْتِي عَلَى حَسَبِ العِصْيَانِ فِي القِسَمِ
burda.b: Will be apportioned in accordance with the magnitude of sins

burda.f: يَا رَبِّ وَاجْعَلْ رَجَائِي غَيْرَ مُنْعَكِسٍ
burda.b: O my Lord, let not my hopes in You be cast back unfulfilled,
Nor let my firm conviction of Your goodness be thrown into disarray

burda.f: وَالْطُفْ بِعَبْدِكَ فِي الدَّارَيْنِ إِنَّ لَهُ
burda.b: Be kind to Your servant, both in this world and the Next,
For his patience, when called upon by dreadful fears, just disappears
And let a cloud of blessings from You pour down
Upon the Prophet ﷺ, raining down unceasingly

burda.f: مَا رَنَّحَتْ عَذَبَاتِ البَانِ رِيحُ صَبًا
burda.b: As long as the easterly breezes sway the willow boughs,
And the caravan leader urges on his white camels, Delighting them with his songs

burda.f: ثُمَّ الرِّضَا عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعَنْ عُمَرٍ
burda.b: And grant Your good pleasure to Abu Bakr and ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما,

burda.f: وَعَنْ عَلِيٍّ وَعَنْ عُثْمَانَ ذِي الكَرَمِ
burda.b: And to ʿAli رضي الله عنه and ʿUthman رضي الله عنه, the noble and generous
And to the Family and the Companions and Followers,
For they are the people of true mindfulness of God, And of purity, forbearance, and generosity
O my Lord, by the Chosen One, let us attain all that we are hoping for,

burda.f: وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا مَا مَضَى يَا وَاسِعَ الكَرَمِ
burda.b: And pardon us for what has passed, O Boundlessly Generous One
And, O God, forgive all the Muslims their wrong actions,

burda.f: يَتْلُونَ فِي المَسْجِدِ الأَقْصَى وَفِي الحَرَمِ
burda.b: By that which they recite in the Masjid al-Aqsa, As well as in the Ancient Sanctuary

burda.f: بِجَاهِ مَنْ بَيْتُهُ فِي طَيْبَةٍ حَرَمٌ
burda.b: By the rank of the one whose dwelling is a sanctuary in Tayba,
And whose very name is one of the greatest of oaths
This Burda of the Chosen One is now complete,

burda.f: وَالحَمْدُ لِلّهِ فِي بَدْءٍ وَفِي خَتَمِ
burda.b: Praise be to Allah for its beginning and for its end

burda.f: أَبْيَاتُهَا قَدْ أَتَتْ سِتِّينَ مَعْ مِائَةٍ
burda.b: Its verses number one hundred and sixty,

burda.f: فَرِّجْ بِهَا كَرْبَنَا يَا وَاسِعَ الكَرَمِ
burda.b: Ease, by them, all of our difficulties, O Boundlessly Generous Lord
